title: Chinese HSK 6
description: The sixth step in Mandarin Chinese, from HSK 5 to the new HSK 6 (HSK 3.0), the top of the intermediate band. Grammar lessons cover 要么…要么, 除非…才 and 除非…否则, 凡是…都, 就算…也, 与其…不如, 虽…却, 以便, the word-forming prefixes and suffixes (超-, 多-, 反-, 无-, 准-, -化, -性, -型, -式), the structural particle 所, written prepositions such as 于, 至于, 因 and 除, the colloquial formats of the level (X 归 X，Y 归 Y; 早不…晚不…; 看把你…的; 好不容易) and the register of formal notices, reports and arguments, with a lesson on idioms and set phrases. Topics run from careers, negotiation and finance through cities, health, the law and the media to cultures compared, heritage and history, science, energy and disasters, family life and values. The 1,800 new words (5,400 in all) are learned through typed review cards and the 413 new characters (1,940 in all) through notecards, words and tracing, with pinyin you can turn off and a switch to traditional characters. Readings grow to about 900 characters, and the last lessons practise the practical text, the argued essay, the speaking test and the exam format. Requires Chinese HSK 5.
author: Erudior

lessons.title: Careers, posts and promotion
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Welcome to HSK 6, the last level of the intermediate band. You know 3,600 words and 1,527
characters: the complex sentences of HSK 4 and 5 ({一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù}, {哪怕|nǎ pà}…{也|yě}, {不但|bú dàn}{不|bù}…{反而|fǎn ér}, {再|zài}…{也|yě}), the adverbs of
mood ({毕竟|bì jìng}, {居然|jū rán}, {简直|jiǎn zhí}, {反正|fǎn zhèng}), the written words of notices and news ({便|biàn}, {较|jiào}, {及|jí}, {其|qí}, {如何|rú hé}, {从而|cóng ér}) and the first
idioms. This course adds 1,800 words and 413 characters. Four things grow:

- **Register.** HSK 6 completes the written style ({于|yú}, {至于|zhì yú}, {之所以|zhī suǒ yǐ}…{是|shì}{因为|yīn wèi}, {以便|yǐ biàn}) and brings the colloquial
  formats of everyday speech ({早|zǎo}{不|bù}{来|lái}{晚|wǎn}{不|bù}{来|lái}, {看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}). You'll often see the same thing said both ways.
- **Word formation.** Many new words are built from parts you know. This lesson starts with the
  endings -{化|huà}, -{性|xìng}, -{型|xíng}, -{式|shì} and {业|yè}, and the front part {副|fù}.
- **Length.** Readings are 600 to 750 characters in the first three modules and up to 900 later, like
  the reading passages of the HSK 6 exam.
- **Writing and speaking.** Every lesson has a practical text to write (a notice, an email, a
  request, a letter) of 150 to 200 characters; from module 3 you also write an argued essay. The
  speaking tasks now use four pictures.

The story moves on to 2031. {李明|Lǐ Míng} (Li Ming) is back in Beijing and works as a translator at a
company; {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) writes commentary for the news website; {安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) is a guide and
translator at an art museum. {大卫|Dà wèi} (David) and his partner {白涛|Bái Tāo} (Bai Tao) run the small company that
brings British secondary-school students on study trips to China. Business is good, and in this
lesson they are hiring.

## Word formation: suffixes and prefixes

Most Chinese words are built from syllables that each mean something. Some of those syllables have
become regular building blocks. A **[[suffix]]** is one that goes at the end and makes a word of a
certain kind (an ending like English *-ize* or *-ity*); a **[[prefix]]** goes at the front (like *vice-*).
Knowing the common ones lets you understand words you have never met, and HSK 6 is full of them.

### -{化|huà}: to become, to make (-ize)

{化|huà} after an adjective or a noun makes a word for becoming, or making something, more like it:

| Word | Built from | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {现代化|xiàn dài huà} | {现代|xiàn dài} modern + {化|huà} | to modernize; modernization |
| {国际|guó jì}{化|huà} | {国际|guó jì} international + {化|huà} | to internationalize; internationalization |
| {年轻|nián qīng}{化|huà} | {年轻|nián qīng} young + {化|huà} | to get younger (of a group) |
| {美|měi}{化|huà} | {美|měi} beautiful + {化|huà} | to beautify |
| {强化|qiáng huà} | {强|qiáng} strong + {化|huà} | to strengthen (lesson 03's word) |
| {简化|jiǎn huà} | {简单|jiǎn dān} simple → {简|jiǎn} + {化|huà} | to simplify (lesson 28's word) |

{我们|wǒ men}{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{管理|guǎn lǐ}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{现代化|xiàn dài huà}{了|le}。 — Our company's management is getting more and more modern.

{这|zhè}{几|jǐ}{年|nián}，{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{员工|yuán gōng}{明显|míng xiǎn}{年轻|nián qīng}{化|huà}{了|le}。 — In the last few years the company's staff have clearly got younger.

{白领|bái lǐng}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}{方式|fāng shì}{正在|zhèng zài}{发生|fā shēng}{变化|biàn huà}。 — The way white-collar workers work is changing. ({变化|biàn huà}, a change, is
the same {化|huà}.)

An X{化|huà} word works as a verb (often with {了|le}: {年轻|nián qīng}{化|huà}{了|le}) or as a noun ({实现|shí xiàn}{现代化|xiàn dài huà}, to achieve
modernization). In speech some also work like adjectives: {这个|zhè ge}{城市|chéng shì}{很|hěn}{现代化|xiàn dài huà} (this city is very modern) is
common. Written reports prefer the verb and noun uses.

### -{性|xìng}: the quality of being… (-ity, -ness)

{性|xìng} after an adjective or a verb makes an abstract noun: the quality, or how much of it there is.

| Word | Built from | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {重要|zhòng yào}{性|xìng} | {重要|zhòng yào} important | importance |
| {可能|kě néng}{性|xìng} | {可能|kě néng} possible | possibility |
| {积极|jī jí}{性|xìng} | {积极|jī jí} active, keen | enthusiasm, motivation |
| {必要|bì yào}{性|xìng} | {必要|bì yào} necessary | necessity |
| {安全|ān quán}{性|xìng} | {安全|ān quán} safe | safety |
| {专业|zhuān yè}{性|xìng} | {专业|zhuān yè} professional | professionalism, expertise |

The noun goes where nouns go, with verbs like {有|yǒu}, {提高|tí gāo} and {认识|rèn shi} and adjectives like {大|dà}, {高|gāo}, {强|qiáng}:

{福利|fú lì}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{公司|gōng sī}，{员工|yuán gōng}{的|de}{积极|jī jí}{性|xìng}{往往|wǎng wǎng}{比较|bǐ jiào}{高|gāo}。 — At companies with good benefits, staff motivation is usually higher.

{他|tā}{还|hái}{没|méi}{认识|rèn shi}{到|dào}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{的|de}{重要|zhòng yào}{性|xìng}。 — He hasn't yet realised how important this is.

{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{可能|kě néng}{性|xìng}{不|bú}{大|dà}。 — That's not very likely. (Literally "this possibility isn't big".)

The adjective and the {性|xìng} noun don't swap: {他|tā}{很|hěn}{积极|jī jí} (he's keen) or {他|tā}{的|de}{积极|jī jí}{性|xìng}{很|hěn}{高|gāo} (his motivation is high),
never ~~{他|tā}{很|hěn}{积极|jī jí}{性|xìng}~~. Words you already have use the same {性|xìng}: {个性|gè xìng} (personality), {性格|xìng gé}, {性别|xìng bié}, and lesson 02
brings {性价比|xìng jià bǐ} (value for money).

### -{型|xíng}: type, model

{型|xíng} is a type or a model. Words with {型|xíng} at the end name a kind or a size and go straight before a noun:

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {大型|dà xíng} | large-scale | {大型|dà xíng}{企业|qǐ yè} (a large company) |
| {中型|zhōng xíng} | medium-sized | {中型|zhōng xíng}{城市|chéng shì} |
| {小型|xiǎo xíng} | small-scale | {小型|xiǎo xíng}{公司|gōng sī} |
| {新型|xīn xíng} | new type of | {新型|xīn xíng}{材料|cái liào} (new materials) |
| {技术|jì shù}{型|xíng} | technical, technically minded | {技术|jì shù}{型|xíng}{人才|rén cái} (technical talent) |

These words don't take {很|hěn} and don't stand alone as the predicate: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{大型|dà xíng}{企业|qǐ yè} (it's a large company), not
~~{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{企业|qǐ yè}{很|hěn}{大型|dà xíng}~~. If you must put one after the noun, frame it with {是|shì}…{的|de}: {这|zhè}{家|jiā}{企业|qǐ yè}{是|shì}{大型|dà xíng}{的|de}. In job
advertisements you'll meet whole chains: {技术|jì shù}{型|xíng}{人才|rén cái}, {管理|guǎn lǐ}{型|xíng}{人才|rén cái} (people suited to management).

### -{式|shì}: style, manner

{式|shì} is a style or a way of doing something:

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {中式|zhōng shì} | Chinese-style | {中式|zhōng shì}{早餐|zǎo cān} |
| {西式|xī shì} | Western-style | {西式|xī shì}{快餐|kuài cān} |
| {老式|lǎo shì} | old-fashioned | {老式|lǎo shì}{手机|shǒu jī} |
| {新式|xīn shì} | new-style | {新式|xīn shì}{教育|jiào yù} |
| {方式|fāng shì} | way, manner (HSK 4) | {工作|gōng zuò}{方式|fāng shì} |
| {正式|zhèng shì} | formal; official (HSK 4) | {正式|zhèng shì}{员工|yuán gōng} (a permanent member of staff) |

Like the {型|xíng} words, {中式|zhōng shì}, {西式|xī shì}, {老式|lǎo shì} and {新式|xīn shì} go before a noun. The difference: {型|xíng} says *what type or size*
a thing is ({大型|dà xíng}, {新型|xīn xíng}), {式|shì} says *in what style* it's made or done ({中式|zhōng shì}, {老式|lǎo shì}).

### {业|yè}: trade, industry

{业|yè} at the end of a word names a trade or a whole sector:

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {服务|fú wù}{业|yè} | the service industry |
| {旅游|lǚ yóu}{业|yè} | tourism, the travel trade |
| {农业|nóng yè} / {工业|gōng yè} / {商业|shāng yè} | agriculture / industry / commerce (HSK 5) |
| {行业|háng yè} | trade, line of business (HSK 5) |

The same {业|yè} is in {毕业|bì yè}, {专业|zhuān yè}, {就业|jiù yè}, {企业|qǐ yè} and in this lesson's {从业|cóng yè}: to work in a trade. {从业|cóng yè} is written
style, mostly in {从业人员|cóng yè rén yuán} (people working in the trade) and {从业|cóng yè}{经验|jīng yàn} (experience in the trade):
{本|běn}{公司|gōng sī}{招聘|zhāo pìn}{导游|dǎo yóu}，{要求|yāo qiú}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{年|nián}{以上|yǐ shàng}{从业|cóng yè}{经验|jīng yàn}。 (We are hiring tour guides; at least two years' experience in
the trade required.)

### {副|fù}-: deputy, vice-

{副|fù} before a job title makes the deputy post:

| Chief | Deputy |
|---|---|
| {经理|jīng lǐ} manager | {副|fù}{经理|jīng lǐ} deputy manager |
| {总|zǒng}{经理|jīng lǐ} general manager | {副|fù}{总|zǒng}{经理|jīng lǐ} deputy general manager |
| {主任|zhǔ rèn} director | {副|fù}{主任|zhǔ rèn} deputy director |
| {校长|xiào zhǎng} head teacher | {副|fù}{校长|xiào zhǎng} deputy head |
| {教授|jiào shòu} professor | {副|fù}{教授|jiào shòu} associate professor |

{白涛|Bái Tāo}{是|shì}{总|zǒng}{经理|jīng lǐ}，{大卫|Dà wèi}{是|shì}{副|fù}{总|zǒng}{经理|jīng lǐ}。 — Bai Tao is the general manager and David is the deputy general
manager.

You know a different {副|fù} from HSK 5, the measure word for pairs and sets ({一|yí}{副|fù}{眼镜|yǎn jìng}, a pair of glasses);
the deputy {副|fù} is an adjective that only goes before nouns. Its opposite is {正|zhèng} in a few pairs ({正|zhèng}{教授|jiào shòu},
a full professor; {正职|zhèng zhí} and {副职|fù zhí}, the chief and the deputy posts). In the same way {总|zǒng} (chief, general)
makes {总|zǒng}{经理|jīng lǐ}, {总部|zǒng bù} (headquarters) and this lesson's {总裁|zǒng cái} (president, CEO).

Lesson 16 adds the prefixes {超|chāo}-, {多|duō}-, {反|fǎn}-, {无|wú}-, {亚|yà}- and {准|zhǔn}-.

## Words for careers

### Posts and people

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {职位|zhí wèi} | position (the title you hold) | {申请|shēn qǐng}{这个|zhè ge}{职位|zhí wèi} |
| {职务|zhí wù} | post, duties (formal) | {担任|dān rèn}{副|fù}{经理|jīng lǐ}{职务|zhí wù} |
| {岗位|gǎng wèi} | post, job (a place in the work) | {他|tā}{在|zài}{新|xīn}{的|de}{岗位|gǎng wèi}{上|shàng}{干|gàn}{得|de}{不错|bú cuò}。 |
| {职责|zhí zé} | duties, responsibilities of a post | {明确|míng què}{每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{的|de}{职责|zhí zé} |
| {职员|zhí yuán} | clerk, office worker | {公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{普通|pǔ tōng}{职员|zhí yuán} |
| {白领|bái lǐng} | white-collar worker | {北京|Běi jīng}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{白领|bái lǐng}。 |
| {上级|shàng jí} | superior, higher level | {向|xiàng}{上级|shàng jí}{汇报|huì bào} (report to your superior; {汇报|huì bào} is lesson 03's) |
| {主管|zhǔ guǎn} | person in charge; to be in charge of | {人事|rén shì}{主管|zhǔ guǎn} (the HR manager); {他|tā}{主管|zhǔ guǎn}{销售|xiāo shòu}。 |
| {总裁|zǒng cái} | president, CEO (of a large company) | {集团|jí tuán}{总裁|zǒng cái} |
| {助理|zhù lǐ} | assistant (a job title) | {总|zǒng}{经理|jīng lǐ}{助理|zhù lǐ}, {运营助理|yùn yíng zhù lǐ} |
| {助手|zhù shǒu} | helper, assistant (a person who helps) | {她|tā}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{好|hǎo}{助手|zhù shǒu}。 |
| {人事|rén shì} | personnel matters | {人事部|rén shì bù} (the personnel department), {人事|rén shì}{主管|zhǔ guǎn} |

- {职位|zhí wèi}, {职务|zhí wù} and {岗位|gǎng wèi} overlap. {职位|zhí wèi} is the position as a rank or title ({申请|shēn qǐng}{职位|zhí wèi}, apply for a position); {职务|zhí wù}
  is the post with its duties, in formal writing ({担任|dān rèn}{职务|zhí wù}, hold a post); {岗位|gǎng wèi} is the job as a place in
  the work, often with {上|shàng} or {在|zài} ({在|zài}{工作|gōng zuò}{岗位|gǎng wèi}{上|shàng}, at one's post; {新|xīn}{的|de}{岗位|gǎng wèi}, a new job).
- {助理|zhù lǐ} is a title on a business card ({经理|jīng lǐ}{助理|zhù lǐ}); {助手|zhù shǒu} is anyone who helps you, at work or at home.
- {主管|zhǔ guǎn} is a noun (the manager in charge) and a verb ({主管|zhǔ guǎn}{销售|xiāo shòu}, to be in charge of sales).

### Hiring

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {招|zhāo} | to recruit; to beckon | {公司|gōng sī}{要|yào}{招|zhāo}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}。 |
| {用人|yòng rén} | to employ people | {用人单位|yòng rén dān wèi} (an employer: {单位|dān wèi}, organisation) |
| {求职|qiú zhí} | to look for a job | {求职信|qiú zhí xìn} (a covering letter) |
| {筛选|shāi xuǎn} | to screen, sift | {筛选|shāi xuǎn}{简历|jiǎn lì} |
| {录用|lù yòng} | to hire, take on | {她|tā}{被|bèi}{录用|lù yòng}{了|le}。 |
| {兼职|jiān zhí} | to work part-time, hold a second job; part-time job | {找|zhǎo}{一|yí}{份|fèn}{兼职|jiān zhí}, {兼职|jiān zhí}{导游|dǎo yóu} |

- {招|zhāo} in speech is {招聘|zhāo pìn} (HSK 4) cut short: {招|zhāo}{人|rén}, {招|zhāo}{两|liǎng}{名|míng}{导游|dǎo yóu}. It also means "to beckon": {他|tā}{向|xiàng}{我|wǒ}{招|zhāo}{了|le}{招手|zhāo shǒu}. (lesson
  25 has {招手|zhāo shǒu}, to wave.)
- {录用|lù yòng} is the decision to take someone on, the end of {招聘|zhāo pìn}: {经过|jīng guò}{面试|miàn shì}，{公司|gōng sī}{决定|jué dìng}{录用|lù yòng}{她|tā}。
- {兼职|jiān zhí} is a verb ({他|tā}{在|zài}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{兼职|jiān zhí}, he works part-time at a website) and a noun ({一|yí}{份|fèn}{兼职|jiān zhí}). Its opposite is {全职|quán zhí}
  (full-time): {全职|quán zhí}{工作|gōng zuò}.
- {用人|yòng rén} is the employer's side: {用人单位|yòng rén dān wèi} (the employer), {公司|gōng sī}{用人|yòng rén}{很|hěn}{严格|yán gé} (the company is strict about whom it
  hires).

### Pay and the working day

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {薪水|xīn shuǐ} | salary, pay | {薪水|xīn shuǐ}{不|bù}{高|gāo} |
| {福利|fú lì} | benefits, welfare | {福利|fú lì}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} |
| {年终|nián zhōng} | end of the year | {年终奖|nián zhōng jiǎng} (an end-of-year bonus) |
| {打卡|dǎ kǎ} | to clock in | {每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{前|qián}{打卡|dǎ kǎ} |
| {值班|zhí bān} | to be on duty | {周末|zhōu mò}{轮流|lún liú}{值班|zhí bān} (take turns on duty at weekends: {轮流|lún liú} is lesson 03's) |

- {薪水|xīn shuǐ} and {工资|gōng zī} (HSK 4) both mean pay. {工资|gōng zī} is the everyday word and the one on a payslip; {薪水|xīn shuǐ} sounds a
  little more literary and is common in talk about jobs ({薪水|xīn shuǐ}{高|gāo}, {薪水|xīn shuǐ}{不错|bú cuò}) and in job advertisements
  ({薪水|xīn shuǐ}{面议|miàn yì}, below); advertisements also write {薪资|xīn zī} or {待遇|dài yù}.
- {福利|fú lì} is what comes on top of pay: holidays, insurance, meals, training.
- {打卡|dǎ kǎ} is to clock in or out ({打|dǎ} + {卡|kǎ}, a card). It's also slang for visiting a famous place and posting a
  photo: {去|qù}{网红|wǎng hóng}{店|diàn}{打卡|dǎ kǎ} ({网红|wǎng hóng}: internet-famous). Here it's the office meaning.

### The company

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {集团|jí tuán} | group (of companies) | {一|yì}{家|jiā}{大型|dà xíng}{集团|jí tuán} |
| {创办|chuàng bàn} | to found, set up (a school, a company, a paper) | {他|tā}{创办|chuàng bàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{小|xiǎo}{公司|gōng sī}。 |
| {创建|chuàng jiàn} | to found, establish (an organisation, a system) | {创建|chuàng jiàn}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{的|de}{部门|bù mén} |
| {创立|chuàng lì} | to found (formal; a company, a school of thought) | {这|zhè}{家|jiā}{公司|gōng sī}{创立|chuàng lì}{于|yú}1990{年|nián}。 |
| {开设|kāi shè} | to open, set up (a course, a branch, an account) | {开设|kāi shè}{培训|péi xùn}{课|kè}, {开设|kāi shè}{分|fēn}{公司|gōng sī} |

- {创办|chuàng bàn}, {创建|chuàng jiàn} and {创立|chuàng lì} all mean "to found". {创办|chuàng bàn} is the most general (you found and run it: {创办|chuàng bàn}{学校|xué xiào}, {创办|chuàng bàn}{公司|gōng sī});
  {创建|chuàng jiàn} stresses building a new structure ({创建|chuàng jiàn}{部门|bù mén}, {创建|chuàng jiàn}{网站|wǎng zhàn}); {创立|chuàng lì} is formal and often has a date: {创立|chuàng lì}{于|yú}…
  (founded in…, written; {于|yú} is lesson 27's word).
- {开设|kāi shè} is to open something that offers a service: a course, a branch, a bank account.

do well may become permanent staff. Those interested should send a CV and covering letter to the
company email address by 15 May, with the subject 'Application + post'. Applicants who pass the
screening will be invited to interview. We regret that materials cannot be returned. Contact: Mr
David."
</details>

### The same message, spoken

Here's how David tells a friend about the job, in everyday speech. Compare the two registers:

> {我们|wǒ men}{公司|gōng sī}{在|zài}{招|zhāo}{人|rén}，{要|yào}{一|yí}{个|gè}{全职|quán zhí}{的|de}{运营助理|yùn yíng zhù lǐ}，{帮|bāng}{白涛|Bái Tāo}{安排|ān pái}{行程|xíng chéng}、{联系|lián xì}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{什么|shén me}{的|de}。{最好|zuì hǎo}{在|zài}{旅游|lǚ yóu}{或者|huò zhě}{教育|jiào yù}{行业|háng yè}{干|gàn}{过|guo}，{英语|Yīng yǔ}{得|děi}{好|hǎo}。{工资|gōng zī}{可以|kě yǐ}{谈|tán}，{年底|nián dǐ}{有|yǒu}{奖金|jiǎng jīn}，{中午|zhōng wǔ}{公司|gōng sī}{管饭|guǎn fàn}。{另外|lìng wài}{还|hái}{要|yào}{三|sān}{个|gè}{暑假|shǔ jià}{兼职|jiān zhí}{的|de}{导游|dǎo yóu}，{学|xué}{历史|lì shǐ}{的|de}{研究生|yán jiū shēng}{最好|zuì hǎo}。{有|yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù}{的话|de huà}，{五|wǔ}{月|yuè}{十五|shí wǔ}{号|hào}{以前|yǐ qián}{把|bǎ}{简历|jiǎn lì}{发|fā}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{行|xíng}。

| Advertisement | Speech |
|---|---|
| {诚聘|chéng pìn}{以下|yǐ xià}{人员|rén yuán} | {我们|wǒ men}{公司|gōng sī}{在|zài}{招|zhāo}{人|rén} |
| {有|yǒu}…{经验|jīng yàn}{者|zhě}{优先|yōu xiān} | {最好|zuì hǎo}{在|zài}…{干|gàn}{过|guo} |
| {薪水|xīn shuǐ}{面议|miàn yì} | {工资|gōng zī}{可以|kě yǐ}{谈|tán} |
| {另|lìng}{有|yǒu}{年终奖|nián zhōng jiǎng} | {年底|nián dǐ}{有|yǒu}{奖金|jiǎng jīn} |
| {提供|tí gōng}{免费|miǎn fèi}{午餐|wǔ cān} | {中午|zhōng wǔ}{公司|gōng sī}{管饭|guǎn fàn} ({管饭|guǎn fàn}: to provide meals) |
| {有意者|yǒu yì zhě}{请|qǐng}{于|yú}5{月|yuè}15{日|rì}{前|qián}{将|jiāng}{简历|jiǎn lì}{发至|fā zhì}… | {有|yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù}{的话|de huà}，{五|wǔ}{月|yuè}{十五|shí wǔ}{号|hào}{以前|yǐ qián}{把|bǎ}{简历|jiǎn lì}{发|fā}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{行|xíng} |

## A written text: a CV summary

{江欣|Jiāng Xīn} (Jiang Xin) opens her CV with a short summary of herself, the part an employer reads first:

> {个人|gè rén}{简介|jiǎn jiè}
>
> {江欣|Jiāng Xīn}，{女|nǚ}，{二十八|èr shí bā}{岁|suì}，{英语|Yīng yǔ}{专业|zhuān yè}{本科|běn kē}{毕业|bì yè}。{曾|céng}{在|zài}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{大型|dà xíng}{集团|jí tuán}{担任|dān rèn}{总裁|zǒng cái}{助理|zhù lǐ}{两|liǎng}{年|nián}，{主要|zhǔ yào}{负责|fù zé}{安排|ān pái}{会议|huì yì}{和|hé}{出差|chū chāi}{行程|xíng chéng}、{处理|chǔ lǐ}{各种|gè zhǒng}{邮件|yóu jiàn}，{熟悉|shú xī}{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{日常|rì cháng}{管理|guǎn lǐ}{工作|gōng zuò}。{大学|dà xué}{期间|qī jiān}{曾|céng}{做|zuò}{过|guo}{三|sān}{年|nián}{兼职|jiān zhí}{导游|dǎo yóu}，{带|dài}{过|guo}{来自|lái zì}{十|shí}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{国家|guó jiā}{的|de}{游客|yóu kè}。{本人|běn rén}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{认真|rèn zhēn}{细致|xì zhì}，{沟通|gōu tōng}{能力|néng lì}{强|qiáng}，{有|yǒu}{团队精神|tuán duì jīng shén}，{能|néng}{适应|shì yìng}{较|jiào}{大|dà}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}{压力|yā lì}。{特长|tè cháng}：{英语|Yīng yǔ}{口语|kǒu yǔ}{和|hé}{写作|xiě zuò}，{摄影|shè yǐng}。{希望|xī wàng}{在|zài}{新|xīn}{的|de}{岗位|gǎng wèi}{上|shàng}{发挥|fā huī}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{才能|cái néng}，{和|hé}{公司|gōng sī}{一起|yì qǐ}{成长|chéng zhǎng}。

- {个人|gè rén}{简介|jiǎn jiè} (jiǎn jiè: lesson 10's {简介|jiǎn jiè}): a short personal profile. {曾|céng} (HSK 5): once, formerly.
- {本人|běn rén} (HSK 5): I (formal), the person writing. {较|jiào}{大|dà}{的|de} (HSK 5's {较|jiào}): fairly great.
- {认真|rèn zhēn}{细致|xì zhì} ({细致|xì zhì}, lesson 03's word: careful, meticulous), {团队精神|tuán duì jīng shén} (team spirit).
- {发挥|fā huī}{才能|cái néng}: to bring one's abilities into play.

"Profile. Jiang Xin, female, 28, graduate in English. Worked for two years as assistant to the CEO of
a large group, mainly arranging meetings and business trips and handling emails; familiar
with a company's day-to-day management. At university worked for three years as a part-time guide,
guiding visitors from more than ten countries. I am conscientious and careful, communicate well,
work well in a team and can cope with a fair amount of pressure. Special skills: spoken and written
English, photography. I hope to use my abilities in a new post and grow with the company."

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 岗 (traditional 崗) ✎ | mound; post, sentry post | gǎng | 山 | 7 | {岗位|gǎng wèi} |
| 兼 | double; at the same time | jiān | 丷 | 10 | {兼职|jiān zhí} |
| 潜 (traditional 潛) | to dive; hidden | qián | 氵 | 15 | {潜力|qián lì} |
| 筛 (traditional 篩) | sieve; to sift | shāi | ⺮ | 12 | {筛选|shāi xuǎn} |
| 薪 | firewood; pay | xīn | 艹 | 16 | {薪水|xīn shuǐ} |

Traditional strokes: 崗 11, 篩 16; 潛 has 15, like 潜.

### A new radical: 山 (mountain)

山 is a picture of three peaks. As a radical it sits on top (岗, 岁) or on the left (later 峰, a
peak: lesson 07), and marks characters for hills, mountains and high ground. The characters you know
with it are few: 山 itself and 岁 (age), which Make Me a Hanzi files under the 山 on top. This
lesson brings 岗 (in {岗位|gǎng wèi}). Its oldest sense is a ridge or mound, and the post at work came from it
by way of a lookout post (a memory aid, not a documented history). Later lessons add 峰 (07), 岸
and 岛 (17), 崭 (20) and 崇 (24).

### Sound families

- 岗 gǎng is 山 over 冈 gāng (ridge), the sound part. The same 冈 is in 刚 gāng (just, HSK 2) and
  钢 gāng (steel: {钢琴|gāng qín}, HSK 4). Learn them together: 冈 → 刚 钢 岗. (Traditional 崗 has the
  older form 岡 under 山.)
- 薪 xīn is 艹 (grass) over 新 xīn (new), which gives the sound exactly. Its first meaning is
  firewood, hence the grass part; {薪水|xīn shuǐ} (pay) is literally "firewood and water", the costs of daily
  life.
- 兼 jiān began as a hand holding two stalks of grain (禾) at once, hence "double, at the same
  time" (Shuowen). It's the sound part of 谦 qiān (modest: {谦虚|qiān xū}, lesson 24), 嫌 xián (to dislike:
  lesson 23) and 歉 qiàn ({道歉|dào qiàn}, HSK 4): the sound has drifted, but the 兼 is easy to spot.
- 筛 shāi is ⺮ (bamboo: sieves were woven from it) over 师 shī, which gives a similar sound.
  Traditional 篩 has 師.
- 潜 qián is 氵 (water) + 朁 cǎn: under the water, hidden; {潜力|qián lì} is hidden strength.

### Look-alikes

- 兼 and 谦 嫌 歉: the same part, with 讠, 女 or 欠 added.
- 薪 and 新: only the grass on top differs.
- 筛 and 师: ⺮ on top makes the sieve.

### Stroke order

- **岗**: 山 first (the middle vertical, the vertical that turns right, then the third vertical),
  then 冈 below: its left vertical, the horizontal that turns down with a hook, then the
  left-falling stroke and the dot inside.
- **兼**: a dot and a short left-falling stroke on top, then a horizontal; then the turn and the
  horizontals of the middle part; two verticals down through it, and the left-falling and
  right-falling strokes last.
- **薪**: 艹, then 亲 on the left (立 over a 木 whose last stroke is shortened to a dot), then
  斤 on the right.

```trace
岗兼潜筛薪
```

**Write it**: 岗 is a handwriting character (✎). Write it three times from memory, then the word
{岗位|gǎng wèi}.
=}

## Write it: a covering letter

The HSK 6 exam asks for a practical text of at least 150 characters. Write a short covering letter
({求职信|qiú zhí xìn}) of 150–200 characters for the part-time guide job in the advertisement above. Say who you
are, why you want the job, what makes you suitable, and when you're free. Use at least four of:
{兼职|jiān zhí}, {岗位|gǎng wèi}, {特长|tè cháng}, {潜力|qián lì}, {录用|lù yòng}, {职责|zhí zé}, {优先|yōu xiān}, {曾|céng}.

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

> {大卫|Dà wèi}{先生|xiān sheng}：
>
> {您|nín}{好|hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{贵公司|guì gōng sī}{的|de}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{上|shàng}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{了|le}{招聘|zhāo pìn}{兼职|jiān zhí}{导游|dǎo yóu}{的|de}{信息|xìn xī}，{很|hěn}{想|xiǎng}{申请|shēn qǐng}{这个|zhè ge}{岗位|gǎng wèi}。{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{叶远|Yè Yuǎn}，{是|shì}{北京|Běi jīng}{一|yì}{所|suǒ}{大学|dà xué}{历史|lì shǐ}{专业|zhuān yè}{的|de}{研究生|yán jiū shēng}，{对|duì}{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{历史|lì shǐ}{和|hé}{文化|wén huà}{十分|shí fēn}{熟悉|shú xī}。{我|wǒ}{曾|céng}{在|zài}{博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{做|zuò}{过|guo}{一|yì}{年|nián}{志愿者|zhì yuàn zhě}，{给|gěi}{外国|wài guó}{游客|yóu kè}{介绍|jiè shào}{展览|zhǎn lǎn}，{英语|Yīng yǔ}{口语|kǒu yǔ}{比较|bǐ jiào}{流利|liú lì}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{特长|tè cháng}{是|shì}{摄影|shè yǐng}，{可以|kě yǐ}{帮|bāng}{学生|xué sheng}{们|men}{拍照|pāi zhào}{留念|liú niàn}。{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{和|hé}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{交流|jiāo liú}，{也|yě}{明白|míng bai}{导游|dǎo yóu}{的|de}{职责|zhí zé}{首先|shǒu xiān}{是|shì}{照顾|zhào gù}{好|hǎo}{学生|xué sheng}{的|de}{安全|ān quán}。{七|qī}{月|yuè}{和|hé}{八|bā}{月|yuè}{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}。{如果|rú guǒ}{能|néng}{被|bèi}{录用|lù yòng}，{我|wǒ}{一定|yí dìng}{认真|rèn zhēn}{工作|gōng zuò}。{附上|fù shàng}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{简历|jiǎn lì}，{希望|xī wàng}{有|yǒu}{机会|jī huì}{面谈|miàn tán}。
>
> {叶远|Yè Yuǎn}
> 5{月|yuè}8{日|rì}

(about 190 characters) {贵公司|guì gōng sī} (guì gōng sī): your company (polite, written). {留念|liú niàn}: to keep as a
souvenir. {面谈|miàn tán} (miàn tán): to talk face to face. {附上|fù shàng}: to attach. "Dear Mr David, I saw the
advertisement for part-time guides on your company's website and would very much like to apply. My
name is Ye Yuan; I'm a history postgraduate at a university in Beijing and know Beijing's history and
culture well. I was a volunteer at a museum for a year, showing foreign visitors round the exhibitions, and
my spoken English is fairly fluent. My special skill is photography, so I can take pictures of the
students as souvenirs. I enjoy talking with young people, and I understand that a guide's first duty
is the students' safety. I'm free in July and August. If I'm taken on, I'll work hard. I attach my CV
and hope to have the chance of an interview. Ye Yuan, 8 May."

A checklist: greeting and a closing name and date; why you're writing in the first sentence; two or
three reasons with facts; polite written words ({贵公司|guì gōng sī}, {曾|céng}, {附上|fù shàng}); a closing wish.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Talking about jobs
{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{申请|shēn qǐng}{贵公司|guì gōng sī}{的|de}{运营助理|yùn yíng zhù lǐ}{职位|zhí wèi}。
= I'd like to apply for the operations assistant post at your company.
{我|wǒ}{曾|céng}{在|zài}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{集团|jí tuán}{担任|dān rèn}{总裁|zǒng cái}{助理|zhù lǐ}。
= I worked as assistant to the CEO of a group.
{我|wǒ}{的|de}{特长|tè cháng}{是|shì}{英语|Yīng yǔ}{和|hé}{摄影|shè yǐng}。
= My strong points are English and photography.
{福利|fú lì}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{公司|gōng sī}，{员工|yuán gōng}{的|de}{积极|jī jí}{性|xìng}{往往|wǎng wǎng}{比较|bǐ jiào}{高|gāo}。
= At companies with good benefits, staff motivation tends to be higher.
{这|zhè}{份|fèn}{工作|gōng zuò}{需要|xū yào}{轮流|lún liú}{值班|zhí bān}{吗|ma}？
= Does this job involve taking turns on duty?
{她|tā}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{潜力|qián lì}，{我们|wǒ men}{决定|jué dìng}{录用|lù yòng}{她|tā}。
= She has a lot of potential; we've decided to take her on.
```

## Pronunciation

- 职 zhí in {职位|zhí wèi}, {职务|zhí wù}, {职员|zhí yuán}, {职责|zhí zé}: zh with the tongue curled back and a rising tone. {职责|zhí zé} and {指责|zhǐ zé}
  (lesson 23: to criticise) differ only in the first syllable's tone (zhí zé / zhǐ zé).
- {兼职|jiān zhí} and {简直|jiǎn zhí} (HSK 5: simply) are the same syllables with different tones: jiān zhí, jiǎn zhí.
- 薪 xīn: x is soft, like the start of *she* said with a smile.
- {筛选|shāi xuǎn} shāi xuǎn: sh, then x: keep them apart.
- {录用|lù yòng} lù yòng: l, not n. {才华|cái huá} cái huá and {才能|cái néng} cái néng both start with the c of *its*.
- {主管|zhǔ guǎn} zhǔ guǎn: two third tones, said zhú guǎn (third-tone sandhi; written zhǔ guǎn).
- 副 fù: a falling tone, like 父 and 付.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{他|tā}{很|hěn}{积极|jī jí}{性|xìng}~~: {积极|jī jí}{性|xìng} is a noun. {他|tā}{很|hěn}{积极|jī jí} (he's keen) or {他|tā}{的|de}{积极|jī jí}{性|xìng}{很|hěn}{高|gāo} (his motivation is high).
- ~~{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{企业|qǐ yè}{很|hěn}{大型|dà xíng}~~: {大型|dà xíng}, {新型|xīn xíng}, {中式|zhōng shì} go straight before a noun: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{大型|dà xíng}{企业|qǐ yè}.
- {薪水|xīn shuǐ} in a contract: contracts and payslips say {工资|gōng zī} or {薪资|xīn zī}.
- {创立|chuàng lì}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{读书|dú shū}{小组|xiǎo zǔ} sounds far too grand: {创立|chuàng lì} is formal, for companies, schools and schools of thought. For a small group
  of friends, {成立|chéng lì} or {建|jiàn}: {我们|wǒ men}{成立|chéng lì}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{读书|dú shū}{小组|xiǎo zǔ}。
- {助理|zhù lǐ} and {助手|zhù shǒu}: a job title is {助理|zhù lǐ} ({经理|jīng lǐ}{助理|zhù lǐ}); {我|wǒ}{的|de}{好|hǎo}{助手|zhù shǒu} is a person who helps you.
- {兼职|jiān zhí} is a verb as well as a noun: {他|tā}{在|zài}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{兼职|jiān zhí} (no {做|zuò} needed); {做|zuò}{兼职|jiān zhí} / {找|zhǎo}{兼职|jiān zhí} are also fine.
- {副|fù} is "deputy" only before a noun: {他|tā}{是|shì}{副|fù}{经理|jīng lǐ}, not ~~{他|tā}{很|hěn}{副|fù}~~. As a measure word it's another word
  ({一|yí}{副|fù}{手套|shǒu tào}, a pair of gloves).

## Key points

- Suffixes: X{化|huà} (to become / make X: {现代化|xiàn dài huà}, {年轻|nián qīng}{化|huà}), X{性|xìng} (the quality: {重要|zhòng yào}{性|xìng}, {积极|jī jí}{性|xìng}: a noun), X{型|xíng} (type,
  size: {大型|dà xíng}, {新型|xīn xíng}: before a noun, no {很|hěn}), X{式|shì} (style: {中式|zhōng shì}, {老式|lǎo shì}), X{业|yè} (trade: {服务|fú wù}{业|yè}, {旅游|lǚ yóu}{业|yè}).
- Prefix {副|fù} (deputy: {副|fù}{经理|jīng lǐ}, {副|fù}{总|zǒng}{经理|jīng lǐ}); {总|zǒng} (chief: {总|zǒng}{经理|jīng lǐ}, {总裁|zǒng cái}).
- Near-synonyms: {职位|zhí wèi} (title) / {职务|zhí wù} (post, formal) / {岗位|gǎng wèi} (place in the work); {薪水|xīn shuǐ} (spoken) / {工资|gōng zī}
  (everyday, official); {创办|chuàng bàn} / {创建|chuàng jiàn} / {创立|chuàng lì} (to found); {助理|zhù lǐ} (title) / {助手|zhù shǒu} (helper); {才华|cái huá} / {才能|cái néng}.
- Job advertisements: {诚聘|chéng pìn}, {有|yǒu}…{者|zhě}{优先|yōu xiān}, {薪水|xīn shuǐ}{面议|miàn yì}, {有意者|yǒu yì zhě}{请|qǐng}{于|yú}…{前|qián}{将|jiāng}…{发至|fā zhì}….
- New characters: 岗 兼 潜 筛 薪; new radical 山.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Suppliers, orders and negotiation
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

{大卫|Dà wèi} (David) and {白涛|Bái Tāo} (Bai Tao) want their summer students to arrive with a backpack in the
company's colours and a set of earphones for the guided visits. They find a manufacturer at a trade
fair and sit down to negotiate. The lesson brings:

- **{要么|yào me}…{要么|yào me}**: either… or… (**[[alternatives]]**), a choice between two courses of action, set beside {或者|huò zhě}, {还是|hái shi} and {不|bú}{是|shì}…{就是|jiù shì}.
- The written {限|xiàn} (to limit, be limited to) of notices and offers, and {可行|kě xíng} (feasible).
- The words of buying from a supplier: orders, prices, models, deadlines, warranties and invoices.
- A formal email confirming an order, the same message as it's said on the phone, and the first
  **[[retelling]]** task of the speaking test.

## {要么|yào me}…{要么|yào me}: either… or…

{要么|yào me} X，{要么|yào me} Y sets out two (or more) alternatives, of which one has to be chosen. Often neither is
perfect: the speaker is narrowing things down.

{要么|yào me}{降价|jiàng jià}，{要么|yào me}{延期|yán qī}{交货|jiāo huò}，{你们|nǐ men}{得|děi}{选|xuǎn}{一|yí}{个|gè}。 — Either you lower the price or you deliver later: you'll have
to choose one. ({交货|jiāo huò}: to deliver goods)

{我们|wǒ men}{要么|yào me}{今天|jīn tiān}{下单|xià dān}，{要么|yào me}{等|děng}{下|xià}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{的|de}{新款|xīn kuǎn}。 — Either we place the order today, or we wait for next month's
new model.

{要么|yào me}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}，{要么|yào me}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}，{总|zǒng}{得|děi}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{跟|gēn}{厂家|chǎng jiā}{谈|tán}{一|yi}{谈|tán}。 — Either you go or I go: someone has to talk to the
manufacturer.

- {要么|yào me} goes at the start of each alternative: before the subject ({要么|yào me}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}，{要么|yào me}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}) or, with one
  subject, before each verb ({我们|wǒ men}{要么|yào me}{今天|jīn tiān}{下单|xià dān}，{要么|yào me}{等|děng}…).
- The second part often has {就|jiù} to push the choice: {要么|yào me}{改|gǎi}，{要么|yào me}{就|jiù}{别|bié}{做|zuò}{了|le}.
- A third alternative is fine: {要么|yào me}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}，{要么|yào me}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}，{要么|yào me}{开车|kāi chē}，{你|nǐ}{决定|jué dìng}。
- On its own, {要么|yào me} at the start of a reply suggests one way out: "how about…" (spoken): {要么|yào me}{这样|zhè yàng}{吧|ba}，
  {我们|wǒ men}{先|xiān}{订|dìng}{一半|yí bàn}。 (How about this: we order half first.)

### {要么|yào me}…{要么|yào me} and other kinds of "or"

| Pattern | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| X {或者|huò zhě} Y | "or" in a statement, an open list | {下午|xià wǔ}{或者|huò zhě}{明天|míng tiān}{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}。 |
| X {还是|hái shi} Y？ | "or?" in a question | {你|nǐ}{要|yào}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}{还是|hái shi}{蓝|lán}{色|sè}{的|de}？ |
| {要么|yào me} X，{要么|yào me} Y | choose one of these courses (and only these) | {要么|yào me}{退|tuì}{货|huò}，{要么|yào me}{换|huàn}{一|yí}{个|gè}。 |
| {不|bú}{是|shì} X {就是|jiù shì} Y | it's always one or the other (a fact, often a complaint) | {他|tā}{不|bú}{是|shì}{迟到|chí dào}{就是|jiù shì}{请假|qǐng jià}。 |
| {或是|huò shì} X，{或是|huò shì} Y | either… or… (written) | {或是|huò shì}{电话|diàn huà}，{或是|huò shì}{邮件|yóu jiàn}，{均|jūn}{可|kě}。 |

The key difference: {要么|yào me}…{要么|yào me} is above all about a choice to be made ({要么|yào me}{降价|jiàng jià}，{要么|yào me}{延期|yán qī}). It can also list
someone's usual options ({周末|zhōu mò}{他|tā}{要么|yào me}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{看|kàn}{书|shū}，{要么|yào me}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}: at weekends he either reads at home or goes
climbing). {不|bú}{是|shì}…{就是|jiù shì} adds "it's always one or the other", often as a complaint: {他|tā}{不|bú}{是|shì}{迟到|chí dào}{就是|jiù shì}{请假|qǐng jià} (he's always
either late or off sick).

## {限|xiàn}: a limit (written)

{限|xiàn} is "to limit; to be limited to". It's short and formal, at home in notices, offers and rules:

| Phrase | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {每|měi}{人|rén}{限|xiàn}{购|gòu}{两|liǎng}{件|jiàn} | limited to two items per person |
| {限|xiàn}{本|běn}{公司|gōng sī}{员工|yuán gōng} | staff of this company only |
| {限|xiàn}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{内|nèi}{答复|dá fù} | a reply is required within three days |
| {限|xiàn}{时|shí}{优惠|yōu huì} | a limited-time offer |
| {限|xiàn}{五十|wǔ shí}{人|rén} | limited to fifty people |

The pattern is {限|xiàn} + who or what + (number): {限|xiàn} + time or number puts a ceiling on it. In speech you'd
say {只能|zhǐ néng} or {最|zuì}{多|duō}: {每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{最|zuì}{多|duō}{买|mǎi}{两|liǎng}{件|jiàn}. Related words you know or meet here: {有限|yǒu xiàn} (limited, HSK 5), {限制|xiàn zhì} (to restrict,
HSK 5), and this lesson's {期限|qī xiàn} (a time limit, deadline): {付款|fù kuǎn}{期限|qī xiàn} (the payment deadline), {在|zài}{期限|qī xiàn}{内|nèi} (within
the time limit).

## {可行|kě xíng}: feasible

{可行|kě xíng} ({可|kě} + {行|xíng}, "can go ahead") is an adjective: a plan, a method or an idea that will work.

{这个|zhè ge}{方案|fāng àn}{可行|kě xíng}{吗|ma}？ — Is this plan feasible?

{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{先|xiān}{做|zuò}{一百|yì bǎi}{个|gè}{样品|yàng pǐn}{是|shì}{可行|kě xíng}{的|de}。 — I think making a hundred samples first is workable. ({样品|yàng pǐn}: sample)

There are several workable ideas: {有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{可行|kě xíng}{的|de}{办法|bàn fǎ}. The noun is {可行性|kě xíng xìng} (feasibility, with lesson
01's -{性|xìng}): {先|xiān}{研究|yán jiū}{一下|yí xià}{可行性|kě xíng xìng}. In speech you'd usually ask {行不行|xíng bu xíng}？ or {这样|zhè yàng}{行|xíng}{吗|ma}？.

spoken, by word of mouth. {写明|xiě míng}: to state in writing. {约定|yuē dìng} (HSK 5): agreement. {带|dài}{子|zi}: strap. {列为|liè wéi}: to list as. {优惠|yōu huì} (HSK 5): favourable (price). {肯|kěn} (lesson 22's word): to be willing to.

1. What is the article mainly about?
2. Why did they ask a friend who had worked in purchasing to help?
3. Why did {白涛|Bái Tāo} offer two options instead of simply asking for a lower price?
4. What do {大卫|Dà wèi}'s last words suggest about how he sees suppliers?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Three lessons David draws from his small company's first purchase from a manufacturer: prepare,
   give the other side a choice, and put promises in the contract.
2. To advise them, so that they "know where they stand" ({心里有数|xīn lǐ yǒu shù}) and aren't on the back foot in the
   talks.
3. Asking only for a concession tends to stall the talks; given two ways out, the other side thinks
   about which suits it better.
4. He sees them as partners in a long relationship: the aim is a deal that is workable and worth it
   for both sides, not just a low price.

"How a small company negotiates with a manufacturer. For many small companies, negotiating with a
manufacturer is a headache. Their orders are small, so they have little to bargain with; but money is
tight too, and every fen has to be spent where it is needed most. The company David founded with his friend
Bai Tao has just over ten staff and mainly arranges study and sightseeing trips to China for British
students. This spring, for the first time, they had backpacks and guide earphones made for their
students. Talking about the purchase, David sums up three lessons. First, prepare before you
negotiate. At the trade fair they looked at more than ten firms in all, noting down each one's prices,
models and warranty periods, and they asked a friend who had worked in purchasing to act as adviser.
'If you know where you stand, you won't be on the back foot when you talk,' says David. Second, leave
the other side room to choose. The manufacturer's price was higher than they had expected. Bai Tao
didn't simply keep asking for a discount; he put forward two options: either lower the price a
little, or print the logo free. 'If you only ask the other side to give way, talks easily get stuck.
Give them two paths and they'll think seriously about which suits them better.' In the end the
manufacturer lowered the price and didn't charge for the logo either. Third, whatever is promised must
go into the contract. The manufacturer promised by word of mouth to deliver before 5 June; David
insisted on putting the date in the contract, and on stating that if delivery was late the company
could withdraw the order. 'It isn't that we don't trust them: both sides need an agreement that can
be kept.' After the talks, David also put the students' feedback on the ordinary backpacks they had bought last year together
and sent it to the manufacturer, which took up two of the suggestions and made the straps
wider. 'Small orders can lead to good partnerships too,' says David. 'The key is to make the other
side feel that doing business with you is workable, and worth it.' Of course, negotiations don't
always go well. They once talked three times to another manufacturer, which would never give a
delivery date, and in the end David had to give up. 'If the other side won't even put a deadline in
writing, there will only be more problems later.' As he sees it, a good negotiation isn't about who
wins and who loses: both sides are clear about what they want and what they can give. The
manufacturer now lists them as a long-term customer, and the next order will be cheaper still."
</details>

entrust: 委託, 託運) and 托 (to hold up; also in 摩托車, where it only gives the sound of "motor").

### Sound families

- 略 lüè has 各 gè on the right. 各 is a sound part with a wide family whose sounds have spread
  far apart: 客 kè, 格 gé, 落 luò, 路 lù, 略 lüè. Historians of Chinese sounds explain the mix of l-
  and g-/k- by older pronunciations; today, learn the family by its shape.
- 纳 nà: 纟 (silk) + 内 nèi, the sound part (nèi → nà). The same 内 gives 呐 nà.
- 诺 nuò: 讠 (speech) + 若 ruò: a spoken promise. 若 is the sound part of 惹 rě as well.
- 馈 kuì: 饣 (food) + 贵 guì: to present food, to give; {反馈|fǎn kuì} is "giving back". 贵 is also the
  sound part of 溃 kuì.
- 策 cè: ⺮ (bamboo) + 朿 cì (a thorn), the same part as in 刺 cì (to prick: lesson 08). A
  bamboo whip was the first meaning (Shuowen); slips of bamboo for writing gave "plan".
- 托 tuō: 扌 (hand) + 乇 zhé: to hold up on the palm. 乇 also sounds in 宅 zhái (residence:
  lesson 07's {住宅|zhù zhái}).

### Look-alikes and components

- 撤 chè: 扌 + 育 + 攵. Traditional 徹 chè (simplified 彻, in {彻底|chè dǐ}, HSK 5) has the same right
  side after 彳; simplified 彻 replaced it with 切.
- 履 is 尸 over 彳 and 复: a shoe, then to tread, then to carry out ({履行|lǚ xíng}).
- 委 is 禾 (grain) over 女. Don't confuse it with 季 (season), 禾 over 子.

### Stroke order

- **策**: ⺮ (six strokes: left-falling, horizontal, dot, then the same again), then 朿: the
  horizontal; a short vertical and the horizontal that turns down with a hook (a frame like 冂); the
  long vertical through the middle; the left-falling and right-falling strokes.
- **纳**: 纟 (two turning strokes and a rising stroke), then 内: the vertical, the horizontal that
  turns down with a hook, then the left-falling stroke and the dot inside.
- **委**: 禾 on top (a short left-falling stroke, the horizontal, the vertical, then left-falling and
  right-falling), then 女 (the turning dot, the left-falling stroke and the horizontal).
- **托**: 扌, then a left-falling stroke, a horizontal and the vertical-bend-hook that sweeps right.

## Pronunciation

- {策略|cè lüè} cè lüè: lüè has ü, written with the dots after l (lüè, not lue). {履行|lǚ xíng} lǚ xíng: ü again, a dipping
  tone. {履行|lǚ xíng} and {旅行|lǚ xíng} (HSK 4: to travel) sound the same.
- {预定|yù dìng} (to fix in advance) and {预订|yù dìng} (HSK 5: to book) are both yù dìng.
- {采购|cǎi gòu} cǎi gòu, {采纳|cǎi nà} cǎi nà: c is *ts* with a puff of air.
- {答复|dá fù} dá fù: the {答|dá} of {回答|huí dá}, a rising tone. {大幅|dà fú} (lesson 04: by a large margin) is dà fú.
- {承诺|chéng nuò} chéng nuò, {成交|chéng jiāo} chéng jiāo: ch, curled back.
- {要么|yào me} yào me: the second syllable is light.

## Common mistakes

- For a complaint that something always goes one way or the other, {不|bú}{是|shì}…{就是|jiù shì} is the natural choice
  ({他|tā}{不|bú}{是|shì}{迟到|chí dào}{就是|jiù shì}{请假|qǐng jià}); {他|tā}{要么|yào me}{迟到|chí dào}，{要么|yào me}{请假|qǐng jià} sounds like a neutral list of his options.
- {要么|yào me} in a question: ~~{你|nǐ}{要么|yào me}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}{要么|yào me}{喝|hē}{咖啡|kā fēi}？~~ Ask with {还是|hái shi}: {你|nǐ}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}{还是|hái shi}{喝|hē}{咖啡|kā fēi}？
- ~~{采纳|cǎi nà}{礼物|lǐ wù}~~: {采纳|cǎi nà} takes suggestions, opinions, plans. For a gift or an invitation, {接受|jiē shòu}.
- {履行|lǚ xíng} and {旅行|lǚ xíng} (HSK 4: to travel) sound the same, lǚ xíng: {履行|lǚ xíng} takes {合同|hé tong}, {承诺|chéng nuò}, {职责|zhí zé}.
- {预定|yù dìng} and {预订|yù dìng}: you {预订|yù dìng} a room or a ticket; a date or a plan is {预定|yù dìng} ({预定|yù dìng}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}).
- {限|xiàn} is written: in a chat, {每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{只能|zhǐ néng}{买|mǎi}{两|liǎng}{件|jiàn} is natural; {每|měi}{人|rén}{限|xiàn}{购|gòu}{两|liǎng}{件|jiàn} belongs on a sign.
- ~~{这个|zhè ge}{方案|fāng àn}{很|hěn}{可行性|kě xíng xìng}~~: {可行|kě xíng} is the adjective ({这个|zhè ge}{方案|fāng àn}{可行|kě xíng}), {可行性|kě xíng xìng} the noun ({研究|yán jiū}{可行性|kě xíng xìng}).

## Key points

- {要么|yào me} X，{要么|yào me} Y: a choice between courses of action ({要么|yào me}{降价|jiàng jià}，{要么|yào me}{延期|yán qī}), or someone's usual options; {不|bú}{是|shì} X {就是|jiù shì} Y:
  always one or the other (often a complaint); {还是|hái shi} in questions; {或者|huò zhě} in open statements.
- {限|xiàn} (written): {每|měi}{人|rén}{限|xiàn}{购|gòu}{两|liǎng}{件|jiàn}, {限|xiàn}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{内|nèi}{答复|dá fù}, {限|xiàn}{本|běn}{公司|gōng sī}{员工|yuán gōng}; {期限|qī xiàn} (deadline); {有限|yǒu xiàn}, {限制|xiàn zhì}.
- {可行|kě xíng} (feasible): {这个|zhè ge}{方案|fāng àn}{可行|kě xíng}; {可行性|kě xíng xìng}; spoken {行不行|xíng bu xíng}.
- Pairs: {厂家|chǎng jiā} (the maker) / {厂商|chǎng shāng} (firms); {预定|yù dìng} (fixed in advance) / {预订|yù dìng} (to book); {答复|dá fù} (formal reply) / {回复|huí fù};
  {承诺|chéng nuò} → {履行|lǚ xíng}; {采纳|cǎi nà} + {建议|jiàn yì} / {意见|yì jiàn}.
- New characters: 策 略 纳 撤 诺 馈 履 委 托.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Managing people and projects
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This summer {大卫|Dà wèi} (David) and {白涛|Bái Tāo} (Bai Tao)'s company is taking on its biggest job yet: a two-week
exchange programme for British and Chinese secondary-school students, run together with a Beijing
school. Someone has to plan it, share out the work and check that it gets done. This lesson brings:

- Two written words of notices and reports: {一道|yí dào} (together) and {为期|wéi qī} (lasting).
- A first look at **{凡是|fán shì}…{都|dōu}** (every… without exception), which lesson 24 teaches fully.
- The largest word set of the module: planning, leading, working together, rules and checking. Learn
  them in the groups below, with the words they go with: management Chinese is a language of fixed
  pairs ({听取|tīng qǔ}{汇报|huì bào}, {征求|zhēng qiú}{意见|yì jiàn}, {推行|tuī xíng}{制度|zhì dù}, {加|jiā}{大|dà}{力度|lì dù}).
- A staff notice and the same news as it's said at a meeting, and a reading on management that
  becomes an exam-style "sentences for the gaps" question.

## {一道|yí dào}: together (written)

{一道|yí dào} is the written partner of {一起|yì qǐ}. It comes after {与|yǔ} / {和|hé} / {跟|gēn} + a person and before the verb:

{我|wǒ}{公司|gōng sī}{将|jiāng}{与|yǔ}{北京|Běi jīng}{一|yì}{所|suǒ}{中学|zhōng xué}{一道|yí dào}{举办|jǔ bàn}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{交流|jiāo liú}{活动|huó dòng}。 — Our company will hold this exchange together with a
Beijing secondary school.

{欢迎|huān yíng}{家长|jiā zhǎng}{与|yǔ}{孩子|hái zi}{一道|yí dào}{参加|cān jiā}。 — Parents are welcome to take part with their children.

{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{一道|yí dào}{努力|nǔ lì}，{把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{做|zuò}{好|hǎo}。 — Let's all work together to do this well.

In conversation you say {一起|yì qǐ} ({我们|wǒ men}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{吧|ba}); {一道|yí dào} belongs in notices, speeches and reports, and in
older-style speech. Lesson 17's {一同|yì tóng} is used the same way.

Don't confuse it with the number and measure word {一|yī} + {道|dào} (a, one: {道|dào} for questions, dishes and stages):
{一道|yí dào}{题|tí} (a question), {一道|yí dào}{菜|cài} (a dish), {每|měi}{一道|yí dào}{工序|gōng xù} (every stage). They are read the same, yí dào; the
word that follows tells you which it is: a verb ({一道|yí dào}{参加|cān jiā}) or a noun ({一道|yí dào}{菜|cài}).

## {为期|wéi qī}: lasting, for a period of (written)

{为期|wéi qī} + a length of time says how long something planned will last. 为 is read wéi here (to be, as in
{为期|wéi qī}), and {期|qī} is a period:

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{交流|jiāo liú}{活动|huó dòng}{为期|wéi qī}{两|liǎng}{周|zhōu}。 — The exchange lasts two weeks.

{公司|gōng sī}{将|jiāng}{举办|jǔ bàn}{为期|wéi qī}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{的|de}{培训|péi xùn}。 — The company will hold a three-day training course.

- {为期|wéi qī} is a verb: it's the predicate ({活动|huó dòng}{为期|wéi qī}{两|liǎng}{周|zhōu}), or it goes with {的|de} before a noun ({为期|wéi qī}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{的|de}{培训|péi xùn}).
- Only for planned events with a set length: courses, meetings, exhibitions, contracts, visits.
  It's not for how long something took by chance: ~~{他|tā}{生病|shēng bìng}{为期|wéi qī}{一|yì}{周|zhōu}~~ → {他|tā}{病|bìng}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}.
- In speech: {这|zhè}{次|cì}{活动|huó dòng}{一共|yí gòng}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī} / {培训|péi xùn}{三|sān}{天|tiān}.

## {凡是|fán shì}…{都|dōu}: every… without exception (preview)

**{凡是|fán shì}…{都|dōu}** picks out a whole group and says the same thing holds for all of it: {凡是|fán shì} + description,
{都|dōu} + what holds. It's lesson 24's pattern; you'll meet it now in notices and rules:

{凡是|fán shì}{参加|cān jiā}{活动|huó dòng}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}，{都|dōu}{要|yào}{准时|zhǔn shí}{到|dào}{校|xiào}。 — Every student taking part must arrive at the school on time.

{凡是|fán shì}{跟|gēn}{安全|ān quán}{有关|yǒu guān}{的|de}{问题|wèn tí}，{都|dōu}{要|yào}{马上|mǎ shàng}{向|xiàng}{负责人|fù zé rén}{汇报|huì bào}。 — Any problem to do with safety must be reported to the
person in charge at once.

{凡是|fán shì} is a little formal; the meaning is close to {所有|suǒ yǒu}…{都|dōu} or {只要|zhǐ yào}{是|shì}…{都|dōu} (anything that is…). The {都|dōu} in the
second half is needed.

## Words for managing

### Planning and organising

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {策划|cè huà} | to plan (an event, a campaign); planning | {活动|huó dòng}{是|shì}{她|tā}{策划|cè huà}{的|de}。 |
| {筹备|chóu bèi} | to prepare, organise (in advance) | {筹备会|chóu bèi huì} (a planning meeting) |
| {前期|qián qī} | early stage | {前期|qián qī}{准备|zhǔn bèi} |
| {初步|chū bù} | preliminary, initial | {初步|chū bù}{方案|fāng àn}, {初步|chū bù}{决定|jué dìng} |
| {步骤|bù zhòu} | step (in a process) | {分|fēn}{三|sān}{个|gè}{步骤|bù zhòu} |
| {流程|liú chéng} | process, procedure (a fixed sequence) | {报名|bào míng}{流程|liú chéng} |
| {进度|jìn dù} | progress, pace (against a plan) | {工作|gōng zuò}{进度|jìn dù} |
| {进展|jìn zhǎn} | progress, development (how far it has got) | {有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{新|xīn}{进展|jìn zhǎn}？ |
| {年度|nián dù} | year (for reports and budgets) | {年度|nián dù}{计划|jì huà}, {年度|nián dù}{总结|zǒng jié} |
| {常规|cháng guī} | routine; the usual | {常规|cháng guī}{检查|jiǎn chá} |

- {进度|jìn dù} is progress measured against a plan: {进度|jìn dù}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}, {跟|gēn}{上|shàng}{进度|jìn dù} (keep up). {进展|jìn zhǎn} is how far things have got:
  {谈判|tán pàn}{有|yǒu}{了|le}{进展|jìn zhǎn} (the talks have made progress), {进展|jìn zhǎn}{顺利|shùn lì}.
- {步骤|bù zhòu} is one step; {流程|liú chéng} is the whole sequence: {报名|bào míng}{流程|liú chéng}{分|fēn}{三|sān}{个|gè}{步骤|bù zhòu}.
- {策划|cè huà} is the creative planning of an event or a campaign ({活动|huó dòng}{策划|cè huà}, an events planner); {筹备|chóu bèi} is the
  practical preparation ({筹备|chóu bèi}{工作|gōng zuò}, {筹备|chóu bèi}{会议|huì yì}).

### Hosting

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {主办|zhǔ bàn} | to host, sponsor (the main organiser) | {由|yóu}{学校|xué xiào}{主办|zhǔ bàn} |
| {承办|chéng bàn} | to undertake, run (for the host) | {由|yóu}{我|wǒ}{公司|gōng sī}{承办|chéng bàn} |
| {学会|xué huì} | society (academic, professional); to learn | {中学英语教学学会|zhōng xué Yīng yǔ jiào xué xué huì} |

On a poster you'll often read both: {主办单位|zhǔ bàn dān wèi} (the host) and {承办单位|chéng bàn dān wèi} (the organiser who actually runs
it). {学会|xué huì} as a noun is a professional society; as a verb it's "to learn (to do)", as you know it:
{学会|xué huì}{开车|kāi chē}.

### Leading and deciding

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {带领|dài lǐng} | to lead (people, a group) | {带领|dài lǐng}{学生|xué sheng}{参观|cān guān} |
| {指挥|zhǐ huī} | to direct, conduct | {指挥|zhǐ huī}{交通|jiāo tōng}, {指挥|zhǐ huī}{乐队|yuè duì} |
| {命令|mìng lìng} | order, command; to order | {服从|fú cóng}{命令|mìng lìng} |
| {指示|zhǐ shì} | instruction (from above); to instruct | {按照|àn zhào}{上级|shàng jí}{的|de}{指示|zhǐ shì} |
| {引导|yǐn dǎo} | to guide (gently, by example) | {引导|yǐn dǎo}{学生|xué sheng}{自己|zì jǐ}{思考|sī kǎo} |
| {主导|zhǔ dǎo} | leading, dominant; to lead | {起|qǐ}{主导|zhǔ dǎo}{作用|zuò yòng} (play the leading role) |
| {决策|jué cè} | decision (policy); to decide | {公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{决策|jué cè} |
| {高层|gāo céng} | senior level; high-rise | {公司|gōng sī}{高层|gāo céng} |
| {跟随|gēn suí} | to follow | {跟随|gēn suí}{导游|dǎo yóu} |
| {服从|fú cóng} | to obey, submit to | {服从|fú cóng}{安排|ān pái} |

- {带领|dài lǐng} is leading people where you go with them; {指挥|zhǐ huī} is directing from the front (traffic, an orchestra,
  an operation); {引导|yǐn dǎo} is guiding someone towards something, often gently.
- {命令|mìng lìng} is an order you must obey ({必须|bì xū}{服从|fú cóng}{命令|mìng lìng}); {指示|zhǐ shì} is an instruction from a superior, less harsh.
- {决策|jué cè} is a decision at the top, about direction or policy: {重大|zhòng dà}{决策|jué cè} (a major decision); everyday
  decisions are {决定|jué dìng}.
- {高层|gāo céng} is "the top" of an organisation ({公司|gōng sī}{高层|gāo céng}, senior management); {高层建筑|gāo céng jiàn zhù} is a high-rise building.

### Working together

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {分工|fēn gōng} | division of labour; to divide the work | {分工|fēn gōng}{明确|míng què} |
| {轮流|lún liú} | to take turns | {轮流|lún liú}{值班|zhí bān} |
| {协调|xié tiáo} | to coordinate; well coordinated | {协调|xié tiáo}{各|gè}{部门|bù mén}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò} |
| {协助|xié zhù} | to assist | {协助|xié zhù}{经理|jīng lǐ}{工作|gōng zuò} |
| {出力|chū lì} | to put in effort, do one's bit | {大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{出|chū}{了|le}{力|lì}。 |
| {大伙儿|dà huǒr} | everyone, all of us (spoken) | {大伙儿|dà huǒr}{辛苦|xīn kǔ}{了|le}！ |
| {调动|diào dòng} | to transfer (a person); to arouse, mobilise | {调动|diào dòng}{工作|gōng zuò}, {调动|diào dòng}{积极|jī jí}{性|xìng} |
| {分散|fēn sàn} | to disperse; scattered | {注意力|zhù yì lì}{分散|fēn sàn} |
| {事务|shì wù} | affairs, routine work | {日常|rì cháng}{事务|shì wù} |

- {协调|xié tiáo} is getting people or parts to work together ({协调|xié tiáo}{关系|guān xi}, {协调|xié tiáo}{时间|shí jiān}); as an adjective, "well
  balanced": {颜色|yán sè}{很|hěn}{协调|xié tiáo}. {协助|xié zhù} is helping someone in their task ({协助|xié zhù} + person).
- {大伙儿|dà huǒr} (dà huǒr) is warmly colloquial: a boss says it at a team dinner, not in a notice. Notices say
  {全体员工|quán tǐ yuán gōng} (all staff).
- {调动|diào dòng} with a person is transferring them ({调动|diào dòng}{工作|gōng zuò}, to change jobs within the system); with {积极|jī jí}{性|xìng} it's
  "to arouse": {调动|diào dòng}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{积极|jī jí}{性|xìng} (motivate everyone) is one of the commonest phrases in management talk.
- {分散|fēn sàn} is spreading out: {学生|xué sheng}{分散|fēn sàn}{在|zài}{三|sān}{个|gè}{地方|dì fang} (the students are spread over three places), {注意力|zhù yì lì}{分散|fēn sàn} (attention
  scattered).

### Rules and checking

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {机制|jī zhì} | mechanism (how a system works) | {建立|jiàn lì}{反馈|fǎn kuì}{机制|jī zhì} |
| {体系|tǐ xì} | system (a whole made of parts) | {管理|guǎn lǐ}{体系|tǐ xì} |
| {规范|guī fàn} | norm, standard; standardised; to standardise | {行为|xíng wéi}{规范|guī fàn}, {规范|guī fàn}{管理|guǎn lǐ} |
| {纪律|jì lǜ} | discipline, rules | {遵守|zūn shǒu}{纪律|jì lǜ} |
| {约束|yuē shù} | to restrain; restraint | {约束|yuē shù}{自己|zì jǐ} |
| {监督|jiān dū} | to supervise; supervision | {监督|jiān dū}{执行|zhí xíng} |
| {考核|kǎo hé} | to assess (staff); appraisal | {年度|nián dù}{考核|kǎo hé} |
| {评估|píng gū} | to assess, evaluate | {评估|píng gū}{效果|xiào guǒ} |
| {成效|chéng xiào} | effect, results (of efforts) | {取得|qǔ dé}{了|le}{成效|chéng xiào} |
| {力度|lì dù} | strength, intensity (of a measure) | {加|jiā}{大|dà}{力度|lì dù} |
| {等级|děng jí} | grade, level | {分为|fēn wéi}{三|sān}{个|gè}{等级|děng jí} |

- {考核|kǎo hé} is assessing people's work ({员工|yuán gōng}{考核|kǎo hé}, a staff appraisal); {评估|píng gū} is evaluating a plan, a risk or a
  result ({评估|píng gū}{风险|fēng xiǎn}, {评估|píng gū}{效果|xiào guǒ}).
- {机制|jī zhì} is how something works inside ({反馈|fǎn kuì}{机制|jī zhì}, a feedback mechanism); {体系|tǐ xì} is the whole structure ({教育|jiào yù}{体系|tǐ xì}).
- {规范|guī fàn} is a noun ({行为|xíng wéi}{规范|guī fàn}, rules of conduct), an adjective ({很|hěn}{规范|guī fàn}, done properly) and a verb ({规范|guī fàn}{管理|guǎn lǐ}).
- {力度|lì dù} is the force behind a measure: {加|jiā}{大|dà}{力度|lì dù} (step up the effort) is fixed.

### Improving things

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {强化|qiáng huà} | to strengthen | {强化|qiáng huà}{安全|ān quán}{意识|yì shí} |
| {巩固|gǒng gù} | to consolidate; solid | {巩固|gǒng gù}{成果|chéng guǒ} |
| {推行|tuī xíng} | to put into practice (a measure, a system) | {推行|tuī xíng}{新|xīn}{制度|zhì dù} |
| {优先|yōu xiān} | to have priority; priority | {安全|ān quán}{优先|yōu xiān} |
| {征求|zhēng qiú} | to ask for, solicit (views) | {征求|zhēng qiú}{意见|yì jiàn} |
| {听取|tīng qǔ} | to listen to (reports, opinions) | {听取|tīng qǔ}{汇报|huì bào} |
| {汇报|huì bào} | to report (to a superior or a meeting) | {向|xiàng}{总|zǒng}{经理|jīng lǐ}{汇报|huì bào}{进度|jìn dù} |
| {示范|shì fàn} | to demonstrate; demonstration | {示范|shì fàn}{一|yí}{遍|biàn} |
| {纠正|jiū zhèng} | to correct (a mistake) | {纠正|jiū zhèng}{错误|cuò wù} |
| {补|bǔ} | to make up for; to mend | {补|bǔ}{上|shàng}, {补|bǔ}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{票|piào} |

- The pairs are the thing to learn: {征求|zhēng qiú}{意见|yì jiàn}, {听取|tīng qǔ}{汇报|huì bào} / {听取|tīng qǔ}{意见|yì jiàn}, {推行|tuī xíng}{制度|zhì dù}, {纠正|jiū zhèng}{错误|cuò wù}, {巩固|gǒng gù}{成果|chéng guǒ}, {强化|qiáng huà}{意识|yì shí}.
- {汇报|huì bào} is reporting upwards ({向|xiàng}{上级|shàng jí}{汇报|huì bào}); a news report is {报道|bào dào} (HSK 5).
- {补|bǔ} is making up what's missing: {补|bǔ}{上|shàng} (fill in), {补|bǔ}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{票|piào} (buy a ticket afterwards), {补觉|bǔ jiào} (catch up on
  sleep).

### Qualities of work

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {精心|jīng xīn} | meticulous, with great care | {精心|jīng xīn}{准备|zhǔn bèi} |
| {细致|xì zhì} | careful, thorough | {工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{细致|xì zhì} |
| {切实|qiè shí} | practical, earnest; really | {切实|qiè shí}{可行|kě xíng} |
| {被动|bèi dòng} | passive, on the back foot | {很|hěn}{被动|bèi dòng} |
| {薄弱|bó ruò} | weak (a weak point) | {薄弱|bó ruò}{环节|huán jié} (a weak link) |
| {多余|duō yú} | superfluous, unnecessary | {多余|duō yú}{的|de}{步骤|bù zhòu} |

- {精心|jīng xīn} goes before a verb ({精心|jīng xīn}{设计|shè jì}, {精心|jīng xīn}{安排|ān pái}); {细致|xì zhì} describes how someone works ({认真|rèn zhēn}{细致|xì zhì}).
- {切实|qiè shí} is "real, practical" and goes before verbs ({切实|qiè shí}{做|zuò}{好|hǎo}, {切实|qiè shí}{解决|jiě jué}) or in {切实|qiè shí}{可行|kě xíng} (practical and
  feasible: lesson 02's {可行|kě xíng}).
- {薄弱|bó ruò} is bó ruò ({薄|báo} is báo in {很|hěn}{薄|báo}, thin; bó in words like this one).

## Dialogue: the planning meeting

The company's staff meet to plan the exchange. {江欣|Jiāng Xīn} (Jiang Xin) is the new operations assistant.

```dialogue
# {筹备会|chóu bèi huì}
```

> {最后|zuì hòu}，{管理|guǎn lǐ}{者|zhě}{自己|zì jǐ}{要|yào}{做|zuò}{示范|shì fàn}。{要求|yāo qiú}{员工|yuán gōng}{准时|zhǔn shí}，{自己|zì jǐ}{先|xiān}{不|bù}{迟到|chí dào}；{要求|yāo qiú}{员工|yuán gōng}{细致|xì zhì}，{自己|zì jǐ}{先|xiān}{认真|rèn zhēn}{对待|duì dài}{每|měi}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{小|xiǎo}{事|shì}。{员工|yuán gōng}{看|kàn}{的|de}{不|bú}{是|shì}{领导|lǐng dǎo}{怎么|zěn me}{说|shuō}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{领导|lǐng dǎo}{怎么|zěn me}{做|zuò}。
>
> {管理|guǎn lǐ}{没有|méi yǒu}{一成不变|yì chéng bú biàn}{的|de}{办法|bàn fǎ}。{一|yì}{家|jiā}{十|shí}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{的|de}{小|xiǎo}{公司|gōng sī}{和|hé}{一|yí}{个|gè}{几|jǐ}{千|qiān}{人|rén}{的|de}{大|dà}{集团|jí tuán}，{管理|guǎn lǐ}{的|de}{体系|tǐ xì}{当然|dāng rán}{不同|bù tóng}。{但|dàn}{不管|bù guǎn}{规模|guī mó}{大小|dà xiǎo}，{道理|dào li}{是|shì}{相通|xiāng tōng}{的|de}：{把|bǎ}{人|rén}{放|fàng}{在|zài}{合适|hé shì}{的|de}{岗位|gǎng wèi}{上|shàng}，{让|ràng}{他们|tā men}{清楚|qīng chu}{目标|mù biāo}、{愿意|yuàn yì}{出力|chū lì}，{管理|guǎn lǐ}{就|jiù}{成功|chéng gōng}{了|le}{一大半|yí dà bàn}。{管理|guǎn lǐ}{者|zhě}{不必|bú bì}{什么|shén me}{事|shì}{都|dōu}{亲自|qīn zì}{去|qù}{管|guǎn}，{重要|zhòng yào}{的|de}{是|shì}{让|ràng}{每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}{为什么|wèi shén me}{做|zuò}、{怎么|zěn me}{做|zuò}。

Words to know: {下级|xià jí}: subordinate (the opposite of {上级|shàng jí}). {交|jiāo}{代|dài} (HSK 5): to give (someone) a task. {推来推去|tuī lái tuī qù}:
to pass the buck. {合理|hé lǐ} (HSK 5): reasonable. {第一线|dì yí xiàn}: the front line. {空话|kōng huà}: empty words. {出错|chū cuò}: to make a
mistake. {对待|duì dài} (HSK 5): to treat. {一成不变|yì chéng bú biàn} (yì chéng bú biàn): never changing (an idiom; {成|chéng} here is
"finished", not the measure word of lesson 04). {相通|xiāng tōng}: to be linked, the same at root. {一大半|yí dà bàn}: the
greater part.

1. What is the main idea?
2. Why does the writer think ordinary staff should be asked for their views?
3. What is wrong with appraisal that asks too much?
4. How is the article organised?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Good management isn't orders and discipline alone: it needs a clear division of work and
   process, listening to staff, appraisal of the right strength, and managers who set an example.
2. They know the weak links best, from working on the front line every day; asking them finds
   problems early and motivates everyone.
3. Staff become afraid of making mistakes and dare not try anything new.
4. A common view and its weakness (paragraph 1), then four points introduced by {首先|shǒu xiān}, {其次|qí cì}, {再次|zài cì}, {最后|zuì hòu},
   and a conclusion (the principle is the same whatever the size).

"What does good management depend on? When management comes up, many people think first of orders
and discipline: superiors decide, subordinates do as they're told, and whoever does badly gets
criticised. Management like this may work for a short time, but before long staff grow more and
more passive, doing only what they're told and refusing to take one step more. Good management
first needs a clear division of work. When everyone knows what they're responsible for and whom to
go to with a problem, work doesn't get passed back and forth. When you prepare a three-day event,
for example, if nobody coordinates, three departments may all contact the same hotel, or none of
them may. The division can't stay on paper; it
also needs a sensible process: which step comes first, which later, and who checks each one. The
clearer the process, the fewer unnecessary stages. Second, managers must learn to listen. In many
organisations a meeting means the boss talking and everyone else listening. In fact, the people who
know the weak links best are often the ordinary staff on the front line every day. Asking their
views often finds problems early and also motivates everyone. Some managers worry that listening
wastes time; in fact, ten more minutes of discussion at a meeting often saves days of trouble later. Third, supervision and appraisal are
necessary, but at the right strength. If appraisal asks too little, the norms are empty words; if it
asks too much, staff are afraid of making mistakes and won't try anything new. A good appraisal system
should guide rather than restrain: it lets staff know how to do better, not just where they went
wrong. Finally, managers must set an example. If they want staff to be punctual, they mustn't be late
themselves; if they want staff to be careful, they must take every small matter seriously
themselves. Staff watch not what the boss says but what the boss does. There is no fixed method of
management. A small company of a dozen people and a group of several thousand will of course have
different systems. But whatever the size, the principle is the same: put people in the right posts,
let them be clear about the goals and willing to do their bit, and management is more than half
done. Managers needn't handle everything themselves: what matters is that everyone knows why they do
things and how."
</details>

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 骤 (traditional 驟) | sudden; a step | zhòu | 马 | 17 | {步骤|bù zhòu} |
| 筹 (traditional 籌) | tally; to plan, raise | chóu | ⺮ | 13 | {筹备|chóu bèi} |
| 巩 (traditional 鞏) ✎ | firm | gǒng | 工 | 6 | {巩固|gǒng gù} |
| 监 (traditional 監) | to watch over | jiān | 皿 | 10 | {监督|jiān dū}, {监测|jiān cè} (lesson 18) |
| 督 | to supervise | dū | 目 | 13 | {监督|jiān dū} |
| 纠 (traditional 糾) ✎ | to tangle; to correct | jiū | 纟 | 5 | {纠正|jiū zhèng}, {纠纷|jiū fēn} (lesson 09) |
| 核 | stone (of a fruit); core; to check | hé | 木 | 10 | {考核|kǎo hé}, {核心|hé xīn} (lesson 26) |
| 轮 (traditional 輪) ✎ | wheel; to take turns | lún | 车 | 8 | {轮流|lún liú}, {轮椅|lún yǐ} (06), {轮船|lún chuán} (17), {轮子|lún zi} (20) |

Traditional strokes: 驟 24, 籌 20, 鞏 15, 監 14, 糾 8, 輪 15.

### Sound families

- 轮 lún: 车 (vehicle) + 仑 lún, the sound part: a wheel. 仑 is the family of 论 lùn (to discuss:
  {讨论|tǎo lùn}, HSK 4) and 伦 lún (in 伦敦, London). Traditional 輪, 論, 倫 share 侖.
- 核 hé: 木 (tree) + 亥 hài: the stone of a fruit, then the core, then "to check thoroughly"
  ({考核|kǎo hé}). 亥 also sounds in 孩 hái ({孩子|hái zi}) and 该 gāi ({应该|yīng gāi}): the sounds have drifted apart.
- 督 dū: 目 (eye) under 叔 shū (uncle: {叔叔|shū shu}, HSK 2), the sound part: watching over.
- 骤 zhòu: 马 (horse) + 聚 jù (to gather: {聚会|jù huì}, HSK 4): a horse running fast, then "sudden",
  "step". The sound has moved (jù → zhòu).
- 筹 chóu: ⺮ over 寿 shòu (long life: lesson 06's {长寿|cháng shòu}), the sound part: bamboo sticks (Shuowen: the
  arrows of a throwing game), then sticks for counting, then "to plan, to raise (money)". Traditional 籌
  has 壽.
- 纠 jiū: 纟 (thread) + 丩 jiū (twisted): threads twisted together, then "to straighten out" ({纠正|jiū zhèng}).
  The same 丩 is the sound part of 叫 jiào.

### 监 and 临

监 in its oldest forms shows a person bending over a basin of water (皿) to look at their
reflection: "to look down on, watch over" (the usual explanation in character dictionaries). Simplified
监 and 临 (HSK 5: {临时|lín shí}) share their first five strokes: two verticals, then a left-falling stroke, a
horizontal and a dot. The bottom tells them apart: 监 has 皿 (five strokes), 临 a box with one
dividing vertical (four strokes). In traditional they look nothing alike: 監, 臨.

### Stroke order

- **巩**: 工 on the left (horizontal, vertical, then the rising stroke that ends it), then 凡 on the
  right: a left-falling stroke, the horizontal that turns into a slanting hook, and the dot inside.
- **纠**: 纟, then 丩: the vertical that ends with a rising flick, then the long vertical on the right.
- **轮**: 车 on the left (its last stroke rises to the right), then 仑: a left-falling stroke and a
  right-falling stroke like a roof, then a left-falling stroke and the vertical-bend-hook.
- **监**: two verticals on the left, then the left-falling stroke, the horizontal and the dot on the
  right; then 皿 at the bottom: its vertical, the turn, two short verticals and the long horizontal
  last.

## Write it: a notice

Write a staff notice of 150–200 characters. Your company is holding a three-day training course for
new staff (8–10 March) on the second floor. Say what it is, who must attend, what to bring, and that
anyone who can't come must tell the personnel department in advance. Use at least four of: {为期|wéi qī}, {一道|yí dào},
{凡是|fán shì}…{都|dōu}, {须|xū}, {关于|guān yú}…{的|de}{通知|tōng zhī}, {安排|ān pái}, {汇报|huì bào}, {提前|tí qián}.

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

> {关于|guān yú}{新|xīn}{员工|yuán gōng}{培训|péi xùn}{的|de}{通知|tōng zhī}
>
> {各|gè}{部门|bù mén}：
>
> {为了|wèi le}{帮助|bāng zhù}{新|xīn}{员工|yuán gōng}{尽快|jǐn kuài}{熟悉|shú xī}{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}{流程|liú chéng}，{人事部|rén shì bù}{将|jiāng}{于|yú}3{月|yuè}8{日|rì}{至|zhì}10{日|rì}{在|zài}{二|èr}{楼|lóu}{会议|huì yì}{室|shì}{举办|jǔ bàn}{为期|wéi qī}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{的|de}{新|xīn}{员工|yuán gōng}{培训|péi xùn}。{凡是|fán shì}{今年|jīn nián}{入职|rù zhí}{的|de}{员工|yuán gōng}，{都|dōu}{须|xū}{参加|cān jiā}。{培训|péi xùn}{内容|nèi róng}{包括|bāo kuò}{公司|gōng sī}{介绍|jiè shào}、{各|gè}{部门|bù mén}{的|de}{业务|yè wù}{流程|liú chéng}{和|hé}{安全|ān quán}{规范|guī fàn}，{最后|zuì hòu}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{将|jiāng}{由|yóu}{各|gè}{部门|bù mén}{主管|zhǔ guǎn}{与|yǔ}{新|xīn}{员工|yuán gōng}{一道|yí dào}{进行|jìn xíng}{交流|jiāo liú}。{请|qǐng}{参加|cān jiā}{培训|péi xùn}{的|de}{员工|yuán gōng}{带|dài}{好|hǎo}{笔记本|bǐ jì běn}{和|hé}{员工|yuán gōng}{卡|kǎ}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{上午|shàng wǔ}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{准时|zhǔn shí}{到场|dào chǎng}。{如|rú}{因|yīn}{工作|gōng zuò}{安排|ān pái}{不|bù}{能|néng}{参加|cān jiā}，{须|xū}{提前|tí qián}{两|liǎng}{天|tiān}{向|xiàng}{人事部|rén shì bù}{汇报|huì bào}，{并|bìng}{由|yóu}{部门|bù mén}{主管|zhǔ guǎn}{签字|qiān zì}。
>
> {人事部|rén shì bù}
> 3{月|yuè}1{日|rì}

(about 190 characters) {入职|rù zhí} (rù zhí): to join a company. {到场|dào chǎng}: to be present. {签字|qiān zì} (HSK 5): to sign.
"Notice concerning training for new staff. To all departments: to help new staff become familiar with
the company's procedures as soon as possible, the personnel department will hold a three-day
training course for new staff from 8 to 10 March in the second-floor meeting room. All staff who have
joined this year must attend. The training covers an introduction to the company, each department's
business procedures and the safety rules; on the last day department heads will hold a discussion
together with the new staff. Staff attending should bring a notebook and their staff card and be
present at nine sharp each morning. Anyone unable to attend because of work must report it to the
personnel department two days in advance, with their department head's signature. Personnel
department, 1 March."

A checklist: the title {关于|guān yú}…{的|de}{通知|tōng zhī}; whom it's for; purpose ({为了|wèi le}…), time, place, who, content; what to
do ({请|qǐng}…); exceptions ({如|rú}…，{须|xū}…); who sends it and the date.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Managing a project
{这|zhè}{次|cì}{活动|huó dòng}{为期|wéi qī}{两|liǎng}{周|zhōu}，{由|yóu}{我们|wǒ men}{公司|gōng sī}{承办|chéng bàn}。
= The programme lasts two weeks and our company is running it.
{我们|wǒ men}{分|fēn}{三|sān}{个|gè}{组|zǔ}，{分工|fēn gōng}{要|yào}{明确|míng què}。
= We'll split into three groups, and the division of work must be clear.
{每|měi}{天|tiān}{下午|xià wǔ}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}，{各|gè}{组|zǔ}{汇报|huì bào}{一下|yí xià}{进度|jìn dù}。
= Every day at five, each group reports on its progress.
{发现|fā xiàn}{问题|wèn tí}{要|yào}{马上|mǎ shàng}{纠正|jiū zhèng}。
= When you find a problem, put it right at once.
{活动|huó dòng}{结束|jié shù}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{我们|wǒ men}{要|yào}{征求|zhēng qiú}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{意见|yì jiàn}。
= After the programme, we'll ask everyone for their views.
{大伙儿|dà huǒr}{辛苦|xīn kǔ}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{一道|yí dào}{把|bǎ}{它|tā}{做|zuò}{好|hǎo}。
= Thank you all for your hard work: let's do it well together.
```

## Pronunciation

- {薄弱|bó ruò} bó ruò: 薄 is bó in words like this one, báo in everyday "thin" ({很|hěn}{薄|báo}).
- {调动|diào dòng} diào dòng: 调 diào (transfer), as in HSK 5's {调|diào}; tiáo is "to adjust" ({协调|xié tiáo} xié tiáo in this lesson).
- {为期|wéi qī} wéi qī: 为 wéi, rising (as in {成为|chéng wéi}), not wèi (for).
- {大伙儿|dà huǒr} dà huǒr: the {儿|ér} joins the syllable (huǒr).
- {纪律|jì lǜ} jì lǜ: lǜ with ü, as in {绿|lǜ} lǜ. {一道|yí dào} yí dào: {一|yī} rises before a falling tone.
- {监督|jiān dū} jiān dū, {考核|kǎo hé} kǎo hé, {巩固|gǒng gù} gǒng gù (a dipping tone, then a falling one).

## Common mistakes

- ~~{他|tā}{生病|shēng bìng}{为期|wéi qī}{一|yì}{周|zhōu}~~: {为期|wéi qī} is for planned events of a set length ({活动|huó dòng}{为期|wéi qī}{两|liǎng}{周|zhōu}). For illness: {他|tā}{病|bìng}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}.
- {我们|wǒ men}{一道|yí dào}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{吧|ba} in a chat: not wrong, but stiff or old-fashioned; friends say {一起|yì qǐ}.
- ~~{凡是|fán shì}{学生|xué sheng}，{要|yào}{准时|zhǔn shí}~~: {凡是|fán shì} needs {都|dōu} in the second half: {凡是|fán shì}{学生|xué sheng}，{都|dōu}{要|yào}{准时|zhǔn shí}.
- {进度|jìn dù} and {进展|jìn zhǎn}: {工作|gōng zuò}{进度|jìn dù} (progress against the plan); {谈判|tán pàn}{有|yǒu}{了|le}{进展|jìn zhǎn} (the talks have moved forward).
- {考核|kǎo hé} and {评估|píng gū}: you {考核|kǎo hé} staff ({员工|yuán gōng}{考核|kǎo hé}) and {评估|píng gū} plans, risks and results.
- {汇报|huì bào} is to a superior or a meeting: {向|xiàng}{经理|jīng lǐ}{汇报|huì bào}. A journalist's report is {报道|bào dào}.
- {征求|zhēng qiú} goes with {意见|yì jiàn} / {建议|jiàn yì}; ~~{征求|zhēng qiú}{问题|wèn tí}~~ → {提出|tí chū}{问题|wèn tí} (raise a question).

## Key points

- {与|yǔ} / {和|hé} + person + {一道|yí dào} + verb: together (written; spoken {一起|yì qǐ}). {一道|yí dào}{题|tí} / {一道|yí dào}{菜|cài} is another {一道|yí dào}.
- {为期|wéi qī} + time (+ {的|de} + event): lasting (written); only for planned events.
- {凡是|fán shì} X，{都|dōu} Y: every X, without exception (lesson 24).
- Fixed pairs: {听取|tīng qǔ}{汇报|huì bào}, {征求|zhēng qiú}{意见|yì jiàn}, {推行|tuī xíng}{制度|zhì dù}, {加|jiā}{大|dà}{力度|lì dù}, {纠正|jiū zhèng}{错误|cuò wù}, {巩固|gǒng gù}{成果|chéng guǒ}, {调动|diào dòng}{积极|jī jí}{性|xìng}, {薄弱|bó ruò}{环节|huán jié}, {切实|qiè shí}{可行|kě xíng}.
- Near-synonyms: {进度|jìn dù} / {进展|jìn zhǎn}; {步骤|bù zhòu} / {流程|liú chéng}; {策划|cè huà} / {筹备|chóu bèi}; {带领|dài lǐng} / {指挥|zhǐ huī} / {引导|yǐn dǎo}; {命令|mìng lìng} / {指示|zhǐ shì}; {考核|kǎo hé} / {评估|píng gū}; {协调|xié tiáo} / {协助|xié zhù};
  {精心|jīng xīn} / {细致|xì zhì}.
- New characters: 骤 筹 巩 监 督 纠 核 轮.

lessons.title: Money, investment and the economy
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Halfway through 2031, {大卫|Dà wèi} (David) sits down with the company's accountant to look at the figures,
and {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) writes a commentary on how young people talk about money. The lesson is about
saying how much things change and what share they have:

- the measure word {成|chéng} (tenths: {三|sān}{成|chéng} = 30 %), and {百分点|bǎi fēn diǎn} (percentage points) beside {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī};
- {占比|zhàn bǐ} and {比重|bǐ zhòng} (share, proportion), with {占据|zhàn jù} and {占有|zhàn yǒu};
- {加倍|jiā bèi} and {倍增|bèi zēng} (to double, to multiply), and the trap in {增加|zēng jiā}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi};
- {预期|yù qī} (expected; expectation).

It also explains, in plain terms, what a loan, a share and a fund are. This is a language lesson,
not financial advice: the texts describe how things work and what people say about them.

## {成|chéng}: tenths

{成|chéng} after a number is a measure word for tenths: {一|yì}{成|chéng} is a tenth, 10 %; {三|sān}{成|chéng} is 30 %.

| {成|chéng} | Meaning | {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}… |
|---|---|---|
| {一|yì}{成|chéng} | a tenth | {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{十|shí} |
| {三|sān}{成|chéng} | three tenths | {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{三十|sān shí} |
| {七八|qī bā}{成|chéng} | seven or eight tenths | {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{七八十|qī bā shí} |
| {十|shí}{成|chéng} | all of it | {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{百|bǎi} |

{今年|jīn nián}{上|shàng}{半年|bàn nián}{的|de}{收益|shōu yì}{增长|zēng zhǎng}{了|le}{三|sān}{成|chéng}。 — Income for the first half of this year rose by 30 %.

{参加|cān jiā}{活动|huó dòng}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}{里|lǐ}，{有|yǒu}{七|qī}{成|chéng}{是|shì}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{来|lái}{中国|Zhōng guó}。 — Seven in ten of the students on the programme are in China for
the first time.

- {成|chéng} is used for round figures, in speech and in the press; exact figures use {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī} + number ({百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{三十二|sān shí èr}).
- It works like {折|zhé} (HSK 4's {打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé}, 20 % off) but the other way round: {八|bā}{折|zhé} is the price you pay (80 %), {降价|jiàng jià}{两|liǎng}{成|chéng} is the
  cut (20 %). Both come to the same price.
- In speech {八|bā}{成|chéng} also means "very probably": {他|tā}{八|bā}{成|chéng}{是|shì}{忘|wàng}{了|le}。 (He's most likely forgotten.)

## {百分点|bǎi fēn diǎn}: percentage points

When a rate changes, Chinese keeps two things apart, as careful English does:

{利润率|lì rùn lǜ}{从|cóng}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{十|shí}{提高|tí gāo}{到|dào}{了|le}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{十二|shí èr}，{提高|tí gāo}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{百分点|bǎi fēn diǎn}。 — The profit rate rose from 10 % to 12 %: up two percentage
points. ({利润率|lì rùn lǜ}: profit rate)

The same change is a rise of 20 % in the rate itself (two is a fifth of ten): {提高|tí gāo}{了|le}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{二十|èr shí}. News
reports use {百分点|bǎi fēn diǎn} for rates (interest rates, shares of a market, unemployment) so that "two points" and
"twenty per cent" don't get confused. {百分点|bǎi fēn diǎn} counts with {个|gè}: {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{百分点|bǎi fēn diǎn}, {零|líng}{点|diǎn}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{百分点|bǎi fēn diǎn} (0.5 points).

## {占比|zhàn bǐ} and {比重|bǐ zhòng}: share, proportion

To say what share a part has of a whole, use {占|zhàn} (to make up, to take: HSK 5):

{英国|Yīng guó}{学生|xué sheng}{占|zhàn}{全部|quán bù}{学生|xué sheng}{的|de}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{六十|liù shí}。 — British students make up 60 % of all students.

Turned into nouns, this gives {占比|zhàn bǐ} (share: the figure) and {比重|bǐ zhòng} (proportion, weight: how much the part
counts in the whole):

| Pattern | Example |
|---|---|
| A {占|zhàn} B {的|de} x | {交通|jiāo tōng}{费|fèi}{占|zhàn}{总|zǒng}{支出|zhī chū}{的|de}{两|liǎng}{成|chéng}。 Transport is 20 % of total spending. |
| A {在|zài} B {中|zhōng}{的|de}{占比|zhàn bǐ}{是|shì} x | {线上|xiàn shàng}{报名|bào míng}{在|zài}{全部|quán bù}{报名|bào míng}{中|zhōng}{的|de}{占比|zhàn bǐ}{是|shì}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{八十|bā shí}。 |
| A {在|zài} B {中|zhōng}{所|suǒ}{占|zhàn}{的|de}{比重|bǐ zhòng} + {大|dà} / {小|xiǎo} / {提高|tí gāo} | {教育|jiào yù}{行业|háng yè}{在|zài}{服务|fú wù}{业|yè}{中|zhōng}{所|suǒ}{占|zhàn}{的|de}{比重|bǐ zhòng}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{大|dà}。 |

- {占比|zhàn bǐ} is the number itself ({占比|zhàn bǐ}{是|shì}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{八十|bā shí}, {占比|zhàn bǐ}{提高|tí gāo}{了|le}); it's newer and common in business and news.
- {比重|bǐ zhòng} is weight or importance in a whole and goes with {大|dà}, {小|xiǎo}, {增加|zēng jiā}, {提高|tí gāo}: {比重|bǐ zhòng}{很|hěn}{大|dà}. (In physics it's also
  specific gravity.)
- {所|suǒ}{占|zhàn}{的|de}: the {所|suǒ} is the structural particle of written style (lesson 14); read {在|zài}…{中|zhōng}{所|suǒ}{占|zhàn}{的|de}{比重|bǐ zhòng} as "the share
  that A takes in B".

Two related verbs from this lesson: {占据|zhàn jù} (to occupy, hold: a position, a market) and {占有|zhàn yǒu} (to own,
possess: resources, a share). {这|zhè}{家|jiā}{公司|gōng sī}{占据|zhàn jù}{了|le}{一半|yí bàn}{的|de}{市场|shì chǎng}。 (The company holds half the market.) {他们|tā men}{占有|zhàn yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}
{资源|zī yuán}。 (They have a lot of resources.)

## {加倍|jiā bèi} and {倍增|bèi zēng}: to double, to multiply

{倍|bèi} (HSK 4) is "times". {加倍|jiā bèi} is to double, make twice as much; it's also an adverb, "doubly, twice as
hard":

{周末|zhōu mò}{的|de}{工资|gōng zī}{加倍|jiā bèi}。 — Weekend pay is doubled.

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{出|chū}{了|le}{问题|wèn tí}，{以后|yǐ hòu}{我们|wǒ men}{要|yào}{加倍|jiā bèi}{小心|xiǎo xīn}。 — Something went wrong this time: from now on we must be twice as
careful.

{倍增|bèi zēng} is to multiply, grow several times over: a written word for fast growth.

{两|liǎng}{年|nián}{来|lái}，{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{业务|yè wù}{倍增|bèi zēng}。 — In two years the company's business has multiplied.

The trap is in {增加|zēng jiā}{了|le} + {倍|bèi}: Chinese counts the increase, not the result.

| Chinese | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {增加|zēng jiā}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi} | went up by one times = doubled (100 → 200) |
| {增加|zēng jiā}{到|dào}{两|liǎng}{倍|bèi} | went up to twice (100 → 200) |
| {增加|zēng jiā}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{倍|bèi} | went up by two times = tripled (100 → 300) |

{去年|qù nián}{接待|jiē dài}{了|le}{三百|sān bǎi}{名|míng}{学生|xué sheng}，{今年|jīn nián}{接待|jiē dài}{了|le}{六百|liù bǎi}{名|míng}，{增加|zēng jiā}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi}。 — Last year we received 300 students, this year 600:
twice as many.

{预期|yù qī} is what you expect to happen, often in figures:

| Phrase | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {超出|chāo chū}{预期|yù qī} | better than expected |
| {达到|dá dào}{预期|yù qī} | to meet expectations |
| {低于|dī yú}{预期|yù qī} | below expectations ({低于|dī yú}: lower than, written) |
| {预期|yù qī}{收益|shōu yì} | expected return |
| {预期|yù qī}{目标|mù biāo} | the target |

{上|shàng}{半年|bàn nián}{的|de}{收益|shōu yì}{超出|chāo chū}{了|le}{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{预期|yù qī}。 — Income in the first half was better than we expected.

As a verb it's formal: {公司|gōng sī}{预期|yù qī}{明年|míng nián}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}{人数|rén shù}{会|huì}{继续|jì xù}{增长|zēng zhǎng}。 (The company expects student numbers to keep
growing next year.) In speech: {我们|wǒ men}{估计|gū jì}…, {我们|wǒ men}{以为|yǐ wéi}…, {比|bǐ}{我们|wǒ men}{想|xiǎng}{的|de}{好|hǎo}.

## Dialogue: the half-year figures

{大卫|Dà wèi} goes through the first half of 2031 with {马会计|Mǎ kuài jì} (Ma, the company's part-time accountant).

```dialogue
# {半年|bàn nián}{的|de}{账|zhàng}

= David, I've finished the report for the first half. Overall, things are better than expected.
大卫: {太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}。{具体|jù tǐ}{说说|shuō shuo}？
= Great. Can you give me the details?
马会计: {收益|shōu yì}{比|bǐ}{去年同期|qù nián tóng qī}{增长|zēng zhǎng}{了|le}{三|sān}{成|chéng}，{学生|xué sheng}{人数|rén shù}{差不多|chà bu duō}{增加|zēng jiā}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi}。
= Income is up 30 % on the same period last year, and student numbers have almost doubled.
```

1. The website's own small survey of readers on how they manage money.
2. Young people take saving and managing money more seriously than before; but many are vague about
