"Managing money starts with understanding your own bills. Last month our website ran a small survey,
asking readers how they manage their money. Over three hundred readers answered, seven in ten of
them under thirty. Two things in the results struck me. First, young people take managing money more
and more seriously. Over 80 % of those who answered save a little every month; some even write down
every item of spending and look at the end of the month to see where the money went. Compared with
the 'spend whatever you earn' attitude of a few years ago, this is quite a change. Second, quite a
few people are vague about what managing money means. Some said it means trading shares; others said
buying lottery tickets is a kind of money management ('what if I win?'). Others pay every bill in
instalments but can't say how much interest they pay. The survey also asked: 'If you had a sum of
money, what would you do with it?' The most common answer was to put it in the bank, because saving
feels safest; second came buying funds, 'because the return is higher than on savings'. But asked why
funds return more, and whether they can lose money, many couldn't answer. Quite a few readers left comments after the survey asking us to explain more
of the basics. As I see it, managing money isn't first of all
about making it grow: it's about understanding how money comes in and goes out. If you don't know
what you spend each month, or how the interest on a loan is calculated, then however many shares and
funds you hold, you can't be said to manage your money. Shares go up and down, and funds don't return
the same every year: these things take time to understand. Treating lottery tickets as money
management is mistaking luck for a plan. Of course, I'm not saying young people shouldn't invest.
Wanting to understand finance and caring about the economy's prospects is a good thing in itself.
What I want to say is that the first step is simple: understand your own bills. What is the balance
in your account, how large a share of your income goes on fixed costs each month, which spending is
necessary and which could be saved? Once you've thought these questions through, it isn't too late to
consider anything else. Money isn't everything, but seeing your own money clearly is also seeing your
own life clearly."

### The money radical 贝

贝 is a cowrie shell, used as money in ancient China. Characters with it are about money and
value: three of this lesson's (财, 贷, 贸) join a family you already know: 货 (goods), 费
(fee), 贵 (expensive), 购 (to buy), 资 (capital), 账 (account), 赚 (to earn), 赔 (to pay
compensation). In traditional it's 貝 (財, 貸, 貿, 貨, 費…), which is why those forms have more strokes.

### Sound families

- 财 cái: 贝 + 才 cái, the sound part. The same 才 sounds in 材 cái ({材料|cái liào}, HSK 4).
- 贷 dài: 贝 under 代 dài (generation, to stand in for), the sound part: money that "stands in" for
  a while. 代 also gives 袋 dài (bag: {口袋|kǒu dài}).
- 储 chǔ: 亻 + 诸 zhū. Traditional 儲 has 諸: the sound has moved (zhū → chǔ).
- 蓄 xù: 艹 over 畜 xù / chù (livestock): to store up.
- 跌 diē: ⻊ (foot) + 失 shī (to lose): to lose your footing. 失 also sits in 铁 tiě and in
  lesson 07's 秩 zhì.
- 额 é: 客 kè + 页 (head): the forehead, then a fixed amount. 客 is the sound part, as in lesson
  02's family 各 → 客 格 略.
- 贸 mào: 卯 mǎo over 贝: 卯 gives the sound.
- 股 gǔ: ⺼ (flesh) + 殳 shū: the thigh, then a strand or a part, then a share. The same 殳 is the
  right side of 设 shè and of simplified 没 méi.

### Look-alikes

- 贷 and 货: both have 贝 below; 贷 has 代 on top (with the dot), 货 has 化.
- 蓄 and 畜: only the grass on top.
- 融 is 鬲 (an old cooking pot) + 虫 (insect: here a sound part in its old form): steam rising
  from the pot, then "to melt, blend" (Shuowen).

### Stroke order

- **财**: 贝 first (vertical, the turn, a left-falling stroke and a dot), then 才: the horizontal,
  the vertical with a hook, and the left-falling stroke.
- **股**: ⺼ (left-falling, the turn with a hook, two short horizontals), then 殳: a left-falling
  stroke, the turn, then 又 (the horizontal-left-falling and the right-falling stroke).
- **贸**: the top: a left-falling stroke, a vertical that rises, a dot, then the turn with a hook and
  a left-falling stroke; 贝 at the bottom.

```trace
财股储蓄贷
```

```trace
跌额融贸
```

**Write it**: 财 股 贸 are handwriting characters (✎). Write each three times from memory, then
{理财|lǐ cái}, {股票|gǔ piào}, {贸易|mào yì}.
=}

## Write it: splitting the bills

You share a flat with two friends. Write a note of 150–200 characters for the group chat proposing how
to share the monthly bills (rent, water and electricity, the internet). Give the amounts, the share
for each person, how and by when to pay, and ask for their views. Use at least four of: {账单|zhàng dān}, {金额|jīn é}, {共计|gòng jì},
{支出|zhī chū}, {占|zhàn}, {成|chéng}, {分期|fēn qī}, {余额|yú é}.

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

> {大家|dà jiā}{好|hǎo}！{这个|zhè ge}{月|yuè}{的|de}{账单|zhàng dān}{都|dōu}{到|dào}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{整理|zhěng lǐ}{了|le}{一下|yí xià}：{房租|fáng zū}{六千|liù qiān}{元|yuán}，{水电费|shuǐ diàn fèi}{四百五十|sì bǎi wǔ shí}{元|yuán}，{网费|wǎng fèi}{九十|jiǔ shí}{元|yuán}，{共计|gòng jì}{六千五百四十|liù qiān wǔ bǎi sì shí}{元|yuán}。{房租|fáng zū}{占|zhàn}{了|le}{我们|wǒ men}{支出|zhī chū}{的|de}{九|jiǔ}{成|chéng}{多|duō}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{建议|jiàn yì}{房租|fáng zū}{按|àn}{房间|fáng jiān}{大小|dà xiǎo}{分|fēn}：{大|dà}{房间|fáng jiān}{两|liǎng}{千四|qiān sì}，{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{房间|fáng jiān}{各|gè}{一千八|yì qiān bā}；{水电费|shuǐ diàn fèi}{和|hé}{网费|wǎng fèi}{三|sān}{个|gè}{人|rén}{平分|píng fēn}，{每|měi}{人|rén}{一百八十|yì bǎi bā shí}{元|yuán}。{这样|zhè yàng}，{我|wǒ}{付|fù}{两|liǎng}{千五百八十|qiān wǔ bǎi bā shí}{元|yuán}，{你们|nǐ men}{俩|liǎ}{每|měi}{人|rén}{一千九百八十|yì qiān jiǔ bǎi bā shí}{元|yuán}。{房东|fáng dōng}{希望|xī wàng}{我们|wǒ men}{每|měi}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{五|wǔ}{号|hào}{以前|yǐ qián}{付款|fù kuǎn}，{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{在|zài}{三|sān}{号|hào}{以前|yǐ qián}{把|bǎ}{钱|qián}{转给|zhuǎn gěi}{我|wǒ}，{我|wǒ}{统一|tǒng yī}{交|jiāo}。{另外|lìng wài}，{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{共用|gòng yòng}{账户|zhàng hù}{里|lǐ}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{三百|sān bǎi}{元|yuán}{余额|yú é}，{可以|kě yǐ}{先|xiān}{用来|yòng lái}{买|mǎi}{日用品|rì yòng pǐn}。{大家|dà jiā}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{意见|yì jiàn}，{今天|jīn tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{说|shuō}{一下|yí xià}{吧|ba}！

(about 200 characters) {水电费|shuǐ diàn fèi}: water and electricity. {网费|wǎng fèi}: internet charges. {平分|píng fēn}: to split equally. {房东|fáng dōng}
(HSK 4): landlord. {转给|zhuǎn gěi}: to transfer to. {统一|tǒng yī}{交|jiāo}: to pay together. {共用|gòng yòng}: shared. {日用品|rì yòng pǐn}: household
necessities. "Hi everyone! This month's bills have all come in and I've sorted them out: rent 6,000
yuan, water and electricity 450, internet 90, 6,540 in all. Rent is over 90 % of our spending, so I
suggest we split it by room size: the big room 2,400 and each small room 1,800; water, electricity and
internet split equally, 180 each. So I pay 2,580 and you each pay 1,980. The landlord wants payment by
the 5th of every month, so please transfer the money to me by the 3rd and I'll pay it all together.
Also, there's a balance of 300 yuan in our shared account, which we could use for household things
first. If you have any views, say so this evening!"

A checklist: the figures first, then the proposal and the reason ({所以|suǒ yǐ}); each person's amount; the
deadline; a question to close.
</details>

## Speaking: a story from four photos

In the HSK 6 speaking test, as reported, you see four numbered photos and tell a story from them
(three minutes to prepare, two to speak). Here the photos are described in words:

1. A young woman puts a coin into a big glass jar on her desk; on the wall, a calendar with a red
   circle round a date in December.
2. Months later, at the bank, she hands the full jar to a clerk, who smiles.
3. At home, she looks at her phone: her account balance has gone up. She writes something on a
   slip of paper.
4. At a station in December, she gives an envelope to her surprised parents; behind them, a poster
   for a trip abroad.

Tell the story in about two minutes. Say who she is, what she's saving for, how the saving goes, and
how it ends; use {储蓄|chǔ xù} / {存|cún}{钱|qián}, {余额|yú é}, {数目|shù mù}, {预期|yù qī}, {成|chéng}, {加倍|jiā bèi}.

<details>
<summary>A model answer</summary>

{小林|Xiǎo Lín}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{刚|gāng}{工作|gōng zuò}{的|de}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}，{薪水|xīn shuǐ}{不|bù}{高|gāo}。{她|tā}{的|de}{父母|fù mǔ}{结婚|jié hūn}{三十|sān shí}{年|nián}{了|le}，{一直|yì zhí}{想|xiǎng}{出国|chū guó}{旅游|lǚ yóu}，{可是|kě shì}{舍不得|shě bu de}{花|huā}{钱|qián}。{小林|Xiǎo Lín}{决定|jué dìng}{给|gěi}{他们|tā men}{一|yí}{个|gè}{惊喜|jīng xǐ}：{从|cóng}{一|yī}{月|yuè}{开始|kāi shǐ}，{她|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{把|bǎ}{零钱|líng qián}{放|fàng}{进|jìn}{桌|zhuō}{上|shàng}{的|de}{一|yí}{个|gè}{大|dà}{玻璃瓶|bō li píng}{里|lǐ}，{日历|rì lì}{上|shàng}{的|de}{十二|shí èr}{月|yuè}{二十|èr shí}{号|hào}{用|yòng}{红|hóng}{笔|bǐ}{标|biāo}{了|le}{出来|chū lái}，{那|nà}{是|shì}{父母|fù mǔ}{结婚|jié hūn}{的|de}{纪念日|jì niàn rì}。

{一|yì}{年|nián}{快|kuài}{过去|guò qù}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{瓶子|píng zi}{满|mǎn}{了|le}。{她|tā}{把|bǎ}{它|tā}{拿|ná}{到|dào}{银行|yín háng}，{工作|gōng zuò}{人员|rén yuán}{帮|bāng}{她|tā}{数|shǔ}{了|le}{数|shǔ}，{数目|shù mù}{比|bǐ}{她|tā}{的|de}{预期|yù qī}{还|hái}{多|duō}。{她|tā}{又|yòu}{把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{一|yì}{年|nián}{存在|cún zài}{银行|yín háng}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{工资|gōng zī}{储蓄|chǔ xù}{加|jiā}{在|zài}{一起|yì qǐ}，{看|kàn}{了|le}{看|kàn}{手机|shǒu jī}：{账户|zhàng hù}{余额|yú é}{比|bǐ}{年初|nián chū}{加倍|jiā bèi}{了|le}。{她|tā}{在|zài}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{纸条|zhǐ tiáo}{上|shàng}{写|xiě}{了|le}{几|jǐ}{句|jù}{话|huà}。

{十二|shí èr}{月|yuè}{二十|èr shí}{号|hào}，{小林|Xiǎo Lín}{到|dào}{车站|chē zhàn}{去|qù}{接|jiē}{父母|fù mǔ}，{把|bǎ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{信封|xìn fēng}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{他们|tā men}。{信封|xìn fēng}{里|lǐ}{是|shì}{两|liǎng}{张|zhāng}{去|qù}{国外|guó wài}{旅游|lǚ yóu}{的|de}{机票|jī piào}{和|hé}{那|nà}{张|zhāng}{纸条|zhǐ tiáo}。{父母|fù mǔ}{打开|dǎ kāi}{一|yí}{看|kàn}，{又|yòu}{吃惊|chī jīng}{又|yòu}{感动|gǎn dòng}。{小林|Xiǎo Lín}{说|shuō}，{钱|qián}{虽然|suī rán}{只|zhǐ}{够|gòu}{玩|wán}{几|jǐ}{天|tiān}，{但|dàn}{这|zhè}{是|shì}{她|tā}{工作|gōng zuò}{以后|yǐ hòu}{最|zuì}{开心|kāi xīn}{的|de}{一|yí}{次|cì}{花|huā}{钱|qián}。

(about 280 characters) {舍不得|shě bu de} (HSK 5): to hate to part with. {惊喜|jīng xǐ}: a pleasant surprise. {玻璃瓶|bō li píng} (bō li píng): glass jar.
{纪念日|jì niàn rì}: anniversary. {吃惊|chī jīng} (HSK 4): surprised. {感动|gǎn dòng} (HSK 4): moved. A checklist: one or two
sentences per photo; a reason at the start (why she saves); time words to move on ({从|cóng}{一|yī}{月|yuè}{开始|kāi shǐ}, {一|yì}{年|nián}{快|kuài}{过去|guò qù}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}, {十二|shí èr}{月|yuè}{二十|èr shí}{号|hào});
an ending with a feeling.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Talking about money
{今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{收益|shōu yì}{增长|zēng zhǎng}{了|le}{三|sān}{成|chéng}。
= This year's income has risen by 30 %.
{利润率|lì rùn lǜ}{降|jiàng}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{百分点|bǎi fēn diǎn}。
= The profit rate is down two percentage points.
{交通|jiāo tōng}{费|fèi}{在|zài}{总|zǒng}{支出|zhī chū}{中|zhōng}{的|de}{占比|zhàn bǐ}{最|zuì}{大|dà}。
= Transport has the largest share of total spending.
{学生|xué sheng}{人数|rén shù}{增加|zēng jiā}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi}。
= Student numbers have doubled.
{结果|jié guǒ}{比|bǐ}{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{预期|yù qī}{好|hǎo}。
= The results are better than we expected.
{分期|fēn qī}{付款|fù kuǎn}{的话|de huà}，{要|yào}{多|duō}{付|fù}{一些|yì xiē}{利息|lì xī}。
= If you pay in instalments, you pay a bit more in interest.
```

## Pronunciation

- {会计|kuài jì} kuài jì: 会 is kuài here, not huì.
- {跌|diē} diē (to fall): first tone. Don't read it like {失|shī} shī, its sound part: the sound has moved.
- {储蓄|chǔ xù} chǔ xù: ch then x; {股票|gǔ piào} gǔ piào: the {票|piào} of {车|chē}{票|piào}. {炒股|chǎo gǔ} chǎo gǔ: two third tones, said cháo gǔ.
- {贸易|mào yì} mào yì: two falling tones. {毛衣|máo yī} (HSK 4: sweater) is máo yī.
- {金额|jīn é} jīn é and {余额|yú é} yú é: the apostrophe goes in the pinyin word (jīn'é, yú'é); {额|é} é has no initial.
- {亏损|kuī sǔn} kuī sǔn, {汇款|huì kuǎn} huì kuǎn: kuī, kuǎn with u after k.

## Common mistakes

- {增加|zēng jiā}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi} is "doubled", not "tripled": Chinese counts the increase. {增加|zēng jiā}{到|dào}{两|liǎng}{倍|bèi} is also "doubled".
- {提高|tí gāo}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{百分点|bǎi fēn diǎn} (12 % from 10 %) is not {提高|tí gāo}{了|le}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{二|èr}: for rates, use {百分点|bǎi fēn diǎn}.
- {占比|zhàn bǐ}{很|hěn}{大|dà} is fine in business speech, but {比重|bǐ zhòng} is the word that goes with {大|dà} / {小|xiǎo} in writing: {所|suǒ}{占|zhàn}{的|de}{比重|bǐ zhòng}{很|hěn}{大|dà}.
- ~~{他|tā}{的|de}{财富|cái fù}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{钱|qián}~~: {财富|cái fù} is the wealth itself: {他|tā}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{财富|cái fù} / {他|tā}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{钱|qián}.
- {财产|cái chǎn} (a person's) and {资产|zī chǎn} (a company's): {公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{资产|zī chǎn}, {个人|gè rén}{财产|cái chǎn}.
- {股票|gǔ piào}{上市|shàng shì} is said, but the usual subject of {上市|shàng shì} is the company or a product: {公司|gōng sī}{上市|shàng shì}, {新款|xīn kuǎn}{上市|shàng shì}.
- {预期|yù qī} as a verb is formal: in a chat, {我们|wǒ men}{以为|yǐ wéi}… or {比|bǐ}{我们|wǒ men}{想|xiǎng}{的|de}{好|hǎo}.

## Key points

- {成|chéng} = tenths ({三|sān}{成|chéng} = 30 %; {降价|jiàng jià}{两|liǎng}{成|chéng} = 20 % off); spoken {八|bā}{成|chéng} = very probably.
- {百分点|bǎi fēn diǎn} for changes in rates; {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī} for the rates themselves.
- A {占|zhàn} B {的|de} x; {占比|zhàn bǐ} (the figure); {比重|bǐ zhòng} (weight, with {大|dà} / {小|xiǎo}); {占据|zhàn jù} (hold a position), {占有|zhàn yǒu} (possess).
- {加倍|jiā bèi} (double; doubly), {倍增|bèi zēng} (multiply, written); {增加|zēng jiā}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi} = doubled, {增加|zēng jiā}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{倍|bèi} = tripled.
- {预期|yù qī}: {超出|chāo chū}{预期|yù qī}, {达到|dá dào}{预期|yù qī}, {低于|dī yú}{预期|yù qī}, {预期|yù qī}{收益|shōu yì}.
- What a loan ({贷款|dài kuǎn}, {利息|lì xī}, {分期还款|fēn qī huán kuǎn}), a share ({股票|gǔ piào}, {上市|shàng shì}, {股市|gǔ shì}, {炒股|chǎo gǔ}) and a fund ({基金|jī jīn}) are.
- New characters: 财 股 储 蓄 贷 跌 额 融 贸.

lessons.title: Pressure, setbacks and coping
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Two days before a student group arrives in Xi'an, the company's partner there changes the hotel and
asks for more money. For {大卫|Dà wèi} (David) it's the hardest week of the year. This lesson is about
difficulty and getting through it:

- **{好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì}** / {好容易|hǎo róng yì} (with great difficulty, at long last) and the trap in {好容易|hǎo róng yì} on its own;
- {只得|zhǐ dé} (to have no choice but to) and {总算|zǒng suàn} (at last; all in all);
- **冲** chòng (towards, at; on the strength of), a second reading of HSK 5's 冲 chōng;
- the **[[verbal measure word]]** {番|fān} ({一|yì}{番|fān}{努力|nǔ lì}, {研究|yán jiū}{一|yì}{番|fān});
- a first look at **{就算|jiù suàn}…{也|yě}** (even if), lesson 23's word;
- the words of pressure, setbacks, feelings and coping, and the module's **[[opinion question]]** for
  the speaking test.

## {好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì} and {好容易|hǎo róng yì}: with great difficulty

{好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì} before a verb says that something happened only after a struggle, usually with {才|cái}:

{我们|wǒ men}{好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì}{才|cái}{订|dìng}{到|dào}{了|le}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}。 — It was a real struggle, but we managed to book a hotel.

{等|děng}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}，{车|chē}{好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì}{来|lái}{了|le}。 — We waited two hours before the bus finally came.

The surprise: {好容易|hǎo róng yì} means the same in this position. {好|hǎo} here is "very", and both forms are heard:

{他|tā}{好容易|hǎo róng yì}{才|cái}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{那|nà}{家|jiā}{店|diàn}。 = {他|tā}{好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì}{才|cái}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{那|nà}{家|jiā}{店|diàn}。 — It took him ages to find the shop.

But only before a verb. As the predicate of a sentence, they part company:

| Sentence | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì}。 | This is really not easy. |
| {这|zhè}{道|dào}{题|tí}{好容易|hǎo róng yì}！ | This question is so easy! (spoken) |
| {我们|wǒ men}{好|hǎo}({不|bù}){容易|róng yì}{才|cái}{做|zuò}{完|wán}。 | We only just managed to finish. |

So when you mean "difficult", say {好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì} or {真|zhēn}{不|bù}{容易|róng yì}; when {好容易|hǎo róng yì} comes straight before a verb (or before
{才|cái}), read it as "with difficulty".

## {只得|zhǐ dé} and {总算|zǒng suàn}

{只得|zhǐ dé} is "to have no choice but to": something forces your hand. It's the slightly written partner
of {只好|zhǐ hǎo} (HSK 4):

{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{没有|méi yǒu}{房间|fáng jiān}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{只得|zhǐ dé}{换|huàn}{一|yì}{家|jiā}。 — The hotel had no rooms left, so we had to change to another.

{雨|yǔ}{太|tài}{大|dà}，{活动|huó dòng}{只得|zhǐ dé}{延期|yán qī}。 — The rain was so heavy that the event had to be put off.

{总算|zǒng suàn} has two uses:

- "at last", with relief after waiting or effort: {问题|wèn tí}{总算|zǒng suàn}{解决|jiě jué}{了|le}。 (The problem is solved at last.) {等|děng}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{月|yuè}，
  {签证|qiān zhèng}{总算|zǒng suàn}{下来|xià lái}{了|le}。 (After a month the visa finally came through.)
- "all in all, more or less": the result is acceptable, though not perfect: {虽然|suī rán}{累|lèi}，{这|zhè}{次|cì}{总算|zǒng suàn}{没|méi}{白|bái}{来|lái}。 (Tired as
  we are, all in all it wasn't a wasted trip.) {他|tā}{的|de}{中文|Zhōng wén}{总算|zǒng suàn}{还|hái}{可以|kě yǐ}。 (His Chinese is passable, more or less.)

{终于|zhōng yú} (HSK 3) is "finally" without the relief or the "all in all"; {总算|zǒng suàn} is warmer and more spoken.

## {冲|chòng}: towards; on the strength of

HSK 5 taught {冲|chōng}, "to rush, charge". The same character read chòng (fourth tone) is a spoken
preposition: "towards, at, facing":

{她|tā}{冲|chòng}{我|wǒ}{笑|xiào}{了|le}{笑|xiào}。 — She smiled at me.

{你|nǐ}{别|bié}{冲|chòng}{我|wǒ}{发脾气|fā pí qi}。 — Don't take it out on me. ({发脾气|fā pí qi}: to lose your temper)

It also means "on the strength of, for the sake of", often as {冲着|chòng zhe}:

{冲着|chòng zhe}{你|nǐ}{这|zhè}{句|jù}{话|huà}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{得|děi}{帮|bāng}{这个|zhè ge}{忙|máng}。 — For your saying that, I'll have to help.

{冲着|chòng zhe}{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{店|diàn}{的|de}{名气|míng qi}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{专门|zhuān mén}{来|lái}{吃|chī}。 — Lots of people come specially, because of the restaurant's name. ({名气|míng qi}, lesson 10's word: fame)

As an adjective, chòng is "strong, blunt": {他|tā}{说话|shuō huà}{很|hěn}{冲|chòng} (he speaks bluntly), {这|zhè}{酒|jiǔ}{很|hěn}{冲|chòng} (this drink is strong).
Both readings are 衝 in traditional characters. Context decides the reading: 冲 + a person, followed
by a verb ({冲|chòng}{我|wǒ}{笑|xiào}) is chòng; 冲 + a direction verb ({冲|chōng}{进去|jìn qù}, {冲|chōng}{过来|guò lái}) is chōng.

## {番|fān}: a verbal measure word for effort

{番|fān} counts actions that take time and effort, nearly always with {一|yī}:

| Phrase | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {一|yì}{番|fān}{努力|nǔ lì} | a lot of effort |
| {一|yì}{番|fān}{话|huà} | a few (heartfelt or serious) words |
| {研究|yán jiū}{一|yì}{番|fān} | to study it carefully |
| {打扮|dǎ ban}{了|le}{一|yì}{番|fān} | to dress up (with some care) |
| {费|fèi}{了|le}{一|yì}{番|fān}{功夫|gōng fu} | to go to a lot of trouble ({功夫|gōng fu}: effort) |

{经过|jīng guò}{一|yì}{番|fān}{努力|nǔ lì}，{问题|wèn tí}{总算|zǒng suàn}{解决|jiě jué}{了|le}。 — After a great deal of effort, the problem was finally solved.

{他|tā}{的|de}{一|yì}{番|fān}{话|huà}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{感动|gǎn dòng}。 — What he said moved me.

- Before a noun: {一|yì}{番|fān} + {努力|nǔ lì} / {话|huà} / {心思|xīn si} (thought, care). After a verb: verb + {了|le} + {一|yì}{番|fān} ({研究|yán jiū}{了|le}{一|yì}{番|fān}).
- Compare {一下|yí xià} (HSK 1), which is a quick, light try: {研究|yán jiū}{一下|yí xià} (have a look at it) vs {研究|yán jiū}{一|yì}{番|fān} (study it
  properly).
- {番|fān} is also "times, -fold" in {翻|fān}{了|le}{一|yì}{番|fān} (doubled): {学生|xué sheng}{人数|rén shù}{翻|fān}{了|le}{一|yì}{番|fān} is lesson 04's {增加|zēng jiā}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi} said another
  way.
- In {三番五次|sān fān wǔ cì} (again and again; an idiom) {番|fān} counts repeated times.

## {就算|jiù suàn}…{也|yě}: even if (preview)

{就算|jiù suàn} X，{也|yě} Y is "even if X, still Y". It's lesson 23's word; you'll hear it all the time:

{就算|jiù suàn}{失败|shī bài}{了|le}，{也|yě}{要|yào}{吸取|xī qǔ}{经验|jīng yàn}。 — Even if we fail, we must learn from it.

{就算|jiù suàn}{再|zài}{忙|máng}，{他|tā}{也|yě}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{给|gěi}{父母|fù mǔ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。 — However busy he is, he phones his parents every day.

{就算|jiù suàn} is spoken; {即使|jí shǐ} (HSK 4) is neutral and {哪怕|nǎ pà} (HSK 5) is emphatic. {即便|jí biàn} (lesson 26) is the written form.

## Words for pressure and coping

### When things go wrong

| Word | Meaning | Example |

| {挫折|cuò zhé} | setback, frustration | {遇到|yù dào}{挫折|cuò zhé} |

| {危机|wēi jī} | crisis | {经济|jīng jì}{危机|wēi jī}, {一|yì}{场|chǎng}{危机|wēi jī} |
| {考验|kǎo yàn} | test, trial; to test | {经|jīng}{受|shòu}{考验|kǎo yàn} (stand the test) |
| {困扰|kùn rǎo} | to trouble, bother; worry | {这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{困扰|kùn rǎo}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{久|jiǔ}。 |
| {陷入|xiàn rù} | to fall into (a difficult state) | {陷入|xiàn rù}{困境|kùn jìng} (get into a fix) |
| {逼|bī} | to force, press | {逼|bī}{他|tā}{马上|mǎ shàng}{做|zuò}{决定|jué dìng} |
| {被迫|bèi pò} | to be forced to | {被迫|bèi pò}{取消|qǔ xiāo} |
| {代价|dài jià} | price, cost (what it costs you) | {付出|fù chū}{代价|dài jià} |
| {耽误|dān wu} | to delay, hold up; to waste (time) | {耽误|dān wu}{时间|shí jiān}, {别|bié}{耽误|dān wu}{了|le}{工作|gōng zuò} |
| {拖|tuō} | to drag; to put off | {拖|tuō}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{月|yuè} |
| {拖延|tuō yán} | to delay, put off | {拖延|tuō yán}{时间|shí jiān} |
| {误|wù} | to miss (through delay); mistake | {误|wù}{了|le}{火车|huǒ chē} |
| {白白|bái bái} | in vain, for nothing | {白白|bái bái}{浪费|làng fèi}{了|le}{一|yì}{天|tiān} |

- {挫折|cuò zhé} is a setback you meet ({遇到|yù dào}{挫折|cuò zhé}, {经历|jīng lì}{挫折|cuò zhé}); {打击|dǎ jī} is a blow you receive ({受到|shòu dào}{打击|dǎ jī}). Both are nouns here.
- {逼|bī} is pressing someone hard ({逼|bī}{他|tā}{做|zuò}{决定|jué dìng}); {被迫|bèi pò} is being forced, usually by circumstances ({被迫|bèi pò}{离开|lí kāi}).
- {代价|dài jià} is what you pay for something, not in money: {成功|chéng gōng}{的|de}{代价|dài jià} (the price of success), {付出|fù chū}{了|le}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{代价|dài jià}.
- {耽误|dān wu} is a delay that costs you something: {耽误|dān wu}{了|le}{一|yì}{天|tiān}, {耽误|dān wu}{学习|xué xí}. {误|wù} alone is a little literary: {误|wù}{了|le}{时间|shí jiān}, {误事|wù shì}
  (to mess things up), and in words like {误会|wù huì} (HSK 4).
- {拖|tuō} is to drag ({拖|tuō}{箱子|xiāng zi}) and, in speech, to put off ({拖|tuō}{到|dào}{明天|míng tiān}). {拖延|tuō yán} is the more formal "to delay": {拖延|tuō yán}
  {时间|shí jiān}.

  also written.

{大卫|Dà wèi} phones {陆经理|Lù jīng lǐ} (Manager Lu) of the Xi'an travel company that books hotels for their groups. The
students arrive the day after tomorrow.

```dialogue

大卫: {陆经理|Lù jīng lǐ}，{我|wǒ}{刚|gāng}{收到|shōu dào}{您|nín}{的|de}{邮件|yóu jiàn}，{说|shuō}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{换|huàn}{了|le}？{学生|xué sheng}{后天|hòu tiān}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}！
```

### Two new radicals: 勹 and 尢

- 勹 (wrapping) is the frame round 包 bāo (to wrap: {包子|bāo zi}, HSK 1) and 勺 sháo (spoon: HSK 3). This
  lesson's 匆 is filed under it; lesson 12's 匀 (even: {均匀|jūn yún}) is the fourth. Make Me a Hanzi and most
  dictionaries put these four under 勹.
- 尢 (a lame leg, in its old meaning) is the left part of 就 jiù (HSK 2: dictionaries file {就|jiù} under
  尢) and the whole of 尤 yóu (HSK 4: {尤其|yóu qí}). 尴 and 尬 both have it, wrapped round their sound parts:
  监 jiān in 尴 gān, 介 jiè in 尬 gà. Traditional 尷 has 監.

### Families and look-alikes

- 愁 chóu: 秋 qiū (autumn) over 心: the sound part on top, the heart below. A memory aid: autumn in the
  heart.
- 悲 bēi: 非 fēi (not) over 心; 非 gives the sound. The same 非 is in 排 pái, 辈 bèi (lesson 21),
  罪 zuì (lesson 09).
- 迫 pò: 辶 + 白 bái, the sound part: as in 怕 pà, 拍 pāi, 伯 bó.
- 逼 bī: 辶 + 畐 fú, the sound part of 福 fú ({福利|fú lì}, lesson 01) and 富 fù.
- 挫 cuò: 扌 + 坐 zuò; 坐 gives the sound (zuò → cuò). Don't confuse it with 座 zuò.
- 陷 xiàn: 阝 (a hill on the left) + 臽 xiàn: a pit. The same 臽 is in 馅 xiàn (filling: {饺子馅|jiǎo zi xiàn}).
- 耽 dān: 耳 (ear) + 冘; 枕 zhěn (pillow: lesson 07's {枕头|zhěn tou}) has the same right side.
- 焦 jiāo: 隹 (a short-tailed bird) over 灬 (fire). A memory aid: a bird over the fire, scorched. 灬 at the bottom is fire, as in 热 and 点.
- 呆 dāi is 口 over 木; read upside down it's 杏 xìng (apricot: 木 over 口).

### Stroke order

- **匆**: the left-falling stroke and 勹's turn with a hook first, then a left-falling stroke, a
  second left-falling stroke, and the dot inside last.
- **击**: a horizontal, a second horizontal, the vertical through them, then the vertical that turns
  right (the bottom left of the frame 凵), and the short vertical on the right last.
- **闯**: 门 (a dot, the left vertical, the horizontal-turn-hook), then 马 inside it.
- **忧**: 忄 (the two short strokes, then the vertical), then 尤: a horizontal, a left-falling stroke,
  the vertical-bend-hook, and a dot.
- **尬**: 尢 first (a horizontal, a left-falling stroke and the vertical-bend-hook), then 介: a
  left-falling stroke, a right-falling stroke, a left-falling stroke and a vertical.
- **摆**: 扌, then 罒 (five strokes), then 去 at the bottom right: a horizontal, a vertical, a
  horizontal, then the turn and the dot.



```trace

```

times from memory, then {摆脱|bǎi tuō}, {被迫|bèi pò}, {发愁|fā chóu}, {悲观|bēi guān}, {闯|chuǎng}, {打击|dǎ jī}, {担忧|dān yōu}, {匆忙|cōng máng}, {呆|dāi}.

## Write it: a thank-you letter

After the Xi'an trip, write a thank-you letter ({感谢信|gǎn xiè xìn}) of 150–200 characters from {大卫|Dà wèi}'s company to the
staff of the new hotel, who helped at short notice. Say what happened, what they did, what it meant
to the students, and end with thanks and good wishes. Use at least four of: {匆忙|cōng máng}, {总算|zǒng suàn}, {好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì}, {耽误|dān wu}, {一|yì}{番|fān},
{尽|jìn}, {冲着|chòng zhe}, {解决|jiě jué}.

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

> {感谢信|gǎn xiè xìn}
>
> {尊敬|zūn jìng}{的|de}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{全体员工|quán tǐ yuán gōng}：
>
> {你们|nǐ men}{好|hǎo}！{上|shàng}{周|zhōu}，{我|wǒ}{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{四十|sì shí}{名|míng}{英国|Yīng guó}{学生|xué sheng}{在|zài}{西安|Xī ān}{参观|cān guān}{学习|xué xí}。{由于|yóu yú}{原来|yuán lái}{的|de}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{突然|tū rán}{没有|méi yǒu}{房间|fáng jiān}，{我们|wǒ men}{只得|zhǐ dé}{在|zài}{出发|chū fā}{前|qián}{两|liǎng}{天|tiān}{匆忙|cōng máng}{换|huàn}{到|dào}{贵|guì}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}。{学生|xué sheng}{到达|dào dá}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{已经|yǐ jīng}{是|shì}{夜|yè}{里|lǐ}{十二|shí èr}{点|diǎn}，{你们|nǐ men}{却|què}{一直|yì zhí}{等|děng}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}，{帮|bāng}{大家|dà jiā}{搬|bān}{行李|xíng li}、{安排|ān pái}{房间|fáng jiān}。{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}，{你们|nǐ men}{还|hái}{专门|zhuān mén}{为|wèi}{学生|xué sheng}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{了|le}{西式|xī shì}{早餐|zǎo cān}，{让|ràng}{他们|tā men}{好好|hǎo hǎo}{休息|xiū xi}，{没有|méi yǒu}{耽误|dān wu}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{的|de}{参观|cān guān}。{经过|jīng guò}{你们|nǐ men}{一|yì}{番|fān}{努力|nǔ lì}，{这|zhè}{次|cì}{活动|huó dòng}{总算|zǒng suàn}{顺利|shùn lì}{结束|jié shù}{了|le}。{学生|xué sheng}{们|men}{都|dōu}{说|shuō}，{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{的|de}{服务|fú wù}{让|ràng}{他们|tā men}{感到|gǎn dào}{像|xiàng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{一样|yí yàng}。{在此|zài cǐ}，{我们|wǒ men}{向|xiàng}{你们|nǐ men}{表示|biǎo shì}{真诚|zhēn chéng}{的|de}{感谢|gǎn xiè}，{并|bìng}{祝|zhù}{贵|guì}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{生意|shēng yi}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{好|hǎo}！
>
> {大卫|Dà wèi}
> 6{月|yuè}30{日|rì}

(about 200 characters) {尊敬|zūn jìng}{的|de} (HSK 4): dear (respected). {在此|zài cǐ}: hereby. {真诚|zhēn chéng} (HSK 5): sincere. "Thank-you letter. To all
the staff of the hotel: last week forty British students from our company were visiting Xi'an.
Because the original hotel suddenly had no rooms, we had to move to your hotel in a hurry two days
before setting out. It was midnight when the students arrived, yet you were waiting at the door
the whole time, carrying luggage and sorting out rooms. The next morning you had even made a Western
breakfast specially, so that they could rest properly and not lose a day of visits. Thanks to all
your efforts, the programme ended smoothly in the end. The students all say the service made them
feel at home. We hereby express our sincere thanks and wish your hotel ever better business. David,
30 June."

A checklist: {感谢信|gǎn xiè xìn} as the title; a respectful greeting; what happened ({由于|yóu yú}…{只得|zhǐ dé}…); what they did, with
details; the result ({总算|zǒng suàn}); the formula {在此|zài cǐ}…{表示|biǎo shì}{真诚|zhēn chéng}{的|de}{感谢|gǎn xiè}; a closing wish.
</details>

## Speaking: an opinion question

In the HSK 6 speaking test, as reported, you answer two opinion questions (a few minutes to prepare,
then about two and a half minutes to speak for both). Prepare an answer to this one: give your view, two
reasons with an example each, and a conclusion.

{你|nǐ}{认为|rèn wéi}{压力|yā lì}{是|shì}{好|hǎo}{事|shì}{还是|hái shi}{坏|huài}{事|shì}？{为什么|wèi shén me}？

<details>
<summary>A model answer</summary>

{我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}，{压力|yā lì}{不|bù}{一定|yí dìng}{是|shì}{好|hǎo}{事|shì}，{也|yě}{不|bù}{一定|yí dìng}{是|shì}{坏|huài}{事|shì}，{关键|guān jiàn}{要|yào}{看|kàn}{压力|yā lì}{有|yǒu}{多|duō}{大|dà}，{以及|yǐ jí}{我们|wǒ men}{怎么|zěn me}{面对|miàn duì}{它|tā}。

{首先|shǒu xiān}，{适度|shì dù}{的|de}{压力|yā lì}{能|néng}{让|ràng}{人|rén}{进步|jìn bù}。{比如|bǐ rú}{考试|kǎo shì}{以前|yǐ qián}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{会|huì}{更|gèng}{认真|rèn zhēn}{地|de}{复习|fù xí}；{工作|gōng zuò}{中|zhōng}{有|yǒu}{了|le}{期限|qī xiàn}，{我们|wǒ men}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{也|yě}{会|huì}{更|gèng}{有|yǒu}{效率|xiào lǜ}。{如果|rú guǒ}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{压力|yā lì}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}，{人|rén}{很|hěn}{容易|róng yì}{变|biàn}{得|de}{懒|lǎn}，{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{努力|nǔ lì}。

{其次|qí cì}，{压力|yā lì}{太|tài}{大|dà}{的话|de huà}，{对|duì}{身心|shēn xīn}{都|dōu}{有害|yǒu hài}。{有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{长|cháng}{时间|shí jiān}{加班|jiā bān}，{又|yòu}{不|bú}{愿意|yuàn yì}{跟|gēn}{别人|bié ren}{说|shuō}，{最后|zuì hòu}{陷入|xiàn rù}{焦虑|jiāo lǜ}，{甚至|shèn zhì}{生病|shēng bìng}。{这样|zhè yàng}{的|de}{压力|yā lì}{只|zhǐ}{会|huì}{让|ràng}{人|rén}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{脆弱|cuì ruò}。

{所以|suǒ yǐ}，{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{重要|zhòng yào}{的|de}{是|shì}{学会|xué huì}{给|gěi}{自己|zì jǐ}{减压|jiǎn yā}：{遇到|yù dào}{挫折|cuò zhé}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{不要|bú yào}{灰心|huī xīn}，{可以|kě yǐ}{运动|yùn dòng}、{跟|gēn}{朋友|péng you}{聊|liáo}{天|tiān}，{必要|bì yào}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{寻求|xún qiú}{别人|bié ren}{的|de}{帮助|bāng zhù}。{压力|yā lì}{是|shì}{生活|shēng huó}{的|de}{一|yí}{部分|bù fen}，{我们|wǒ men}{没|méi}{法|fǎ}{完全|wán quán}{摆脱|bǎi tuō}{它|tā}，{但是|dàn shì}{可以|kě yǐ}{让|ràng}{它|tā}{变成|biàn chéng}{让|ràng}{我们|wǒ men}{进步|jìn bù}{的|de}{力量|lì liang}。

(about 260 characters) {面对|miàn duì} (HSK 4): to face. {懒|lǎn} (HSK 4): lazy. {有害|yǒu hài}: harmful. {力量|lì liang} (HSK 5): strength. A checklist: a clear opening view; {首先|shǒu xiān} / {其次|qí cì} / {所以|suǒ yǐ} to mark the structure; an example for each
reason ({比如|bǐ rú}…); a concession ({没|méi}{法|fǎ}{完全|wán quán}{摆脱|bǎi tuō}{它|tā}，{但是|dàn shì}…); a closing sentence that returns to the view.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Under pressure
{我们|wǒ men}{好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì}{才|cái}{订|dìng}{到|dào}{了|le}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}。
= It was a struggle, but we managed to book a hotel.
{时间|shí jiān}{太|tài}{紧|jǐn}，{只得|zhǐ dé}{这样|zhè yàng}{了|le}。
= Time is too short: we'll have to leave it like this.
{问题|wèn tí}{总算|zǒng suàn}{解决|jiě jué}{了|le}。
= The problem's solved at last.
{你|nǐ}{别|bié}{冲|chòng}{我|wǒ}{发火|fā huǒ}。
= Don't take it out on me.
{经过|jīng guò}{一|yì}{番|fān}{努力|nǔ lì}，{结果|jié guǒ}{还|hái}{不错|bú cuò}。
= After a lot of effort, the result isn't bad.
{就算|jiù suàn}{遇到|yù dào}{挫折|cuò zhé}，{也|yě}{别|bié}{灰心|huī xīn}。
= Even if you have setbacks, don't lose heart.
```

## Pronunciation

- 冲 has two readings: chōng (to rush: {冲|chōng}{进去|jìn qù}) and chòng (towards: {冲|chòng}{我|wǒ}{笑|xiào}; blunt: {说话|shuō huà}{很|hěn}{冲|chòng}). Same character,
  both 衝 in traditional.
- {尴尬|gān gà} gān gà: both a; the first syllable high and level, the second falling.
- {委屈|wěi qu} wěi qu: the second syllable is light. On its own 屈 is qū ({屈服|qū fú}, to give in).
- {呆|dāi} dāi: a high level tone.
- {焦虑|jiāo lǜ} jiāo lǜ: lǜ with ü, like {绿|lǜ}. {疲劳|pí láo} pí láo: two rising tones.
- {耽误|dān wu} dān wu: light second syllable. {担忧|dān yōu} dān yōu: both first tones.
- {尽|jìn} jìn (to do one's utmost) and {尽管|jǐn guǎn} jǐn guǎn (HSK 4): different tones.
- {挫折|cuò zhé} cuò zhé: c then zh.

## Common mistakes

- {这|zhè}{道|dào}{题|tí}{好容易|hǎo róng yì} means "this question is so easy". For "not easy", say {好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì} or {真|zhēn}{不|bù}{容易|róng yì}. Only before a verb
  are {好容易|hǎo róng yì} and {好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì} the same.
- {总算|zǒng suàn} normally goes after the subject: {我们|wǒ men}{总算|zǒng suàn}{解决|jiě jué}{了|le}{问题|wèn tí} (or {问题|wèn tí}{总算|zǒng suàn}{解决|jiě jué}{了|le}).
- {只得|zhǐ dé} is stiffer than {只好|zhǐ hǎo}: in a chat, {我|wǒ}{只好|zhǐ hǎo}{换|huàn}{一|yì}{家|jiā} is more natural.
- 冲 chòng + person needs a verb after it: {她|tā}{冲|chòng}{我|wǒ}{笑|xiào} (not ~~{她|tā}{冲|chòng}{我|wǒ}~~ alone, unless 冲 means "aimed at": {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{冲|chòng}{你|nǐ}, "it isn't
  aimed at you", which is fine).
- ~~{两|liǎng}{番|fān}{努力|nǔ lì}~~: {番|fān} is almost always {一|yì}{番|fān} (or {几|jǐ}{番|fān}, {三番五次|sān fān wǔ cì}).
- {发愁|fā chóu} doesn't take a direct object: ~~{发愁|fā chóu}{工作|gōng zuò}~~ → {为|wèi}{工作|gōng zuò}{发愁|fā chóu} or {愁|chóu}{工作|gōng zuò}.
- {吸取|xī qǔ} most often takes {经验|jīng yàn} / {教训|jiào xun}; for knowledge, the everyday verb is {学习|xué xí} ({学习|xué xí}{知识|zhī shi}).
- {机遇|jī yù} / {机会|jī huì}: {机遇|jī yù} is a big chance in life ({抓|zhuā}{住|zhù}{机遇|jī yù}); for "a chance to talk", {机会|jī huì}.

## Key points

- {好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì} / {好容易|hǎo róng yì} + ({才|cái}) + verb: with great difficulty; as a predicate, {好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì} = not easy, {好容易|hǎo róng yì} = so easy.
- {只得|zhǐ dé} (have no choice but to; written for {只好|zhǐ hǎo}); {总算|zǒng suàn} (at last, with relief; all in all).
- {冲|chòng}: towards ({冲|chòng}{我|wǒ}{笑|xiào}), for the sake of ({冲着|chòng zhe}{你|nǐ}{这|zhè}{句|jù}{话|huà}), blunt ({说话|shuō huà}{很|hěn}{冲|chòng}); {冲|chōng}: to rush.
- {番|fān}: {一|yì}{番|fān}{努力|nǔ lì} / {一|yì}{番|fān}{话|huà}; verb + {了|le} + {一|yì}{番|fān} ({研究|yán jiū}{了|le}{一|yì}{番|fān}); {翻|fān}{了|le}{一|yì}{番|fān} = doubled.
- {就算|jiù suàn} X，{也|yě} Y: even if (spoken); {即使|jí shǐ} (neutral), {哪怕|nǎ pà} (emphatic), {即便|jí biàn} (written).
- Feelings: {焦虑|jiāo lǜ} (anxiety), {担忧|dān yōu} (concern), {发愁|fā chóu} / {愁|chóu} (worry), {委屈|wěi qu} (wronged), {尴尬|gān gà} (awkward), {灰心|huī xīn} / {绝望|jué wàng} / {悲观|bēi guān}.
  Coping: {减压|jiǎn yā}, {释放|shì fàng}, {摆脱|bǎi tuō}, {消除|xiāo chú}, {吸取|xī qǔ}{经验|jīng yàn}, {寻求|xún qiú}{帮助|bāng zhù}.
- New characters: 摆 迫 逼 愁 悲 闯 挫 击 耽 忧 匆 脆 呆 尴 尬 焦 疲 屈 陷; new
  radicals 勹 and 尢.

lessons.title: Lu Xun's "My Old Home"
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This honors lesson meets {鲁迅|Lǔ Xùn} (Lǔ Xùn, Lu Xun), the writer most Chinese readers think of first when
they think of modern Chinese literature, and one of his best-loved short stories, 《{故乡|gù xiāng}》 (Gù xiāng, "My
Old Home", also translated "Hometown"). You read the story retold in our own Chinese, then its
famous closing lines in Lu Xun's own words, with notes, a paraphrase in modern Chinese and our
translation.

Lu Xun wrote in the new written vernacular of the early twentieth century. It is close to the
Chinese you know, but older in places: you'll see {便|biàn} for {就|jiù}, {本|běn} for "originally", and turns of phrase
nobody uses today. Read the notes, then the paraphrase, then the original aloud.

Lu Xun's stories are free to read: he died in 1936, and under China's copyright law protection lasts
for the author's life and fifty years after, so his works have been in the public domain in China
since the start of 1987; 《{故乡|gù xiāng}》, published in 1921, is also in the public domain in the United
States, where works published before 1931 are no longer protected.

## Lu Xun in a paragraph

{鲁迅|Lǔ Xùn} is a pen name; he was born {周树人|Zhōu Shù rén} (Zhōu Shùrén) in 1881 in {绍兴|Shào xīng} (Shàoxīng), a town of rivers and
canals in today's Zhejiang, and died in Shanghai in 1936. As a young man he went to Japan to study
medicine, then turned to writing. In 1918 he published 《{狂人日记|Kuáng rén Rì jì}》 ("A Madman's Diary"), one of the
first short stories written in the modern vernacular; his first collection of stories, 《{呐喊|Nà hǎn}》
(*Nàhǎn*, "Call to Arms"), followed in 1923. 《{故乡|gù xiāng}》 first appeared in 1921, in the magazine 《{新青年|Xīn Qīng nián}》
(*New Youth*), and was later included in 《{呐喊|Nà hǎn}》. He also wrote essays, prose poems and memoirs,
and translated foreign literature. At the end of 1919 he himself went back to {绍兴|Shào xīng}, where the
family house had been sold, and moved his mother and family to Beijing, setting out by boat; readers often link
《{故乡|gù xiāng}》 with that journey, though the story's "I" is a character, not a diary.

## Reading: the story in our own words

> 《{故乡|gù xiāng}》
>
> 《{故乡|gù xiāng}》{是|shì}{鲁迅|Lǔ Xùn}{一九二一|yī jiǔ èr yī}{年|nián}{写|xiě}{的|de}{一|yì}{篇|piān}{短|duǎn}{篇|piān}{小说|xiǎo shuō}。{小说|xiǎo shuō}{里|lǐ}{的|de}“{我|wǒ}”{离开|lí kāi}{故乡|gù xiāng}{已经|yǐ jīng}{二十|èr shí}{多|duō}{年|nián}{了|le}。{这|zhè}{年|nián}{冬天|dōng tiān}，“{我|wǒ}”{冒着|mào zhe}{寒冷|hán lěng}，{坐|zuò}{船|chuán}{回|huí}{到|dào}{两|liǎng}{千|qiān}{多|duō}{里|lǐ}{以外|yǐ wài}{的|de}{老家|lǎo jiā}。{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{老|lǎo}{房子|fáng zi}{已经|yǐ jīng}{卖|mài}{给|gěi}{了|le}{别人|bié ren}，{这|zhè}{次|cì}{回来|huí lái}，{是|shì}{要|yào}{把|bǎ}{母亲|mǔ qīn}{和|hé}{家人|jiā rén}{接|jiē}{走|zǒu}，{以后|yǐ hòu}{就|jiù}{在|zài}{外地|wài dì}{生活|shēng huó}{了|le}。
>

rough. {恭恭敬敬|gōng gōng jìng jìng} (gōng gōng jìng jìng): respectfully, formally. {老爷|lǎo ye} (lǎo ye): "master", how a servant or a
poor farmer addressed a gentleman. {心里|xīn li}{一|yì}{冷|lěng}: to feel a chill inside. {隔|gé}{着|zhe} (HSK 5's {隔|gé}): separated by. {墙|qiáng} (HSK 5): wall. {水生|Shuǐ shēng}
(Shuǐ shēng): the boy's name. {一模一样|yì mú yí yàng} (lesson 28's idiom): exactly alike. {收成|shōu cheng}: harvest. {家具|jiā jù} (HSK 4): furniture.
{一|yí}{副|fù} (HSK 5's {副|fù}, the measure word): a set. {香炉|xiāng lú} (xiāng lú): incense burner. {烛台|zhú tái} (zhú tái): candlestick. {两岸|liǎng àn}
(lesson 17's word): both banks (of the river). {侄子|zhí zi} (lesson 22's word): nephew. {宏儿|Hóng ér} (Hóng'ér): the nephew's name.

dì): sandy ground. {一|yì}{轮|lún} ({轮|lún}, lesson 03's character): measure word for the moon. {金黄|jīn huáng}: golden.

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

"'My Old Home' is a short story Lu Xun wrote in 1921. The 'I' of the story has been away from his
home town for more than twenty years. This winter, braving the cold, he returns by boat to his old
home, over two thousand li away. The family's old house has been sold, and he has come back to take
his mother and family away to live elsewhere from now on. As the boat draws near, the weather is
gloomy; in the distance there are only a few quiet villages, without a trace of life. He feels a
sadness he can't put into words: is this the home he has so often missed? At home, his mother tells
him that Runtu has heard he's back and wants to see him. At the name, his childhood comes back to him
at once. One year the family had a great occasion to prepare for at New Year and asked Runtu's
father to help, and Runtu came too. He was about the same age, with a round face, and knew
everything: how to catch birds on the ground when it snowed, the shells of every colour on the beach,
how to guard the watermelon field by moonlight on summer nights. The narrator felt Runtu's head was
full of endless new things. When New Year was over and Runtu had to go home, the two boys couldn't
bear to part and cried for a long time. A few days later Runtu really comes. He is much bigger than
before, but his face is grey and yellow and full of wrinkles, and his hands are rough and hard. The
narrator is overjoyed and wants to say a great deal to him; Runtu's face shows both joy and sadness.
His lips move, but in the end he says respectfully: 'Master!…' The narrator feels a chill inside. He understands that a thick wall now stands between them. Runtu has brought his son
Shuisheng, who looks exactly like Runtu as a child. Runtu says he has many children, the harvests are
bad and life is very hard. The narrator's mother tells him to choose some things the family no
longer needs; he chooses a few pieces of furniture and asks for an incense burner and a pair of
candlesticks. On the day they leave, the narrator sits in the boat watching the green hills on both
banks slip away. His nephew Hong'er asks, 'When are we coming back?' He says Shuisheng has invited
him to his home to play. The narrator thinks: Runtu and I have grown so far apart, yet the children
are still of one mind. He hopes they won't end up like the two of them, and that they can have a new
life, one that neither of them has lived. At this thought he feels a little afraid. When Runtu asked
for the incense burner and candlesticks, he had laughed at him inwardly for never letting go of the
old ways. But isn't his own hope something he has made for himself, too? It's only that Runtu's wish
is near at hand and his is far away. As night falls, half asleep in the boat, he seems to see again
the sandy shore of his childhood, and a golden moon hanging in the sky, big and round."
</details>

## The closing lines

The story ends with the narrator's thoughts in the boat. These are Lu Xun's own words, among the most
quoted lines in modern Chinese:

> {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}：{希望|xī wàng}{本|běn}{是|shì}{无所谓|wú suǒ wèi}{有|yǒu}，{无所谓|wú suǒ wèi}{无|wú}{的|de}。{这|zhè}{正如|zhèng rú}{地上|dì shang}{的|de}{路|lù}；{其实|qí shí}{地上|dì shang}{本|běn}{没有|méi yǒu}{路|lù}，{走|zǒu}{的|de}{人|rén}{多|duō}{了|le}，{也|yě}{便|biàn}{成|chéng}{了|le}{路|lù}。

Notes:

- {本|běn} (HSK 5's {本|běn}, adverb): originally, in itself. {本|běn}{是|shì}: was, in itself; {本|běn}{没有|méi yǒu}: there was originally no….
- {无所谓|wú suǒ wèi} (lesson 23's word): here not "it doesn't matter" but its literal sense: "cannot be said to be". {无所谓|wú suǒ wèi}{有|yǒu}，
  {无所谓|wú suǒ wèi}{无|wú}: you can't say it exists, and you can't say it doesn't.
- {正如|zhèng rú} (zhèng rú): just as, just like (written).
- {其实|qí shí} (HSK 3): in fact.
- {便|biàn} (HSK 5): written for {就|jiù}.

A paraphrase in modern Chinese: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}：{希望|xī wàng}{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{东西|dōng xi}，{不|bù}{能|néng}{说|shuō}{它|tā}{一定|yí dìng}{有|yǒu}，{也|yě}{不|bù}{能|néng}{说|shuō}{它|tā}{一定|yí dìng}{没有|méi yǒu}。{这|zhè}{就|jiù}{像|xiàng}{地上|dì shang}{的|de}{路|lù}{一样|yí yàng}：{其实|qí shí}{地上|dì shang}{原来|yuán lái}{没有|méi yǒu}{路|lù}，{走|zǒu}{的|de}{人|rén}{多|duō}{了|le}，{也|yě}{就|jiù}{成|chéng}{了|le}{路|lù}。

Our translation: "I thought: hope cannot be said to exist, nor can it be said not to exist. It is
just like the roads across the earth: in fact there were no roads to begin with, but when many people
walk the same way, a road comes into being."

- The comparison works in two steps. First, hope is neither there nor not there: it depends on what
  people do. Second, a road is the same: no one finds a road already made; it appears because many
  people walk there.
- {走|zǒu}{的|de}{人|rén}{多|duō}{了|le} is plain spoken Chinese, and the whole sentence has the rhythm of speech: that is part of
  why people remember it. You'll hear {走|zǒu}{的|de}{人|rén}{多|duō}{了|le}，{也|yě}{便|biàn}{成|chéng}{了|le}{路|lù} quoted in speeches, school essays and
  advertisements, often to encourage someone doing something new.

## Why it is still read

《{故乡|gù xiāng}》 has long been in Chinese secondary-school textbooks, and most adults can tell you who {闰土|Rùn tǔ} is. Readers come
back to it for several reasons, and you don't need any history to feel them:

- **Memory against reality.** The home town of the narrator's memories (the moonlit melon field, the
  shells) is set against the grey villages he actually sees. Anyone who has gone back to a childhood
  place knows the feeling.
- **Distance between people.** The single word {老爷|lǎo ye} does more than a page of explanation: the two
  friends have grown into people who can no longer speak as equals. Lu Xun shows it in a moment, and
  the narrator's shock, rather than explaining it.
- **Hope without certainty.** The ending neither promises nor denies a better future. It hands it to
  the next generation ({宏儿|Hóng ér} and {水生|Shuǐ shēng}) and to "the people who walk".

The story is also a good example of how Lu Xun writes: short, exact pictures (the round face, the
rough hands), few adjectives, and much left for the reader to feel.

## Say it

```speak
# The closing lines
{希望|xī wàng}{本|běn}{是|shì}{无所谓|wú suǒ wèi}{有|yǒu}，{无所谓|wú suǒ wèi}{无|wú}{的|de}。
= Hope cannot be said to exist, nor not to exist.
{这|zhè}{正如|zhèng rú}{地上|dì shang}{的|de}{路|lù}；{其实|qí shí}{地上|dì shang}{本|běn}{没有|méi yǒu}{路|lù}，{走|zǒu}{的|de}{人|rén}{多|duō}{了|le}，{也|yě}{便|biàn}{成|chéng}{了|le}{路|lù}。
= It is just like the roads across the earth: in fact there were no roads to begin with, but when many people walk the same way, a road comes into being.
```

## Key points

- {鲁迅|Lǔ Xùn} (1881–1936), born {周树人|Zhōu Shù rén} in {绍兴|Shào xīng}; studied medicine in Japan, then wrote; 《{狂人日记|Kuáng rén Rì jì}》 (1918), 《{呐喊|Nà hǎn}》 (1923).
- 《{故乡|gù xiāng}》 (1921): a man returns to move his family away and meets his childhood friend {闰土|Rùn tǔ}, who greets him
  as {老爷|lǎo ye}; the friendship of their sons gives him hope.
- The closing lines: {希望|xī wàng}{本|běn}{是|shì}{无所谓|wú suǒ wèi}{有|yǒu}，{无所谓|wú suǒ wèi}{无|wú}{的|de}……{走|zǒu}{的|de}{人|rén}{多|duō}{了|le}，{也|yě}{便|biàn}{成|chéng}{了|le}{路|lù}。 Older vernacular: {本|běn} (originally), {便|biàn} (= {就|jiù}),
  {正如|zhèng rú} (just as), {无所谓|wú suǒ wèi} in its literal sense.
- The story is in the public domain in China (author's life + 50 years: since 1987) and in the
  United States (published before 1931).

lessons.title: Tu Youyou and artemisinin
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

In 2015 the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went, in part, to {屠呦呦|Tú Yōu yōu} (Tú Yōuyōu, Tu Youyou), a
pharmaceutical chemist in Beijing, "for her discoveries concerning a novel therapy against Malaria".
The medicine her team found, artemisinin ({青蒿素|qīng hāo sù}), comes from a plant, and the key idea came from a
book of remedies written about 1,600 years earlier. This honors lesson tells that story: a piece of
the history of science, in the language of research and work you've met in this module ({筹备|chóu bèi}, {步骤|bù zhòu},
{进展|jìn zhǎn}, {成效|chéng xiào}, {突破|tū pò} is lesson 20's word).

This is history, not medical advice: the lesson says what was found and how, not how anyone should
be treated.

## The people and the book

- {屠呦呦|Tú Yōu yōu} was born in 1930 in {宁波|Níng bō} (Níngbō), Zhejiang. She studied pharmacy at the medical school
  of Peking University, graduating in 1955, and went to work at the Academy of Traditional Chinese
  Medicine in Beijing, studying the plants and other materials used in traditional medicines.
- {疟疾|nüè ji} (nüè ji, malaria) is a disease carried by mosquitoes; in the 1960s the usual medicine,
  chloroquine, was working less and less well, because the parasites had become resistant to it. In 1969
  {屠呦呦|Tú Yōu yōu} was asked to lead a research group searching for new malaria medicines among the remedies of
  traditional Chinese medicine.
- {葛洪|Gě Hóng} (Gě Hóng) was a writer on medicine and alchemy of the Eastern Jin dynasty (the 4th century
  CE; his dates differ between sources). His 《{肘后备急方|Zhǒu hòu Bèi jí Fāng}》 (Zhǒu hòu bèi jí fāng, roughly "Emergency
  remedies to keep at hand", literally "behind the elbow", i.e. in your sleeve) collects simple
  treatments that ordinary people could use.

## The line that changed the method

The group tested hundreds of traditional remedies. An extract of {青蒿|qīng hāo} (qīng hāo, sweet wormwood,
*Artemisia annua*) sometimes worked against malaria in mice and sometimes didn't. Reading old texts
again, {屠呦呦|Tú Yōu yōu} stopped at this line in {葛洪|Gě Hóng}'s book:

> {青蒿|qīng hāo}{一握|yí wò}，{以|yǐ}{水|shuǐ}{二|èr}{升|shēng}{渍|zì}，{绞|jiǎo}{取汁|qǔ zhī}，{尽|jìn}{服|fú}{之|zhī}。

Notes:

- {一握|yí wò} (yí wò): a handful ({握|wò}, to grip).
- {以|yǐ}{水|shuǐ}{二|èr}{升|shēng} ({以|yǐ}, HSK 5's written "with"; {升|shēng}, lesson 12's "litre", here an old measure, much smaller than
  a litre: measuring vessels of the Han dynasty hold about 200 ml): with two *sheng* of water.
- {渍|zì} (zì): to soak.
- {绞|jiǎo} (jiǎo): to wring, twist. {取汁|qǔ zhī} (qǔ zhī): to take the juice.
- {尽|jìn} (lesson 05's word): all, completely. {服|fú} (lesson 08's {服用|fú yòng} is "to take medicine"): to take. {之|zhī}: it (HSK 4's
  structural {之|zhī}, here the classical object "it").

A paraphrase: {拿|ná}{一|yì}{把|bǎ}{青蒿|qīng hāo}，{用|yòng}{两|liǎng}{升|shēng}{水|shuǐ}{泡|pào}{一|yi}{泡|pào}，{把|bǎ}{它|tā}{拧|nǐng}{出|chū}{汁|zhī}{来|lái}，{全部|quán bù}{喝|hē}{下去|xià qù}。

Our translation: "Take a handful of sweet wormwood, soak it in two *sheng* of water, wring out the
juice and drink it all."

What struck her was what the recipe *doesn't* do: it doesn't boil the plant, as most traditional
remedies are boiled. She thought heat might be destroying whatever made the plant work, and in her
own words the extraction "might need to avoid high temperatures" ({提取|tí qǔ}{过程|guò chéng}{可能|kě néng}{需要|xū yào}{避免|bì miǎn}{高温|gāo wēn}). The group
switched to a solvent that boils at a low temperature (ether), and the results changed.

## Reading: from an old book to a new medicine

> {从|cóng}{一|yì}{本|běn}{古|gǔ}{书|shū}{到|dào}{一|yì}{种|zhǒng}{新|xīn}{药|yào}
>
> {疟疾|nüè ji}{是|shì}{一|yì}{种|zhǒng}{很|hěn}{古老|gǔ lǎo}{的|de}{传染病|chuán rǎn bìng}，{主要|zhǔ yào}{通过|tōng guò}{蚊子|wén zi}{传播|chuán bō}。{二十世纪六十年代|èr shí shì jì liù shí nián dài}，{原来|yuán lái}{用来|yòng lái}{治疗|zhì liáo}{疟疾|nüè ji}{的|de}{药|yào}{效果|xiào guǒ}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{差|chà}，{世界|shì jiè}{各地|gè dì}{都|dōu}{迫切|pò qiè}{需要|xū yào}{新|xīn}{的|de}{药物|yào wù}。{一九六九|yī jiǔ liù jiǔ}{年|nián}，{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{中医研究院|Zhōng yī yán jiū yuàn}{工作|gōng zuò}{的|de}{屠呦呦|Tú Yōu yōu}{被|bèi}{任命|rèn mìng}{为|wéi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{研究|yán jiū}{小组|xiǎo zǔ}{的|de}{组长|zǔ zhǎng}，{任务|rèn wu}{是|shì}{从|cóng}{传统|chuán tǒng}{中药|zhōng yào}{里|lǐ}{寻找|xún zhǎo}{治疗|zhì liáo}{疟疾|nüè ji}{的|de}{新|xīn}{药|yào}。

Words to know: {疟疾|nüè ji} (nüè ji): malaria. {蚊子|wén zi} (wén zi): mosquito. {传染病|chuán rǎn bìng} (lesson 08's word): infectious disease. {传播|chuán bō} (HSK 5): to spread. {二十世纪六十年代|èr shí shì jì liù shí nián dài}:
the 1960s. {治疗|zhì liáo} (HSK 5): to treat. {药物|yào wù}: medicines. {中医研究院|Zhōng yī yán jiū yuàn}: the Academy of Traditional Chinese Medicine
({中医|zhōng yī}, traditional Chinese medicine). {被|bèi}{任命|rèn mìng}{为|wéi} (rèn mìng): to be appointed as. {组长|zǔ zhǎng}: group leader. {艰难|jiān nán} (lesson 19's word): hard, difficult. {中药|zhōng yào}:
traditional Chinese medicines. {查阅|chá yuè} (chá yuè): to look through (books). {请教|qǐng jiào} (HSK 5): to consult. {老中医|lǎo zhōng yī}: an experienced doctor of
Chinese medicine. {药方|yào fāng}: a prescription, recipe. {实验|shí yàn} (HSK 5): experiment. {提取物|tí qǔ wù} ({提取|tí qǔ}, lesson 16's word:
to extract): extract. {小白鼠|xiǎo bái shǔ}: laboratory mouse. {检验|jiǎn yàn} (lesson 20's word): to test. {理想|lǐ xiǎng} (HSK 4): satisfactory,
ideal. {煮|zhǔ} (HSK 5): to boil. {古人|gǔ rén} (lesson 15's word): people of old. {泡|pào} (lesson 12's word): to soak. {拧|nǐng} (nǐng): to wring. {高温|gāo wēn}: high temperature. {破坏|pò huài} (HSK 5): to destroy. {有效成分|yǒu xiào chéng fèn}
(chéng fèn): active ingredient. {沸点|fèi diǎn} (fèi diǎn): boiling point. {乙醚|yǐ mí} (yǐ mí): ether. {编号|biān hào}: serial number.
{突破|tū pò} (lesson 20's word): breakthrough. {分离|fēn lí} (HSK 5): to separate. {物质|wù zhì} (HSK 5): substance. {命名|mìng míng} (lesson 28's
word): to name. {复合药物|fù hé yào wù}: combination medicines. {广泛|guǎng fàn} (HSK 5): wide. {数以亿计|shù yǐ yì jì} (shù yǐ yì jì): in the hundreds of
millions. {诺贝尔|Nuò bèi ěr}: Nobel. {生理学或医学奖|shēng lǐ xué huò yī xué jiǎng}: the Prize in Physiology or Medicine. {获奖演讲|huò jiǎng yǎn jiǎng}: prize lecture. {无私|wú sī} (wú sī): selfless. {贡献|gòng xiàn} (HSK 5): to contribute. {成果|chéng guǒ}
(HSK 5): achievement. {团队|tuán duì} (HSK 5): team. {藏|cáng} (cáng, HSK 5): to hide. {宝贵|bǎo guì} (HSK 5): precious. {本身|běn shēn} (lesson 27's word): itself. {田|tián} (lesson 06's word): field. {线索|xiàn suǒ} (lesson 10's
word): clue.

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

"From an old book to a new medicine. Malaria is a very old infectious disease, spread mainly by
mosquitoes. In the 1960s the medicines then used to treat it were working less and less well, and the
whole world urgently needed new ones. In 1969 Tu Youyou, who worked at the Academy of Traditional
Chinese Medicine in Beijing, was appointed head of a research group whose task was to look for new
malaria medicines among traditional Chinese remedies. The early stage of the work was very hard. Tu
and her colleagues first read through large numbers of old medical books and consulted many
experienced doctors of Chinese medicine, writing down one by one every recipe that might be useful:
over two thousand in all. The next step was experiments: the medicines were made into extracts and tested on mice.
After many had been tried, none of the results was satisfactory. The extract of sweet
wormwood sometimes worked and sometimes didn't, and the research was stuck. How could they get out of
it? Tu opened the old books again. In Ge Hong's Emergency Remedies, written in the Eastern Jin, she
read this sentence: 'Take a handful of sweet wormwood, soak it in two sheng of water, wring out the
juice and drink it all.' She noticed that the ancient method wasn't the usual boiling of medicine,
but soaking in cold water and then wringing the juice out. Perhaps, she thought, it was the high
temperature that destroyed the active ingredient in the plant. So she switched to ether, which has a
lower boiling point, to make the extract. On 4 October 1971, the ether extract of sweet wormwood
numbered 191 was 100 % effective in mice. It was a crucial breakthrough. The next year the group
isolated a new substance from the plant, later named artemisinin. From taking on the task to obtaining artemisinin took a little over three
years in all. Sweet wormwood itself is a very ordinary plant, growing by roads and fields in many
parts of China, and no one had imagined it held such a precious substance. Turning the discovery into a
usable medicine took many more years. In the decades since, artemisinin and combination medicines
made with it have been used widely around the world, treating hundreds of millions of patients. In
2015, at eighty-four, Tu Youyou received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, the first Chinese
scientist to win that prize. In her prize lecture she said that artemisinin was a
gift from traditional Chinese medicine to the people of the world. She also said that without everyone's
selfless teamwork, artemisinin could not have been given to the world in so short a time. Tu Youyou's story shows that the
experience of earlier people may hide valuable clues, but a real discovery still has to be tested,
step by step, with the methods of modern science."
</details>

## Words for research

The reading uses the vocabulary of a research project, much of it the management words of lesson 03:

| Stage | Words |
|---|---|
| Planning | {任务|rèn wu} (task), {前期|qián qī} (early stage), {步骤|bù zhòu} (step), {计划|jì huà} |
| Searching | {查阅|chá yuè} (to look through), {寻找|xún zhǎo} / {寻求|xún qiú} (to seek), {记录|jì lù} (to record) |
| Testing | {实验|shí yàn} (experiment), {检验|jiǎn yàn} (to test), {效果|xiào guǒ} / {成效|chéng xiào} (result), {理想|lǐ xiǎng} (satisfactory) |
| Difficulty | {艰难|jiān nán} (hard), {陷入|xiàn rù}{困境|kùn jìng} (to get stuck), {摆脱|bǎi tuō}{困境|kùn jìng} (to get out of it) |
| Success | {突破|tū pò} (breakthrough), {发现|fā xiàn} (discovery), {成果|chéng guǒ} (achievement) |

## Key points

- {屠呦呦|Tú Yōu yōu} (born 1930, {宁波|Níng bō}) led, from 1969, a group looking for malaria medicines in traditional remedies;
  in 1971 an ether extract of {青蒿|qīng hāo} worked in mice; in 1972 the group isolated {青蒿素|qīng hāo sù} (artemisinin).
- The idea: {葛洪|Gě Hóng} (Eastern Jin, 4th century), 《{肘后备急方|Zhǒu hòu Bèi jí Fāng}》: {青蒿|qīng hāo}{一握|yí wò}，{以|yǐ}{水|shuǐ}{二|èr}{升|shēng}{渍|zì}，{绞|jiǎo}{取汁|qǔ zhī}，{尽|jìn}{服|fú}{之|zhī} (soak, wring, drink:
  no boiling), which suggested avoiding heat.
- 2015 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (half the prize; the other half went to William C.
  Campbell and Satoshi Ōmura for a treatment against roundworm parasites).
- The language of research: {前期|qián qī}, {步骤|bù zhòu}, {实验|shí yàn}, {检验|jiǎn yàn}, {陷入|xiàn rù}{困境|kùn jìng}, {摆脱|bǎi tuō}, {突破|tū pò}, {成果|chéng guǒ}.

lessons.title: Ageing, care and the countryside
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 2 is about society today: how people grow old, where they live, how they keep well, the
rules they live by and the news they read. It starts in the countryside. {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang), who now
writes commentary for the news website, goes to a village three hours from Beijing where most of the
young people have left for the cities, and talks to the people who stayed.

The grammar is small; the vocabulary is large:

- {日益|rì yì} (increasingly, day by day), the written partner of {越来越|yuè lái yuè}, and how it changes the register of
  a sentence;
- {往年|wǎng nián} (in former years, in an ordinary year) beside {过去|guò qù}, {以前|yǐ qián} and {今年|jīn nián};
- the words of ageing and care ({养老|yǎng lǎo}, {寿命|shòu mìng}, {关爱|guān ài}, {保障|bǎo zhàng}, {补贴|bǔ tiē}…), of disability ({残疾|cán jí}, {盲人|máng rén}, {轮椅|lún yǐ}, {障碍|zhàng ài}), and
  of the village and its fields ({农田|nóng tián}, {庄稼|zhuāng jia}, {水稻|shuǐ dào}, {小麦|xiǎo mài}, {播种|bō zhǒng}, {土壤|tǔ rǎng}…).

The lesson describes; it doesn't argue for or against any policy. The level's list also has the word
{自杀|zì shā} (zìshā, suicide). It's taught here as a word, in the vocabulary only; it doesn't appear in the
texts.

## {日益|rì yì}: increasingly, day by day

{日益|rì yì} (rìyì) is "more and more, day by day": {日|rì} (day) + {益|yì} (to increase; HSK 5's {有益|yǒu yì}, "beneficial").
It says a change keeps growing, and it belongs to writing: reports, news, essays, speeches. In speech
the same idea is {越来越|yuè lái yuè}.

| Spoken | Written |
|---|---|
| {村|cūn}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{老人|lǎo rén}{越来越|yuè lái yuè}{多|duō}{了|le}。 | {村|cūn}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{老年|lǎo nián}{人口|rén kǒu}{日益|rì yì}{增加|zēng jiā}。 |
| {这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{越来越|yuè lái yuè}{严重|yán zhòng}{了|le}。 | {这|zhè}{一|yí}{问题|wèn tí}{日益|rì yì}{严重|yán zhòng}。 |
| {她|tā}{的|de}{身体|shēn tǐ}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{差|chà}。 | {她|tā}{的|de}{身体|shēn tǐ}{日益|rì yì}{衰弱|shuāi ruò}。 |
| {大家|dà jiā}{越来越|yuè lái yuè}{重视|zhòng shì}{养老|yǎng lǎo}。 | {养老|yǎng lǎo}{问题|wèn tí}{日益|rì yì}{受到|shòu dào}{重视|zhòng shì}。 |

{衰弱|shuāi ruò} (shuāiruò): weak, frail (from {衰老|shuāi lǎo}, ageing, and {弱|ruò}, weak).

Two rules:

- {日益|rì yì} goes straight before a verb or adjective of *two syllables*: {日益|rì yì}{增加|zēng jiā}, {日益|rì yì}{严重|yán zhòng}, {日益|rì yì}{明显|míng xiǎn}, {日益|rì yì}{重要|zhòng yào},
  {日益|rì yì}{富裕|fù yù}. With a one-syllable word it doesn't work: not ~~{日益|rì yì}{多|duō}~~, but {日益|rì yì}{增加|zēng jiā} or (spoken) {越来越|yuè lái yuè}{多|duō}.
- It takes no degree word, since the change is already in {日益|rì yì}: not ~~{日益|rì yì}{很|hěn}{严重|yán zhòng}~~. A short clause with
  {日益|rì yì} usually ends without {了|le}: {问题|wèn tí}{日益|rì yì}{严重|yán zhòng}。 ({问题|wèn tí}{日益|rì yì}{严重|yán zhòng}{了|le} sounds odd.)

{日益|rì yì} often comes in pairs in a news paragraph: {城市|chéng shì}{日益|rì yì}{扩大|kuò dà}，{农村|nóng cūn}{人口|rén kǒu}{日益|rì yì}{减少|jiǎn shǎo} (cities keep growing, and the
village population keeps falling). As an attributive with {的|de}: {日益|rì yì}{增长|zēng zhǎng}{的|de}{需要|xū yào} (growing
needs).

## {往年|wǎng nián}: in former years

{往年|wǎng nián} (wǎngnián) is "former years", and also "an ordinary year, the years before this one". It's a time
noun, so it goes where {去年|qù nián} and {今年|jīn nián} go: before the verb, or after {比|bǐ} and {跟|gēn}.

{往年|wǎng nián}{这个|zhè ge}{时候|shí hou}，{田|tián}{里|lǐ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{开始|kāi shǐ}{割|gē}{小麦|xiǎo mài}{了|le}。 — By this time in other years, they'd already have started cutting the wheat.

{今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{雨|yǔ}{比|bǐ}{往年|wǎng nián}{少|shǎo}。 — There's been less rain this year than usual.

{跟|gēn}{往年|wǎng nián}{一样|yí yàng}，{春节|Chūn jié}{以后|yǐ hòu}{年轻人|nián qīng rén}{都|dōu}{出去|chū qù}{打工|dǎ gōng}{了|le}。 — As every year, the young people went off to work after the Spring Festival.

Compare {过去|guò qù} (in the past, generally), {以前|yǐ qián} (before, formerly: {以前|yǐ qián}{这里|zhè lǐ}{是|shì}{一|yí}{片|piàn}{农田|nóng tián}) and {往年|wǎng nián}, which always
compares one year with the ones before. {往年|wǎng nián} is neutral in register: both spoken and written.

## Words: growing old

{养老|yǎng lǎo} (yǎnglǎo) is to provide for old age, to live out one's old age: {养老|yǎng lǎo}{问题|wèn tí} (the question of care in old
age), {在|zài}{家|jiā}{养老|yǎng lǎo} (to spend one's old age at home). {养老院|yǎng lǎo yuàn} is a care home for the elderly, {老太太|lǎo tài tai} an old lady (a
friendly, spoken word; politely, to her face, {奶奶|nǎi nai} or {阿姨|ā yí}). {岁数|suì shu} (suìshu, spoken) is a person's age, mostly
of older people: {您|nín}{多|duō}{大|dà}{岁数|suì shu}{了|le}？ (how old are you, may I ask?); {年纪|nián jì} (HSK 5) is the same.

{寿命|shòu mìng} (shòumìng) is lifespan, also of things ({手机|shǒu jī}{的|de}{寿命|shòu mìng} the life of a phone); {长寿|cháng shòu} (chángshòu) is long-lived,
and as a noun longevity: {祝|zhù}{您|nín}{健康|jiàn kāng}{长寿|cháng shòu}！ (wishing you good health and a long life, said at an old person's
birthday). {衰老|shuāi lǎo} (shuāilǎo) is to age, ageing: {衰老|shuāi lǎo}{是|shì}{自然|zì rán}{的|de}{过程|guò chéng} (ageing is a natural process).

The body: {骨头|gǔ tou} (gǔtou, with a light second syllable) is a bone; {颈椎|jǐng zhuī} (jǐngzhuī) the vertebrae of the neck, and in everyday talk
"the neck" when it aches: {颈椎|jǐng zhuī}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}, {颈椎|jǐng zhuī}{病|bìng} (neck trouble, common among office workers). {保健|bǎo jiàn} (bǎojiàn) is health
care, keeping fit: {保健|bǎo jiàn}{知识|zhī shi} (health tips), {保健|bǎo jiàn}{品|pǐn} (health supplements). {按摩|àn mó} (ànmó) is massage, to massage:
{给|gěi}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{按摩|àn mó}{肩膀|jiān bǎng} (to massage Grandma's shoulders; {肩膀|jiān bǎng} is lesson 08's word).

## Words: care and support

Two words for caring, both a little formal: {关爱|guān ài} (guān'ài: care and love, often for children, the old,
the sick) and {关怀|guān huái} (guānhuái: warm concern, often from above: a school for its students, a community for
its old people). {关心|guān xīn} (HSK 3) is the everyday word.

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {互助|hù zhù} (hùzhù) | mutual help | {老人|lǎo rén}{们|men}{成立|chéng lì}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{互助|hù zhù}{小组|xiǎo zǔ}。 The old people have set up a mutual-help group. |
| {救助|jiù zhù} (jiùzhù) | to help people in need, aid | {救助|jiù zhù}{贫困|pín kùn}{家庭|jiā tíng} to help poor families |
| {求助|qiú zhù} (qiúzhù) | to ask for help | {遇到|yù dào}{困难|kùn nan}，{可以|kě yǐ}{向|xiàng}{社区|shè qū}{求助|qiú zhù}。 If you're in difficulty, you can ask the community for help. |
| {保障|bǎo zhàng} (bǎozhàng) | to guarantee, safeguard; a guarantee | {保障|bǎo zhàng}{老人|lǎo rén}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó} to safeguard old people's livelihood; {医疗|yī liáo}{保障|bǎo zhàng} health cover |
| {补贴|bǔ tiē} (bǔtiē) | an allowance, a subsidy; to subsidise | {交通|jiāo tōng}{补贴|bǔ tiē} a travel allowance |
| {发放|fā fàng} (fāfàng) | to issue, hand out (money, things, formally) | {发放|fā fàng}{补贴|bǔ tiē} to pay out an allowance |
| {政策|zhèng cè} (zhèngcè) | policy | {公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{新|xīn}{政策|zhèng cè} the company's new policy |
| {自愿|zì yuàn} (zìyuàn) | voluntary, of one's own accord | {自愿|zì yuàn}{参加|cān jiā} to take part voluntarily |
| {依赖|yī lài} (yīlài) | to depend on, rely on (often too much) | {不|bù}{能|néng}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{依赖|yī lài}{父母|fù mǔ}。 You can't rely on your parents for everything. |

{政策|zhèng cè} is any organisation's policy: a company's, a school's, a city's. In this course it's described, not
judged: {按照|àn zhào}{学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{政策|zhèng cè}，{学生|xué sheng}{可以|kě yǐ}… (under the school's policy, students may…).

Hardship and well-being: {贫困|pín kùn} (pínkùn) is poor, poverty (written; {穷|qióng} is the spoken word); {富裕|fù yù} (fùyù) is
well-off, prosperous; {人均|rén jūn} (rénjūn) is per head, per person: {人均|rén jūn}{收入|shōu rù} (income per head). {劳动力|láo dòng lì} (láodònglì) is
the labour force, the people who can work; {流动|liú dòng} (liúdòng) is to flow, to move about: {人口|rén kǒu}{流动|liú dòng} (people moving
from place to place); {剩余|shèng yú} (shèngyú) is remaining, left over: {剩余|shèng yú}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān} (the time that's left). {丧失|sàng shī} (sàngshī)
is to lose (an ability, a chance, formally): {丧失|sàng shī}{劳动|láo dòng}{能力|néng lì} (to lose the ability to work).

Disability: {残疾|cán jí} (cánjí) is disability, disabled: {残疾|cán jí}{人|rén} (a disabled person); {盲人|máng rén} (mángrén) a blind person;
{轮椅|lún yǐ} (lúnyǐ) a wheelchair ({轮|lún} wheel + {椅|yǐ} chair); {障碍|zhàng ài} (zhàng'ài) an obstacle, a barrier. With the prefix {无|wú}-
(without) it makes a word you'll see on signs: {无障碍|wú zhàng ài}{通道|tōng dào} (a barrier-free entrance, a ramp). {健全|jiàn quán} (jiànquán)
is sound, complete, in good working order: {身体|shēn tǐ}{健全|jiàn quán} (able-bodied), {健全|jiàn quán}{的|de}{制度|zhì dù} (a sound system).

Feelings: {孤独|gū dú} (gūdú) is lonely, alone (a state, often lasting); {寂寞|jì mò} (jìmò) is lonely, missing company (a
feeling, often for a while). {可怜|kě lián} (kělián) is pitiful, poor (thing): {这|zhè}{只|zhī}{小|xiǎo}{猫|māo}{真|zhēn}{可怜|kě lián}。 {家园|jiā yuán} (jiāyuán) is one's
home, homeland, with feeling: {保护|bǎo hù}{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{家园|jiā yuán} (protect our home, the earth or a village).

Six differ in traditional: 殘 (12 strokes, with 戔), 壽 (14), 頸 (16, with 巠 and 頁), 憐 (15, with
粦), 貧 (11, with 貝) and 喪 (12). The lesson's words also use seven characters that lesson 07 teaches:
{庄|zhuāng} and {稼|jià} ({庄稼|zhuāng jia}), {衰|shuāi} ({衰老|shuāi lǎo}), {赖|lài} ({依赖|yī lài}), {麦|mài} ({小麦|xiǎo mài}), {碍|ài} ({障碍|zhàng ài}) and {杀|shā} ({自杀|zì shā}).

### A new radical: 歹

歹 (dǎi) is a radical you meet in four characters of levels 1–6: {死|sǐ} (to die, HSK 4), {殊|shū} ({特殊|tè shū}, special,
HSK 5), {残|cán} (here) and {殖|zhí} ({繁殖|fán zhí}, to breed, lesson 18). In {死|sǐ} and {残|cán} it goes with death and harm; in {殊|shū} and {殖|zhí}
it gives no clear meaning any more. It has four strokes: a horizontal, a left-falling stroke, a
horizontal-turning stroke (横撇), and a dot.

### Sound parts across the levels

- 莫 mò in {寞|mò} mò, and in {摸|mō} mō (HSK 5) and {模|mó} mó ({模特儿|mó tèr}, lesson 11; múyàng in {模样|mú yàng}, lesson 22).
- {令|lìng} lìng in {怜|lián} lián, as in {领|lǐng} lǐng, {零|líng} líng, {铃|líng} líng, {冷|lěng} lěng, {邻|lín} lín, {龄|líng} líng: all l- syllables. Traditional
  writes {怜|lián} and {邻|lín} with 粦 instead (憐, 鄰).
- {亡|wáng} wáng in {盲|máng} máng, as in {忙|máng} máng, {忘|wàng} wàng, {望|wàng} wàng ({亡|wáng} is in lesson 19's {死亡|sǐ wáng}, death).
- 隹 zhuī in {椎|zhuī} zhuī (an exact match), and drifted in {谁|shéi} shéi, {推|tuī} tuī, {准|zhǔn} zhǔn, {维|wéi} wéi, {堆|duī} duī.
- {颈|jǐng} jǐng has on its left the part that is the right side of {经|jīng} jīng, {轻|qīng} qīng and {径|jìng} jìng (lesson 26) and the left side of {劲|jìn} jìn (lesson 29); in
  traditional it's 巠 in all of them.
- {章|zhāng} zhāng in {障|zhàng} zhàng (阝 + {章|zhāng}). {麻|má} má in {摩|mó} mó ({麻|má} over {手|shǒu}), as in {嘛|ma} ma (lesson 23).
- 谷 gǔ in {裕|yù} yù (衤 + 谷), with {浴|yù} yù (lesson 08) and {欲|yù} yù (lesson 12): the three share yù, which
  isn't 谷's own sound.
- {寿|shòu} shòu is the sound part of {筹|chóu} chóu ({筹备|chóu bèi}, lesson 03), the sound drifted; traditional 籌 has 壽.
- {害|hài} hài is in {割|gē} gē ({害|hài} + 刂, a knife), the sound drifted; {分|fēn} fēn in {贫|pín} pín ({分|fēn} over {贝|bèi}, money), drifted
  too.
- {叔|shū} shū in {寂|jì} jì, as in {督|dū} dū ({监督|jiān dū}, lesson 03): a drifted series.
- 舀 yǎo in {稻|dào} dào (禾 + 舀); 襄 xiāng in {壤|rǎng} rǎng (traditional 讓 ràng, "to let", has it too).

### Look-alikes and stroke traps

- {孤|gū} has {瓜|guā} (guā, melon) on the right: write {子|zi} first, then {瓜|guā}, which ends with a dot and a right-falling
  stroke.

"Stone Bridge village lies below a small hill, forty-odd kilometres from the county town. The soil here is
very fertile. Thirty years ago all three hundred-odd households in the village lived by farming: they sowed
wheat in the autumn, cut it the next summer, then planted maize. In those days the village had plenty of
hands, and the fields were full of people.

Later, more and more young people went to work in the cities. People moving brought the village an
income: today villagers' income per head is much higher than in earlier years, most families are no
longer poor, and some are quite well off. On the other hand, the number of old people keeps growing. Of
the four hundred or so people now living in the village, more than half are over sixty. Old people now
live much longer than they used to, and people in their eighties are not rare. Some are still fit and
work in the fields; others can no longer work and depend on others entirely in daily life. Much of the
farmland has been rented to people from elsewhere, and some of the rest simply lies empty.

The old people's greatest difficulty isn't food or clothing but loneliness. Grandma Qin, seventy-eight,
lives alone; her son's family is in the south and comes back only once a year. 'The daytime's all right.
What I dread is the night,' she says. 'It's so quiet in the house I can hear my own heart beating.'

So that the old people would no longer be lonely, the village doctor, Wei Gang, set up a 'mutual-help
group for old people' three years ago. Its members all joined of their own accord: the healthy look after
the frail, and the younger ones buy medicine and cook for the older. An old man with a disability, in a
wheelchair, told the reporter that it used to be very hard for him to get out; now someone pushes him to
the village entrance every day to sit in the sun.

The town is doing some things too. Under the present policy, people over eighty receive an allowance every
month, paid out by the village committee. Last year the town also built a care home, and some old people
in poor health, with no children nearby, have chosen to move in.

But allowances and care homes can't solve every problem. Dr Wei says ageing is a natural process: besides
health cover, old people need their families' love. 'Many old people won't ask for help even when they're
ill, for fear of putting their children to trouble,' he says. 'In fact, a phone call or a visit home is
the best care there is.'

When I left Stone Bridge village it was already dark. Under the lamp at the village entrance, a few old
people were still sitting and chatting. People often say that old age needs families and society to work
together. In Stone Bridge village, that isn't empty words: it's everyday life."
</details>

"I don't think there's one right answer to this: it depends on the old person's situation and wishes. On
the one hand, growing old at home has many advantages. Old people are attached to their homes, they have
neighbours they know around them, and they don't have to change their habits. Take my grandmother: she's
lived in one place for over fifty years, and if you made her move she'd certainly feel out of place, even
lonely. On the other hand, care homes have their advantages too. If an old person's health is poor and
their children aren't nearby, a care home has doctors and nurses who can look after them at any time,
which is much safer than being alone at home. And there are many people of the same age there, so they
can do things together and may even be less lonely. So I think the most important thing is to respect the
old person's own choice. Those still in good health can grow old at home, and their children should visit
often; if those who need care choose to go into a care home, their families should support them and visit
them often. Wherever they live, what old people need most is their families' love."

## Pronunciation

- {骨头|gǔ tou} gǔtou and {岁数|suì shu} suìshu end on a light syllable; so does {庄稼|zhuāng jia} zhuāngjia (zhuāng jia, not jià).
- 种: zhòng in {种地|zhòng dì} (to plant), zhǒng in {播种|bō zhǒng} (a seed) and {一|yì}{种|zhǒng} (a kind).
- {丧失|sàng shī} sàngshī: fourth tone. (The same character is sāng in the funeral word {丧事|sāng shì}, which isn't a course
  word.)
- {残疾|cán jí} cánjí: two rising tones. {寂寞|jì mò} jìmò: two falling tones.
- {障碍|zhàng ài} zhàng'ài: the apostrophe marks the syllable break before a.
- {长寿|cháng shòu} chángshòu: {长|cháng} is cháng (long), not zhǎng (to grow).

## Common mistakes

- ~~{日益|rì yì}{多|duō}~~: {日益|rì yì} wants a two-syllable verb or adjective: {日益|rì yì}{增加|zēng jiā}, {日益|rì yì}{严重|yán zhòng}. In speech, {越来越|yuè lái yuè}{多|duō}.
- ~~{日益|rì yì}{很|hěn}{严重|yán zhòng}~~: no degree word with {日益|rì yì}. A short clause with {日益|rì yì} usually ends without {了|le} ({问题|wèn tí}{日益|rì yì}{严重|yán zhòng}。).
- {日益|rì yì} in a chat sounds like a newsreader. To a friend, say {越来越|yuè lái yuè} or {一|yì}{天|tiān}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{天|tiān}.
- {往年|wǎng nián} is "other years, usual years", not "next year" ({明年|míng nián}) or "the year before last" ({前年|qián nián}): {今年|jīn nián}{比|bǐ}{往年|wǎng nián}{冷|lěng} is
  "colder this year than usual".
- {孤独|gū dú} and {寂寞|jì mò}: {他|tā}{是|shì}{个|gè}{孤独|gū dú}{的|de}{人|rén} (a solitary person, a lasting state) is more natural than {他|tā}{是|shì}{个|gè}{寂寞|jì mò}{的|de}{人|rén};
  for a passing feeling, {一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{寂寞|jì mò}.
- {关怀|guān huái} is warm and a little formal: {公司|gōng sī}{对|duì}{员工|yuán gōng}{的|de}{关怀|guān huái} (a company's care for its staff). Of a friend, say {关心|guān xīn}.

- New characters: {残|cán} {摩|mó} {障|zhàng} {寿|shòu} {沃|wò} {骨|gǔ} {割|gē} {裕|yù} {孤|gū} {颈|jǐng} {椎|zhuī} {寂|jì} {寞|mò} {怜|lián} {盲|máng} {田|tián} {贫|pín} {丧|sàng} {稻|dào} {壤|rǎng} (✎ {寿|shòu} {沃|wò} {骨|gǔ} {孤|gū} {盲|máng} {贫|pín} {丧|sàng}); a new radical, {=歹=}.
