the lesson.

lessons.title: City life and housing
topics: 东一A，西一A and 左A右B
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

From the village to the city. {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) and {李明|Lǐ Míng} (Li Ming), now back in Beijing from Britain,
are looking for a flat of their own, which means {安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) needs a new flatmate for the {新城|Xīn chéng} flat. The
lesson's reading is about an old housing compound brought back to life.

- Two **[[colloquial formats]]**, frames with slots that speech fills: {东|dōng}{一|yī}A，{西|xī}{一|yī}A (here a…, there a…:
  scattered, all over the place) and {左|zuǒ}A{右|yòu}B (again and again: {左思右想|zuǒ sī yòu xiǎng}, {左|zuǒ}{看|kàn}{右|yòu}{看|kàn});
- the measure words {栋|dòng} (buildings), {户|hù} (households), {扇|shàn} (doors and windows), and the verb {支|zhī} (to prop
  up, set up);
- {地方|dì fāng} dìfāng "local", beside HSK 3's {地方|dì fang} dìfang "place";
- the words of the city: its streets, buildings, flats, traffic and pace of life.

The colloquial formats of the level are collected on the reference sheet (colloquial formats).

## {东|dōng}{一|yī}A，{西|xī}{一|yī}A: here a…, there a…

{东|dōng}{一|yī} + measure word (+ noun), {西|xī}{一|yī} + the same measure word: things are scattered about with no order. {东|dōng} and
{西|xī} don't mean east and west here, only "this side… that side…".

{楼道|lóu dào}{里|lǐ}{东|dōng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{箱子|xiāng zi}，{西|xī}{一|yí}{辆|liàng}{自行车|zì xíng chē}，{走|zǒu}{都|dōu}{走|zǒu}{不|bu}{过去|guò qù}。 — There are boxes here and bikes there in the stairwell: you can hardly get through.

{他|tā}{的|de}{书|shū}{东|dōng}{一|yì}{本|běn}，{西|xī}{一|yì}{本|běn}，{到处|dào chù}{都|dōu}{是|shì}。 — His books are here, there and everywhere.

A verbal measure word works too: {他|tā}{东|dōng}{一|yí}{句|jù}，{西|xī}{一|yí}{句|jù}，{说|shuō}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}{也|yě}{没|méi}{说|shuō}{清楚|qīng chu}。 (He said a bit about this, a bit
about that, and after all that time still hadn't made it clear.) {东|dōng}{一下|yí xià}，{西|xī}{一下|yí xià} is doing something in fits and
starts.

The format is spoken and descriptive, and nearly always a complaint about mess or disorder. It's two
short clauses with a comma, the same measure word in both; the noun can be left out of the second ({东|dōng}{一|yí}
{块|kuài}，{西|xī}{一|yí}{块|kuài} bits all over the place). Not ~~{东|dōng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{箱子|xiāng zi}，{西|xī}{一|yí}{辆|liàng}{箱子|xiāng zi}~~: the measure word repeats, the nouns may
differ.

## {左|zuǒ}A{右|yòu}B: again and again

{左|zuǒ} + verb + {右|yòu} + a verb of the same meaning (or the same verb): an action done over and over, usually
before a result or a decision, often with a sense of effort.

| Format | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {左思右想|zuǒ sī yòu xiǎng} | to think it over and over | {他|tā}{左思右想|zuǒ sī yòu xiǎng}，{还是|hái shi}{决定|jué dìng}{搬家|bān jiā}。 He thought it over and over and still decided to move. |
| {左|zuǒ}{看|kàn}{右|yòu}{看|kàn} | to look again and again | {她|tā}{左|zuǒ}{看|kàn}{右|yòu}{看|kàn}，{也|yě}{没|méi}{发现|fā xiàn}{什么|shén me}{问题|wèn tí}。 She looked and looked but found nothing wrong. |
| {左|zuǒ}{等|děng}{右|yòu}{等|děng} | to wait and wait | {我|wǒ}{左|zuǒ}{等|děng}{右|yòu}{等|děng}，{他|tā}{就是|jiù shì}{不|bù}{来|lái}。 I waited and waited, but he just didn't come. |
| {左|zuǒ}{挑|tiāo}{右|yòu}{选|xuǎn} | to pick and choose | {我们|wǒ men}{左|zuǒ}{挑|tiāo}{右|yòu}{选|xuǎn}，{最后|zuì hòu}{选|xuǎn}{了|le}{这|zhè}{套|tào}{房子|fáng zi}。 We picked and chose and finally settled on this flat. |

{思|sī} and {想|xiǎng}, {挑|tiāo} and {选|xuǎn} are near-synonyms; {看|kàn} and {等|děng} repeat. After {左|zuǒ}A{右|yòu}B comes the result, often with {还是|hái shi}, {也|yě},
{就是|jiù shì} or {最后|zuì hòu}. {左思右想|zuǒ sī yòu xiǎng} is a fixed phrase (also in writing); the others are spoken.

## {栋|dòng}, {户|hù}, {扇|shàn} and the verb {支|zhī}

| Measure word | For | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {栋|dòng} (dòng) | buildings | {一|yí}{栋|dòng}{楼|lóu}, {三|sān}{栋|dòng}{住宅|zhù zhái} |
| {户|hù} (hù) | households, families | {这|zhè}{栋|dòng}{楼|lóu}{住|zhù}{着|zhe}{二十|èr shí}{户|hù}{人家|rén jiā}。 Twenty families live in this building. |
| {扇|shàn} (shàn) | doors, windows, screens | {一|yí}{扇|shàn}{门|mén}, {两|liǎng}{扇|shàn}{窗户|chuāng hu} |

{栋|dòng} is the everyday measure word for a building ("{一|yí}{座|zuò}{楼|lóu}" is more written, and {座|zuò} also takes bridges and
mountains). {户|hù} counts households, often with {人家|rén jiā} (households, families: {一|yí}{户|hù}{人家|rén jiā}; not lesson 22's {人家|rén jia}, "other people") or alone ({全|quán}{村|cūn}{三百|sān bǎi}{多|duō}{户|hù});
it's also the "household" in {住户|zhù hù} (residents, households). 扇 is shàn here, not HSK 5's
shān (to fan): {一|yí}{扇|shàn}{窗|chuāng} (a window), {关|guān}{上|shàng}{那|nà}{扇|shàn}{门|mén} (shut that door).

{支|zhī} zhī as a verb is "to prop up, to set up, to put up": {在|zài}{街头|jiē tóu}{支|zhī}{起|qǐ}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{桌子|zhuō zi} (to set up a table on the street),
{用|yòng}{手|shǒu}{支|zhī}{着|zhe}{头|tóu} (propping one's head on one's hand), {把|bǎ}{窗户|chuāng hu}{支|zhī}{开|kāi} (to prop the window open). You know {支|zhī} as the
measure word for pens and songs (HSK 5: {一|yì}{支|zhī}{笔|bǐ}, {一|yì}{支|zhī}{歌|gē}); the verb is the same character and the same reading.
{支撑|zhī chēng} (to prop up, support) is lesson 20's word.

## {地方|dì fang} dìfāng: local

HSK 3's {地方|dì fang} (dìfang, with a light {方|fāng}) is "a place". {地方|dì fāng} dìfāng, with both syllables full, is "local", the
level below the nation, and is used before a noun:

- {地方|dì fāng}{特色|tè sè} (local character), {地方菜|dì fāng cài} (local dishes), {地方戏|dì fāng xì} (local opera): {地方|dì fāng}{特色|tè sè}{的|de}{小吃|xiǎo chī} (local snacks);
- {地方|dì fāng}{政府|zhèng fǔ} (local government), {中央|zhōng yāng}{和|hé}{地方|dì fāng} (central and local): neutral words of administration.

{这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{地方|dì fāng}{特色|tè sè}。 — This place has a lot of local character.

{中央|zhōng yāng} (zhōngyāng) is the centre, central: {广场|guǎng chǎng}{中央|zhōng yāng} (the middle of the square), and in administration "central"
(as in {中央|zhōng yāng} and {地方|dì fāng}).

## Words: the city and its streets

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {都市|dū shì} (dūshì) | city, metropolis (written) | {现代|xiàn dài}{都市|dū shì} a modern metropolis; 都 is dū here |
| {城镇|chéng zhèn} (chéngzhèn) | cities and towns | {城镇|chéng zhèn}{人口|rén kǒu} the urban population |
| {镇|zhèn} (zhèn) | a town | {镇|zhèn}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{医院|yī yuàn}。 There's a hospital in the town. |
| {村庄|cūn zhuāng} (cūnzhuāng) | a village (written) | {一|yí}{个|gè}{美丽|měi lì}{的|de}{村庄|cūn zhuāng} a beautiful village |
| {街头|jiē tóu} (jiētóu) | the street, street corner | {街头|jiē tóu}{小吃|xiǎo chī} street food |
| {人行道|rén xíng dào} (rénxíngdào) | the pavement | {车|chē}{不|bù}{能|néng}{停|tíng}{在|zài}{人行道|rén xíng dào}{上|shàng}。 Cars can't park on the pavement. |
| {桥梁|qiáo liáng} (qiáoliáng) | a bridge (written); a link | {河|hé}{上|shàng}{的|de}{桥梁|qiáo liáng} the bridges over the river |
| {建筑物|jiàn zhù wù} (jiànzhùwù) | a building, a structure | {城|chéng}{里|lǐ}{最|zuì}{高|gāo}{的|de}{建筑物|jiàn zhù wù} the city's tallest building |
| {景观|jǐng guān} (jǐngguān) | landscape, view; scenery made by design | {城市|chéng shì}{景观|jǐng guān} the cityscape |
| {百货|bǎi huò} (bǎihuò) | general goods; a department store ({百货|bǎi huò}{商店|shāng diàn}, {百货|bǎi huò}{大楼|dà lóu}) | {去|qù}{百货|bǎi huò}{商店|shāng diàn}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi} |
| {店铺|diàn pù} (diànpù) | a shop (written) | {街|jiē}{两|liǎng}{边|biān}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{店铺|diàn pù}。 There are shops on both sides of the street. |
| {游人|yóu rén} (yóurén) | visitors, sightseers | {公园|gōng yuán}{里|lǐ}{游人|yóu rén}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。 The park is full of visitors. |

The city at full speed: {繁忙|fán máng} (fánmáng) is busy (a place, a job: {繁忙|fán máng}{的|de}{街道|jiē dào}); {拥挤|yōng jǐ} (yōngjǐ) crowded; {密集|mì jí}
(mìjí) dense ({人口|rén kǒu}{密集|mì jí}, densely populated); {高峰|gāo fēng} (gāofēng) a peak, and in traffic the rush hour ({早晚|zǎo wǎn}{高峰|gāo fēng},
the morning and evening rush hours); {噪声|zào shēng} (zàoshēng) noise (written; {噪音|zào yīn} is common in speech); {节奏|jié zòu} (jiézòu)
rhythm, pace: {生活|shēng huó}{节奏|jié zòu} (the pace of life). {流入|liú rù} (liúrù) is to flow into: {大量|dà liàng}{人口|rén kǒu}{流入|liú rù}{城市|chéng shì} (large numbers of people
moving into the cities); {穿过|chuān guò} (chuānguò) is to go through, cross: {穿过|chuān guò}{马路|mǎ lù} (cross the road); {相连|xiāng lián} (xiānglián) to
be joined: {两|liǎng}{栋|dòng}{楼|lóu}{相连|xiāng lián} (the two buildings are joined).

Order and planning: {秩序|zhì xù} (zhìxù) is order (public order: {排队|pái duì}{守|shǒu}{秩序|zhì xù}, queue in good order); {有序|yǒu xù} (yǒuxù) orderly;
{规划|guī huà} (guīhuà) a long-term plan, to plan ({城市|chéng shì}{规划|guī huà}, town planning). The verb in it, huà, is to draw a line, to mark off ({划线|huà xiàn}, to draw a line), and
{划分|huà fēn} (huàfēn) is to divide into parts: {在|zài}{地上|dì shang}{划|huà}{一|yì}{条|tiáo}{线|xiàn} (draw a line on the ground; {线|xiàn} xiàn, a line, is lesson 20's word), {把|bǎ}{城市|chéng shì}{划分|huà fēn}{成|chéng}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{区|qū} (divide the
city into districts). HSK 5's {划|huá} is huá (to row a boat): the same character in simplified, another word (traditional writes
huà {+劃+} and huá {+划+}). {改造|gǎi zào} (gǎizào) is to
transform, rebuild; {拆除|chāi chú} (chāichú) to pull down, demolish; {空地|kòng dì} (kòngdì) an empty plot, open space; {封闭|fēng bì}
(fēngbì) to close off, closed: {封闭|fēng bì}{式|shì}{小区|xiǎo qū} (a gated compound, with the suffix -{式|shì} of lesson 01). {周边|zhōu biān} (zhōubiān)
is the surrounding area: {学校|xué xiào}{周边|zhōu biān} (around the school).

Fashions and taste: {潮流|cháo liú} (cháoliú) is a trend, the tide; {过时|guò shí} (guòshí) outdated; {单调|dān diào} (dāndiào) monotonous, dull
({单调|dān diào}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}); {家居|jiā jū} (jiājū) the home and its furnishings ({家居|jiā jū}{用品|yòng pǐn}, home furnishings).

## Words: a flat of one's own

The flat: {住宅|zhù zhái} (zhùzhái, a residence, housing: {住宅|zhù zhái}{区|qū}, a residential area), {房价|fáng jià} (fángjià, house prices: {房价|fáng jià}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}),
{昂贵|áng guì} (ángguì, expensive: written; {贵|guì} in speech). {平方米|píng fāng mǐ} is a square metre, {平方|píng fāng} for short in speech ({七十|qī shí}{平方|píng fāng}, seventy
square metres). Rooms: {隔壁|gé bì} (gébì, next door: {隔壁|gé bì}{邻居|lín jū}), {墙壁|qiáng bì} (qiángbì, a wall, its surface: {墙|qiáng} is the everyday
word), {走廊|zǒu láng} (zǒuláng) and {通道|tōng dào} (tōngdào) corridors and passages, {楼道|lóu dào} (lóudào) the stairwell, the corridor
of a block of flats, {浴室|yù shì} (yùshì) the bathroom (with a bath or shower), {侧|cè} (cè) a side: {走廊|zǒu láng}{的|de}{另|lìng}{一|yí}{侧|cè} (the other
side of the corridor). A good flat is {明亮|míng liàng} (míngliàng, bright), {通风|tōng fēng} (tōngfēng, well ventilated), its
facilities {齐全|qí quán} (qíquán, complete: {家具|jiā jù}{齐全|qí quán}, fully furnished) and its area {配套|pèi tào} (pèitào, with services to match:
{配套|pèi tào}{设施|shè shī}, amenities).

Living there: {洗漱|xǐ shù} (xǐshù) is to wash and brush one's teeth; {枕头|zhěn tou} (zhěntou) a pillow; {歇|xiē} (xiē) to rest, have a
break (spoken: {歇|xiē}{一会儿|yí huìr}); {清扫|qīng sǎo} (qīngsǎo) to sweep, clean (written: {清扫|qīng sǎo}{楼道|lóu dào}).

Putting things where they go:

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {摆|bǎi} (bǎi) | to put, arrange; to swing | {把|bǎ}{花|huā}{摆|bǎi}{在|zài}{窗台|chuāng tái}{上|shàng} to put the flowers on the windowsill |
| {摆放|bǎi fàng} (bǎifàng) | to place, set out (more formal) | {东西|dōng xi}{要|yào}{摆放|bǎi fàng}{整齐|zhěng qí}。 Things should be set out tidily. |
| {搭|dā} (dā) | to put up (a frame, a shelter); to take (a ride) | {搭|dā}{一|yí}{个|gè}{架子|jià zi} to put up a frame; {搭|dā}{车|chē} to get a lift |
| {吊|diào} (diào) | to hang (from above) | {屋子|wū zi}{中间|zhōng jiān}{吊|diào}{着|zhe}{一|yì}{盏|zhǎn}{灯|dēng}。 A lamp hangs in the middle of the room. |
| {撑|chēng} (chēng) | to prop up; to hold up (an umbrella) | {撑|chēng}{伞|sǎn} to hold up an umbrella |
| {铺|pū} (pū) | to spread, lay, pave | {铺|pū}{地毯|dì tǎn} to lay a carpet; {铺|pū}{路|lù} to pave a road |

{盏|zhǎn} (zhǎn) is the measure word for lamps; {地毯|dì tǎn} (dìtǎn), a carpet. {铺|pū} is pū as a verb and pù in {店铺|diàn pù} (a shop).

## Characters

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {衰|shuāi} | decline | shuāi | {衣|yī} | 10 | {衰老|shuāi lǎo} (lesson 06) |
| {麦|mài} ✎ (traditional 麥) | wheat | mài | {麦|mài} | 7 | {小麦|xiǎo mài} (lesson 06), {麦克风|mài kè fēng} (lesson 10) |
| {赖|lài} (traditional 賴) | rely on | lài | {贝|bèi} | 13 | {依赖|yī lài} (lesson 06), {赖|lài} and {信赖|xìn lài} (lessons 23, 24) |
| {庄|zhuāng} ✎ (traditional 莊) | village; farm | zhuāng | {广|guǎng} | 6 | {庄稼|zhuāng jia} (lesson 06), {村庄|cūn zhuāng} |

| {杀|shā} ✎ (traditional 殺) | kill | shā | {木|mù} | 6 | {自杀|zì shā} (lesson 06), {杀|shā} (lesson 15) |
| {侧|cè} ✎ (traditional 側) | side | cè | 亻 | 8 | {侧|cè} |
| {潮|cháo} | tide; damp | cháo | 氵 | 15 | {潮流|cháo liú}, {潮湿|cháo shī} (lesson 17) |
| {镇|zhèn} (traditional 鎮) | town | zhèn | 钅 | 15 | {城镇|chéng zhèn}, {镇|zhèn} |
| {撑|chēng} (traditional 撐) | prop up | chēng | 扌 | 15 | {撑|chēng}, {支撑|zhī chēng} (lesson 20) |
| {昂|áng} ✎ | raise (the head); high | áng | {日|rì} | 8 | {昂贵|áng guì} |
| {铺|pū} (traditional 鋪) | spread; shop | pū, pù | 钅 | 12 | {铺|pū}, {店铺|diàn pù} |
| {搭|dā} | put up; take (a ride) | dā | 扌 | 12 | {搭|dā}, {搭配|dā pèi} (lesson 12) |
| {吊|diào} ✎ | hang | diào | {口|kǒu} | 6 | {吊|diào} |
| {栋|dòng} (traditional 棟) | (measure word for buildings) | dòng | {木|mù} | 9 | {栋|dòng} |
| {峰|fēng} | peak | fēng | {山|shān} | 10 | {高峰|gāo fēng}, {山峰|shān fēng} (lesson 18) |
| {壁|bì} | wall | bì | {土|tǔ} | 16 | {隔壁|gé bì}, {墙壁|qiáng bì} |
| {奏|zòu} | play (music) | zòu | {大|dà} | 9 | {节奏|jié zòu}, {演奏|yǎn zòu} (lesson 14) |

Ten differ in traditional: 麥 (11 strokes), 賴 (16), 莊 (11, 艹 over 壯), 礙 (19, {石|shí} + {疑|yí}), 殺 (10),
側 (11), 鎮 (18), 撐 (15), 鋪 (15) and 棟 (12). The first seven finish lesson 06's words. Lesson 07's
own words also use nine characters that lesson 08 teaches: {噪|zào} ({噪声|zào shēng}), {央|yāng} ({中央|zhōng yāng}), {宅|zhái} ({住宅|zhù zhái}), {廊|láng} ({走廊|zǒu láng}), {枕|zhěn} ({枕头|zhěn tou}), {歇|xiē},
{浴|yù} ({浴室|yù shì}), {漱|shù} ({洗漱|xǐ shù}) and {秩|zhì} ({秩序|zhì xù}).

### Sound parts across the levels

- {则|zé} zé in {侧|cè} cè, as in {测|cè} cè ({测试|cè shì}, HSK 5) and {厕|cè} cè ({厕所|cè suǒ}, HSK 4): three cè. Traditional: 側, 測, 廁, with
  則.
- {朝|cháo} cháo in {潮|cháo} cháo (氵 + {朝|cháo}: the tide that comes "towards" the shore is a memory aid, not a history), and in
  {嘲|cháo} cháo ({嘲笑|cháo xiào}, lesson 23).
- {真|zhēn} zhēn in {镇|zhèn} zhèn, as in {慎|shèn} shèn ({谨慎|jǐn shèn}, HSK 5) and {填|tián} tián ({填写|tián xiě}, HSK 4): drifted.
- 卬 in {昂|áng} áng, {仰|yǎng} yǎng (lesson 21) and {迎|yíng} yíng ({欢迎|huān yíng}): the sound has drifted, but the part is easy to spot.
- 甫 fǔ in {铺|pū} pū, {捕|bǔ} bǔ (lesson 17) and {辅|fǔ} fǔ (lesson 16). In traditional, {补|bǔ} bǔ is 補, with 甫 too.
- {合|hé} hé in {搭|dā} dā (扌 + 艹 + {合|hé}), {塔|tǎ} tǎ (lesson 14) and {答|dá} dá: an a-sound family.
- {东|dōng} dōng in {栋|dòng} dòng, as in {冻|dòng} dòng (HSK 5): 棟, 凍 in traditional.
- 夆 in {峰|fēng} fēng and {蜂|fēng} fēng ({蜜蜂|mì fēng}, lesson 18): an exact match.
- 辟 in {壁|bì} bì, {避|bì} bì (lesson 19) and {臂|bì} bì ({手臂|shǒu bì}, lesson 08): an exact series; the meaning comes from the other
  part ({土|tǔ} earth for a wall, 辶 for moving away, ⺼ for the arm).
- {家|jiā} jiā in {稼|jià} jià (禾 + {家|jiā}) and {嫁|jià} jià (lesson 22): both jià.

### Look-alikes and stroke traps

- {衰|shuāi} has {衣|yī} split around its middle: write {衣|yī}'s top (dot, horizontal), then the middle part, then {衣|yī}'s bottom
  (a left-falling stroke, a vertical with a rising hook, then the left- and right-falling strokes).
- {麦|mài}: two horizontals, a vertical through them, a third horizontal, then 夂 below (a left-falling stroke, a
  horizontal-turning stroke, a right-falling stroke). Compare {素|sù} and {表|biǎo}, with the same top.
- {杀|shā}: a left-falling stroke and a dot first (like an X), then {木|mù}'s horizontal; the vertical has a hook.
  6 strokes.
- {吊|diào} is {口|kǒu} over {巾|jīn}; {带|dài} and {常|cháng} also end in {巾|jīn}.
- {梁|liáng} has 氵 and 刅 over {木|mù}: the dots of 刅 come after its hooked stroke. Don't write 粱 (with {米|mǐ} at the bottom, sorghum).
- {栋|dòng}: {木|mù}, then {东|dōng}, whose second stroke turns (撇折).
- {撑|chēng} is 扌 + {掌|zhǎng} in simplified; traditional 撐 has 牚.

   in the daytime, and the basement for things with nowhere else to go.
3. In favour, but not uncritically: it didn't solve everything (the flats are still small, there still
   aren't enough parking spaces), but with house prices so high it may mean more than pulling the old

4. A compound isn't alive in a literal sense: the quotation marks show the word is used figuratively,

"In the centre of many big cities there are still plenty of old compounds built in the eighties and
nineties. Their blocks of flats are usually only six or seven storeys high, with no lift, and their
stairwells are narrow and dark, airless even in summer. Yet most of these compounds are in the city centre, with
everything close by: hospitals, schools and food markets are all near, and many long-time residents can't bear to
move away. As the residents grow older, 'the stairs' has become a worry for many old
people.

A few years ago my compound was like that too. There were bikes and cardboard boxes all over the
stairwells, and you had to turn sideways to get past. The compound had no car park, so cars had to park
on the pavement, and in the morning and evening rush hours the gate was unbearably crowded and noisy.

Last year, under the city plan, our compound began to be done up. The first step was pulling down the
sheds people had put up at random and turning the space into green areas and a car park. The compound's gate was redesigned too: people on the
pavement, cars in the traffic lane, each going their own way. Then every block
had a lift put in and a barrier-free ramp built at the entrance, so that old people in wheelchairs can go
out on their own. The walls were repainted, and bright lights went up in the stairwells.

The work didn't go smoothly. Some residents worried the noise would disturb their rest; some didn't want to
part with the things they kept in the stairwells. The community workers visited every household to talk it
through, thought hard and came up with plenty of solutions: building work only in the daytime, and things
with nowhere to go could be stored in the basement for the time being. One old man refused whatever anyone
said; the workers went to his home five times in all, and only when they put up a little bike shed for him
downstairs was the problem solved.

Now the compound is much tidier and more orderly than before: nothing is left lying about in the stairwells
any more, and someone sweeps them every morning. In the mornings old people walk and do tai
chi in the little garden; in the afternoons children play football on the open ground; in the evenings
neighbours sit and chat downstairs. Auntie Huo, who lives next door to me, says: 'I've lived here thirty
years and never thought an old building could be so comfortable.'

Of course, the work can't solve every problem: the flats are as small as ever, and there still aren't
enough parking spaces. But today, with house prices so high and new housing ever further from the city
centre, bringing old compounds back to life may mean more than pulling them all down and rebuilding.
After all, there's more here than buildings: there are decades of friendship between neighbours."

## Pronunciation

- 扇: shàn as the measure word ({一|yí}{扇|shàn}{门|mén}), shān as the verb "to fan" (HSK 5).
- huà in {规划|guī huà}, {划分|huà fēn} and {划线|huà xiàn} (to mark off); huá in HSK 5's {划船|huá chuán} (to row): one character in simplified, two words.
- 地方: dìfāng (local: both syllables full) and dìfang (a place: light {方|fāng}).
- {都市|dū shì} dūshì: 都 is dū here, as in {首都|shǒu dū}; dōu is "all".
- {铺|pū}: pū as a verb (to spread), pù in {店铺|diàn pù} (a shop).
- {住宅|zhù zhái} zhùzhái, not zhùzé; {宅|zhái} is zhái.
- {噪声|zào shēng} zàoshēng: z-, not c-.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{东|dōng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{箱子|xiāng zi}，{西|xī}{一|yí}{辆|liàng}{箱子|xiāng zi}~~: the measure word repeats in both halves, and so does the noun if there is one
  ({东|dōng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{箱子|xiāng zi}，{西|xī}{一|yí}{个|gè}{箱子|xiāng zi}), or the nouns differ with their own measure words ({东|dōng}{一|yí}{辆|liàng}{自行车|zì xíng chē}，{西|xī}{一|yí}{个|gè}{纸箱|zhǐ xiāng}).
- {东|dōng}{一|yī}A，{西|xī}{一|yī}A is spoken and critical: in a report on a tidy, well-planned square, say {广场|guǎng chǎng}{上|shàng}{摆放|bǎi fàng}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}, not
  {东|dōng}{一|yì}{盆|pén}{花|huā}，{西|xī}{一|yì}{盆|pén}{花|huā}.
- {左思右想|zuǒ sī yòu xiǎng} is fine in writing; {左|zuǒ}{看|kàn}{右|yòu}{看|kàn} and {左|zuǒ}{等|děng}{右|yòu}{等|děng} belong to speech and stories.
- {一|yí}{扇|shàn}{门|mén} and {一|yí}{个|gè}{门|mén}: {一|yí}{个|gè}{门|mén} is common in speech, but {扇|shàn} is the right measure word for a door or window in
  writing.
- {房价|fáng jià} is the price of property, the price to buy; the monthly rent is {租金|zū jīn} or {房租|fáng zū}.
- {昂贵|áng guì} is written: {太|tài}{昂贵|áng guì}{了|le} isn't wrong, but in a chat it sounds like an advertisement. Say {太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}.

## Key points

- {东|dōng}{一|yī} + M (+ noun)，{西|xī}{一|yī} + M (+ noun): scattered all over, in a mess (spoken).
- {左|zuǒ}A{右|yòu}B: again and again, before a result: {左思右想|zuǒ sī yòu xiǎng}, {左|zuǒ}{看|kàn}{右|yòu}{看|kàn}, {左|zuǒ}{等|děng}{右|yòu}{等|děng}, {左|zuǒ}{挑|tiāo}{右|yòu}{选|xuǎn}.
- Measure words {栋|dòng} (buildings), {户|hù} (households), {扇|shàn} (doors, windows); the verb {支|zhī} (to prop up, set up).
- {地方|dì fāng} dìfāng "local" ({地方|dì fāng}{特色|tè sè}) beside {地方|dì fang} dìfang "place"; {中央|zhōng yāng} central.
- The city: {都市|dū shì}, {城镇|chéng zhèn}, {镇|zhèn}, {街头|jiē tóu}, {人行道|rén xíng dào}, {繁忙|fán máng}, {拥挤|yōng jǐ}, {高峰|gāo fēng}, {噪声|zào shēng}, {节奏|jié zòu}, {规划|guī huà}, {改造|gǎi zào}, {拆除|chāi chú}; a flat: {住宅|zhù zhái}, {房价|fáng jià}, {昂贵|áng guì}, {平方米|píng fāng mǐ},
  {隔壁|gé bì}, {明亮|míng liàng}, {通风|tōng fēng}, {齐全|qí quán}, {配套|pèi tào}.
- New characters: {衰|shuāi} {麦|mài} {赖|lài} {庄|zhuāng} {稼|jià} {碍|ài} {杀|shā} {侧|cè} {潮|cháo} {镇|zhèn} {撑|chēng} {昂|áng} {铺|pū} {搭|dā} {吊|diào} {栋|dòng} {峰|fēng} {壁|bì} {奏|zòu} {梁|liáng} (✎ {麦|mài} {庄|zhuāng} {杀|shā} {侧|cè} {昂|áng} {吊|diào}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: The body, health and medicine
topics: 除非…才 and 除非…否则
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 5 took you into the hospital: registering, A&E, a diagnosis. This lesson goes inside the body: its
organs and cells, how an infection starts and how the body fights it, and the words a doctor uses to
explain it. {李明|Lǐ Míng} (Li Ming) has a bad throat and goes to see a doctor; then a doctor explains the body's
defences in a popular-science article.

- **{除非|chú fēi}…{才|cái}** (only if…: {除非|chú fēi}{休息|xiū xi}{好|hǎo}，{才能|cái néng}{恢复|huī fù}) and **{除非|chú fēi}…{否则|fǒu zé} / {不然|bù rán}** (unless…, otherwise…), the strongest
  conditions of the level;
- the written **{于|yú}** in {高于|gāo yú}, {低于|dī yú} and {用于|yòng yú} (higher than, lower than, used for), the first of the **written
  prepositions** that lesson 27 brings together;
- the body ({心脏|xīn zàng}, {肺|fèi}, {肝|gān}, {肠|cháng}, {血液|xuè yè}, {神经|shén jīng}…), illness and its signs ({病毒|bìng dú}, {细菌|xì jūn}, {感染|gǎn rǎn}, {发炎|fā yán}, {症状|zhèng zhuàng}…) and treatment
  ({服用|fú yòng}, {消毒|xiāo dú}, {康复|kāng fù}…).

The lesson explains; it gives no medical advice beyond the everyday: rest, drink water, see a doctor.

## {除非|chú fēi}…{才|cái}: only if…

{除非|chú fēi} (chúfēi) sets the one condition without which the result won't happen. With {才|cái} in the second clause it's
"only if A will B", like HSK 3's {只有|zhǐ yǒu}…{才|cái}, but stronger: A is the only way.

{除非|chú fēi}{休息|xiū xi}{好|hǎo}，{嗓子|sǎng zi}{才能|cái néng}{恢复|huī fù}。 — Your throat will only recover if you rest properly.

{除非|chú fēi}{医生|yī shēng}{同意|tóng yì}，{你|nǐ}{才能|cái néng}{出院|chū yuàn}。 — You can only leave hospital if the doctor agrees.

The result can come first, with {除非|chú fēi} after it: "B won't happen, unless A".

{他|tā}{不|bú}{会|huì}{去|qù}{看病|kàn bìng}{的|de}，{除非|chú fēi}{疼|téng}{得|de}{受不了|shòu bu liǎo}。 — He won't go to the doctor unless the pain becomes unbearable.

## {除非|chú fēi}…{否则|fǒu zé} / {不然|bù rán}: unless…, otherwise…

With {否则|fǒu zé} (written, HSK 4) or {不然|bù rán} (spoken) in the second clause, the sentence says what happens if the
condition is not met:

{除非|chú fēi}{按时|àn shí}{吃|chī}{药|yào}，{否则|fǒu zé}{病|bìng}{很|hěn}{难|nán}{好|hǎo}。 — Unless you take the medicine on time, you won't get well easily.

{除非|chú fēi}{你|nǐ}{戴|dài}{上|shàng}{口罩|kǒu zhào}，{不然|bù rán}{会|huì}{传染|chuán rǎn}{给|gěi}{别人|bié ren}{的|de}。 — Unless you put on a mask, you'll pass it on to other people.

{口罩|kǒu zhào} (kǒuzhào): a face mask.

The two patterns say the same thing in two ways. Compare:

| Pattern | Sentence | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {除非|chú fēi} A，{才|cái} B | {除非|chú fēi}{多|duō}{休息|xiū xi}，{才能|cái néng}{好|hǎo}{得|de}{快|kuài}。 | Only if you rest a lot will you get better fast. |
| {除非|chú fēi} A，{否则|fǒu zé} ({不|bù}) B | {除非|chú fēi}{多|duō}{休息|xiū xi}，{否则|fǒu zé}{好不了|hǎo bu liǎo}。 | Unless you rest a lot, you won't get better. |

Keep the logic straight: after {才|cái} comes what happens *with* A; after {否则|fǒu zé} comes what happens *without* A.
So not ~~{除非|chú fēi}{多|duō}{休息|xiū xi}，{否则|fǒu zé}{能|néng}{好|hǎo}{得|de}{快|kuài}~~: that says resting is needed for you *not* to get better fast. Register:
{除非|chú fēi} is at home in both speech and writing; {否则|fǒu zé} is more written, {不然|bù rán} more spoken.

## The written {于|yú}: {高于|gāo yú}, {低于|dī yú}, {用于|yòng yú}

{于|yú} (yú) is a written preposition: in comparisons it is "than", after {用|yòng} it is "for". It sits right after an
adjective or verb and stays there: you can't put {很|hěn} inside.

| Written | Spoken | Example |
|---|---|---|
| A {高于|gāo yú} B | A {比|bǐ} B {高|gāo} | {他|tā}{的|de}{血压|xuè yā}{高于|gāo yú}{正常|zhèng cháng}{水平|shuǐ píng}。 His blood pressure is above normal. |
| A {低于|dī yú} B | A {比|bǐ} B {低|dī} | {今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{气温|qì wēn}{低于|dī yú}{往年|wǎng nián}。 Today's temperature is lower than usual. |
| A {用于|yòng yú} B | A {用来|yòng lái} B | {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{药|yào}{主要|zhǔ yào}{用于|yòng yú}{治疗|zhì liáo}{肺炎|fèi yán}。 This medicine is mainly used to treat pneumonia. |

{水平|shuǐ píng} (shuǐpíng, HSK 3): a level. {高于|gāo yú}, {低于|dī yú} and {用于|yòng yú} are HSK 4 words; lesson 27 adds {位于|wèi yú}, {源于|yuán yú}, {易于|yì yú}, {限于|xiàn yú}, {出于|chū yú} and the
preposition {于|yú} on its own ({于|yú}2031{年|nián}, in 2031). A **[[written preposition]]** like {于|yú} belongs to reports, labels,
instructions and news; {比|bǐ} and {用来|yòng lái} are the everyday forms. On a medicine box: {本|běn}{品|pǐn}{用于|yòng yú}… (this product is used
for…).

## Words: the body

| Word | Meaning | Word | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| {脑袋|nǎo dai} (nǎodai) | the head (spoken) | {脑子|nǎo zi} (nǎozi) | the brain; the mind (spoken) |
| {面部|miàn bù} (miànbù) | the face (medical, written) | {口腔|kǒu qiāng} (kǒuqiāng) | the mouth (medical) |
| {舌头|shé tou} (shétou) | the tongue | {嗓子|sǎng zi} (sǎngzi) | the throat; the voice |
| {脖子|bó zi} (bózi) | the neck | {肩膀|jiān bǎng} (jiānbǎng) | the shoulder |
| {手臂|shǒu bì} (shǒubì) | the arm (written) | {胸|xiōng} (xiōng) | the chest |
| {心脏|xīn zàng} (xīnzàng) | the heart (the organ) | {肺|fèi} (fèi) | the lungs, a lung |
| {肝|gān} (gān) | the liver | {肠|cháng} (cháng) | the intestines |
| {血液|xuè yè} (xuèyè) | blood (written) | {血管|xuè guǎn} (xuèguǎn) | a blood vessel |
| {神经|shén jīng} (shénjīng) | a nerve | {细胞|xì bāo} (xìbāo) | a cell |

The spoken and written pairs again: {脑袋|nǎo dai} and {头|tóu} (the everyday word for the head), {嗓子|sǎng zi} and {喉咙|hóu lóng} (hóulóng, the throat,
more formal), {手臂|shǒu bì} and {胳膊|gē bo} (the arm, spoken). {心|xīn} is the heart in everyday speech and feelings ({心里|xīn li}); {心脏|xīn zàng} is the organ.
{部位|bù wèi} (bùwèi) is a part or position of the body: {疼|téng}{的|de}{部位|bù wèi} (where it hurts). Blood words: {血压|xuè yā} (xuèyā, blood
pressure: {量|liáng}{血压|xuè yā}, to take someone's blood pressure; {高|gāo}{血压|xuè yā}, high blood pressure), {血型|xuè xíng} (xuèxíng, blood group: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}
{血型|xuè xíng}？). {血|xuè} is xuè in these words; in speech it's often xiě on its own ({流|liú}{血|xiě}{了|le}, it's bleeding).

Seeing: {视力|shì lì} (shìlì) is eyesight; {近视|jìn shì} (jìnshì) short-sighted: {他|tā}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{近视|jìn shì}. {基因|jī yīn} (jīyīn) is a gene, and {遗传|yí chuán}
(yíchuán) heredity, to be inherited: {近视|jìn shì}{会|huì}{遗传|yí chuán}{吗|ma}？ (is short sight inherited?). {本能|běn néng} (běnnéng) is instinct, an
instinctive reaction: {闭|bì} (bì, to close) the eyes when something flies at them is {本能|běn néng}. {闭|bì}{上|shàng}{眼睛|yǎn jing} (close your
eyes); {闭|bì} is the verb for the eyes and the mouth; for doors and windows the everyday verb is {关|guān}.

## Words: illness and its signs

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {病毒|bìng dú} (bìngdú) | a virus | {感冒|gǎn mào}{多数|duō shù}{是|shì}{病毒|bìng dú}{引起|yǐn qǐ}{的|de}。 Most colds are caused by viruses. |
| {细菌|xì jūn} (xìjūn) | bacteria | {有的|yǒu de}{细菌|xì jūn}{对|duì}{人|rén}{有益|yǒu yì}。 Some bacteria are good for people. |
| {毒|dú} (dú) | poison; poisonous | {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{蘑菇|mó gu}{有|yǒu}{毒|dú}。 This mushroom ({蘑菇|mó gu}, mógu) is poisonous. |
| {中毒|zhòng dú} (zhòngdú) | to be poisoned, poisoning | {食物|shí wù}{中毒|zhòng dú} food poisoning; 中 is zhòng here |
| {感染|gǎn rǎn} (gǎnrǎn) | to infect, infection | {伤口|shāng kǒu}{感染|gǎn rǎn}{了|le}。 The wound is infected. |
| {传染|chuán rǎn} (chuánrǎn) | to pass on (an illness) | {流感|liú gǎn}{很|hěn}{容易|róng yì}{传染|chuán rǎn}。 Flu is easily passed on. |
| {传染病|chuán rǎn bìng} (chuánrǎnbìng) | an infectious disease | {防治|fáng zhì}{传染病|chuán rǎn bìng} to prevent and treat infectious diseases |
| {发病|fā bìng} (fābìng) | (an illness) to start, break out | {发病|fā bìng}{的|de}{原因|yuán yīn} the cause of the illness |
| {患|huàn} (huàn) | to suffer from (written) | {他|tā}{患|huàn}{了|le}{肺炎|fèi yán}。 He has pneumonia. |
| {患者|huàn zhě} (huànzhě) | a patient (written) | {肺炎|fèi yán}{患者|huàn zhě} pneumonia patients |
| {发炎|fā yán} (fāyán) | to become inflamed | {嗓子|sǎng zi}{发炎|fā yán}{了|le}。 My throat is inflamed. |
| {炎症|yán zhèng} (yánzhèng) | inflammation | {消除|xiāo chú}{炎症|yán zhèng} to clear up inflammation |
| {肺炎|fèi yán} (fèiyán) | pneumonia | {他|tā}{得|dé}{了|le}{肺炎|fèi yán}，{住院|zhù yuàn}{了|le}。 He got pneumonia and went into hospital. |
| {症状|zhèng zhuàng} (zhèngzhuàng) | a symptom | {发烧|fā shāo}{是|shì}{常见|cháng jiàn}{的|de}{症状|zhèng zhuàng}。 A fever is a common symptom. |

How it feels: {不适|bú shì} (búshì) is discomfort, unwell (written: {身体|shēn tǐ}{不适|bú shì}, feeling unwell); {恶心|ě xīn} (ěxīn) is to feel
sick, and also disgusting; 吐 is tǔ "to spit, to spit out" ({吐痰|tǔ tán}, to spit; {吐|tǔ}{出来|chū lái}, to spit it out) and tù "to
vomit" ({他|tā}{吐|tù}{了|le}, he was sick). {晕|yūn} (yūn) is dizzy: {头晕|tóu yūn} (light-headed); {痒|yǎng} (yǎng) itchy; {肿|zhǒng} (zhǒng) swollen: {脚|jiǎo}{肿|zhǒng}{了|le}.
{刺|cì} (cì) is a thorn, and to prick: {手|shǒu}{被|bèi}{刺|cì}{了|le}{一下|yí xià} (I pricked my hand); {针|zhēn} (zhēn) a needle, an injection: {打针|dǎ zhēn}. {伤口|shāng kǒu}
(shāngkǒu) is a wound, {损伤|sǔn shāng} (sǔnshāng) an injury, damage (written: {肝|gān}{损伤|sǔn shāng}, liver damage); {加重|jiā zhòng} (jiāzhòng) to get
worse, to make heavier: {病情|bìng qíng}{加重|jiā zhòng}{了|le} (the condition got worse). {肥胖|féi pàng} (féipàng) is obese, obesity (medical; {胖|pàng} is the
everyday word).

{痰|tán} (tán): phlegm. {头晕|tóu yūn} (tóuyūn): dizzy, light-headed.

## Words: the hospital and treatment

Hospital departments are {科|kē} (kē): {内科|nèi kē} (internal medicine), {外科|wài kē} (surgery), {儿科|ér kē} (paediatrics), and with a body
part {口腔科|kǒu qiāng kē} (dentistry), {眼科|yǎn kē} (ophthalmology). {你|nǐ}{挂|guà}{哪个|nǎ ge}{科|kē}？ (which department are you registering for?)

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {检测|jiǎn cè} (jiǎncè) | to test, detect | {检测|jiǎn cè}{血液|xuè yè} to test the blood |
| {服用|fú yòng} (fúyòng) | to take (medicine: written) | {每|měi}{日|rì}{服用|fú yòng}{三|sān}{次|cì} to be taken three times a day |
| {医药|yī yào} (yīyào) | medicine, drugs; medical | {医药费|yī yào fèi} medical costs |
| {消毒|xiāo dú} (xiāodú) | to disinfect | {伤口|shāng kǒu}{要|yào}{先|xiān}{消毒|xiāo dú}。 First disinfect the wound. |
| {防治|fáng zhì} (fángzhì) | to prevent and treat | {防治|fáng zhì}{近视|jìn shì} to prevent and treat short sight |
| {抵抗|dǐ kàng} (dǐkàng) | to resist | {抵抗|dǐ kàng}{病毒|bìng dú} to resist viruses |
| {免疫|miǎn yì} (miǎnyì) | immunity, to be immune | {免疫|miǎn yì}{系统|xì tǒng} the immune system |
| {抑制|yì zhì} (yìzhì) | to inhibit, restrain, suppress | {抑制|yì zhì}{细菌|xì jūn}{生长|shēng zhǎng} to inhibit the growth of bacteria |
| {康复|kāng fù} (kāngfù) | to recover, rehabilitation | {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{早日|zǎo rì}{康复|kāng fù}！ Get well soon! |
| {功效|gōng xiào} (gōngxiào) | efficacy, effect (as claimed) | {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{茶|chá}{的|de}{功效|gōng xiào} what this tea is supposed to do |
| {益处|yì chù} (yìchù) | a benefit (written) | {运动|yùn dòng}{的|de}{益处|yì chù} the benefits of exercise |

{功效|gōng xiào} is the word of advertisements and labels: what a product says it does. The lesson describes such claims;
it doesn't make them. {早日|zǎo rì} (zǎorì): soon (written). {免疫|miǎn yì}{系统|xì tǒng} is the immune system ({系统|xì tǒng}, HSK 5).

## Characters

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {漱|shù} | rinse (the mouth) | shù | 氵 | 14 | {洗漱|xǐ shù} (lesson 07) |
| {歇|xiē} | rest | xiē | {欠|qiàn} | 13 | {歇|xiē} (lesson 07) |
| {浴|yù} | bathe | yù | 氵 | 10 | {浴室|yù shì} (lesson 07) |
| {噪|zào} | noisy | zào | {口|kǒu} | 16 | {噪声|zào shēng} (lesson 07) |
| {枕|zhěn} | pillow | zhěn | {木|mù} | 8 | {枕头|zhěn tou} (lesson 07) |
| {秩|zhì} | order | zhì | 禾 | 10 | {秩序|zhì xù} (lesson 07) |
| {央|yāng} ✎ | centre | yāng | {大|dà} | 5 | {中央|zhōng yāng} (lesson 07) |

| {毒|dú} | poison | dú | {母|mǔ} | 9 | {病毒|bìng dú}, {毒|dú}, {消毒|xiāo dú}, {中毒|zhòng dú} |
| {脖|bó} | neck | bó | ⺼ | 11 | {脖子|bó zi} |
| {肠|cháng} ✎ (traditional 腸) | intestines | cháng | ⺼ | 7 | {肠|cháng}, {香肠|xiāng cháng} (lesson 12) |
| {肺|fèi} ✎ | lung | fèi | ⺼ | 8 | {肺|fèi}, {肺炎|fèi yán} |
| {炎|yán} ✎ | inflammation; hot | yán | {火|huǒ} | 8 | {肺炎|fèi yán}, {发炎|fā yán}, {炎症|yán zhèng}, {炎热|yán rè} (lesson 19) |
| {抵|dǐ} ✎ | resist; reach | dǐ | 扌 | 8 | {抵抗|dǐ kàng}, {抵达|dǐ dá} (lesson 11) |
| {抗|kàng} ✎ | resist | kàng | 扌 | 7 | {抵抗|dǐ kàng}, {对抗|duì kàng} (lesson 23) |
| {恶|è} ✎ (traditional 噁, 惡) | nausea; evil | ě, è | {心|xīn} | 10 | {恶心|ě xīn}, {恶劣|è liè} (lesson 19) |
| {肝|gān} ✎ | liver | gān | ⺼ | 7 | {肝|gān} |
| {患|huàn} | suffer from | huàn | {心|xīn} | 11 | {患者|huàn zhě}, {患|huàn} |

Two differ in traditional. {肠|cháng} is 腸 (13 strokes). 恶 has two traditional forms: 噁 (15, with {口|kǒu}) in {恶心|ě xīn} ě,
"nauseous", and 惡 (12) in {恶劣|è liè} è, "bad, vile" (lesson 19). The first nine finish lesson 07's words. Lesson
08's own words use fifteen characters that lesson 09 teaches: {吐|tǔ}, {嗓|sǎng} ({嗓子|sǎng zi}), {抑|yì} ({抑制|yì zhì}), {晕|yūn}, {液|yè} ({血液|xuè yè}), {疫|yì} ({免疫|miǎn yì}), {症|zhèng}

### A new radical: {母|mǔ}

{母|mǔ} (mǔ, mother) is the radical of three characters of levels 1–6: {每|měi} (HSK 2), {母|mǔ} itself ({父母|fù mǔ}, HSK 4) and {毒|dú}.
In {每|měi} and {毒|dú} it no longer means "mother"; it's the bottom part, written like {母|mǔ}: five strokes, a vertical that
turns, a hooked turning stroke, a dot, a horizontal, a dot. Don't confuse it with 毋 (wú), which has a
left-falling stroke through the middle instead of two dots.

### The flesh radical ⺼

⺼ ("flesh", a form of {肉|ròu}) looks like {月|yuè} (moon) but means the body: {脖|bó} {肠|cháng} {肺|fèi} {肝|gān} {肩|jiān} here, with {腿|tuǐ} {脚|jiǎo} {脸|liǎn} {胖|pàng} {胃|wèi}

- {肺|fèi} has 巿 (fú) on the right, not {市|shì} (shì, market, with a dot on top): 巿 is 4 strokes, a horizontal, a
  short vertical, a hooked turning stroke, and the long vertical last, straight through the horizontal.

- {恶|è}: {亚|yà} first (a horizontal, two short verticals, a dot and a left-falling stroke, the bottom horizontal),

- {央|yāng}: 冂 and a horizontal, then {大|dà}'s left- and right-falling strokes through it: 5 strokes.
- {患|huàn}: {串|chuàn} has two {口|kǒu} on one vertical; write the vertical after both {口|kǒu}.

> {当然|dāng rán}，{免疫|miǎn yì}{力|lì}{并|bìng}{不|bú}{是|shì}{一成不变|yì chéng bú biàn}{的|de}。{长期|cháng qī}{熬夜|áo yè}、{压力|yā lì}{过|guò}{大|dà}、{营养不良|yíng yǎng bù liáng}，{都|dōu}{会|huì}{让|ràng}{抵抗力|dǐ kàng lì}{下降|xià jiàng}，{抽|chōu}{烟|yān}{会|huì}{损伤|sǔn shāng}{肺|fèi}，{长期|cháng qī}{大量|dà liàng}{喝|hē}{酒|jiǔ}{会|huì}{损伤|sǔn shāng}{肝|gān}；{而|ér}{规律|guī lǜ}{的|de}{作息|zuò xī}、{适当|shì dàng}{的|de}{运动|yùn dòng}{和|hé}{均衡|jūn héng}{的|de}{饮食|yǐn shí}，{对|duì}{免疫|miǎn yì}{系统|xì tǒng}{大|dà}{有|yǒu}{益处|yì chù}。{心情|xīn qíng}{愉快|yú kuài}、{睡眠|shuì mián}{充足|chōng zú}{的|de}{人|rén}，{往往|wǎng wǎng}{不|bù}{容易|róng yì}{生病|shēng bìng}。{有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{天生|tiān shēng}{体质|tǐ zhì}{好|hǎo}，{这|zhè}{和|hé}{遗传|yí chuán}、{基因|jī yīn}{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{一定|yí dìng}{的|de}{关系|guān xi}。

> {需要|xū yào}{提醒|tí xǐng}{的|de}{是|shì}，{发烧|fā shāo}、{咳嗽|ké sou}{等|děng}{症状|zhèng zhuàng}{本身|běn shēn}{并|bìng}{不|bú}{是|shì}{病|bìng}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{身体|shēn tǐ}{在|zài}"{报警|bào jǐng}"。{除非|chú fēi}{症状|zhèng zhuàng}{严重|yán zhòng}{或|huò}{持续不退|chí xù bú tuì}，{一般|yì bān}{不必|bú bì}{过于|guò yú}{紧张|jǐn zhāng}；{但是|dàn shì}{如果|rú guǒ}{出现|chū xiàn}{呼吸|hū xī}{困难|kùn nan}、{胸口|xiōng kǒu}{疼|téng}{等|děng}{情况|qíng kuàng}，{就|jiù}{应当|yīng dāng}{马上|mǎ shàng}{就医|jiù yī}。{至于|zhì yú}{该|gāi}{不|bu}{该|gāi}{服用|fú yòng}{某|mǒu}{种|zhǒng}{药物|yào wù}，{要|yào}{由|yóu}{医生|yī shēng}{来|lái}{判断|pàn duàn}，{不要|bú yào}{自己|zì jǐ}{随便|suí biàn}{决定|jué dìng}。

{微生物|wēi shēng wù} (wēishēngwù): micro-organisms. {每时每刻|měi shí měi kè} (měi shí měi kè): every moment. {黏膜|nián mó} (niánmó): mucous membranes. {城墙|chéng qiáng}
(chéngqiáng): a city wall. {呼吸道|hū xī dào} (hūxīdào): the airways. {突破|tū pò} (tūpò, lesson 20): to break through. {包围|bāo wéi}
(bāowéi): to surround. {本领|běn lǐng} (běnlǐng, HSK 5): a skill. {对付|duì fu} (duìfu): to deal with. {原理|yuán lǐ} (yuánlǐ, lesson 20): a
principle. {一成不变|yì chéng bú biàn} (yì chéng bú biàn): fixed and unchanging (an idiom). {均衡|jūn héng} (jūnhéng): balanced. {体质|tǐ zhì} (tǐzhì):
constitution. {报警|bào jǐng} (bàojǐng): to raise the alarm. {持续不退|chí xù bú tuì} (chíxù bú tuì): not going down. {就医|jiù yī} (jiùyī): to see a
doctor (written). {至于|zhì yú} (zhìyú): as for (lesson 09 looks at it). {消灭|xiāo miè} (xiāomiè, lesson 19): to wipe out. {本身|běn shēn} (běnshēn, lesson 27):
itself. {防线|fáng xiàn} (fángxiàn): a line of defence. {打喷嚏|dǎ pēn tì} (dǎ pēntì): to sneeze. {升高|shēng gāo} (shēnggāo): to rise.

1. What is the article mainly about?
2. Why does the writer call inflammation a "signal"?
3. What does the fourth paragraph explain, and how is it linked to vaccines?
4. What is the writer's attitude to symptoms like a fever, in the last paragraph?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. How the body defends itself against bacteria and viruses: the skin and mucous membranes first, then the
   immune system, its "memory", and what weakens or strengthens it.
2. Because the redness, swelling, heat and pain show the body is fighting the illness ({身体|shēn tǐ}{在|zài}{抵抗|dǐ kàng}{疾病|jí bìng}{的|de}{信号|xìn hào}):
   unpleasant, but a sign the defences are working.
3. That the immune system "remembers" an enemy and makes antibodies, so it recognises and stops the same
   virus faster next time; vaccines use exactly this principle ({疫苗|yì miáo}{正|zhèng}{是|shì}{利用|lì yòng}{了|le}{这个|zhè ge}{原理|yuán lǐ}).
4. Calm and balanced: symptoms are the body "raising the alarm", not the illness itself, so there's no need
   to panic unless they're serious or don't go away; but serious signs mean seeing a doctor at once, and a
   doctor, not the patient, decides on medicine.

"We live every day in a world full of bacteria and viruses. The air, water, food, even our own hands carry
vast numbers of micro-organisms invisible to the naked eye. Yet most of the time we don't fall ill. Why is
that? Because inside our bodies an invisible 'defensive battle' is going on every moment. In medicine, the body's ability to protect itself is called 'immunity'.

The first line of defence is the skin and the mucous membranes in the mouth and nose. They're like a city
wall, keeping most bacteria and viruses out. Sneezing and coughing are instincts too: their purpose is to
drive out whatever has got into the airways.

Once a virus or bacterium breaks through this line and gets into the body, the immune system goes to work.
White blood cells in the blood rush to the infected part, surround the invaders and destroy them. At this
point the area often turns red, swells, gets hot and hurts: this is what we call 'inflammation'.
Unpleasant as it is, inflammation is in fact a signal that the body is fighting the illness. Sometimes, to
wipe out a virus, the body also raises its temperature: that's a fever.

The immune system has another remarkable skill: it 'remembers' enemies it has met. After the body beats a
virus, it produces antibodies made to deal with it. Next time the same virus comes, the immune system can
recognise it and stop it faster. That's why some illnesses, once you've had them, seldom come a second time. Vaccines make use of exactly this principle.

Of course, immunity isn't fixed. Staying up late over a long time, too much stress and poor nutrition all
lower resistance, smoking damages the lungs and heavy drinking over a long time damages the liver, while a regular routine, moderate exercise and a balanced diet do the immune system a
great deal of good. People who are cheerful and sleep enough tend not to fall ill easily. Some people are born with a strong constitution, which also has something to do with
heredity and genes.

It should be said that symptoms like fever and coughing are not illnesses in themselves but the body
'raising the alarm'. Unless the symptoms are serious or don't go down, there's usually no need to worry
too much; but if difficulty breathing or chest pain appears, you should see a doctor at once. As for
whether to take a particular medicine, that is for a doctor to judge: don't decide it yourself."
</details>

## Write it: a request for sick leave

Write the email {李明|Lǐ Míng} sends his manager (150–200 characters): what's wrong, what the doctor said, how many days
he needs, how his work will be handled, and how to reach him. Keep it polite and written: {您|nín}, {因此|yīn cǐ}, {望|wàng}.

<details>
<summary>A model email</summary>

{主题|zhǔ tí}：{请假|qǐng jià}{三|sān}{天|tiān}

{邹经理|Zōu jīng lǐ}：

{您|nín}{好|hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{翻译部|fān yì bù}{的|de}{李明|Lǐ Míng}。{我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{周一|zhōu yī}{开始|kāi shǐ}{嗓子|sǎng zi}{疼|téng}，{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{发烧|fā shāo}{到|dào}{三十八|sān shí bā}{度|dù}{多|duō}。{今天|jīn tiān}{上午|shàng wǔ}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}{看|kàn}{了|le}{内科|nèi kē}，{医生|yī shēng}{说|shuō}{是|shì}{嗓子|sǎng zi}{发炎|fā yán}，{病毒|bìng dú}{感染|gǎn rǎn}{引起|yǐn qǐ}{的|de}，{需要|xū yào}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}{三|sān}{天|tiān}，{并且|bìng qiě}{注意|zhù yì}{不要|bú yào}{传染|chuán rǎn}{给|gěi}{别人|bié ren}。{因此|yīn cǐ}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{请|qǐng}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{病假|bìng jià}，{从|cóng}{本|běn}{周三|zhōu sān}{到|dào}{周五|zhōu wǔ}。

{我|wǒ}{手|shǒu}{上|shàng}{的|de}{翻译|fān yì}{稿子|gǎo zi}{已经|yǐ jīng}{完成|wán chéng}{了|le}{一|yí}{大|dà}{半|bàn}，{剩|shèng}{下|xià}{的|de}{部分|bù fen}{我|wǒ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{同事|tóng shì}{小段|Xiǎo Duàn}，{跟|gēn}{她|tā}{说|shuō}{清楚|qīng chu}{了|le}。{如果|rú guǒ}{有|yǒu}{急|jí}{事|shì}，{您|nín}{可以|kě yǐ}{随时|suí shí}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{发|fā}{邮件|yóu jiàn}，{我|wǒ}{身体|shēn tǐ}{好|hǎo}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{就|jiù}{会|huì}{回复|huí fù}。{医院|yī yuàn}{开|kāi}{的|de}{病假|bìng jià}{证明|zhèng míng}{我|wǒ}{下|xià}{周一|zhōu yī}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{人事部|rén shì bù}。

{给|gěi}{您|nín}{和|hé}{同事|tóng shì}{们|men}{添麻烦|tiān má fan}{了|le}，{望|wàng}{您|nín}{批准|pī zhǔn}。

{李明|Lǐ Míng}
{十一|shí yī}{月|yuè}{十九|shí jiǔ}{日|rì}

(About 200 characters. {主题|zhǔ tí} zhǔtí, the subject line; {翻译部|fān yì bù} fānyìbù, the translation department; {小段|Xiǎo Duàn} Xiǎo Duàn, a
colleague; {证明|zhèng míng} zhèngmíng, HSK 4, a certificate; {人事部|rén shì bù} rénshìbù, the personnel department; {人事|rén shì} is lesson 01's word;
{望|wàng} wàng, to hope (written; lesson 25's word); {批准|pī zhǔn} pīzhǔn, HSK 5, to approve.)

"Subject: three days' leave. Dear Manager Zou, This is Li Ming of the translation department. My throat
has been sore since Monday, and last night my temperature went over 38. This morning I saw a doctor in the
department of internal medicine at the hospital: my throat is inflamed, from a viral infection, and I need
to rest at home for three days and take care not to pass it on. I'd therefore like to take three days'
sick leave, from this Wednesday to Friday. I've finished well over half of the translation I'm working on,
and I've handed the rest to my colleague Xiao Duan and explained it to her. If anything urgent comes up,
you can email me at any time, and I'll reply as soon as I feel a little better. I'll give the hospital's
sick note to the personnel department next Monday. I'm sorry for the trouble to you and my colleagues, and
hope you'll approve. Li Ming, 19 November"
</details>

## Say it

```speak

{我|wǒ}{嗓子|sǎng zi}{疼|téng}，{咽|yàn}{东西|dōng xi}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{特别|tè bié}{疼|téng}。
```

## Pronunciation

- 吐: tǔ is "to spit (out)": {吐痰|tǔ tán}; tù is "to vomit": {他|tā}{吐|tù}{了|le}. Both are words of this lesson.
- {恶心|ě xīn} ěxīn: {=恶=} (traditional {+噁+}) is ě here (third tone); in {恶劣|è liè} (lesson 19) it's è (traditional {+惡+}).
- {血|xuè} is xuè in words ({血液|xuè yè}, {血压|xuè yā}, {血型|xuè xíng}, {血管|xuè guǎn}); in speech, on its own, it's often xiě ({流|liú}{血|xiě}{了|le}).
- {中毒|zhòng dú} zhòngdú: 中 is zhòng, "to be hit by", as in lesson 29's {中|zhòng} zhòng.
- {晕|yūn} yūn (dizzy) here; in lesson 09's {晕车|yùn chē} (carsick) it's yùn.
- {肺|fèi} fèi and {费|fèi} fèi (a fee): the same syllable.
- {不适|bú shì} búshì: 不 changes before the fourth tone.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{除非|chú fēi}{多|duō}{休息|xiū xi}，{否则|fǒu zé}{能|néng}{好|hǎo}{得|de}{快|kuài}~~: after {否则|fǒu zé} comes what happens without the condition ({否则|fǒu zé}{好不了|hǎo bu liǎo}). With {才|cái}, the
  result with it: {除非|chú fēi}{多|duō}{休息|xiū xi}，{才能|cái néng}{好|hǎo}{得|de}{快|kuài}.
- {除非|chú fēi} needs its partner: {除非|chú fēi}…{才|cái}, {除非|chú fēi}…{否则|fǒu zé} / {不然|bù rán}, or the result first ({他|tā}{不|bú}{会|huì}{去|qù}，{除非|chú fēi}…). {除非|chú fēi}{你|nǐ}{来|lái} on its own is
  an unfinished sentence.
- ~~{他|tā}{的|de}{血压|xuè yā}{很|hěn}{高于|gāo yú}{正常|zhèng cháng}~~: no {很|hěn} with {高于|gāo yú}. Say {他|tā}{的|de}{血压|xuè yā}{高于|gāo yú}{正常|zhèng cháng} (written) or {他|tā}{的|de}{血压|xuè yā}{比|bǐ}{正常|zhèng cháng}{高|gāo} (spoken).
- {患|huàn} is written: {他|tā}{患|huàn}{了|le}{肺炎|fèi yán} in a report, {他|tā}{得|dé}{了|le}{肺炎|fèi yán} in speech. {患者|huàn zhě} is the patient in news and research; {病人|bìng rén} at
  the bedside.
- {心脏|xīn zàng} is the organ only: {他|tā}{心脏|xīn zàng}{不|bù}{好|hǎo} (he has heart trouble). For feelings, {心|xīn}: {我|wǒ}{心里|xīn li}{很|hěn}{难过|nán guò}.
- {服用|fú yòng} is for medicine, in instructions: {每|měi}{日|rì}{服用|fú yòng}{三|sān}{次|cì}. You don't {服用|fú yòng} a meal.

## Key points

- {除非|chú fēi} A，{才|cái} B: only if A will B. B，{除非|chú fēi} A: B won't happen unless A.
- {除非|chú fēi} A，{否则|fǒu zé} (written) / {不然|bù rán} (spoken) B: unless A, B (what happens without A).
- Written {于|yú}: {高于|gāo yú} / {低于|dī yú} (higher / lower than), {用于|yòng yú} (used for). Spoken: {比|bǐ}…{高|gāo}, {比|bǐ}…{低|dī}, {用来|yòng lái}.
- The body: {脑袋|nǎo dai}, {脑子|nǎo zi}, {面部|miàn bù}, {口腔|kǒu qiāng}, {舌头|shé tou}, {嗓子|sǎng zi}, {脖子|bó zi}, {肩膀|jiān bǎng}, {手臂|shǒu bì}, {胸|xiōng}, {心脏|xīn zàng}, {肺|fèi}, {肝|gān}, {肠|cháng}, {血液|xuè yè}, {血管|xuè guǎn}, {神经|shén jīng}, {细胞|xì bāo}.
- Illness: {病毒|bìng dú}, {细菌|xì jūn}, {感染|gǎn rǎn}, {传染|chuán rǎn}, {发病|fā bìng}, {患|huàn}, {患者|huàn zhě}, {发炎|fā yán}, {炎症|yán zhèng}, {症状|zhèng zhuàng}, {不适|bú shì}, {恶心|ě xīn}, {吐|tǔ} tǔ / tù, {晕|yūn}, {痒|yǎng}, {肿|zhǒng}.

- New characters: {漱|shù} {歇|xiē} {浴|yù} {噪|zào} {枕|zhěn} {秩|zhì} {央|yāng} {宅|zhái} {廊|láng} {毒|dú} {脖|bó} {肠|cháng} {肺|fèi} {炎|yán} {抵|dǐ} {抗|kàng} {恶|è} {肝|gān} {患|huàn} {肩|jiān} (✎ {央|yāng} {宅|zhái} {肠|cháng} {肺|fèi} {炎|yán} {抵|dǐ} {抗|kàng} {恶|è} {肝|gān} {肩|jiān}); a new

lessons.title: Law, rules and traffic
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Rules keep a city running: traffic rules, shop rules, the law. This lesson has the words for all three,
from {刹车|shā chē} (to brake) to {法官|fǎ guān} (a judge). {大卫|Dà wèi} (David) and {白涛|Bái Tāo} (Bai Tao) drive out to a supplier's factory, and a
news story tells how a customer whose privacy was broken by a phone repair shop got compensation.

- **{除|chú}…({以|yǐ}){外|wài}**, the written "except, besides", and {除|chú} as a **[[written preposition]]**;
- **{至于|zhì yú}** (as for…), which turns to a related point; lesson 27 teaches it fully;
- the words of the law ({法规|fǎ guī}, {法官|fǎ guān}, {公正|gōng zhèng}, {权力|quán lì}, {公民|gōng mín}, {投诉|tóu sù}, {赔偿|péi cháng}…), of crime ({偷|tōu}, {骗子|piàn zi}, {逃跑|táo pǎo}, {罪|zuì}…) and of traffic
  ({机动车|jī dòng chē}, {时速|shí sù}, {路况|lù kuàng}, {刹车|shā chē}, {倒车|dào chē}, {拐弯|guǎi wān}…);
- a case told twice: as a news report (written) and as you'd tell a friend (spoken).

The law here is everyday law: shops, roads, contracts and privacy. Words of public life such as {民主|mín zhǔ} and
{权力|quán lì} are taught as words, with plain examples.

## {除|chú}…({以|yǐ}){外|wài}: except, besides

HSK 3's {除了|chú le}…{以外|yǐ wài} is the spoken frame. Its written form drops {了|le}: {除|chú} + noun or clause + {外|wài} (or {以外|yǐ wài}). Like
{除了|chú le}…{以外|yǐ wài}, it has two meanings, decided by what follows:

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {除|chú} A ({以|yǐ}){外|wài}，{都|dōu} / {一律|yí lǜ}… | except A: A is left out | {除|chú}{节假日|jié jià rì}{外|wài}，{博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{开放|kāi fàng}。 The museum is open every day except public holidays. |
| {除|chú} A ({以|yǐ}){外|wài}，{还|hái} / {也|yě}… | besides A: A is included | {除|chú}{赔偿|péi cháng}{损失|sǔn shī}{外|wài}，{商店|shāng diàn}{还|hái}{要|yào}{公开|gōng kāi}{道歉|dào qiàn}。 Besides compensating for the loss, the shop must apologise publicly. |

{节假日|jié jià rì} (jiéjiàrì): public holidays. {损失|sǔn shī} (sǔnshī, HSK 5): a loss. {一律|yí lǜ} (yílǜ, lesson 27): all, without exception.

It's at home on notices, in rules and in news: {除|chú}{本人|běn rén}{外|wài}，{任何|rèn hé}{人|rén}{不得|bù dé}{代领|dài lǐng}。 (No one but the person concerned may
collect it on their behalf. {本人|běn rén}, the person themself; {代领|dài lǐng} dàilǐng, to collect for someone else; {不得|bù dé} is lesson
27's "must not".) In speech, use {除了|chú le}…{以外|yǐ wài} (or just {除了|chú le}…): {除了|chú le}{周末|zhōu mò}，{我|wǒ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{上班|shàng bān}。

{除|chú} itself is one of the level's **[[written prepositions]]** (with {于|yú} of lesson 08, and {因|yīn} and {至于|zhì yú}): short,
formal words of the written register that have longer spoken partners ({除|chú} / {除了|chú le}, {于|yú} / {比|bǐ}, {因|yīn} / {因为|yīn wèi}).

## {至于|zhì yú}: as for…

{至于|zhì yú} (zhìyú) moves from what has been said to a related point, often one that is less certain or less
important: "as for…, as to…".

{商店|shāng diàn}{已经|yǐ jīng}{道歉|dào qiàn}{了|le}，{至于|zhì yú}{赔|péi}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}，{还|hái}{要|yào}{再|zài}{商量|shāng liang}。 — The shop has apologised; as for how much it will pay, that still has
to be agreed.

{我|wǒ}{只|zhǐ}{知道|zhī dào}{他|tā}{是|shì}{律师|lǜ shī}，{至于|zhì yú}{他|tā}{在|zài}{哪|nǎ}{家|jiā}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{不|bù}{清楚|qīng chu}{了|le}。 — I only know he's a lawyer; as to which firm he works for,
I couldn't say.

{至于|zhì yú} stands at the head of its clause, and what follows it is the new topic. Compare {关于|guān yú} (about, on: {关于|guān yú}{这个|zhè ge}
{问题|wèn tí}, on this question), which introduces what a whole text or talk is about; {至于|zhì yú} switches topics in the
middle. Lesson 27 has more of it; {不至于|bú zhì yú} (not so bad as to…) is lesson 26's word.

  has it too.
- {臂|bì} is 辟 over ⺼; {壁|bì} (lesson 07) is 辟 over {土|tǔ}, {避|bì} (lesson 19) 辟 with 辶.

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. An employee of the shop that repaired her phone secretly copied some private photos and put them online.
   She went straight to the shop, refused the owner's offer of 300 yuan, complained to the consumers'
   association and sued.
2. The shop had a duty to keep customers' phones safe ({负有|fù yǒu}{保管|bǎo guǎn}{的|de}{责任|zé rèn}), and its management had an obvious gap
   ({管理|guǎn lǐ}{上|shàng}{存在|cún zài}{明显|míng xiǎn}{漏洞|lòu dòng}) that let an employee copy customers' data without permission.
3. Back up important data and delete private information before a repair; check the device and keep the
   receipt when collecting it; and if their rights are infringed, keep the evidence and use the proper
   channels.
4. Responsibility runs both ways: shops must obey the law, and consumers should also be more aware of how to
   protect their own privacy. {至于|zhì yú} turns to that last point.

"From our reporter: A court in the city recently heard a privacy dispute arising from a phone repair. The
judge ruled that the repair shop had violated a customer's privacy and should apologise publicly and
compensate her for her loss.

In March this year, Ms Shao's phone screen broke, and she took it to a repair shop near her home. Pressed for
time, she didn't back up or delete the photos and files on it first. A week later she found that several of
her private photos had, to her astonishment, appeared online. An investigation showed that a member of the
shop's staff had secretly copied and uploaded them while repairing the phone.

Ms Shao went straight to the shop and asked the owner to explain. At first he denied it; later he offered
her 300 yuan as compensation, hoping she would let the matter drop. She refused. She complained first to the
consumers' association, then sued, asking that the shop apologise publicly and compensate her for her
distress.

After hearing the case, the court held that citizens' personal privacy is protected by law. The repair shop
was responsible for keeping customers' phones safe; an employee had copied a customer's data without
permission, and there was an obvious gap in the shop's management, so it must bear responsibility. The judge
also pointed out that once the problem came to light the shop neither deleted the photos promptly nor
contacted the customer, so the harm grew further. Besides
apologising publicly, it must pay Ms Shao 5,000 yuan. The employee involved has been dismissed, and the market
regulation bureau has issued the shop with a warning and a fine.

The judge advises consumers to back up important data and delete private information before sending a phone
or computer for repair, to check for anything unusual when collecting the device, and to keep the receipt. If
their rights are infringed, they should keep the evidence promptly and defend their rights through the proper
channels.

A lawyer said that such cases have not been rare in recent years. Everyone is equal before the law, and
businesses, large or small, must obey the regulations. He suggested that repair shops set up stricter rules,
such as asking customers to be present during a repair and not opening their private files at will. As for consumers themselves, they too should become
more aware of protecting their privacy."

in about a minute and a half). Keep the order of events, use your own words, and turn the written register
into speech. Read this passage twice, cover it, and retell it.

> {上|shàng}{个|gè}{月|yuè}，{我|wǒ}{坐|zuò}{长途|cháng tú}{客车|kè chē}{回|huí}{老家|lǎo jiā}。{车|chē}{上|shàng}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{多|duō}，{我|wǒ}{坐|zuò}{在|zài}{最后|zuì hòu}{一|yì}{排|pái}。{车|chē}{开|kāi}{了|le}{不久|bù jiǔ}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{开始|kāi shǐ}{晕车|yùn chē}，{头晕|tóu yūn}、{恶心|ě xīn}，{一路|yí lù}{上|shang}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。{到|dào}{站|zhàn}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{我|wǒ}{迷迷糊糊|mí mí hū hū}{地|de}{下|xià}{了|le}{车|chē}，{走|zǒu}{出|chū}{车站|chē zhàn}{才|cái}{发现|fā xiàn}，{钱包|qián bāo}{不见|bú jiàn}{了|le}，{里面|lǐ miàn}{有|yǒu}{身份证|shēn fèn zhèng}、{银行卡|yín háng kǎ}{和|hé}{一些|yì xiē}{现金|xiàn jīn}。{我|wǒ}{一下子|yí xià zi}{急|jí}{哭|kū}{了|le}，{以为|yǐ wéi}{是|shì}{被|bèi}{小偷儿|xiǎo tōur}{偷|tōu}{了|le}，{赶紧|gǎn jǐn}{去|qù}{车站|chē zhàn}{的|de}{公安|gōng ān}{值班室|zhí bān shì}{报警|bào jǐng}。{值班|zhí bān}{的|de}{警察|jǐng chá}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{先|xiān}{别|bié}{着急|zháo jí}，{说|shuō}{他们|tā men}{会|huì}{马上|mǎ shàng}{联系|lián xì}{车站|chē zhàn}{和|hé}{司机|sī jī}。{警察|jǐng chá}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{登记|dēng jì}{了|le}{一下|yí xià}，{没|méi}{过|guò}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}，{司机|sī jī}{就|jiù}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}{车|chē}{回来|huí lái}{了|le}。{司机|sī jī}{是|shì}{一|yí}{位|wèi}{四十|sì shí}{多|duō}{岁|suì}{的|de}{师傅|shī fu}，{他|tā}{说|shuō}{他|tā}{开|kāi}{了|le}{二十|èr shí}{年|nián}{车|chē}，{这样|zhè yàng}{的|de}{事|shì}{碰|pèng}{到|dào}{过|guo}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{次|cì}。{原来|yuán lái}，{我|wǒ}{下|xià}{车|chē}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{钱包|qián bāo}{从|cóng}{口袋|kǒu dài}{里|lǐ}{掉|diào}{了|le}{出来|chū lái}，{掉|diào}{在|zài}{了|le}{座位|zuò wèi}{下面|xià miàn}。{司机|sī jī}{打扫|dǎ sǎo}{车厢|chē xiāng}{时|shí}{发现|fā xiàn}{了|le}{它|tā}，{就|jiù}{开车|kāi chē}{送|sòng}{了|le}{回来|huí lái}。{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{给|gěi}{他|tā}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{钱|qián}{表示|biǎo shì}{感谢|gǎn xiè}，{他|tā}{怎么|zěn me}{也|yě}{不|bù}{肯|kěn}{收|shōu}，{只|zhǐ}{说|shuō}："{物归原主|wù guī yuán zhǔ}，{这|zhè}{是|shì}{应该|yīng gāi}{的|de}。"{我|wǒ}{连|lián}{说|shuō}{了|le}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{声|shēng}{谢谢|xiè xie}，{心里|xīn li}{特别|tè bié}{感动|gǎn dòng}。{从|cóng}{那|nà}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{每|měi}{次|cì}{坐|zuò}{车|chē}，{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{会|huì}{把|bǎ}{贵重|guì zhòng}{物品|wù pǐn}{保管|bǎo guǎn}{好|hǎo}，{也|yě}{会|huì}{想|xiǎng}{起|qǐ}{那|nà}{位|wèi}{司机|sī jī}。

{长途|cháng tú} (chángtú): long-distance. {迷迷糊糊|mí mí hū hū} (mímí hūhū): half asleep, in a daze. {身份证|shēn fèn zhèng} (shēnfènzhèng, HSK 5): an ID card.
{值班室|zhí bān shì} (zhíbānshì): the duty office; {值班|zhí bān} is lesson 01's word. {报警|bào jǐng} (bàojǐng): to report to the police. {车厢|chē xiāng}
(chēxiāng): the inside of a coach or carriage. {肯|kěn} (kěn, lesson 22): to be willing. {物归原主|wù guī yuán zhǔ} (wù guī yuán zhǔ): to
return something to its owner (a set phrase).

<details>
<summary>A model retelling</summary>

{这|zhè}{个|gè}{人|rén}{上|shàng}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{坐|zuò}{长途|cháng tú}{客车|kè chē}{回|huí}{老家|lǎo jiā}，{一|yí}{上|shàng}{车|chē}{就|jiù}{晕车|yùn chē}，{一路|yí lù}{上|shang}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。{下|xià}{车|chē}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{他|tā}{发现|fā xiàn}{钱包|qián bāo}{没|méi}{了|le}，{里面|lǐ miàn}{有|yǒu}{身份证|shēn fèn zhèng}、{银行卡|yín háng kǎ}{和|hé}{钱|qián}。{他|tā}{很|hěn}{着急|zháo jí}，{以为|yǐ wéi}{碰|pèng}{到|dào}{小偷儿|xiǎo tōur}{了|le}，{就|jiù}{去|qù}{车站|chē zhàn}{找|zhǎo}{警察|jǐng chá}。{警察|jǐng chá}{帮|bāng}{他|tā}{联系|lián xì}{了|le}{司机|sī jī}。{不|bú}{到|dào}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}，{司机|sī jī}{就|jiù}{把|bǎ}{钱包|qián bāo}{送|sòng}{回来|huí lái}{了|le}。{原来|yuán lái}{钱包|qián bāo}{是|shì}{他|tā}{下|xià}{车|chē}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{掉|diào}{在|zài}{座位|zuò wèi}{下面|xià miàn}{的|de}，{司机|sī jī}{打扫|dǎ sǎo}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{捡|jiǎn}{到|dào}{了|le}。{他|tā}{想|xiǎng}{给|gěi}{司机|sī jī}{钱|qián}，{司机|sī jī}{说什么也|shuō shén me yě}{不要|bú yào}，{说|shuō}{东西|dōng xi}{还|hái}{给|gěi}{主人|zhǔ rén}{是|shì}{应该|yīng gāi}{的|de}。{他|tā}{很|hěn}{感动|gǎn dòng}，{现在|xiàn zài}{坐|zuò}{车|chē}{都|dōu}{会|huì}{把|bǎ}{钱包|qián bāo}{什么|shén me}{的|de}{放|fàng}{好|hǎo}。

(The written {保管|bǎo guǎn}{好|hǎo}{贵重|guì zhòng}{物品|wù pǐn} becomes {把|bǎ}{钱包|qián bāo}{什么|shén me}{的|de}{放|fàng}{好|hǎo}; {物归原主|wù guī yuán zhǔ} becomes {东西|dōng xi}{还|hái}{给|gěi}{主人|zhǔ rén}; {发现|fā xiàn}{了|le}{它|tā} becomes {捡|jiǎn}{到|dào}{了|le}. {捡|jiǎn} jiǎn, HSK 5:
to pick up.)

"Last month this person took a long-distance coach home and got carsick as soon as they got on, so they slept
all the way. After getting off, they found their wallet was gone, with their ID card, bank card and money in
it. They were very worried and thought they'd met a thief, so they went to find the police at the station. The
police contacted the driver for them. Within half an hour the driver brought the wallet back. It turned out the
wallet had fallen under the seat when they got off, and the driver had picked it up while cleaning. They wanted
to give the driver some money, but the driver wouldn't take any, saying it was only right to give things back to
their owner. They were very moved, and now whenever they travel they put their wallet and so on somewhere safe."
</details>

## Write it: a formal complaint

Write a complaint (150–200 characters) to a shop's customer service: what you bought or what service you
used, when, what went wrong, what you've already done, and what you want. Formal register: {本人|běn rén}, {于|yú}, {因|yīn}, {望|wàng}, {特此|tè cǐ}.

<details>
<summary>A model complaint</summary>

{关于|guān yú}{电脑|diàn nǎo}{维修|wéi xiū}{问题|wèn tí}{的|de}{投诉|tóu sù}

{尊敬|zūn jìng}{的|de}{客服|kè fú}{部门|bù mén}：

{本人|běn rén}{于|yú}{十|shí}{月|yuè}{八|bā}{日|rì}{在|zài}{贵店|guì diàn}{维修|wéi xiū}{一|yì}{台|tái}{笔记本电脑|bǐ jì běn diàn nǎo}，{当时|dāng shí}{店员|diàn yuán}{承诺|chéng nuò}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{内|nèi}{修|xiū}{好|hǎo}，{维修|wéi xiū}{费|fèi}{四百|sì bǎi}{元|yuán}。{可是|kě shì}{直到|zhí dào}{十|shí}{月|yuè}{十五|shí wǔ}{日|rì}，{我|wǒ}{才|cái}{拿|ná}{到|dào}{电脑|diàn nǎo}，{比|bǐ}{约定|yuē dìng}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}{四|sì}{天|tiān}。{更|gèng}{严重|yán zhòng}{的|de}{是|shì}，{回|huí}{家|jiā}{以后|yǐ hòu}{我|wǒ}{发现|fā xiàn}，{电脑|diàn nǎo}{的|de}{问题|wèn tí}{并|bìng}{没有|méi yǒu}{解决|jiě jué}，{开机|kāi jī}{后|hòu}{几|jǐ}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{会|huì}{自动|zì dòng}{关机|guān jī}，{而且|ér qiě}{屏幕|píng mù}{边|biān}{上|shàng}{还|hái}{被|bèi}{弄坏|nòng huài}{了|le}{一|yí}{块|kuài}。

{本人|běn rén}{已经|yǐ jīng}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}{联系|lián xì}{贵店|guì diàn}，{店员|diàn yuán}{只|zhǐ}{说|shuō}"{再|zài}{看看|kàn kan}"，{一直|yì zhí}{没有|méi yǒu}{给|gěi}{出|chū}{明确|míng què}{答复|dá fù}。{因此|yīn cǐ}，{特此|tè cǐ}{向|xiàng}{贵店|guì diàn}{投诉|tóu sù}，{希望|xī wàng}{贵店|guì diàn}{在|zài}{一|yì}{周|zhōu}{内|nèi}{重新|chóng xīn}{免费|miǎn fèi}{维修|wéi xiū}，{并|bìng}{赔偿|péi cháng}{屏幕|píng mù}{的|de}{损坏|sǔn huài}。{否则|fǒu zé}，{本人|běn rén}{将|jiāng}{向|xiàng}{消费者|xiāo fèi zhě}{协会|xié huì}{反映|fǎn yìng}。

{望|wàng}{早日|zǎo rì}{回复|huí fù}。

{顾客|gù kè}：{金晨|Jīn Chén}
{十|shí}{月|yuè}{十八|shí bā}{日|rì}

(About 200 characters. {客服|kè fú} kèfú, customer service; {贵店|guì diàn} guìdiàn, your shop (polite); {笔记本电脑|bǐ jì běn diàn nǎo} bǐjìběn diànnǎo, a
laptop; {承诺|chéng nuò} chéngnuò, lesson 02, to promise; {约定|yuē dìng} yuēdìng, agreed; {弄坏|nòng huài} nònghuài, to damage; {明确|míng què} míngquè, HSK 5,
clear; {特此|tè cǐ} tècǐ, hereby; {金晨|Jīn Chén} Jīn Chén, the customer.)

"Complaint about a computer repair. To the customer service department: On 8 October I brought a laptop to your
shop for repair. The assistant promised it would be fixed within three days, for 400 yuan. But I didn't get it
back until 15 October, four days later than agreed. Worse, when I got home I found the problem hadn't been
solved: the computer shuts itself down a few minutes after starting, and the edge of the screen has been damaged. I
have phoned your shop twice; the assistant only said 'we'll look into it' and has never given me a clear answer.
I therefore hereby complain, and ask that you repair it again free of charge within a week and pay for the
damage to the screen. Otherwise I shall report the matter to the consumers' association. I look forward to an
early reply. Customer: Jin Chen, 18 October"

## Say it

```speak
# Rules and the road
{前面|qián miàn}{路口|lù kǒu}{往|wǎng}{左|zuǒ}{拐|guǎi}。

{今天|jīn tiān}{路况|lù kuàng}{不错|bú cuò}，{挺|tǐng}{畅通|chàng tōng}{的|de}。
= The roads are fine today: the traffic's moving nicely.
{除|chú}{节假日|jié jià rì}{外|wài}，{博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{开放|kāi fàng}。
= The museum is open every day except public holidays.
{赔偿|péi cháng}{的|de}{事|shì}{已经|yǐ jīng}{解决|jiě jué}{了|le}，{至于|zhì yú}{以后|yǐ hòu}{怎么办|zěn me bàn}，{再|zài}{商量|shāng liang}{吧|ba}。
= The compensation's been sorted out; as for what happens next, let's talk about it later.
{请|qǐng}{保管|bǎo guǎn}{好|hǎo}{您|nín}{的|de}{贵重|guì zhòng}{物品|wù pǐn}。
= Please look after your valuables.

```

## Pronunciation

- {处罚|chǔ fá} chǔfá: 处 is chǔ (to deal with), as in {处理|chǔ lǐ}; chù is "a place" ({好处|hǎo chù}).
- {刹车|shā chē} shāchē: {刹|shā} is shā here (chà in Buddhist words, not in this course).
- {晕车|yùn chē} yùnchē, but {晕|yūn} yūn alone (dizzy).
- {倒车|dào chē} dàochē (to reverse): 倒 is dào, as in {倒水|dào shuǐ}; dǎo is "to fall" ({摔倒|shuāi dǎo}).
- {塞|sāi} sāi (to stuff); it's sài in {边塞|biān sài} (a frontier fortress, in poems).
- {当场|dāng chǎng} dāngchǎng: 当 is dāng, "right at (that place)".
- {权力|quán lì} quánlì and {权利|quán lì} quánlì sound exactly the same: tell them apart by context and by the character ({力|lì} power,
  {利|lì} benefit, a right).

## Common mistakes

- {除|chú}…{外|wài} is written. In a chat, {除了|chú le}…({以外|yǐ wài}) is the natural form: {除了|chú le}{你|nǐ}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{来|lái}{了|le}.
- Watch what follows: {除|chú} A {外|wài}，{都|dōu}… leaves A out; {除|chú} A {外|wài}，{还|hái}… adds A. {除|chú}{他|tā}{外|wài}，{我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{去|qù}{了|le} (he didn't go); {除|chú}{他|tā}{外|wài}，{我们|wǒ men}
  {也|yě}{去|qù}{了|le} (he went, and so did we).
- {至于|zhì yú} changes the topic; {关于|guān yú} states it. Not ~~{至于|zhì yú}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}，{我|wǒ}{写|xiě}{了|le}{一|yì}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng}~~ for "I've written an article on
  this question": that's {关于|guān yú}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}.
- {赔偿|péi cháng} is for harm done: {商店|shāng diàn}{赔偿|péi cháng}{了|le}{顾客|gù kè}{的|de}{损失|sǔn shī}. For a refund of the price, say {退|tuì}{钱|qián} or {退|tuì}{款|kuǎn}.
- {偷|tōu} is the action; the person is {小偷儿|xiǎo tōur} (spoken) or, in news, {盗窃|dào qiè} suspects ({盗窃|dào qiè} dàoqiè, theft: not a course
  word).
- {上当|shàng dàng} is separable: {上|shàng}{了|le}{他|tā}{的|de}{当|dàng} (fell for his trick).

## Key points

- {除|chú} A ({以|yǐ}){外|wài}，{都|dōu} / {一律|yí lǜ}… (except A) / {还|hái} / {也|yě}… (besides A): written; spoken {除了|chú le}…{以外|yǐ wài}.
- {至于|zhì yú}…: as for…, turning to a related point. {关于|guān yú}: about, on.
- Written prepositions so far: {于|yú} (lesson 08), {除|chú}, and {因|yīn} and {至于|zhì yú} (lesson 27).
- The law: {法规|fǎ guī}, {法定|fǎ dìng}, {法官|fǎ guān}, {案例|àn lì}, {档案|dàng àn}, {纠纷|jiū fēn}, {投诉|tóu sù}, {赔偿|péi cháng}, {补偿|bǔ cháng}, {弥补|mí bǔ}, {追究|zhuī jiū}, {撤销|chè xiāo}, {维护|wéi hù}, {隐私|yǐn sī}, {公正|gōng zhèng}, {正义|zhèng yì}, {平等|píng děng}, {公民|gōng mín},
  {权力|quán lì}, {民主|mín zhǔ}.
- Crime: {偷|tōu}, {小偷儿|xiǎo tōur}, {骗子|piàn zi}, {上当|shàng dàng}, {掏|tāo}, {逃|táo}, {逃跑|táo pǎo}, {害|hài}, {暴力|bào lì}, {犯|fàn}, {罪|zuì}, {牢|láo}, {处罚|chǔ fá}, {惩罚|chéng fá}, {警告|jǐng gào}, {违规|wéi guī}, {当场|dāng chǎng}, {漏洞|lòu dòng}, {公安|gōng ān}, {局|jú}.
- The road: {机动车|jī dòng chē}, {摩托车|mó tuō chē}, {客车|kè chē}, {时速|shí sù}, {路况|lù kuàng}, {路面|lù miàn}, {畅通|chàng tōng}, {刹车|shā chē}, {倒车|dào chē}, {拐|guǎi}, {拐弯|guǎi wān}, {拦|lán}, {塞|sāi}, {晕车|yùn chē}.
- New characters: {腔|qiāng} {疫|yì} {嗓|sǎng} {舌|shé} {臂|bì} {吐|tǔ} {胞|bāo} {菌|jūn} {胸|xiōng} {液|yè} {症|zhèng} {抑|yì} {痒|yǎng} {肿|zhǒng} {晕|yūn} {偿|cháng} {惩|chéng} {畅|chàng} {官|guān} {犯|fàn} (✎ {舌|shé} {吐|tǔ} {抑|yì} {肿|zhǒng} {晕|yūn} {畅|chàng} {官|guān} {犯|fàn}).

lessons.title: News, media and commentary
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The level-6 task of this lesson is **[[commenting on a news article]]**: saying what happened, what you think
of it and why, in the register of a commentary. {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) writes commentary pieces for the news
website now, with {郑华|Zhèng Huá} (Zheng Hua) as her editor. You'll see them plan a piece, read the piece itself and a
reader's reply, and write a letter to the editor.

- **{不料|bú liào}** (unexpectedly, who would have thought), the written partner of {没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào};
- the time words of the news: {日前|rì qián} (a few days ago), {近来|jìn lái} (lately), {当今|dāng jīn} / {当下|dāng xià} (nowadays, at present), beside
  HSK 5's {近日|jìn rì} and {如今|rú jīn}, and {据|jù}…{报道|bào dào} (according to … reports) again;

  {正面|zhèng miàn} / {负面|fù miàn}, {真相|zhēn xiàng}, {透露|tòu lù}…).

## {不料|bú liào}: unexpectedly

{不料|bú liào} (búliào, "not expected") opens the second clause of a story: what happened was not what anyone
expected. It's written; in speech, {没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}. It often comes after {本来|běn lái} / {原|yuán}{以为|yǐ wéi} (had thought), and can be followed
by {却|què} or {竟然|jìng rán} for extra surprise.

{我|wǒ}{原|yuán}{以为|yǐ wéi}{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{新闻|xīn wén}{没|méi}{人|rén}{关注|guān zhù}，{不料|bú liào}{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{就|jiù}{成|chéng}{了|le}{热点|rè diǎn}。 — I thought no one would notice this story; who'd have thought it would be a hot topic the next day.

{他们|tā men}{本来|běn lái}{打算|dǎ suàn}{周末|zhōu mò}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}，{不料|bú liào}{下|xià}{起|qǐ}{了|le}{大|dà}{雨|yǔ}。 — They'd planned to go hiking at the weekend, but it unexpectedly poured with rain.

| Word | Register | Position | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| {不料|bú liào} | written | starts the second clause | {不料|bú liào}{天|tiān}{下|xià}{起|qǐ}{了|le}{雨|yǔ}。 |
| {没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào} | spoken | starts the clause, or {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}… | {没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}。 / {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}{会|huì}{下雨|xià yǔ}。 |
| {竟然|jìng rán} (HSK 4) | both | before the verb | {天|tiān}{竟然|jìng rán}{下|xià}{起|qǐ}{了|le}{雨|yǔ}。 |

{不料|bú liào} has no subject of its own: not ~~{我|wǒ}{不料|bú liào}{他|tā}{会|huì}{来|lái}~~ (that's {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}{他|tā}{会|huì}{来|lái}). It looks back from what happened:
it isn't used for the future.

## {据|jù}…{报道|bào dào}: according to … reports

HSK 5's {据|jù} (according to) heads the source of a piece of news: {据|jù}{报道|bào dào} (according to reports), {据|jù}{本网|běn wǎng}{记者|jì zhě}{报道|bào dào}
(according to our reporter), {据|jù}{了解|liǎo jiě} (it is understood that), {据|jù}{官方|guān fāng}{消息|xiāo xi} (according to official information).
{据|jù} + source + {报道|bào dào} / {介绍|jiè shào} / {透露|tòu lù} / {统计|tǒng jì}: {据|jù}{业内人士|yè nèi rén shì}{透露|tòu lù} (according to people in the industry). The news then
follows the comma. A commentary uses it to say where a fact came from, before giving a view on it.

{人士|rén shì} (rénshì) is a person, a figure, always with a describing word: {业内人士|yè nèi rén shì} (people in the trade), {知情人士|zhī qíng rén shì}
(informed sources), {各界人士|gè jiè rén shì} (people from all walks of life). {透露|tòu lù} (tòulù) is to reveal, disclose (a little,
not everything): {他|tā}{透露|tòu lù}，{新|xīn}{书|shū}{明年|míng nián}{发行|fā xíng} (he revealed that the new book would come out next year). {统计|tǒng jì} (tǒngjì, HSK 5):
statistics.

### A new radical: 罒

罒 ("net", a flattened form of {网|wǎng}) is the radical of three characters of levels 1–6: {置|zhì} ({位置|wèi zhì}, HSK 5), {罚|fá} ({罚款|fá kuǎn},
HSK 5) and {罪|zuì} (here). It sits on top: 罒 over {非|fēi} is {罪|zuì}. It has five strokes: a vertical, a horizontal-turning stroke, two short
verticals and a horizontal.

### Sound parts across the levels

- 扁 biǎn in {编|biān} biān, as in {遍|biàn} biàn, {篇|piān} piān and {骗|piàn} piàn ({骗子|piàn zi}, lesson 09): a b- and p- family.

- {同|tóng} tóng in {筒|tǒng} tǒng (⺮ + {同|tóng}), {铜|tóng} tóng (lesson 14) and {洞|dòng} dòng ({漏洞|lòu dòng}, lesson 09).
- {兰|lán} lán in {拦|lán} lán and {栏|lán} lán, and {烂|làn} làn (lesson 12). In traditional they're 攔, 欄, 爛, all with 闌.
- 巨 jù in {渠|qú} qú, as in {拒|jù} jù ({拒绝|jù jué}) and {距|jù} jù ({距离|jù lí}).
- 兆 zhào in {逃|táo} táo, as in {桃|táo} táo, {跳|tiào} tiào and {挑|tiāo} tiāo: t- syllables.

### Look-alikes and stroke traps

- {塞|sāi} sāi and {寒|hán} hán ({寒冷|hán lěng}, HSK 4): the same top; {塞|sāi} ends in {土|tǔ}, {寒|hán} in two dots.
- {牢|láo} is 宀 over {牛|niú}: a memory aid is an ox in a pen.
- {归|guī}: two short strokes on the left (a short vertical and a left-falling stroke), then 彐 (a horizontal-turning
  stroke and two horizontals). 5 strokes.
- {拐|guǎi}: 扌 + {口|kǒu} + {力|lì}: {口|kǒu} over {力|lì}, not {刀|dāo}.

"Don't let the truth run behind the buzz. Last week a video claiming that a popular snack 'contains harmful
substances' spread rapidly online and was shared hundreds of thousands of times within two days.
Unexpectedly, the test results published a few days ago by the market regulation bureau showed that the snack
fully meets national standards. By then, however, the video's moment had long passed; few people shared the
correction, and the company's sales were noticeably hit.

This isn't an isolated case. Lately, something similar keeps happening: a story becomes a hot topic and sets
off heated discussion, and only days later do people learn that the truth is quite different from the first
version: one says two foods mustn't be eaten together, another that something big has happened somewhere, and
both later turn out to be false. In today's new-media age, anyone can publish news, and information spreads faster than ever before.
Yet what runs fastest is often not the truth but the most eye-catching story.

Why is this? First, negative news worries people more and is more easily shared. Second, some posters
deliberately write exaggerated headlines to chase clicks. Also, some media, to save time, report without
checking properly, turning false information into the 'mainstream' voice.

Of course, that doesn't mean we should ask people to stop sharing or discussing. The public cares about food
safety, which in itself is a good thing, and many important leads come first from ordinary internet users.
The problem lies not in discussion but in whether, before we discuss, we first ask: 'Is this true?'

For the media: better a little slower, so long as it's accurate. For every reader: when you see shocking
news, you might as well wait a moment and see what official channels and experts say. The truth sometimes
comes slowly, but at least we can stop it running behind the buzz.

Comment from user 'Lao Zhou reads the news': Reporter Wang makes a fair point, but I don't think it's quite
fair to ask only readers to 'wait a moment'. Ordinary people have neither the time nor the ability to check
every story. The reason no one reads corrections is that they're usually short and late. I hope that when
the media correct a rumour, they'll give it as prominent a place as they gave the rumour, so that the truth
gets some buzz too."
</details>

## Write it: a letter to the editor

Write a letter (150–200 characters) to the editor of a news website about a story you read there: which story,
what you think of it, one fact or experience that supports your view, and a suggestion. Use the letter
format: {尊敬|zūn jìng}{的|de}{编辑|biān jí}, your text, {此致|cǐ zhì} / {敬礼|jìng lǐ}, your name and the date.

<details>
<summary>A model letter</summary>

{尊敬|zūn jìng}{的|de}{编辑|biān jí}：

{您|nín}{好|hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{贵网站|guì wǎng zhàn}{的|de}{一|yì}{名|míng}{老|lǎo}{读者|dú zhě}。{日前|rì qián}，{我|wǒ}{读|dú}{了|le}{贵网站|guì wǎng zhàn}{关于|guān yú}"{老|lǎo}{小区|xiǎo qū}{改造|gǎi zào}"{的|de}{系列|xì liè}{报道|bào dào}，{很|hěn}{受|shòu}{启发|qǐ fā}。{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{住|zhù}{的|de}{也|yě}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{八十|bā shí}{年代|nián dài}{的|de}{老|lǎo}{小区|xiǎo qū}，{没有|méi yǒu}{电梯|diàn tī}，{楼道|lóu dào}{很|hěn}{暗|àn}，{我|wǒ}{父母|fù mǔ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{上下|shàng xià}{楼|lóu}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{困难|kùn nan}。

{报道|bào dào}{里|lǐ}{介绍|jiè shào}{的|de}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{小区|xiǎo qū}{改造|gǎi zào}{的|de}{案例|àn lì}{很|hěn}{贴近|tiē jìn}{生活|shēng huó}，{特别|tè bié}{是|shì}{社区|shè qū}{工作|gōng zuò}{人员|rén yuán}{一|yí}{户|hù}{一|yí}{户|hù}{上门|shàng mén}{沟通|gōu tōng}{的|de}{做法|zuò fǎ}，{值得|zhí de}{其他|qí tā}{地方|dì fang}{学习|xué xí}。{不过|bú guò}，{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{报道|bào dào}{多|duō}{是|shì}{正面|zhèng miàn}{的|de}{内容|nèi róng}，{对|duì}{改造|gǎi zào}{中|zhōng}{遇到|yù dào}{的|de}{问题|wèn tí}{谈|tán}{得|de}{比较|bǐ jiào}{少|shǎo}，{比如|bǐ rú}{费用|fèi yòng}{由|yóu}{谁|shéi}{出|chū}、{施工|shī gōng}{噪声|zào shēng}{怎么|zěn me}{解决|jiě jué}。

{希望|xī wàng}{贵网站|guì wǎng zhàn}{能|néng}{再|zài}{做|zuò}{一|yì}{期|qī}{专题|zhuān tí}，{请|qǐng}{居民|jū mín}、{专家|zhuān jiā}{和|hé}{社区|shè qū}{一起|yì qǐ}{来|lái}{谈一谈|tán yi tán}{这些|zhè xiē}{问题|wèn tí}。

{此致|cǐ zhì}
{敬礼|jìng lǐ}！

{读者|dú zhě}　{卜文|Bǔ Wén}
{十一|shí yī}{月|yuè}{二十|èr shí}{日|rì}

(About 200 characters. {贵网站|guì wǎng zhàn} guì wǎngzhàn, your website (polite); {启发|qǐ fā} qǐfā, lesson 24, inspiration; {做法|zuò fǎ} zuòfǎ, a
way of doing things; {费用|fèi yòng} fèiyòng, HSK 5, the cost; {一|yì}{期|qī} yì qī, an issue; {此致|cǐ zhì}{敬礼|jìng lǐ} cǐzhì jìnglǐ, the formal close of
a letter, "with respect"; {卜文|Bǔ Wén} Bǔ Wén, the reader.)

"Dear Editor, I am a long-time reader of your website. A few days ago I read your series of reports on
renovating old housing compounds and found it very thought-provoking. My family also lives in an old compound
from the eighties: there's no lift and the stairwells are dark, and my parents find the stairs hard every day.
The cases the reports describe are close to real life, especially the way the community workers went to talk
to each household in turn, which other places could learn from. However, I feel the reports were mostly
positive and said little about the problems that come up, such as who pays and how to deal with the building
noise. I hope you can do another feature in which residents, experts and the community discuss these
questions. Yours respectfully, a reader, Bu Wen, 20 November"
</details>

## Say it
