## Pronunciation

- {不料|bú liào} búliào: 不 is bú before the fourth tone of 料.
- {当今|dāng jīn} dāngjīn, {当下|dāng xià} dāngxià, {当选|dāng xuǎn} dāngxuǎn: 当 is dāng in all three.
- {名气|míng qi} míngqi: a light {气|qì}. {稿子|gǎo zi} gǎozi: a light {子|zi}.
- {编|biān} biān and {版|bǎn} bǎn: first and third tones; {编辑|biān jí} biānjí.
- {栏|lán} lán and {拦|lán} lán (to block, lesson 09): the same syllable, different radicals ({木|mù} and 扌).
- {话筒|huà tǒng} huàtǒng: {筒|tǒng} is tǒng, third tone.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{不料|bú liào}{他|tā}{会|huì}{来|lái}~~: {不料|bú liào} doesn't take a subject or an object clause. Say {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}{他|tā}{会|huì}{来|lái}, or {本来|běn lái}{以为|yǐ wéi}{他|tā}{不|bú}{会|huì}{来|lái}，{不料|bú liào}{他|tā}{来|lái}{了|le}.
- {不料|bú liào} is written: in a chat, {没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào} sounds natural; {不料|bú liào} sounds like a story or a news report.
- {日前|rì qián} is "a few days ago", not "before the day" or "at present". {目前|mù qián} (HSK 4) is "at present".
- {议论|yì lùn} can sound like gossip: {大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{背后|bèi hòu}{议论|yì lùn}{他|tā}. To discuss a question openly, {讨论|tǎo lùn} or {评论|píng lùn}.
- {群众|qún zhòng} in everyday use is "people, bystanders": {围观|wéi guān}{群众|qún zhòng}, {群众演员|qún zhòng yǎn yuán}. For "the public" in a news report, {公众|gōng zhòng} or {民众|mín zhòng}.
- {出名|chū míng} is a verb or adjective: {他|tā}{出名|chū míng}{了|le}, {一|yí}{个|gè}{很|hěn}{出名|chū míng}{的|de}{作家|zuò jiā}. The noun is {名气|míng qi}: {他|tā}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{名气|míng qi}.

## Key points

- {不料|bú liào}: unexpectedly (written), starting the second clause; spoken {没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}.
- News time words: {日前|rì qián}, {近日|jìn rì} (a recent event), {近来|jìn lái} (a recent trend), {当今|dāng jīn}, {当下|dāng xià}, {如今|rú jīn}.
- {据|jù} + source + {报道|bào dào} / {透露|tòu lù} / {了解|liǎo jiě}: according to….
- Media: {报刊|bào kān}, {报社|bào shè}, {社|shè}, {编|biān}, {编辑|biān jí}, {编写|biān xiě}, {稿件|gǎo jiàn}, {稿子|gǎo zi}, {版|bǎn}, {栏|lán}, {专题|zhuān tí}, {系列|xì liè}, {发行|fā xíng}, {简介|jiǎn jiè}, {漫画|màn huà}, {访谈|fǎng tán}, {播|bō}, {频道|pín dào}, {主播|zhǔ bō}, {话筒|huà tǒng}, {麦克风|mài kè fēng},
  {热线|rè xiàn}, {新媒体|xīn méi tǐ}, {渠道|qú dào}.
- Opinion: {热点|rè diǎn}, {热门|rè mén}, {热度|rè dù}, {热议|rè yì}, {焦点|jiāo diǎn}, {动态|dòng tài}, {主流|zhǔ liú}, {评论|píng lùn}, {议论|yì lùn}, {解读|jiě dú}, {传达|chuán dá}, {得知|dé zhī}, {线索|xiàn suǒ}, {真相|zhēn xiàng}, {透露|tòu lù}, {人士|rén shì}, {公众|gōng zhòng}, {民众|mín zhòng}, {群众|qún zhòng},
  {众人|zhòng rén}, {外界|wài jiè}, {官方|guān fāng}, {正面|zhèng miàn}, {负面|fù miàn}, {公开|gōng kāi}, {贴近|tiē jìn}, {出名|chū míng}, {名气|míng qi}, {活跃|huó yuè}, {论坛|lùn tán}, {投票|tóu piào}, {当选|dāng xuǎn}.

lessons.title: Dream of the Red Chamber
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

《{红楼梦|Hóng lóu mèng}》 (*Hóng lóu mèng*, Dream of the Red Chamber) is one of the best-loved novels in Chinese. Its readers argue
about its people as if they were family, and its study has a name of its own. This honors lesson tells you
what the novel is, who wrote it (as far as anyone knows), who its main people are, and retells one famous
scene, the first meeting of {宝玉|Bǎo yù} and {黛玉|Dài yù}, in our own Chinese, with one line from the original.

## The novel and its author

《{红楼梦|Hóng lóu mèng}》 was written in the eighteenth century, under the Qing dynasty, by {曹雪芹|Cáo Xuě qín} (Cáo Xuěqín). His dates
aren't known for certain: he was born some time between 1715 and 1724 and died in 1763 or 1764. His family
had been rich and powerful in the south (in Nanjing) and lost its fortune when he was a boy; he spent his
later years in poverty outside Beijing. He worked on the novel for many years, and it first circulated in
hand-copied manuscripts under the title 《{石头记|Shí tou jì}》 (*Shítou jì*, The Story of the Stone).

The manuscripts have 80 chapters ({回|huí} huí, the chapters of a traditional novel). In 1791 two editors,
{程伟元|Chéng Wěi yuán} (Chéng Wěiyuán) and {高鹗|Gāo È} (Gāo È), published the first printed edition, with 120 chapters, and a
corrected edition the next year. Who wrote the last forty chapters is still debated: they're often
credited to {高鹗|Gāo È}, or to {高鹗|Gāo È} and {程伟元|Chéng Wěi yuán} working from manuscripts they found, and some scholars think another,
unknown writer was involved. What is generally agreed is that the first eighty chapters are {曹雪芹|Cáo Xuě qín}'s.

The study of the novel is called {红学|hóng xué} (hóngxué, "Red-ology"): scholars and amateurs study its manuscripts,
its author's life and its hundreds of characters.

## The Jia family and its garden

The novel follows the rise and fall of a great family, the {贾|Jiǎ} (Jiǎ) family, who live in two neighbouring
mansions in the capital, {荣国府|Róng guó fǔ} (Róngguó fǔ) and {宁国府|Níng guó fǔ} (Níngguó fǔ); {府|fǔ} is a great house, a mansion. They are
linked by marriage to three other great families, {史|Shǐ}, {王|Wáng} and {薛|Xuē}, and the novel is often read as the story of
how such families fall. For one of the family's daughters, who has become an imperial consort, they build a
huge garden, {大观园|Dà guān yuán} (Dàguānyuán, the Grand View Garden), where the young people of the family live and write
poems.

The main characters:

- {贾宝玉|Jiǎ Bǎo yù} (Jiǎ Bǎoyù), the son of the {荣国府|Róng guó fǔ}, born with a piece of jade ({玉|yù}) in his mouth. He hates the
  examinations and official life his father wants for him and prefers the company of his girl cousins.
- {林黛玉|Lín Dài yù} (Lín Dàiyù), his cousin, who comes to live with the family after her mother's death: clever,
  sensitive, often ill, the finest poet in the garden.
- {薛宝钗|Xuē Bǎo chāi} (Xuē Bǎochāi), another cousin: beautiful, sensible, well liked by the older generation.

The love between {宝玉|Bǎo yù} and {黛玉|Dài yù} is the heart of the book. In the 120-chapter version, the family arranges
{宝玉|Bǎo yù}'s marriage to {宝钗|Bǎo chāi}; {黛玉|Dài yù} dies of illness on the night of the wedding, and {宝玉|Bǎo yù} later leaves the world
behind. The novel has a mythical frame too: {宝玉|Bǎo yù}'s jade is said to be a stone left over when the goddess {女娲|Nǚ wā}
(Nǚwā) mended the sky.

## Reading: {黛玉|Dài yù}{进|jìn}{贾府|Jiǎ fǔ}

The scene below, from chapter 3, is retold in our own modern Chinese: only {宝玉|Bǎo yù}'s famous line {这个|zhè ge}{妹妹|mèi mei}{我|wǒ}{曾|céng}{见过|jiàn guo}{的|de} is
quoted from the original, and the rest, the speech included, is ours. Words to know: {外婆|wài pó} (wàipó, HSK 4: one's mother's mother; in the novel {黛玉|Dài yù} calls
her {外祖母|wài zǔ mǔ}), {船|chuán} (chuán: a boat), {轿子|jiào zi} (jiàozi, a sedan chair), {丫鬟|yā huan} (yāhuan, a maidservant), {打量|dǎ liang} (dǎliang, to
look someone up and down), {摔|shuāi} (shuāi, HSK 5: to throw down), {宝贝|bǎo bèi} (bǎobèi, a treasure), {规矩|guī ju} (guīju, lesson 11: rules), {怀|huái} (huái, lesson 22: the arms, one's
embrace), {吓|xià} (xià, lesson 19: to frighten), {偷偷|tōu tōu} (tōutōu, lesson 22: secretly).

> {林黛玉|Lín Dài yù}{的|de}{母亲|mǔ qīn}{去世|qù shì}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{外婆|wài pó}{一定|yí dìng}{要|yào}{接|jiē}{她|tā}{去|qù}，{父亲|fù qīn}{年纪|nián jì}{也|yě}{大|dà}{了|le}，{就|jiù}{让|ràng}{她|tā}{到|dào}{京城|jīng chéng}{的|de}{外婆|wài pó}{家|jiā}{去|qù}{住|zhù}。{黛玉|Dài yù}{那|nà}{年|nián}{年纪|nián jì}{还|hái}{小|xiǎo}，{可是|kě shì}{从小|cóng xiǎo}{就|jiù}{聪明|cōng ming}{敏感|mǐn gǎn}。{她|tā}{听|tīng}{母亲|mǔ qīn}{说|shuō}{过|guo}，{外婆|wài pó}{家|jiā}{和|hé}{别人|bié ren}{家|jiā}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}，{规矩|guī ju}{很|hěn}{多|duō}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{一路|yí lù}{上|shang}{她|tā}{就|jiù}{提醒|tí xǐng}{自己|zì jǐ}：{每|měi}{一|yí}{步|bù}{都|dōu}{要|yào}{小心|xiǎo xīn}，{每|měi}{一|yí}{句|jù}{话|huà}{都|dōu}{要|yào}{想|xiǎng}{好|hǎo}{了|le}{再说|zài shuō}，{千万|qiān wàn}{不|bù}{能|néng}{让|ràng}{人|rén}{笑话|xiào hua}。
>
> {坐|zuò}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{天|tiān}{的|de}{船|chuán}，{又|yòu}{换|huàn}{了|le}{轿子|jiào zi}，{她|tā}{终于|zhōng yú}{来|lái}{到|dào}{了|le}{荣国府|Róng guó fǔ}。{只|zhǐ}{见|jiàn}{大|dà}{门|mén}{前|qián}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}，{院子|yuàn zi}{里|lǐ}{一|yí}{处|chù}{比|bǐ}{一|yí}{处|chù}{漂亮|piào liang}，{来来往往|lái lái wǎng wǎng}{的|de}{丫鬟|yā huan}{都|dōu}{穿|chuān}{得|de}{整整齐齐|zhěng zhěng qí qí}。{外婆|wài pó}{一|yí}{见|jiàn}{到|dào}{她|tā}，{就|jiù}{把|bǎ}{她|tā}{抱|bào}{在|zài}{怀|huái}{里|lǐ}，"{心肝儿肉|xīn gānr ròu}"{地|de}{叫|jiào}{着|zhe}，{哭|kū}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}，{屋里|wū li}{的|de}{人|rén}{也|yě}{都|dōu}{跟|gēn}{着|zhe}{流|liú}{泪|lèi}。{外婆|wài pó}{说|shuō}，{在|zài}{所有|suǒ yǒu}{的|de}{孩子|hái zi}{里|lǐ}，{她|tā}{最|zuì}{疼|téng}{的|de}{就是|jiù shì}{黛玉|Dài yù}{的|de}{母亲|mǔ qīn}，{没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}{女儿|nǚ ér}{先|xiān}{走|zǒu}{了|le}，{如今|rú jīn}{只|zhǐ}{剩|shèng}{下|xià}{这个|zhè ge}{外孙女|wài sūn nǚ}。
>
> {大家|dà jiā}{正|zhèng}{说|shuō}{着|zhe}{话|huà}，{忽然|hū rán}{听见|tīng jiàn}{院子|yuàn zi}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{大|dà}{声|shēng}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}："{我|wǒ}{来|lái}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}，{没|méi}{能|néng}{迎接|yíng jiē}{从|cóng}{远处|yuǎn chù}{来|lái}{的|de}{客人|kè rén}！"{黛玉|Dài yù}{心里|xīn li}{奇怪|qí guài}：{这里|zhè lǐ}{人|rén}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{轻|qīng}{声|shēng}{说话|shuō huà}，{这|zhè}{是|shì}{谁|shéi}{这么|zhè me}{大胆|dà dǎn}？{话音刚落|huà yīn gāng luò}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{打扮|dǎ ban}{得|de}{光彩照人|guāng cǎi zhào rén}{的|de}{年轻|nián qīng}{女人|nǚ rén}{走|zǒu}{了|le}{进来|jìn lái}。{外婆|wài pó}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{向|xiàng}{黛玉|Dài yù}{介绍|jiè shào}：{这|zhè}{就是|jiù shì}{王熙凤|Wáng Xī fèng}，{府|fǔ}{里|lǐ}{上上下下|shàng shàng xià xià}{的|de}{事|shì}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{都|dōu}{由|yóu}{她|tā}{来|lái}{管|guǎn}。
>
> {后来|hòu lái}，{外婆|wài pó}{又|yòu}{说|shuō}{起|qǐ}{了|le}{她|tā}{的|de}{孙子|sūn zi}{宝玉|Bǎo yù}。{黛玉|Dài yù}{早|zǎo}{就|jiù}{听说|tīng shuō}{过|guo}，{这|zhè}{位|wèi}{表哥|biǎo gē}{最|zuì}{受|shòu}{外婆|wài pó}{宠爱|chǒng ài}，{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{谁|shéi}{也|yě}{管|guǎn}{不|bù}{了|le}{他|tā}。{她|tā}{心里|xīn li}{想|xiǎng}：{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{是|shì}{个|gè}{什么样|shén me yàng}{的|de}{人|rén}{呢|ne}？
>
> {正|zhèng}{想|xiǎng}{着|zhe}，{宝玉|Bǎo yù}{来|lái}{了|le}。{黛玉|Dài yù}{一|yí}{看|kàn}，{吃|chī}{了|le}{一|yì}{惊|jīng}：{这|zhè}{个|gè}{人|rén}{怎么|zěn me}{这么|zhè me}{眼熟|yǎn shú}，{好像|hǎo xiàng}{在|zài}{哪里|nǎ lǐ}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}{似的|shì de}。{宝玉|Bǎo yù}{也|yě}{仔细|zǐ xì}{地|de}{打量|dǎ liang}{着|zhe}{这|zhè}{位|wèi}{新|xīn}{来|lái}{的|de}{妹妹|mèi mei}，{看|kàn}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}，{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}："{这个|zhè ge}{妹妹|mèi mei}{我|wǒ}{曾|céng}{见过|jiàn guo}{的|de}。"{外婆|wài pó}{笑|xiào}{他|tā}{胡说|hú shuō}，{说|shuō}{黛玉|Dài yù}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{来|lái}，{他|tā}{怎么|zěn me}{可能|kě néng}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}。{宝玉|Bǎo yù}{却|què}{说|shuō}，{即使|jí shǐ}{没|méi}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}，{看|kàn}{着|zhe}{也|yě}{像|xiàng}{老|lǎo}{朋友|péng you}{一样|yí yàng}。
>
> {宝玉|Bǎo yù}{又|yòu}{问|wèn}{黛玉|Dài yù}："{你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{玉|yù}{没有|méi yǒu}？"{黛玉|Dài yù}{想|xiǎng}，{他|tā}{问|wèn}{的|de}{大概|dà gài}{是|shì}{他|tā}{自己|zì jǐ}{出生|chū shēng}{时|shí}{带|dài}{来|lái}{的|de}{那|nà}{块|kuài}{玉|yù}，{就|jiù}{说|shuō}："{我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}。{那么|nà me}{珍贵|zhēn guì}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}，{哪|nǎ}{能|néng}{人|rén}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{呢|ne}？"{不料|bú liào}{宝玉|Bǎo yù}{听|tīng}{了|le}，{一下子|yí xià zi}{发起|fā qǐ}{脾气|pí qi}{来|lái}，{把|bǎ}{脖子|bó zi}{上|shàng}{的|de}{玉|yù}{摘|zhāi}{下来|xià lái}，{重重|zhòng zhòng}{地|de}{摔|shuāi}{在|zài}{地上|dì shang}，{说|shuō}："{什么|shén me}{宝贝|bǎo bèi}！{姐姐|jiě jie}{妹妹|mèi mei}{们|men}{都|dōu}{没有|méi yǒu}，{就|jiù}{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}，{我|wǒ}{不要|bú yào}{了|le}！"{屋里|wū li}{的|de}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{吓|xià}{坏|huài}{了|le}，{赶紧|gǎn jǐn}{把|bǎ}{玉|yù}{捡|jiǎn}{起来|qǐ lái}。{外婆|wài pó}{一边|yì biān}{哄|hǒng}{他|tā}，{一边|yì biān}{骗|piàn}{他|tā}{说|shuō}，{黛玉|Dài yù}{本来|běn lái}{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{块|kuài}{玉|yù}，{是|shì}{她|tā}{母亲|mǔ qīn}{去世|qù shì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{带|dài}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。{宝玉|Bǎo yù}{听|tīng}{了|le}，{这|zhè}{才|cái}{安静|ān jìng}{下来|xià lái}。
>
> {第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{见面|jiàn miàn}，{就|jiù}{闹|nào}{出|chū}{这么|zhè me}{大|dà}{的|de}{事|shì}。{黛玉|Dài yù}{夜|yè}{里|lǐ}{想|xiǎng}{起来|qǐ lái}，{觉得|jué de}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{因为|yīn wèi}{自己|zì jǐ}，{偷偷|tōu tōu}{地|de}{哭|kū}{了|le}{很|hěn}{久|jiǔ}。{故事|gù shi}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}，{从|cóng}{这|zhè}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{起|qǐ}，{就|jiù}{再|zài}{也|yě}{分|fēn}{不|bu}{开|kāi}{了|le}。

{京城|jīng chéng} (jīngchéng): the capital. {笑话|xiào hua} (xiàohua, HSK 4): to laugh at. {心肝儿肉|xīn gānr ròu} (xīngānr ròu): "my heart and liver", a pet
name for a beloved child (the grandmother's words in the original). {迎接|yíng jiē} (yíngjiē, HSK 5): to welcome. {大胆|dà dǎn} (dàdǎn): bold. {话音刚落|huà yīn gāng luò} (huàyīn gāng luò): no sooner
had the words been said. {光彩照人|guāng cǎi zhào rén} (guāngcǎi zhào rén): dazzling (an idiom). {宠爱|chǒng ài} (chǒng'ài): to dote on. {眼熟|yǎn shú}
(yǎnshú): familiar-looking. {摘|zhāi} (zhāi, HSK 5): to take off. {哄|hǒng} (hǒng): to soothe, coax. {闹|nào} (nào, HSK 4): to make a
scene. In the original, {宝玉|Bǎo yù}'s line is introduced {宝玉|Bǎo yù}{看罢|kàn bà}，{因笑道|yīn xiào dào} ({宝玉|Bǎo yù}, having looked, said with a smile).

1. Why is {黛玉|Dài yù} so careful on her way to the {荣国府|Róng guó fǔ}?
2. How does the scene show what kind of person {王熙凤|Wáng Xī fèng} is?
3. Why does {宝玉|Bǎo yù} throw his jade on the ground?
4. What does the last paragraph suggest about the story to come?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. She has heard from her mother that her grandmother's family is different and has many rules
   ({规矩|guī ju}{很|hěn}{多|duō}), so she resolves to watch every step and every word and not be laughed at.
2. Where everyone else speaks softly, she arrives laughing loudly and apologising for being late: she is
   bold, lively and sure of her place in the house, and she manages much of the household.
3. When {黛玉|Dài yù} says she has no jade and that such a precious thing isn't for everyone, he is angry that he
   alone has one, as if it made him different from his girl cousins, and he says he doesn't want it.
4. That {宝玉|Bǎo yù} and {黛玉|Dài yù} will be bound to each other from now on ({从|cóng}{这|zhè}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{起|qǐ}，{就|jiù}{再|zài}{也|yě}{分|fēn}{不|bu}{开|kāi}{了|le}), and, since {黛玉|Dài yù}
   cries over the trouble, that their story will bring her tears.

"After Lin Daiyu's mother died, her grandmother insisted on having her come, and her father, who was getting
on in years, sent her to live at her grandmother's in the capital. Daiyu was still young that year, but clever and sensitive from early childhood. She had heard her mother say that her grandmother's family wasn't like others, with many rules,
so all the way she kept reminding herself: every step must be careful, every word thought out before she
said it; she mustn't on any account give people cause to laugh at her.

After many days by boat, and then by sedan chair, she finally reached the Rongguo mansion. Crowds of people
stood before the gate; each courtyard was finer than the last, and the maids coming and going were all
neatly dressed. As soon as her grandmother saw her, she took her in her arms, calling her 'my darling', and
wept, and everyone in the room wept with her. Of all her children, her grandmother said, the one she had
loved most was Daiyu's mother; she had never thought her daughter would go first, and now only this
granddaughter was left.

While they were talking, someone in the courtyard suddenly called out, laughing loudly: 'I'm late! I wasn't
here to welcome our guest from far away!' Daiyu wondered: here everyone speaks softly, so who could be so
bold? The words were hardly out when a young woman, dressed to dazzle, swept in. Her grandmother, laughing, introduced her:
this was Wang Xifeng, who ran much of the household, from top to bottom.

Later her grandmother spoke of her grandson Baoyu. Daiyu had long heard that this cousin was his grandmother's
favourite and that no one at home could manage him. She wondered what sort of person he was.

Just then Baoyu arrived. Daiyu looked at him and started: how familiar he looked, as if she had seen him
somewhere before. Baoyu too studied his new cousin for a long while, and then said with a smile: 'I have
seen this cousin before.' Her grandmother laughed at him for talking nonsense: Daiyu had never been here
before, so how could he have seen her? But Baoyu said that even if he hadn't, she seemed like an old friend.

Then Baoyu asked Daiyu: 'Do you have a jade?' Daiyu thought he must mean the jade he had been born with, and
said: 'No. How could everyone have such a precious thing?' To everyone's surprise Baoyu flew into a temper,
tore the jade from his neck and flung it to the ground: 'What treasure! None of my cousins has one, only me.
I don't want it!' Everyone in the room was terrified and rushed to pick it up. His grandmother soothed him,
telling him a story: Daiyu had had a jade too, but her mother had taken it with her when she died. Only then
did Baoyu calm down.

At their very first meeting, such a scene. That night, thinking it over, Daiyu felt it was all her fault and
cried quietly for a long time. From that day on, the two people of this story would never be parted."
</details>

## Why it is read

People read 《{红楼梦|Hóng lóu mèng}》 for many reasons. It describes the daily life of a great Qing household in rich detail:
food, clothes, festivals, medicine, gardens, games. Its hundreds of characters, from the grandmother to the
maids, each speak in their own way. It's full of poems, which the characters write and judge. And its story of
love and loss, set against a family's slow decline, still moves readers. Many readers think it draws on the author's own family;
{红学|hóng xué} scholars still argue about how much.

You'll meet it everywhere in China: in television series and films, in school textbooks (excerpts), in
everyday speech. {林黛玉|Lín Dài yù} is a byword for a delicate, sensitive girl ({他|tā}{的|de}{女朋友|nǚ péng you}{像|xiàng}{林黛玉|Lín Dài yù}{一样|yí yàng}{爱|ài}{哭|kū}), and {大观园|Dà guān yuán} for a
place full of wonders.

## Say it

```speak
# Talking about the novel
《{红楼梦|Hóng lóu mèng}》{是|shì}{曹雪芹|Cáo Xuě qín}{写|xiě}{的|de}。
= Dream of the Red Chamber was written by Cao Xueqin.
{这|zhè}{本|běn}{小说|xiǎo shuō}{一共|yí gòng}{有|yǒu}{一百二十|yì bǎi èr shí}{回|huí}。
= The novel has a hundred and twenty chapters in all.
{后|hòu}{四十|sì shí}{回|huí}{的|de}{作者|zuò zhě}{到|dào}{现在|xiàn zài}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{争议|zhēng yì}。
= Who wrote the last forty chapters is still in dispute.
{宝玉|Bǎo yù}{和|hé}{黛玉|Dài yù}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{见面|jiàn miàn}，{宝玉|Bǎo yù}{就|jiù}{说|shuō}："{这个|zhè ge}{妹妹|mèi mei}{我|wǒ}{曾|céng}{见过|jiàn guo}{的|de}。"
= When Baoyu and Daiyu first met, Baoyu said: "I have seen this cousin before."
```

{争议|zhēng yì} (zhēngyì, lesson 23): a dispute, controversy.

## Key points

- 《{红楼梦|Hóng lóu mèng}》 (also 《{石头记|Shí tou jì}》): eighteenth century; {曹雪芹|Cáo Xuě qín} (born 1715–1724, died 1763 or 1764); 80 chapters in the
  manuscripts, 120 in the edition of 1791 by {程伟元|Chéng Wěi yuán} and {高鹗|Gāo È}; the last forty chapters' author is debated.
- The {贾|Jiǎ} family's two mansions, {荣国府|Róng guó fǔ} and {宁国府|Níng guó fǔ}, and the garden {大观园|Dà guān yuán}; {贾宝玉|Jiǎ Bǎo yù}, {林黛玉|Lín Dài yù}, {薛宝钗|Xuē Bǎo chāi}.
- {红学|hóng xué}: the study of the novel.
- {黛玉|Dài yù}{进|jìn}{贾府|Jiǎ fǔ} (chapter 3): {宝玉|Bǎo yù}{看罢|kàn bà}，{因笑道|yīn xiào dào}："{这个|zhè ge}{妹妹|mèi mei}{我|wǒ}{曾|céng}{见过|jiàn guo}{的|de}。"

lessons.title: Crosstalk
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

{相声|xiàng sheng} (xiàngsheng, crosstalk) is China's best-known comic art: usually two performers in long gowns standing
behind a table, talking, arguing, imitating, and making the audience laugh with quick wordplay. It lives on
the radio, on television (for example in the Spring Festival gala) and in small theatres. This honors lesson
explains its forms and roles, shows how its wordplay works with words from this course, and ends with an
original short sketch.

## Where it comes from

{相声|xiàng sheng} is usually traced to street performers of the late Qing dynasty, in the middle of the nineteenth
century, in places like {天桥|Tiān qiáo} (Tiānqiáo) in Beijing and the markets of Tianjin, where performers drew a crowd,
made people laugh and collected coins. Its roots may be older. In the twentieth century it moved from the
street to tea houses, theatres and broadcasting.

Among the best-known performers of the twentieth century was {侯宝林|Hóu Bǎo lín} (Hóu Bǎolín, 1917–1993). Born in Tianjin, he
was one of the most popular and influential crosstalk performers of his generation and taught many of those
who came after him. Many of his pieces are still performed and replayed.

## Forms and roles

| Form | Performers | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| {单口相声|dān kǒu xiàng sheng} (dānkǒu xiàngsheng) | one | a story told and acted by one performer |
| {对口相声|duì kǒu xiàng sheng} (duìkǒu xiàngsheng) | two | a dialogue: the most common form |
| {群口相声|qún kǒu xiàng sheng} (qúnkǒu xiàngsheng) | three or more | a group act |

In a two-person act, the performers have fixed roles:

- {逗哏|dòu gén} (dòugén) is the lead, who tells the story, makes the jokes and drives the piece forward.
- {捧哏|pěng gén} (pěnggén) is the partner, who listens, questions, objects and reacts, setting up the jokes and making
  them land. {捧|pěng} (pěng) is to hold up in both hands, and also to support, to praise (lesson 13's word).

Performers have a saying, {三分逗|sān fēn dòu}，{七分捧|qī fēn pěng} ("three parts the lead, seven parts the partner"): a joke works only if
the partner sets it up well. The written script marks the two as {甲|jiǎ} (jiǎ, A: the lead) and {乙|yǐ} (yǐ, B: the
partner).

The art's four basic skills are {说|shuō}、{学|xué}、{逗|dòu}、{唱|chàng}: {说|shuō} (speaking: telling, tongue-twisters, riddles), {学|xué} (imitating:
voices, dialects, sounds, the singing of opera), {逗|dòu} (joking, teasing: the heart of it) and {唱|chàng} (singing). The
punchline is called a {包袱|bāo fu} (bāofu, "a bundle"): it's tied up slowly and then "shaken open" ({抖包袱|dǒu bāo fu}).

## How the wordplay works

Much of the fun in {相声|xiàng sheng} comes from the language itself: words that sound alike, characters with two readings,
and words with two meanings. You already know enough to see how. Some examples with words from this course:

- *Same sound, different word.* {忙人|máng rén} (máng rén, a busy person) and {盲人|máng rén} (máng rén, a blind person, lesson 06)
  sound exactly alike. "{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{个|gè}{忙人|máng rén}。" "{什么|shén me}？{你|nǐ}{看不见|kàn bu jiàn}？"
- *One character, two readings.* 吐 is tǔ (to spit) and tù (to vomit), lesson 08. 他吐了 in writing could be
  either, and a {捧哏|pěng gén} can pretend to take it the wrong way.
- *One character, two readings again.* 晕 is yūn (dizzy) and yùn in {晕车|yùn chē} (carsick): "{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{看|kàn}{书|shū}{就|jiù}{晕|yūn}。" "{看|kàn}{书|shū}{也|yě}
  {晕车|yùn chē}？"
- *Same word, two meanings.* 地方 is dìfang (a place) and dìfāng (local, lesson 07); {局|jú} is a bureau (lesson
  09) and a game (lesson 29): "{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{公安局|gōng ān jú}{上班|shàng bān}。" "{哦|ò}，{打牌|dǎ pái}{的|de}{那个|nà ge}{局|jú}？" ({打牌|dǎ pái} dǎ pái, to play cards.)

The trick is always the same: the {逗哏|dòu gén} says something with two possible meanings, the {捧哏|pěng gén} takes it one way (or
the audience does), and the {逗哏|dòu gén} turns it the other way.

## A short sketch: {看病|kàn bìng}

An original {对口相声|duì kǒu xiàng sheng} for two, using the words of this module. {甲|jiǎ} is the {逗哏|dòu gén}, {乙|yǐ} the {捧哏|pěng gén}.

```dialogue
# Seeing the doctor
甲: {最近|zuì jìn}{我|wǒ}{身体|shēn tǐ}{不|bú}{太|tài}{好|hǎo}，{去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{次|cì}{病|bìng}。
= I haven't been well lately, so I went to see a doctor.
乙: {哪儿|nǎr}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}{啊|a}？
= What was wrong?
甲: {我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{医生|yī shēng}{说|shuō}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{个|gè}{忙人|máng rén}，{天天|tiān tiān}{熬夜|áo yè}。
= I told the doctor: I'm a busy man, up late every night.
乙: {医生|yī shēng}{怎么|zěn me}{说|shuō}？
= What did the doctor say?
甲: {医生|yī shēng}{拿|ná}{手|shǒu}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{眼前|yǎn qián}{晃|huàng}{了|le}{晃|huàng}，{问|wèn}{我|wǒ}："{那|nà}{您|nín}{看得见|kàn de jiàn}{我|wǒ}{吗|ma}？"
= The doctor waved a hand in front of my eyes and asked: "Then can you see me?"
乙: {嗐|hài}！{他|tā}{听|tīng}{成|chéng}"{盲人|máng rén}"{了|le}。
= Oh dear! He heard "blind man".
甲: {我|wǒ}{说|shuō}："{看得见|kàn de jiàn}！{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}{特别|tè bié}{忙|máng}！"{医生|yī shēng}{说|shuō}："{哦|ò}，{那|nà}{您|nín}{哪儿|nǎr}{不适|bú shì}？"{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}："{头晕|tóu yūn}。"
= I said: "Of course I can see! I mean I'm extremely busy!" The doctor said: "Oh. Then what's the trouble?" I said: "I feel dizzy."
乙: {这|zhè}{倒是|dào shi}{个|gè}{症状|zhèng zhuàng}。
= Well, that's a symptom.
甲: {医生|yī shēng}{问|wèn}："{什么|shén me}{时候|shí hou}{晕|yūn}？"{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}："{一|yí}{坐|zuò}{车|chē}{就|jiù}{晕|yūn}。"{医生|yī shēng}{说|shuō}："{那|nà}{是|shì}{晕车|yùn chē}，{不|bù}{归|guī}{我们|wǒ men}{内科|nèi kē}{管|guǎn}，{您|nín}{去|qù}{车站|chē zhàn}{吧|ba}。"
= The doctor asked: "When do you feel dizzy?" I said: "Whenever I get in a car." The doctor said: "That's carsickness. Not our department: try the bus station."
乙: {车站|chē zhàn}{还|hái}{看病|kàn bìng}？
= Since when do bus stations treat people?
甲: {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{这么|zhè me}{说|shuō}{啊|a}！{医生|yī shēng}{又|yòu}{问|wèn}："{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{别的|bié de}{症状|zhèng zhuàng}{吗|ma}？"{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}："{早上|zǎo shang}{起来|qǐ lái}{刷牙|shuā yá}，{老|lǎo}{想|xiǎng}{吐|tǔ}。"
= That's what I said! The doctor asked: "Any other symptoms?" I said: "When I brush my teeth in the morning, I always want to spit."
乙: {刷牙|shuā yá}{谁|shéi}{不|bù}{吐|tǔ}{啊|a}？
= Who doesn't spit when they brush their teeth?
甲: {医生|yī shēng}{也|yě}{这么|zhè me}{说|shuō}！{他|tā}{说|shuō}："{吐|tǔ}{没关系|méi guān xi}，{吐|tù}{才|cái}{有|yǒu}{关系|guān xi}。"
= That's what the doctor said! He said: "Spitting's fine. It's vomiting that matters."
乙: {那|nà}{最后|zuì hòu}{医生|yī shēng}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{开|kāi}{了|le}{什么|shén me}{药|yào}？
= So what did the doctor give you in the end?
甲: {医生|yī shēng}{说|shuō}："{除非|chú fēi}{你|nǐ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{按时|àn shí}{睡觉|shuì jiào}，{否则|fǒu zé}{什么|shén me}{药|yào}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{用|yòng}。"
= The doctor said: "Unless you go to bed on time every night, no medicine will do you any good."
乙: {说|shuō}{得|de}{对|duì}{啊|a}。
= He's right.
甲: {我|wǒ}{说|shuō}："{大夫|dài fu}，{我|wǒ}{要是|yào shi}{能|néng}{按时|àn shí}{睡觉|shuì jiào}，{还|hái}{来|lái}{找|zhǎo}{您|nín}{干|gàn}{什么|shén me}？"
= I said: "Doctor, if I could go to bed on time, why would I be here?"
乙: {嗐|hài}，{去你的吧|qù nǐ de ba}！
= Oh, get away with you!
```

- {晃|huàng} (huàng): to wave, shake. {嗐|hài} (hài): an exclamation of regret or exasperation.
- {不|bù}{归|guī}{我们|wǒ men}{管|guǎn} (bù guī wǒmen guǎn): not our business: {归|guī} is lesson 09's "to belong to".
- {刷牙|shuā yá} (shuā yá): to brush one's teeth. {大夫|dài fu} (dàifu): a doctor (spoken, northern).
- {去你的吧|qù nǐ de ba} (qù nǐ de ba): "get away with you!": the traditional line a {捧哏|pěng gén} ends a piece with.

1. Which joke depends on two words with the same sound? Which depends on two readings of one character?
2. What does {乙|yǐ} do in the sketch? Give two examples.
3. Why is the ending funny?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. {忙人|máng rén} and {盲人|máng rén} (máng rén) sound the same: the doctor hears "blind man" and waves a hand. {吐|tǔ} has two readings:
   tǔ (to spit) is harmless after brushing your teeth; tù (to vomit) is the symptom that matters.
2. {乙|yǐ} asks the questions that move the story on ({哪儿|nǎr}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}{啊|a}？ {医生|yī shēng}{怎么|zěn me}{说|shuō}？), explains or reacts to the jokes
   ({他|tā}{听|tīng}{成|chéng}"{盲人|máng rén}"{了|le}, {车站|chē zhàn}{还|hái}{看病|kàn bìng}？, {刷牙|shuā yá}{谁|shéi}{不|bù}{吐|tǔ}{啊|a}？) and closes the piece ({去你的吧|qù nǐ de ba}！).
3. {甲|jiǎ} can't sleep on time because he's too busy; the doctor's only treatment is to sleep on time; so the
   "patient" turns the doctor's logic back on him: if he could follow the advice, he wouldn't need a doctor.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Crosstalk
{相声|xiàng sheng}{一般|yì bān}{是|shì}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{表演|biǎo yǎn}{的|de}。
= Crosstalk is usually performed by two people.
{逗哏|dòu gén}{的|de}{说|shuō}{笑话|xiào hua}，{捧哏|pěng gén}{的|de}{帮|bāng}{他|tā}{把|bǎ}{笑话|xiào hua}{说|shuō}{好|hǎo}。
= The lead tells the jokes, and the partner helps make them work.
{三分逗|sān fēn dòu}，{七分捧|qī fēn pěng}。
= Three parts the lead, seven parts the partner.
{相声|xiàng sheng}{的|de}{四|sì}{个|gè}{基本功|jī běn gōng}{是|shì}{说|shuō}、{学|xué}、{逗|dòu}、{唱|chàng}。
= The four basic skills of crosstalk are speaking, imitating, joking and singing.
```

{基本功|jī běn gōng} (jīběngōng): a basic skill.

## Key points

- {相声|xiàng sheng} (crosstalk): from street performance in late-Qing Beijing ({天桥|Tiān qiáo}) and Tianjin; {侯宝林|Hóu Bǎo lín} (1917–1993).
- {单口相声|dān kǒu xiàng sheng} (one), {对口相声|duì kǒu xiàng sheng} (two: the usual form), {群口相声|qún kǒu xiàng sheng} (three or more).
- {逗哏|dòu gén} (the lead) and {捧哏|pěng gén} (the partner), {甲|jiǎ} and {乙|yǐ} in scripts; {三分逗|sān fēn dòu}，{七分捧|qī fēn pěng}.
- {说|shuō}、{学|xué}、{逗|dòu}、{唱|chàng}; the punchline, {包袱|bāo fu}.
- Wordplay: homophones ({忙人|máng rén} / {盲人|máng rén}), two readings ({吐|tǔ} tǔ / tù, {晕|yūn} yūn / yùn), two meanings ({地方|dì fang}, {局|jú}).

lessons.title: Countries, customs and fashions compared
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This module is about culture: customs, food, festivals, heritage and history. It opens with the
level-6 speaking task of discussing cultural differences informally: saying how two places do
things differently, why, and what you think of it, without turning a difference into a ranking.

David's company is about to welcome another study group, and he asks {王芳|Wáng Fāng} Wang Fang and
{安娜|Ān nà} Anna what British students should know about customs in China. Wang Fang then writes a commentary
for the news website on a question every traveller meets: should you do as the locals do? The lesson
also has the words for travelling between countries, and for clothes and fashion, which change as they
travel.

The grammar:

- **{与其|yǔ qí}…{不如|bù rú}** (rather than A, better B): {与其|yǔ qí}{抱怨|bào yuàn}，{不如|bù rú}{适应|shì yìng} (instead of complaining, adapt);
- {与其|yǔ qí}{说|shuō}…{不如|bù rú}{说|shuō} (it's not so much A as B), the commentary writer's version;
- words for comparing: {差异|chā yì}, {多元|duō yuán}, {融合|róng hé}, {融入|róng rù}, {认同|rèn tóng}, {借鉴|jiè jiàn};
- the shape of an informal discussion of a difference: what you noticed, the reason, your view.

## {与其|yǔ qí} A，{不如|bù rú} B: rather than A, better B

**{与其|yǔ qí}…{不如|bù rú}** weighs two choices and prefers the second. The one you give up comes after {与其|yǔ qí}; the one
you recommend after {不如|bù rú}, very often with {还|hái} or {倒|dào} (still, actually) in front of it:

{与其|yǔ qí}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{抱怨|bào yuàn}{天气|tiān qì}，{不如|bù rú}{出去|chū qù}{走走|zǒu zou}。 — Rather than staying at home complaining about the weather, you'd
do better to go out for a walk.

{与其|yǔ qí}{花|huā}{钱|qián}{买|mǎi}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{便宜|pián yi}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}，{还|hái}{不如|bù rú}{买|mǎi}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{质量|zhì liàng}{好|hǎo}{的|de}。 — Instead of spending money on lots of cheap clothes,
you'd be better off buying one good one.

{到|dào}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}，{与其|yǔ qí}{担心|dān xīn}{自己|zì jǐ}{不|bù}{习惯|xí guàn}，{倒|dào}{不如|bù rú}{先|xiān}{去|qù}{了解|liǎo jiě}{当地|dāng dì}{的|de}{习俗|xí sú}。 — When you arrive somewhere new,
rather than worrying that you won't get used to it, you'd do better to find out about the local customs
first.

- The subject can come first ({我|wǒ}{与其|yǔ qí}…{不如|bù rú}…) or after {与其|yǔ qí} ({与其|yǔ qí}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}，{不如|bù rú}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}: rather than you going, I'd
  better go). When the two halves have different subjects, put each after its word.
- {不如|bù rú} here is HSK 4's comparison "not as good as": {与其|yǔ qí} A，{不如|bù rú} B is "A is not as good as B", said as
  advice. On its own, {不如|bù rú} already does this: {坐|zuò}{车|chē}{不如|bù rú}{走路|zǒu lù}{快|kuài}.
- Both halves are usually verb phrases, often short and parallel: {与其|yǔ qí}{等|děng}，{不如|bù rú}{做|zuò} (rather than wait, act).

### {与其|yǔ qí}{说|shuō} A，{不如|bù rú}{说|shuō} B: not so much A as B

With {说|shuō}, the pattern corrects a description: what people call A is better called B. It is a favourite
of commentaries and essays:

{与其|yǔ qí}{说|shuō}{他|tā}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}，{不如|bù rú}{说|shuō}{他|tā}{不|bù}{敢|gǎn}{去|qù}。 — It's not so much that he doesn't want to go as that he
doesn't dare.

{与其|yǔ qí}{说|shuō}{这|zhè}{是|shì}{一|yí}{次|cì}{旅行|lǚ xíng}，{不如|bù rú}{说|shuō}{这|zhè}{是|shì}{一|yí}{次|cì}{考察|kǎo chá}。 — This was less a holiday than a fact-finding trip.

### Register

{与其|yǔ qí}…{不如|bù rú} fits both speech and writing. In conversation people often shorten it to ({还|hái}){不如|bù rú} alone,
after a sentence that states the first option: {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{这儿|zhèr}{等|děng}？{还|hái}{不如|bù rú}{跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{呢|ne}。 In a written argument
the full form, and {与其|yǔ qí}{说|shuō}…{不如|bù rú}{说|shuō}, sound measured and fair: they grant one side before choosing the
other.

## Words for comparing cultures

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {差异|chā yì} | difference (formal) | {文化|wén huà}{差异|chā yì} cultural differences; {两|liǎng}{地|dì}{的|de}{气候|qì hòu}{差异|chā yì}{很|hěn}{大|dà} |
| {多元|duō yuán} | diverse, plural | {多元|duō yuán}{文化|wén huà} many cultures side by side, multiculturalism; {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多元|duō yuán} |
| {融合|róng hé} | to blend, fuse | {东|dōng}{西方|xī fāng}{文化|wén huà}{的|de}{融合|róng hé} the blending of Eastern and Western cultures |
| {融入|róng rù} | to blend into, become part of | {很|hěn}{快|kuài}{就|jiù}{融入|róng rù}{了|le}{当地|dāng dì}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó} soon became part of local life |
| {认同|rèn tóng} | to identify with; to agree with | {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{认同|rèn tóng}{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{做法|zuò fǎ} I really agree with doing it this way |
| {借鉴|jiè jiàn} | to learn from (others' experience) | {借鉴|jiè jiàn}{别的|bié de}{国家|guó jiā}{的|de}{经验|jīng yàn} draw on other countries' experience |
| {本土|běn tǔ} | native, home-grown | {本土|běn tǔ}{品牌|pǐn pái} a local brand; {本土|běn tǔ}{文化|wén huà} |
| {国情|guó qíng} | a country's conditions | {每|měi}{个|gè}{国家|guó jiā}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{国情|guó qíng} every country has its own circumstances |
| {习俗|xí sú} | custom | {各地|gè dì}{的|de}{习俗|xí sú}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng} customs vary from place to place |
| {规矩|guī ju} | rules; manners | {懂|dǒng}{规矩|guī ju} to know how things are done; {没|méi}{规矩|guī ju} badly behaved |
| {场合|chǎng hé} | occasion, setting | {正式|zhèng shì}{场合|chǎng hé} a formal occasion; {看|kàn}{场合|chǎng hé} it depends on the occasion |

- {差异|chā yì} is the written partner of {不同|bù tóng} and {区别|qū bié}: in speech, {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{地方|dì fang}{很|hěn}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}; in an article, {两|liǎng}{地|dì}{存在|cún zài}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}
  {差异|chā yì}. {差|chā} here is chā, as in {差别|chā bié}; not the chà of {差不多|chà bu duō}.
- {融合|róng hé} is two things becoming one ({东|dōng}{西方|xī fāng}{的|de}{音乐|yīn yuè}{融合|róng hé}{在|zài}{一起|yì qǐ}); {融入|róng rù} is one thing joining a larger one ({融入|róng rù}
  {新|xīn}{的|de}{环境|huán jìng}, {融入|róng rù}{一|yí}{个|gè}{集体|jí tǐ}). Both have {融|róng}, "to melt" (the {融|róng} of {金融|jīn róng}, lesson 04).
- {认同|rèn tóng} is stronger than {同意|tóng yì}: you agree with an idea, but {认同|rèn tóng} a way of life or a value, or feel you
  belong ({文化|wén huà}{认同|rèn tóng} cultural identity).
- {借鉴|jiè jiàn} is learning from someone else's experience and adapting it: {借鉴|jiè jiàn} is to borrow ({借|jiè}) and to look at
  as in a mirror ({鉴|jiàn}). It's for methods and experience, not for copying: {借鉴|jiè jiàn}{别人|bié ren}{的|de}{经验|jīng yàn}, {借鉴|jiè jiàn}{国外|guó wài}{的|de}{做法|zuò fǎ}.
- {规矩|guī ju} guī ju has a light second syllable. {这|zhè}{家人|jiā rén}{规矩|guī ju}{很|hěn}{多|duō} (this family has a lot of rules); {他|tā}{是|shì}{个|gè}{规规矩矩|guī gui jǔ jǔ}{的|de}{人|rén}
  (very proper, well-behaved).

## Meeting, visiting and getting along

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {交际|jiāo jì} | social interaction; to socialise | {交际|jiāo jì}{能力|néng lì} social skills; {她|tā}{很|hěn}{会|huì}{交际|jiāo jì} she's good with people |
| {交谈|jiāo tán} | to talk, converse | {用|yòng}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{交谈|jiāo tán} to converse in Chinese |
| {谈论|tán lùn} | to talk about, discuss | {大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{谈论|tán lùn}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì} everyone is talking about it |
| {打交道|dǎ jiāo dào} | to deal with (people, things) | {跟|gēn}{外国|wài guó}{客人|kè rén}{打交道|dǎ jiāo dào} dealing with foreign guests |
| {来往|lái wǎng} | contact, dealings | {我们|wǒ men}{来往|lái wǎng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{年|nián} we've been in touch for years |
| {往来|wǎng lái} | contacts, exchanges (written) | {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{城市|chéng shì}{之间|zhī jiān}{的|de}{往来|wǎng lái}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō} |
| {拜访|bài fǎng} | to pay a visit (polite) | {拜访|bài fǎng}{老师|lǎo shī} to call on a teacher |
| {会见|huì jiàn} | to meet (formally) | {总裁|zǒng cái}{会见|huì jiàn}{了|le}{合作|hé zuò}{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{客人|kè rén} |
| {陪同|péi tóng} | to accompany (a guest) | {在|zài}{导游|dǎo yóu}{的|de}{陪同|péi tóng}{下|xià}{参观|cān guān} to visit with a guide |
| {考察|kǎo chá} | to inspect, study on the spot | {去|qù}{当地|dāng dì}{考察|kǎo chá}{市场|shì chǎng} to go and study the market there |
| {观光|guān guāng} | to go sightseeing | {观光客|guān guāng kè} tourists; {观光|guān guāng}{车|chē} a sightseeing bus |
| {同伴|tóng bàn} | companion | {旅行|lǚ xíng}{的|de}{同伴|tóng bàn} a travel companion |
| {圈|quān} | circle, ring; a circle (of people) | {画|huà}{一|yí}{个|gè}{圈|quān} draw a circle; {朋友|péng you}{圈|quān} one's circle of friends |
| {好客|hào kè} | hospitable | {当地|dāng dì}{人|rén}{非常|fēi cháng}{好客|hào kè} |
| {周到|zhōu dào} | thoughtful, considerate | {服务|fú wù}{很|hěn}{周到|zhōu dào}; {他|tā}{考虑|kǎo lǜ}{得|de}{很|hěn}{周到|zhōu dào} he thought of everything |
| {面子|miàn zi} | face (reputation, dignity) | {要|yào}{面子|miàn zi}, {给|gěi}{面子|miàn zi}, {丢|diū}{面子|miàn zi} |

- {交谈|jiāo tán} is the act of talking with someone ({两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{在|zài}{交谈|jiāo tán}); {谈论|tán lùn} takes the topic as its object ({谈论|tán lùn}{天气|tiān qì}, {谈论|tán lùn}
  {这|zhè}{部|bù}{电影|diàn yǐng}). You {交谈|jiāo tán} with people and {谈论|tán lùn} things.
- {打交道|dǎ jiāo dào} is always {跟|gēn} / {和|hé} + someone + {打交道|dǎ jiāo dào}: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{太|tài}{会|huì}{跟|gēn}{陌生|mò shēng}{人|rén}{打交道|dǎ jiāo dào}. It's informal and very common.
- {来往|lái wǎng} lái wǎng is everyday ({我们|wǒ men}{已经|yǐ jīng}{没有|méi yǒu}{来往|lái wǎng}{了|le}: we're no longer in touch); {往来|wǎng lái} is its written twin, for
  places and organisations ({海内外|hǎi nèi wài}{的|de}{往来|wǎng lái}). Both are nouns as well as verbs.
- {拜访|bài fǎng} is polite and modest: you {拜访|bài fǎng} someone you respect (a teacher, a client). {会见|huì jiàn} is formal and
  official, for people meeting in their roles, and mostly written.
- {面子|miàn zi} miàn zi is "face": your standing in others' eyes. {要|yào}{面子|miàn zi} is to care about face, {给|gěi}{面子|miàn zi} to save
  someone's face or show them respect (by coming, by not refusing), {丢|diū}{面子|miàn zi} to lose face. Criticising
  someone in front of others can make them {丢|diū}{面子|miàn zi}. The light {子|zi} tells you it's this noun, not the {面|miàn} of {面对|miàn duì}.
- {圈|quān} quān is a ring or a circle ({跑|pǎo}{了|le}{三|sān}{圈|quān}: ran three laps; {一|yì}{圈|quān}{人|rén}: a circle of people); {朋友|péng you}{圈|quān} is also the
  name people use for the friends' feed in a messaging app.
- {好客|hào kè} is hào kè: {好|hào} hào "to be fond of" (HSK 5), as in {好奇|hào qí} and {爱好|ài hào}.

## Countries, borders and travel

The continents in Chinese end in {洲|zhōu} (with water, 氵): {亚洲|Yà zhōu}, {欧洲|Ōu zhōu}, {非洲|Fēi zhōu}, and now {北美洲|Běi měi zhōu} (North America),

"When in Rome, or be yourself? By Wang Fang. Every year large numbers of foreigners come to China to
study, work or see the sights, and more and more Chinese people travel abroad, study abroad, or even
emigrate. The more people come and go between China and the rest of the world, the more often they
meet the same question: in someone else's country, should you do as the locals do, or keep your own
habits? Some people think that following local customs means giving yourself up. A Chinese student
studying in Britain told me that when he first arrived he felt everything had to change: how he ate,
how he spoke, even how he dressed, and he felt very uncomfortable. He even worried that when he went home he would have become "neither Chinese nor Western". That feeling is real, and deserves
understanding. But I believe that following local customs is not the same as giving yourself up.
Customs are the rules that the people of a place have formed over a long time of living there, and
there are reasons behind them. When Chinese people treat you and order lots of dishes, for example,
it isn't waste but a sign of the host's hospitality; when British people arrange a time and are
always punctual, it isn't coldness but respect for others. Or again: in some countries friends hug when they meet; in others a nod and a handshake are enough. Once we understand these reasons, we find
that many differences are just different ways of expressing the same regard. Of course, following
local customs has its limits. Respecting local customs doesn't mean being the same as everyone else
in everything. You can learn to use chopsticks and still love the food of your home town; you can
accept a new attitude to time without changing your personality. My friend Anna has lived in Beijing
for many years: at the Spring Festival she makes dumplings with her Chinese friends, and at
Thanksgiving she has everyone round for turkey. As she sees it, the two festivals don't clash. She says she hasn't lost anything; she has gained a
new way of seeing the world. So when we arrive somewhere new, rather than worrying that we'll be
'changed', we would do better to set aside judgment first, and observe, talk and understand. Doing as
the locals do is not so much a requirement as an attitude: a willingness to understand people who are
not like us. An increasingly diverse society needs exactly this attitude. Different cultures can learn
from each other and blend together, and each of us can, while becoming part of a new environment, keep
our own share of what makes us who we are."
</details>

<details>
<summary>A model answer</summary>

{我|wǒ}{发现|fā xiàn}，{在|zài}{我们|wǒ men}{那儿|nàr}，{请|qǐng}{朋友|péng you}{来|lái}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}，{一般|yì bān}{做|zuò}{两三|liǎng sān}{个|gè}{菜|cài}{就|jiù}{够|gòu}{了|le}，{最|zuì}{好吃|hǎo chī}{完|wán}，{不|bú}{剩|shèng}。{可是|kě shì}{在|zài}{中国|Zhōng guó}，{主人|zhǔ rén}{常常|cháng cháng}{做|zuò}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{菜|cài}，
{还|hái}{一直|yì zhí}{给|gěi}{客人|kè rén}{夹菜|jiā cài}。{这|zhè}{可能|kě néng}{是|shì}{因为|yīn wèi}，{在|zài}{中国|Zhōng guó}，{菜|cài}{多|duō}{说明|shuō míng}{主人|zhǔ rén}{好客|hào kè}，{也|yě}{给|gěi}{客人|kè rén}{面子|miàn zi}。{两|liǎng}{种|zhǒng}{做法|zuò fǎ}{各|gè}{有|yǒu}{各|gè}{的|de}{道理|dào li}。{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{与其|yǔ qí}
{比较|bǐ jiào}{哪|nǎ}{种|zhǒng}{更|gèng}{好|hǎo}，{不如|bù rú}{入乡随俗|rù xiāng suí sú}：{在|zài}{中国|Zhōng guó}{就|jiù}{多|duō}{吃|chī}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}，{夸|kuā}{主人|zhǔ rén}{做|zuò}{的|de}{菜|cài}{好吃|hǎo chī}。

"I've noticed that where I come from, when you have friends to dinner, two or three dishes are
usually enough, and it's best to finish everything. But in China the host often makes lots of dishes
and keeps putting food in the guests' bowls. That's probably because in China plenty of food shows the
host's hospitality, and honours the guests too. Both ways have their reasons. I think rather than
comparing which is better, it's best to do as the locals do: in China, eat a bit more and praise the
host's cooking." ({说明|shuō míng}: to show; {夸|kuā}: to praise, lesson 24's word.)
</details>

## Write it: an essay

The exam's second writing task is an argued essay of at least 300 characters. Write 300–400 characters
on this question: {出国|chū guó}{旅行|lǚ xíng}{或者|huò zhě}{留学|liú xué}，{应该|yīng gāi}{入乡随俗|rù xiāng suí sú}{吗|ma}？ Use {与其|yǔ qí}…{不如|bù rú} at least once, and three of {差异|chā yì}, {习俗|xí sú},
{融入|róng rù}, {认同|rèn tóng}, {借鉴|jiè jiàn}, {场合|chǎng hé}, {规矩|guī ju}.

<details>
<summary>Model essay</summary>

> {出国|chū guó}{旅行|lǚ xíng}{或者|huò zhě}{留学|liú xué}，{应该|yīng gāi}{入乡随俗|rù xiāng suí sú}{吗|ma}？
>
> {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}，{到|dào}{了|le}{别的|bié de}{国家|guó jiā}，{应该|yīng gāi}{尽量|jǐn liàng}{入乡随俗|rù xiāng suí sú}，{但|dàn}{不必|bú bì}{失去|shī qù}{自己|zì jǐ}。
>
> {首先|shǒu xiān}，{入乡随俗|rù xiāng suí sú}{是|shì}{对|duì}{当地|dāng dì}{人|rén}{的|de}{尊重|zūn zhòng}。{每|měi}{个|gè}{地方|dì fang}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{规矩|guī ju}，{比如|bǐ rú}{在|zài}{有的|yǒu de}{国家|guó jiā}，{进|jìn}{别人|bié ren}{家|jiā}{要|yào}{脱鞋|tuō xié}；{在|zài}{正式|zhèng shì}{场合|chǎng hé}，{穿|chuān}{得|de}{太|tài}
> {随意|suí yì}{会|huì}{让|ràng}{主人|zhǔ rén}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}。{遵守|zūn shǒu}{这些|zhè xiē}{习俗|xí sú}，{别人|bié ren}{会|huì}{更|gèng}{愿意|yuàn yì}{跟|gēn}{我们|wǒ men}{打交道|dǎ jiāo dào}。
>
> {其次|qí cì}，{入乡随俗|rù xiāng suí sú}{能|néng}{帮助|bāng zhù}{我们|wǒ men}{更|gèng}{快|kuài}{地|de}{融入|róng rù}{新|xīn}{的|de}{环境|huán jìng}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{一|yí}{位|wèi}{同学|tóng xué}{在|zài}{国外|guó wài}{留学|liú xué}{时|shí}，{主动|zhǔ dòng}{参加|cān jiā}{当地|dāng dì}{的|de}{节日|jié rì}{活动|huó dòng}，{很|hěn}{快|kuài}{就|jiù}{交|jiāo}{到|dào}{了|le}
> {朋友|péng you}，{语言|yǔ yán}{也|yě}{进步|jìn bù}{得|de}{特别|tè bié}{快|kuài}。
>
> {当然|dāng rán}，{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{担心|dān xīn}，{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{跟|gēn}{别人|bié ren}{学|xué}，{最后|zuì hòu}{会|huì}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{自己|zì jǐ}{是|shì}{谁|shéi}。{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{担心|dān xīn}{可以|kě yǐ}{理解|lǐ jiě}，{但|dàn}{入乡随俗|rù xiāng suí sú}{不|bú}{是|shì}{要|yào}{我们|wǒ men}{放弃|fàng qì}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{文化|wén huà}。
> {我们|wǒ men}{可以|kě yǐ}{借鉴|jiè jiàn}{别人|bié ren}{的|de}{长处|cháng chù}，{同时|tóng shí}{保留|bǎo liú}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{习惯|xí guàn}。
>
> {总之|zǒng zhī}，{文化|wén huà}{差异|chā yì}{是|shì}{很|hěn}{正常|zhèng cháng}{的|de}。{与其|yǔ qí}{抱怨|bào yuàn}{不|bù}{习惯|xí guàn}，{不如|bù rú}{带|dài}{着|zhe}{好奇心|hào qí xīn}{去|qù}{了解|liǎo jiě}{它|tā}。{这样|zhè yàng}，{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{旅行|lǚ xíng}{和|hé}{留学|liú xué}{才|cái}{会|huì}{更|gèng}{有|yǒu}{意义|yì yì}。

(About 330 characters. {尽量|jǐn liàng}: as far as possible; {脱鞋|tuō xié} tuō xié: to take off one's shoes; {遵守|zūn shǒu} zūn shǒu: to
observe (rules); {主动|zhǔ dòng}: on one's own initiative; {长处|cháng chù}: strengths; {好奇心|hào qí xīn}: curiosity.)
</details>

Checklist:

- A thesis in the first paragraph ({我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}…).
- Two reasons, each with an example ({首先|shǒu xiān}…{比如|bǐ rú}…; {其次|qí cì}…).
- A concession: grant the other side, then answer it ({当然|dāng rán}，{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{担心|dān xīn}…{但|dàn}…).
- A conclusion that returns to the thesis ({总之|zǒng zhī}…), here with {与其|yǔ qí}…{不如|bù rú}.
- Written style: {认为|rèn wéi}, {尽量|jǐn liàng}, {不必|bú bì}, {遵守|zūn shǒu}; no {吧|ba} or {啊|a}.

## Say it

```speak
# Customs and differences
{与其|yǔ qí}{抱怨|bào yuàn}，{不如|bù rú}{适应|shì yìng}。
= Rather than complain, adapt.
{中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{好客|hào kè}。
= Chinese people are very hospitable.
{正式|zhèng shì}{场合|chǎng hé}{一定|yí dìng}{要|yào}{准时|zhǔn shí}。
= On formal occasions you must be on time.
{差异|chā yì}{就是|jiù shì}{差异|chā yì}，{没有|méi yǒu}{谁|shéi}{对|duì}{谁|shéi}{错|cuò}。
= A difference is just a difference: nobody is right or wrong.
{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{认同|rèn tóng}{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{做法|zuò fǎ}。
= I really agree with doing it this way.
{这个|zhè ge}{箱子|xiāng zi}{要|yào}{托运|tuō yùn}{吗|ma}？
= Does this case need checking in?
{她|tā}{穿|chuān}{了|le}{一身|yì shēn}{黑|hēi}，{还|hái}{戴|dài}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{对|duì}{大|dà}{耳环|ěr huán}。
= She was dressed all in black, with a pair of big earrings.
```

## Pronunciation

- {与其|yǔ qí} yǔ qí: third tone, then second; said as one unit, yǔqí.
- {规矩|guī ju} guī ju and {面子|miàn zi} miàn zi: light second syllables. {模特儿|mó tèr} mó tèr: two syllables, the r joined to tè.
- {好客|hào kè} hào kè: hào, as in {好奇|hào qí} and {爱好|ài hào}, not the hǎo of "good".
- {差异|chā yì} chā yì: chā, as in {差别|chā bié}; {差不多|chà bu duō} has chà.
- {一身|yì shēn} yì shēn: {一|yī} changes before the first tone of {身|shēn}.
- {州|zhōu} zhōu and {洲|zhōu} zhōu sound the same; {粥|zhōu} zhōu (porridge, lesson 12) too.
- {披|pī} pī (to drape) and {皮|pí} pí (skin): first tone against second.
- {扎|zhā} zhā is the vocabulary reading (to prick); tying hair up is zā ({扎|zā}{头发|tóu fa}).

## Common mistakes

- ~~{与其|yǔ qí}{去|qù}，{不如|bù rú}{不|bú}{去|qù}~~ meaning "better go than not": the preferred choice comes after {不如|bù rú}. "Rather than
  stay at home, go" is {与其|yǔ qí}{待|dāi}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}，{不如|bù rú}{出去|chū qù}.
- ~~{与其|yǔ qí}…{但是|dàn shì}…~~ or ~~{与其|yǔ qí}…{还是|hái shi}…~~: {与其|yǔ qí} pairs with {不如|bù rú} (often {还|hái}{不如|bù rú}, {倒|dào}{不如|bù rú}).
- ~~{他|tā}{很|hěn}{肥|féi}~~ of a person is rude: {肥|féi} is for clothes and meat. Say {他|tā}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{胖|pàng}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{谈论|tán lùn}{了|le}{他|tā}~~ for "I talked with him": {谈论|tán lùn} takes the topic ({我们|wǒ men}{谈论|tán lùn}{了|le}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}); to talk with someone is {跟|gēn}{他|tā}
  {交谈|jiāo tán} or {跟|gēn}{他|tā}{聊|liáo}{天|tiān}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{会见|huì jiàn}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{老师|lǎo shī}~~ for a visit: {会见|huì jiàn} is formal and official; you {拜访|bài fǎng} or {去|qù}{看|kàn} a teacher.
- {北美洲|Běi měi zhōu} has {洲|zhōu} (water); {加|jiā}{州|zhōu} has {州|zhōu}. Writing {北|běi}{美|měi}{州|zhōu} is a common slip.
- ~~{跟|gēn}{他|tā}{打交道|dǎ jiāo dào}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{问题|wèn tí}~~: {打交道|dǎ jiāo dào} takes no object; it's {跟|gēn} + person + {打交道|dǎ jiāo dào}.

## Key points

- {与其|yǔ qí} A，({还|hái} / {倒|dào}){不如|bù rú} B: rather than A, better B ({与其|yǔ qí}{抱怨|bào yuàn}，{不如|bù rú}{适应|shì yìng}). {与其|yǔ qí}{说|shuō} A，{不如|bù rú}{说|shuō} B: not so much A as B.
- Comparing: {差异|chā yì} (formal {不同|bù tóng}), {多元|duō yuán}, {融合|róng hé} (blend together), {融入|róng rù} (become part of), {认同|rèn tóng}, {借鉴|jiè jiàn}, {本土|běn tǔ}, {国情|guó qíng}.
- Getting along: {规矩|guī ju}, {场合|chǎng hé}, {面子|miàn zi} ({要|yào} / {给|gěi} / {丢|diū}{面子|miàn zi}), {好客|hào kè}, {周到|zhōu dào}, {打交道|dǎ jiāo dào} ({跟|gēn}…{打交道|dǎ jiāo dào}), {拜访|bài fǎng} (polite), {会见|huì jiàn} (formal),
  {交谈|jiāo tán} (with people) and {谈论|tán lùn} (about things), {来往|lái wǎng} / {往来|wǎng lái} (written).
- Travel: {出境|chū jìng} / {入境|rù jìng}, {免税|miǎn shuì}, {退税|tuì shuì}, {托运|tuō yùn}, {抵达|dǐ dá} (formal), {出入|chū rù}; {北美洲|Běi měi zhōu}, {南美洲|Nán měi zhōu}, {大洋洲|Dà yáng zhōu} ({洲|zhōu}) and {州|zhōu}.
- Fashion: {时尚|shí shàng}, {款式|kuǎn shì}, {造型|zào xíng}, {一身|yì shēn}, {披|pī}, {扎|zhā}, {染|rǎn}, {肥|féi} (clothes and meat, not people).
- Discussing a difference: what you noticed, the reason, your view, without ranking.
- New characters: {透|tòu} {露|lù} {异|yì} {拜|bài} {粉|fěn} {矩|jǔ} {妆|zhuāng} {鉴|jiàn} {披|pī} {圈|quān} {尚|shàng} {柔|róu} {袖|xiù} {艳|yàn} {绒|róng} {州|zhōu} {棕|zōng} {祖|zǔ} {扎|zhā}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Food culture
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Food is where cultures are easiest to compare, and where Chinese has the richest vocabulary: how a dish
tastes and feels in the mouth, what goes into it, how it's served, and how you eat it. {李明|Lǐ Míng} Li Ming
takes {王芳|Wáng Fāng} Wang Fang to a Yunnan restaurant for a dish she has never tried, and the reading explains it:
crossing-the-bridge rice noodles, a dish with a story. There is a menu to read, and you'll talk about
eating out and cooking at home.

The grammar:

- {趁|chèn} (while, taking the chance): {趁|chèn}{热|rè}{吃|chī} (eat it while it's hot);
- {好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì} again (with great difficulty), and the brush-offs {算了|suàn le} and {得了|dé le};
- the measure words {串|chuàn}, {滴|dī}, {粒|lì}, {盘|pán}, {罐|guàn}, {壶|hú}, and the units {升|shēng} (litre) and {毫升|háo shēng} (millilitre);
- {透|tòu} after a verb or adjective: {熟|shú}{透|tòu}{了|le} (completely ripe), {湿|shī}{透|tòu}{了|le} (soaked through).

## {趁|chèn}: while, taking the chance

{趁|chèn} + a time or a situation + a verb: do something while the chance lasts.

{趁|chèn}{热|rè}{吃|chī}{吧|ba}，{凉|liáng}{了|le}{就|jiù}{不|bù}{好吃|hǎo chī}{了|le}。 — Eat it while it's hot: it's not nice cold.

{趁|chèn}{年轻|nián qīng}，{多|duō}{出去|chū qù}{看看|kàn kan}。 — While you're young, get out and see the world.

{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{趁|chèn}{这个|zhè ge}{周末|zhōu mò}{把|bǎ}{房间|fáng jiān}{收拾|shōu shi}{一下|yí xià}。 — I want to use this weekend to tidy my room.

- {趁|chèn} works like a preposition: it comes before the verb phrase, and the subject goes before it
  ({我|wǒ}{趁|chèn}…). {趁|chèn}{着|zhe} is the same, a little more spoken: {趁|chèn}{着|zhe}{天|tiān}{还|hái}{没|méi}{黑|hēi}，{我们|wǒ men}{快|kuài}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}。
- What follows {趁|chèn} is a chance that won't last: heat, youth, good weather, someone's absence ({趁|chèn}{他|tā}{不|bú}{在|zài},
  while he's out). That is the difference from {在|zài}…{的|de}{时候|shí hou}, which is only "when".
- {趁|chèn}{热|rè} is a set phrase: {趁|chèn}{热|rè}{吃|chī}, {趁|chèn}{热|rè}{喝|hē}, and the proverb {趁热打铁|chèn rè dǎ tiě} (strike while the iron is hot: {打铁|dǎ tiě},
  to forge iron).

## {好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì}, {算了|suàn le} and {得了|dé le}

You met {好容易|hǎo róng yì} and {好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì} in lesson 05: both mean "with great difficulty", usually with {才|cái}:

{我们|wǒ men}{好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì}{才|cái}{订|dìng}{到|dào}{了|le}{位|wèi}{子|zi}。 — We only just managed to book a table.

Two short words for giving up or brushing something off, which lesson 23 teaches in full, turn up in
any conversation about food:

- {算了|suàn le} (forget it, never mind): {没有|méi yǒu}{过桥米线|guò qiáo mǐ xiàn}？{算了|suàn le}，{那|nà}{就|jiù}{吃|chī}{别的|bié de}{吧|ba}。
- {得了|dé le} dé le (that's enough, come off it): {得了|dé le}{吧|ba}，{你|nǐ}{哪儿|nǎr}{会|huì}{做饭|zuò fàn}{啊|a}！ (Oh, come on, since when can you cook!)

## Counting food: {串|chuàn}, {滴|dī}, {粒|lì}, {盘|pán}, {罐|guàn}, {壶|hú}, {升|shēng}

| Measure word | For | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {串|chuàn} | things on a string or skewer | {一|yí}{串|chuàn}{葡萄|pú tao} a bunch of grapes; {一|yí}{串|chuàn}{钥匙|yào shi} a bunch of keys; {羊肉串|yáng ròu chuàn} lamb kebabs |
| {滴|dī} | drops | {一|yì}{滴|dī}{水|shuǐ}; {滴|dī}{几|jǐ}{滴|dī}{醋|cù} add a few drops of vinegar |
| {粒|lì} | grains, small round things | {一|yí}{粒|lì}{米|mǐ} a grain of rice; {几|jǐ}{粒|lì}{花生|huā shēng} a few peanuts |
| {盘|pán} | plates, dishes | {一|yì}{盘|pán}{菜|cài} a plate of food; {两|liǎng}{盘|pán}{饺子|jiǎo zi} |
| {罐|guàn} | jars, tins, cans | {一|yí}{罐|guàn}{可乐|kě lè} a can of cola; {一|yí}{罐|guàn}{酱|jiàng} a jar of sauce |
| {壶|hú} | pots, kettles | {一|yì}{壶|hú}{茶|chá} a pot of tea; {一|yì}{壶|hú}{开水|kāi shuǐ} a kettle of boiled water |

- {滴|dī} is also the verb "to drip, to put drops in": {滴|dī}{醋|cù} (add vinegar drop by drop), {水|shuǐ}{从|cóng}{水|shuǐ}{管|guǎn}{里|lǐ}{滴|dī}{下来|xià lái}.
- {盘|pán} is a borrowed measure word: the plate itself is {盘子|pán zi}. {罐|guàn} and {壶|hú} work the same way: {罐|guàn}{子|zi}, a jar; {一|yí}{个|gè}
  {茶|chá}{壶|hú}, a teapot.
- {串|chuàn} fits anything strung together: grapes, keys, beads, and the skewers sold at night markets
  ({烤串|kǎo chuàn}, grilled skewers).

The units of volume are {升|shēng} shēng (a litre) and {毫升|háo shēng} háo shēng (a millilitre): {一|yì}{升|shēng}{水|shuǐ}, {两百五十|liǎng bǎi wǔ shí}{毫升|háo shēng}{牛奶|niú nǎi}. {毫|háo}
is "a thousandth" in measures ({毫米|háo mǐ}, a millimetre, is lesson 20's). On a label you will see the letters
L and mL; you read them {升|shēng} and {毫升|háo shēng}. Don't confuse this {升|shēng} with HSK 5's verb {升|shēng} (to rise): {价格|jià gé}{升|shēng}{了|le}.

## {透|tòu}: right through

{透|tòu} tòu is "to pass through": {光|guāng}{从|cóng}{窗户|chuāng hu}{透|tòu}{进来|jìn lái} (light comes in through the window). After a verb or an
adjective, with {了|le}, it means "through and through, completely":

1. The name comes from a story (a wife carrying food over a bridge), and you cook the dish yourself at

4. That for the most authentic noodles you still have to come to Yunnan: the versions elsewhere are
   good, but locals are proud of the original.

"Crossing-the-bridge rice noodles. In Yunnan, rice noodles are the commonest everyday food, and of
all the kinds of rice noodle, the most famous are crossing-the-bridge noodles. Rice noodles are made
from rice: white, thin and smooth. People in Yunnan eat them for breakfast, lunch and dinner, and there
are noodle shops on every street. The name of crossing-the-bridge noodles is unusual, and so is the way
you eat them. About the name, a story is told locally. Long ago, they say, a scholar
lived in a small city in southern Yunnan. So that he could prepare for his exams in peace, he went
every day to a quiet spot across a lake to study, and his wife crossed a bridge every day to bring
him his meals. But it was rather a long way, and the food was often cold by the time it arrived. One
day his wife made a pot of chicken soup, with a thick layer of chicken fat floating on top. She
found that when it arrived, although the soup gave off no steam, it was still scalding. She put in
raw meat sliced very thin and the rice noodles, and in a moment they were cooked, savoury and
delicious. Later people called this way of eating 'crossing-the-bridge noodles'. Whether the story is
true no one can say any more, but that 'heat-keeping' oil really is the dish's secret. Today, when
you eat crossing-the-bridge noodles in a restaurant, the waiter first brings a big bowl of boiling
soup, then a dozen little dishes: raw sliced meat, egg, vegetables, tofu skin and, of course, a big
plate of noodles. You put the ingredients into the soup in order: first the raw meat, while the soup
is at its hottest, so that it cooks through; then the cooked ingredients and the vegetables; and the
noodles last. If you tip all the ingredients in at once, the soup cools down and the meat won't cook
properly. The soup is too hot to drink at once: it's best to wait a little, ladle out a spoonful
and taste it slowly. Many people eating it for the first time are 'fooled' by a soup that doesn't
seem to steam. A good bowl of crossing-the-bridge noodles is all about the soup. It's made by
simmering chicken and bones slowly for several hours, and it comes out clear in colour and savoury in
taste, yet not greasy at all. How the ingredients go together matters too: meat and vegetables, a
balanced meal. That's why, although the dish is cheap, it's very popular. Now you can eat it not only
in Yunnan but in Beijing and Shanghai, and even in some cities abroad. Still, many people from Yunnan
will tell you: for the most authentic, you have to come to Yunnan."
</details>

(written); {味精|wèi jīng} MSG; {口味|kǒu wèi} flavour; {自取|zì qǔ} help yourself; {按量取用|àn liàng qǔ yòng} take only what you'll eat.

Notice the register: {请|qǐng}{小心|xiǎo xīn}{用餐|yòng cān} is the menu's way of saying {吃|chī}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{小心|xiǎo xīn}{点儿|diǎnr}; {不|bú}{适宜|shì yí}{儿童|ér tóng}{单独|dān dú}{食用|shí yòng} means {小孩儿|xiǎo háir}
{别|bié}{自己|zì jǐ}{吃|chī}; {不|bù}{添加|tiān jiā}{味精|wèi jīng} is {不|bú}{放|fàng}{味精|wèi jīng}.

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

"Yunnan Kitchen: Menu. [Crossing-the-bridge noodle set] (for two) 68 yuan: two bowls of noodles in
chicken soup, with ten side ingredients including raw sliced meat, egg, vegetables and tofu skin.
[Home-style stir-fries] from 28 yuan a dish: egg with tomato, pork with chilli, peanuts.
[Lunch buffet] (Monday to Friday, 11:00–14:00) 39 yuan per person. Please note: 1. Our soups are very
hot: please eat with care; not suitable for children to eat unaccompanied. 2. We add no MSG to our
dishes, which are lightly flavoured; customers who like it hot can help themselves to chilli sauce.
3. At the buffet, please take only what you will eat: don't waste food."
</details>

## Speaking: an opinion question

The last part of the speaking test asks for your opinion (as reported: two questions, with time to
prepare). Give a view, two reasons with an example each, the other side, and a conclusion. Try this one
aloud: {你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}{在|zài}{外面|wài miàn}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{好|hǎo}，{还是|hái shi}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{做饭|zuò fàn}{好|hǎo}？

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{两|liǎng}{种|zhǒng}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{好处|hǎo chù}，{不过|bú guò}{我|wǒ}{更|gèng}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{做饭|zuò fàn}。{第|dì}{一|yī}，{在|zài}{家|jiā}{做饭|zuò fàn}{更|gèng}{健康|jiàn kāng}。{自己|zì jǐ}{做|zuò}{菜|cài}，{可以|kě yǐ}{少|shǎo}{放|fàng}{油|yóu}{和|hé}{盐|yán}，{也|yě}{不用|bú yòng}{担心|dān xīn}
{添加|tiān jiā}{了|le}{什么|shén me}。{我|wǒ}{最近|zuì jìn}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{做|zuò}{一些|yì xiē}{清淡|qīng dàn}{的|de}{家常|jiā cháng}{菜|cài}，{感觉|gǎn jué}{身体|shēn tǐ}{好多|hǎo duō}{了|le}。{第|dì}{二|èr}，{在|zài}{家|jiā}{做饭|zuò fàn}{更|gèng}{实惠|shí huì}。{在|zài}{外面|wài miàn}{吃|chī}{一|yí}{顿|dùn}{饭|fàn}{的|de}{钱|qián}，
{在|zài}{家|jiā}{可以|kě yǐ}{做|zuò}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{顿|dùn}。{当然|dāng rán}，{在|zài}{外面|wài miàn}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{它|tā}{的|de}{好处|hǎo chù}，{比如|bǐ rú}{可以|kě yǐ}{品尝|pǐn cháng}{到|dào}{各地|gè dì}{的|de}{地道|dì dao}{美食|měi shí}，{跟|gēn}{朋友|péng you}{聚会|jù huì}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{方便|fāng biàn}。{所以|suǒ yǐ}，
{平时|píng shí}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{做饭|zuò fàn}，{周末|zhōu mò}{偶尔|ǒu ěr}{和|hé}{朋友|péng you}{出去|chū qù}{吃|chī}{一|yí}{次|cì}。{这样|zhè yàng}{既|jì}{健康|jiàn kāng}，{又|yòu}{不|bú}{会|huì}{觉得|jué de}{生活|shēng huó}{太|tài}{单调|dān diào}。

"I think both have their advantages, but I prefer cooking at home. First, it's healthier: when you
cook yourself, you can use less oil and salt and needn't worry about what's been added. Lately I've
been making light home-style dishes every day, and I feel much better. Second, it's better value: what
one meal out costs will make several at home. Of course, eating out has its good side: you can taste
authentic food from all over, and it's an easy way to get together with friends. So on weekdays I
cook at home, and at weekends now and then I go out with friends. That way it's healthy, and life
doesn't feel too monotonous." ({单调|dān diào}: monotonous, lesson 07.)
</details>

## Write it: a notice

The exam's first writing task is a practical text of at least 150 characters. Write a notice of
150–200 characters for the noticeboard of your building, inviting your neighbours to a dumpling
evening: when and where, what to bring, what you'll provide. Use at least three of {趁|chèn}, {品尝|pǐn cháng}, {搭配|dā pèi}, {实惠|shí huì},
{清淡|qīng dàn}, {盛|chéng}, {一|yì}{壶|hú}.

<details>
<summary>Model notice</summary>

> {邀请|yāo qǐng}：{一起|yì qǐ}{来|lái}{包|bāo}{饺子|jiǎo zi}！
>
> {各位|gè wèi}{邻居|lín jū}：
>
> {大家|dà jiā}{好|hǎo}！{元旦|yuán dàn}{快|kuài}{到|dào}{了|le}，{趁|chèn}{着|zhe}{放假|fàng jià}，{我们|wǒ men}{想|xiǎng}{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{一起|yì qǐ}{包|bāo}{饺子|jiǎo zi}、{过|guò}{新年|xīn nián}。
>
> {时间|shí jiān}：1{月|yuè}1{日|rì}（{星期|xīng qī}{四|sì}）{下午|xià wǔ}{四|sì}{点|diǎn}
>
> {地点|dì diǎn}：3{号|hào}{楼|lóu}{一|yī}{层|céng}{活动室|huó dòng shì}
>
> {面粉|miàn fěn}、{肉|ròu}{和|hé}{菜|cài}{我们|wǒ men}{来|lái}{准备|zhǔn bèi}，{有|yǒu}{猪|zhū}{肉|ròu}{白|bái}{菜|cài}{的|de}，{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{清淡|qīng dàn}{的|de}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}{西红柿|xī hóng shì}{的|de}，{大家|dà jiā}{可以|kě yǐ}{都|dōu}{尝尝|cháng chang}，{看看|kàn kan}{哪|nǎ}{种|zhǒng}{搭配|dā pèi}{最|zuì}{好吃|hǎo chī}。{如果|rú guǒ}{您|nín}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}
> {特别|tè bié}{的|de}{饺子|jiǎo zi}{做法|zuò fǎ}，{欢迎|huān yíng}{带|dài}{上|shàng}{您|nín}{的|de}{拿手|ná shǒu}{调料|tiáo liào}，{让|ràng}{大家|dà jiā}{一起|yì qǐ}{品尝|pǐn cháng}。{我们|wǒ men}{还|hái}{会|huì}{泡|pào}{上|shàng}{几|jǐ}{壶|hú}{热|rè}{茶|chá}。{不|bú}{会|huì}{包|bāo}{饺子|jiǎo zi}{也|yě}{没关系|méi guān xi}，{我们|wǒ men}
> {可以|kě yǐ}{一起|yì qǐ}{学|xué}！
>
> {为了|wèi le}{方便|fāng biàn}{准备|zhǔn bèi}，{请|qǐng}{在|zài}12{月|yuè}29{日|rì}{以前|yǐ qián}{告诉|gào su}{我们|wǒ men}{您|nín}{家|jiā}{几|jǐ}{位|wèi}{参加|cān jiā}。
>
> 502{室|shì}　{赵晨|Zhào Chén}
>
> 12{月|yuè}20{日|rì}

(About 190 characters. {邀请|yāo qǐng}: an invitation; {活动室|huó dòng shì}: a common room; {拿手|ná shǒu}: one's speciality, what one does best; {室|shì}: room (in an address). {赵晨|Zhào Chén} Zhào Chén is a name.)
</details>

A notice needs: a heading, who it's for ({各位|gè wèi}{邻居|lín jū}), the purpose, the time and the place on lines of their
own, the details, what you ask readers to do and by when, and who it's from and the date.

## Say it

```speak
# At the table
{趁|chèn}{热|rè}{吃|chī}{吧|ba}！
= Eat it while it's hot!
{小心|xiǎo xīn}，{汤|tāng}{很|hěn}{烫|tàng}。
= Careful, the soup's scalding.
{服务员|fú wù yuán}，{来|lái}{一|yì}{壶|hú}{菊花茶|jú huā chá}。
= Excuse me, a pot of chrysanthemum tea, please.
{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{盛|chéng}{一|yì}{碗|wǎn}{饭|fàn}，{好|hǎo}{吗|ma}？
= Could you serve me a bowl of rice?
{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{的|de}{菜|cài}{又|yòu}{地道|dì dao}{又|yòu}{实惠|shí huì}。
= The food here is authentic and good value.
{今天|jīn tiān}{没|méi}{什么|shén me}{胃口|wèi kǒu}，{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{点儿|diǎnr}{清淡|qīng dàn}{的|de}。
= I haven't much appetite today: I'd like something light.
{这个|zhè ge}{西瓜|xī guā}{熟|shú}{透|tòu}{了|le}。
= This watermelon is perfectly ripe.
```

## Pronunciation

- {盛|chéng} chéng (to ladle) is the reading taught here: {盛|chéng}{饭|fàn} chéng fàn, {盛|chéng}{汤|tāng} chéng tāng.
- {地道|dì dao} dì dao (authentic): a light second syllable. {地道|dì dào} dì dào (a tunnel) is another word.
- {散|sǎn} sǎn (to fall apart, this lesson) and {散|sàn} sàn (to break up, lesson 13): third and fourth tone.
- {={卷|juǎn}=} juǎn (to roll up): third tone. {={卷|juàn}=} juàn (a volume) is lesson 27's.
- {夹|jiā} jiā, {尖|jiān} jiān, {酱|jiàng} jiàng, {椒|jiāo} jiāo: four j- syllables in one lesson. {辣椒|là jiāo} là jiāo.
- {粥|zhōu} zhōu, {州|zhōu} zhōu (lesson 11) and {周|zhōu} zhōu: the same sound.
- {升|shēng} shēng (a litre) and {生|shēng} shēng (raw): same sound; {毫升|háo shēng} háo shēng.
- {脂肪|zhī fáng} zhī fáng, {维生素|wéi shēng sù} wéi shēng sù, {蛋白质|dàn bái zhì} dàn bái zhì: say them as one word each.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{趁|chèn}{吃|chī}{热|rè}~~: {趁|chèn} takes the chance, then the verb: {趁|chèn}{热|rè}{吃|chī}.
- ~~{盛|chéng}{饭|fàn}~~ read shèng fàn: it's chéng fàn.
- ~~{今天|jīn tiān}{天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{烫|tàng}~~: {烫|tàng} is for things you touch, eat or drink that are hot enough to hurt ({汤|tāng}{很|hěn}{烫|tàng}, {水|shuǐ}{很|hěn}{烫|tàng});
  hot weather is {热|rè}.
- ~~{可口|kě kǒu}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}~~: {可口|kě kǒu} is only for food and drink. A comfortable garment is {舒服|shū fu}.
- ~~{一|yí}{个|gè}{葡萄|pú tao}{串|chuàn}~~ for "a bunch of grapes": the measure word is {串|chuàn}, {一|yí}{串|chuàn}{葡萄|pú tao}.
- ~~{很|hěn}{熟|shú}{透|tòu}{了|le}~~: {透|tòu}{了|le} already means "completely": {熟|shú}{透|tòu}{了|le}, without {很|hěn}.
- {胃口|wèi kǒu} and {食欲|shí yù} go with {好|hǎo} / {不|bù}{好|hǎo} and {有|yǒu} / {没有|méi yǒu} ({胃口|wèi kǒu}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}, {没有|méi yǒu}{食欲|shí yù}). {胃口|wèi kǒu}{很|hěn}{大|dà} (a big appetite) is fine; {食欲|shí yù}{很|hěn}{大|dà} sounds odd.

## Key points

- {趁|chèn} + a passing chance + verb: {趁|chèn}{热|rè}{吃|chī}, {趁|chèn}{年轻|nián qīng}, {趁|chèn}{着|zhe}{周末|zhōu mò}. {好不容易|hǎo bù róng yì}{才|cái}…: only just managed to…. {算了|suàn le} (forget it), {得了|dé le}
  (come off it).
- Measure words: {一|yí}{串|chuàn}{葡萄|pú tao}, {一|yì}{滴|dī}{醋|cù}, {一|yí}{粒|lì}{米|mǐ}, {一|yì}{盘|pán}{菜|cài}, {一|yí}{罐|guàn}{可乐|kě lè}, {一|yì}{壶|hú}{茶|chá}; units {升|shēng} and {毫升|háo shēng}.
- {透|tòu}{了|le} after a verb or adjective: {熟|shú}{透|tòu}{了|le}, {湿|shī}{透|tòu}{了|le}.
- Taste and texture: {口感|kǒu gǎn}, {可口|kě kǒu}, {地道|dì dao} dì dao, {家常|jiā cháng}, {清淡|qīng dàn}, {脆|cuì}, {烂|làn}, {纯|chún}, {杂|zá}, {尖|jiān}, {均匀|jūn yún}, {胃口|wèi kǒu} / {食欲|shí yù}.
- Kitchen verbs: {盛|chéng} chéng, {夹|jiā}, {端|duān}, {泡|pào}, {晾|liàng}, {={卷|juǎn}=} juǎn, {折|zhé}, {散|sǎn} sǎn, {烫|tàng}, {吞|tūn}, {搭配|dā pèi}, {品尝|pǐn cháng}, {清洗|qīng xǐ}, {添加|tiān jiā} (written).
- Menus and labels: {套餐|tào cān}, {自助|zì zhù}, {实惠|shí huì}, {用餐|yòng cān}, {适宜|shì yí}, {产地|chǎn dì}, {常温|cháng wēn}, {变质|biàn zhì}: written words with spoken partners.
- New characters: {盛|chéng} {趁|chèn} {串|chuàn} {醋|cù} {滴|dī} {端|duān} {纯|chún} {罐|guàn} {壶|hú} {毫|háo} {酱|jiàng} {夹|jiā} {尖|jiān} {匀|yún} {椒|jiāo} {粒|lì} {泡|pào} {晾|liàng} {烂|làn} {欲|yù}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Festivals, ceremonies and entertainment
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

A wedding banquet, a Lantern Festival evening and a night at the cinema: this lesson has the words
for celebrating and for being entertained. {李明|Lǐ Míng} Li Ming's colleague {马林|Mǎ Lín} Mǎ Lín is getting married, and
Li Ming and {王芳|Wáng Fāng} Wang Fang are at the banquet when the weather has other ideas. {安娜|Ān nà} Anna writes about
her Lantern Festival, and there are words for films and television: the script, the plot, the lead
role and the subtitles.

The grammar:

- {早|zǎo}{不|bù} X {晚|wǎn}{不|bù} X，{偏偏|piān piān}…: a colloquial format for bad timing ({早|zǎo}{不|bù}{来|lái}{晚|wǎn}{不|bù}{来|lái}，{偏偏|piān piān}{这|zhè}{时候|shí hou}{来|lái});
- {一再|yí zài} and {再三|zài sān} (again and again), which lesson 23 teaches in full;
- the measure word {枝|zhī} ({一|yì}{枝|zhī}{梅花|méi huā}, a sprig of plum blossom), beside {朵|duǒ} and {束|shù};
- {属|shǔ}: {我|wǒ}{属|shǔ}{兔|tù} (I was born in the year of the rabbit);
- {散|sàn} sàn, to break up: {宴会|yàn huì}{散|sàn}{了|le} (the banquet broke up).

## {早|zǎo}{不|bù} X {晚|wǎn}{不|bù} X: of all the times

{早|zǎo}{不|bù} X {晚|wǎn}{不|bù} X (not earlier, not later), usually followed by {偏偏|piān piān} piān piān (of all times, just) and the
moment it happened, complains that something happened at the worst possible time:

{雨|yǔ}{早|zǎo}{不|bú}{下|xià}{晚|wǎn}{不|bú}{下|xià}，{偏偏|piān piān}{在|zài}{婚礼|hūn lǐ}{开始|kāi shǐ}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{下|xià}。 — It could have rained any time, but it had to start just as the
wedding began.

{他|tā}{早|zǎo}{不|bù}{来|lái}{晚|wǎn}{不|bù}{来|lái}，{偏偏|piān piān}{我们|wǒ men}{刚|gāng}{出门|chū mén}{他|tā}{就|jiù}{来|lái}{了|le}。 — Of all the times to come, he turned up just as we'd gone out.

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{早|zǎo}{不|bú}{坏|huài}{晚|wǎn}{不|bú}{坏|huài}，{偏偏|piān piān}{在|zài}{考试|kǎo shì}{前|qián}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{坏|huài}{了|le}。 — My phone had to break the day before the exam.

- The same verb fills both gaps: {早|zǎo}{不|bù}{来|lái}{晚|wǎn}{不|bù}{来|lái}, {早|zǎo}{不|bù}{说|shuō}{晚|wǎn}{不|bù}{说|shuō}, {早|zǎo}{不|bú}{坏|huài}{晚|wǎn}{不|bú}{坏|huài}. With a two-syllable verb, people
  say {早|zǎo}{不|bú}{下雨|xià yǔ}{晚|wǎn}{不|bú}{下雨|xià yǔ} or just {早|zǎo}{不|bú}{下|xià}{晚|wǎn}{不|bú}{下|xià}.
- It's spoken, and it nearly always sounds annoyed: it's for bad timing, hardly ever for a lucky moment.
- A related reproach: {你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{不|bù}{早|zǎo}{说|shuō}？ or just {你|nǐ}{早|zǎo}{说|shuō}{啊|a}！ (why didn't you say so earlier?).

## {一再|yí zài} and {再三|zài sān}: again and again

Both mean "repeatedly", and both are lesson 23's words; they appear here because thanks and invitations
are repeated at every celebration.

- {一再|yí zài} goes before the verb: {他|tā}{一再|yí zài}{表示|biǎo shì}{感谢|gǎn xiè} (he thanked us again and again); {老师|lǎo shī}{一再|yí zài}{提醒|tí xǐng}{我们|wǒ men} (the teacher kept
  reminding us).
- {再三|zài sān} can go before the verb, or after one: {再三|zài sān}{感谢|gǎn xiè} (thanked repeatedly), {考虑|kǎo lǜ}{再三|zài sān} (after thinking it over
  many times).

## Counting flowers: {枝|zhī}, {朵|duǒ}, {束|shù}

| Measure word | For | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {枝|zhī} | a flower on its stem, a sprig, a branch | {一|yì}{枝|zhī}{梅花|méi huā} a sprig of plum blossom; {一|yì}{枝|zhī}{玫瑰|méi guī} a single rose |
| {朵|duǒ} | a flower head (HSK 5) | {一|yì}{朵|duǒ}{花|huā} a flower; {一|yì}{朵|duǒ}{白|bái}{云|yún} |
| {束|shù} | a bunch, a bouquet (HSK 5) | {一|yí}{束|shù}{花|huā} a bunch of flowers |

{枝|zhī} is also "a branch" ({树枝|shù zhī}): a {枝|zhī} of flowers is the stem and all. HSK 5's {支|zhī} zhī, the measure word for
pens and songs ({一|yì}{支|zhī}{笔|bǐ}, {一|yì}{支|zhī}{歌|gē}), sounds the same; for flowers, {枝|zhī} with {木|mù} is the usual written form.

## {属|shǔ}: born in the year of…

The twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac ({生肖|shēng xiào}, HSK 5) go with {属|shǔ} shǔ, "to belong to":

{你|nǐ}{属|shǔ}{什么|shén me}？ — What's your zodiac animal?

{我|wǒ}{属|shǔ}{兔|tù}，{我|wǒ}{姐姐|jiě jie}{属|shǔ}{龙|lóng}。 — I'm a rabbit, and my older sister is a dragon.

Asking {你|nǐ}{属|shǔ}{什么|shén me}？ is a polite way to find out someone's age without asking it, which is why you'll hear it
at family gatherings.

"A Lantern Festival evening. By Anna. Of all the Spring Festivals I've spent in Beijing, my favourite
part is really the last day: the fifteenth of the first month, the Lantern Festival. It's the first
full-moon night of the new year, and they say the festival is more than two thousand years old. On this day people eat {元宵|yuán xiāo}, look at lanterns and guess lantern
riddles, and the joy of the Spring Festival reaches its last high point. A week before this year's Lantern Festival, Wang Fang invited me: 'Don't go anywhere that evening: come to my
place for {元宵|yuán xiāo}, and afterwards we'll go to the lantern fair!' At dusk I arrived at Wang Fang's home. Her
mother had already boiled a big pot of {元宵|yuán xiāo}. Wang Fang told me that northern {元宵|yuán xiāo} are 'rolled' in rice
flour, whereas the {汤圆|tāng yuán} southerners eat are wrapped by hand, so they feel different in the mouth. I took
a bite: inside it was sweet and so hot I nearly burned my tongue. Wang Fang's grandmother laughed
and said, 'Slowly! {元宵|yuán xiāo} are for eating slowly. Eat your {元宵|yuán xiāo}, and the whole family is together.'
After dinner we took the underground to the park for the lantern fair. When we got there I finally knew
what 'a sea of people' meant. A great crowd had gathered at the gate, everyone looking forward to going
in to see the lanterns. Inside, lanterns of every kind were hanging everywhere: big red ones, little ones
in the shapes of rabbits, fish and flowers, and a 'dragon' several dozen metres long, glinting gold on
the lake. Little children ran about through the crowd carrying small lanterns: it was a wonderfully
lively scene. As we walked, Wang Fang told me what each kind of lantern meant: a fish lantern is 'may
there be plenty every year', and rabbit lanterns are for little children to play with. We went to guess lantern riddles too. Under each lantern hung a slip of paper with a riddle
on it. I guessed one right and won a small prize: a tiger lantern. Wang Fang said that since I was born
in the year of the tiger, it was the luckiest prize I could have. On the way home the moon was round
and bright. Wang Fang asked me what wish I had made. I said that if you tell a wish, it won't come true.
In fact my wish is very simple: I hope that next Lantern Festival we can eat {元宵|yuán xiāo} and look at the lanterns
together again, just like today. I often wonder why people look forward to festivals so much. Perhaps
it isn't the food, or how beautiful the lanterns are, but that on that day everyone wants to be with the
people they care about."

> {看|kàn}{到|dào}{最后|zuì hòu}，{不|bù}{少|shǎo}{观众|guān zhòng}{都|dōu}{哭|kū}{了|le}。{电影院|diàn yǐng yuàn}{为|wèi}{外国|wài guó}{观众|guān zhòng}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{了|le}{英文|Yīng wén}{字幕|zì mù}，{周末|zhōu mò}{的|de}{场次|chǎng cì}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}{就|jiù}{满|mǎn}{了|le}。

Words: {改编自|gǎi biān zì} adapted from ({自|zì}, written "from"); {讲|jiǎng}{的|de}{是|shì} it's about; {让|ràng}{人|rén}{想|xiǎng}{起|qǐ} makes one think of; {满|mǎn} full.

What is the film about, and what does the reviewer praise?

<details>
<summary>Answer and translation</summary>

A family in a small town celebrating the Spring Festival. The warm way every scene is shot, and the lead
actor's lively, true-to-life character.

"This film is adapted from a very popular novel, and it's about how a family in a small town spends the
Spring Festival. The subject is ordinary and the plot isn't complicated, but the director has shot every
scene with great warmth, and many shots remind you of your own home. The lead is a young actor who makes
the main character both lovable and real. It's a comedy, yet by the end quite a few people in the
audience were in tears. The cinema has English subtitles for foreign viewers, and the weekend showings
filled up fast."
</details>

## Speaking: a story from four photos

In the speaking test you see four numbered photos and tell a story that joins them (as reported: about
three minutes to prepare and two to speak). Here are the photos in words:

1. At a lantern fair, a small girl holds her grandfather's hand, looking up at a big dragon lantern.
2. In the crowd, her hand has slipped out of his; she looks around, frightened.
3. She stands by a member of staff, who is speaking into a microphone.
4. Her grandfather hurries over and hugs her, and buys her a rabbit lantern.

Plan the order with time words ({那|nà}{天|tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}, {正在|zhèng zài}…{的|de}{时候|shí hou}, {过|guò}{了|le}{一会儿|yí huìr}, {最后|zuì hòu}), give the people feelings ({高兴|gāo xìng},
{害怕|hài pà}, {着急|zháo jí}, {放心|fàng xīn}), and end with a line someone says.

<details>
<summary>Model story</summary>

{元宵节|Yuán xiāo jié}{那|nà}{天|tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}，{爷爷|yé ye}{带|dài}{着|zhe}{小星|Xiǎo Xīng}{去|qù}{公园|gōng yuán}{看|kàn}{灯会|dēng huì}。{公园|gōng yuán}{里|lǐ}{人山人海|rén shān rén hǎi}，{到处|dào chù}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{漂亮|piào liang}{的|de}{灯笼|dēng lóng}。{小星|Xiǎo Xīng}{拉|lā}{着|zhe}{爷爷|yé ye}{的|de}{手|shǒu}，{看|kàn}{着|zhe}{一|yì}{条|tiáo}{长|cháng}{长|cháng}{的|de}
"{龙|lóng}"{灯|dēng}，{高兴|gāo xìng}{极|jí}{了|le}。

{正在|zhèng zài}{大家|dà jiā}{看|kàn}{灯|dēng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{人|rén}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}，{小星|Xiǎo Xīng}{的|de}{手|shǒu}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{什么|shén me}{时候|shí hou}{从|cóng}{爷爷|yé ye}{手|shǒu}{里|lǐ}{滑|huá}{了|le}{出去|chū qù}。{她|tā}{往|wǎng}{旁边|páng biān}{一|yí}{看|kàn}，{爷爷|yé ye}{不见|bú jiàn}{了|le}！{她|tā}{又|yòu}{害怕|hài pà}{又|yòu}{着急|zháo jí}，
{差点儿|chà diǎnr}{哭|kū}{了|le}{出来|chū lái}。

{这|zhè}{时候|shí hou}，{她|tā}{想|xiǎng}{起|qǐ}{爷爷|yé ye}{说|shuō}{过|guo}：{要是|yào shi}{找不到|zhǎo bu dào}{家人|jiā rén}，{就|jiù}{去|qù}{找|zhǎo}{工作人员|gōng zuò rén yuán}。{她|tā}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{一|yí}{位|wèi}{工作人员|gōng zuò rén yuán}，{说|shuō}{了|le}{自己|zì jǐ}{和|hé}{爷爷|yé ye}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}。{工作人员|gōng zuò rén yuán}{马上|mǎ shàng}
{用|yòng}{话筒|huà tǒng}{广播|guǎng bō}{了|le}{一下|yí xià}。

{过|guò}{了|le}{一会儿|yí huìr}，{爷爷|yé ye}{跑|pǎo}{了|le}{过来|guò lái}，{一把抱住|yì bǎ bào zhù}{了|le}{小星|Xiǎo Xīng}。{他|tā}{终于|zhōng yú}{放心|fàng xīn}{了|le}，{还|hái}{给|gěi}{小星|Xiǎo Xīng}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{兔子|tù zi}{灯笼|dēng lóng}。{小星|Xiǎo Xīng}{说|shuō}："{爷爷|yé ye}，{下|xià}{次|cì}{我|wǒ}{一定|yí dìng}
{不|bú}{放|fàng}{开|kāi}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{手|shǒu}！"

({工作人员|gōng zuò rén yuán}: a member of staff; {话筒|huà tǒng}: a microphone (lesson 10); {广播|guǎng bō}: to announce over loudspeakers; {一把抱住|yì bǎ bào zhù}: to
grab in a hug; {放|fàng}{开|kāi}: to let go. {小星|Xiǎo Xīng} Xiǎo Xīng is a name.)
</details>

## Write it: a thank-you letter

Write a letter of 150–200 characters to a friend's family who had you to stay for the Spring Festival.
Thank them, say what you enjoyed most, and add a wish for them. Use at least three of {招待|zhāo dài}, {团圆|tuán yuán}, {气氛|qì fēn},
{盼望|pàn wàng}, {祝愿|zhù yuàn}, {周到|zhōu dào}, {拜年|bài nián}.

<details>

A letter needs: the greeting ({叔叔|shū shu}、{阿姨|ā yí}：), a line of greeting ({你们|nǐ men}{好|hǎo}！), the body in paragraphs, a wish to
close, then the name and the date on lines of their own.

## Say it

