**Two generations' schoolbags**, by Wang Fang. "Last weekend I went to my uncle's and found my
cousin agonising over his seven-year-old son: should he put him in weekend tutoring? My uncle was
against it the moment he heard: 'A seven-year-old, and extra lessons?' The family argued all
afternoon and got nowhere. On the way home I kept thinking: it's the same schooling, so why do two
generations see it so differently?

My uncle's schoolbag as a child was light: two or three textbooks and a pencil case were all the
stationery he had. After school the children fished by the river and caught insects in the fields,
and only went home when it got dark. In his words, childhood then was 'full of free time'. Today,
seven-year-old Doudou carries a schoolbag wider than he is, holding workbooks, a dictionary and a
water bottle as well as textbooks. Before he had even stepped through the gates of primary school,
he had done two years of activity classes.

Why are schoolbags getting heavier? I think what's heavy isn't the books but the parents'
expectations. Places at good secondary schools are limited, competition to move up gets fiercer
every year, and no parent wants to watch their child fall behind. So from the moment a child is
born, the parents start to worry: develop the baby's intelligence, extra classes at primary school,
humanities or sciences in adolescence… Every step a child takes seems to come with its parents'
anxiety.

Of course, I'm not saying tutoring is useless. If a child really finds one subject hard, a teacher's
help can often let them catch up. And my cousin's worry isn't groundless: in such a competitive
world, doing nothing takes real courage.

But the trouble is that much tutoring doesn't start from what the child needs: it's because
'everyone else is doing it'. The result is weekends packed full and learning that gets duller and
duller. A child whose every day is planned for them will find it hard to develop a real interest in
learning, and interest is precisely the best teacher.

Free time in childhood isn't wasted. Playing in the river, children learn to observe; quarrelling
and making up with friends, they learn to get along; daydreaming alone, their heads fill with all
sorts of strange ideas. None of this is in the textbooks, and no tutoring class can teach it, but it
stays with a child all their life.

My uncle has always said, 'Learning takes a lifetime.' I agree. Growing up isn't a sprint but a long
road. On that road what we need isn't heavier schoolbags but children who stay curious, whose
innocent questions get answered, who have time to daydream, play and read a fairy tale. A childhood
like that may not look so 'full', but the energy and vitality it gives a child are something no
tutoring class can.

When I left that day, Doudou was looking up and asking my uncle why the clouds in the sky move. I
thought: that question deserves a serious answer more than tomorrow's maths homework does."
</details>

## Write it: an argued essay

The HSK 6 exam's second writing task is an essay of at least 300 characters giving and defending
your opinion (as reported; RESEARCH §6). Write 300–400 characters on this question:
{上|shàng}{大学|dà xué}{选|xuǎn}{专业|zhuān yè}，{应该|yīng gāi}{看|kàn}{兴趣|xìng qù}，{还是|hái shi}{看|kàn}{将来|jiāng lái}{好|hǎo}{不|bu}{好|hǎo}{找|zhǎo}{工作|gōng zuò}？ (Choosing a degree subject: interest, or job
prospects?)

Plan four parts: your view; two reasons, each with an example; a concession (what the other side
gets right); a conclusion.

<details>
<summary>A model essay and a checklist</summary>

> {选|xuǎn}{专业|zhuān yè}：{兴趣|xìng qù}{比|bǐ}{热门|rè mén}{更|gèng}{重要|zhòng yào}
>
> {每|měi}{年|nián}{高考|gāo kǎo}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{家长|jiā zhǎng}{和|hé}{学生|xué sheng}{都|dōu}{会|huì}{为|wèi}{选|xuǎn}{专业|zhuān yè}{发愁|fā chóu}：{是|shì}{选|xuǎn}{自己|zì jǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{的|de}，{还是|hái shi}{选|xuǎn}{将来|jiāng lái}{好|hǎo}{找|zhǎo}{工作|gōng zuò}{的|de}？{我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}，{选|xuǎn}{专业|zhuān yè}{首先|shǒu xiān}{应该|yīng gāi}{看|kàn}{兴趣|xìng qù}。
>
> {第|dì}{一|yī}，{大学|dà xué}{四|sì}{年|nián}{的|de}{学习|xué xí}{并|bìng}{不|bù}{轻松|qīng sōng}。{很|hěn}{多|duō}{专业|zhuān yè}{课|kè}{既|jì}{难|nán}{又|yòu}{枯燥|kū zào}，{如果|rú guǒ}{对|duì}{它|tā}{没有|méi yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù}，{就|jiù}{很|hěn}{难|nán}{坚持|jiān chí}{下去|xià qù}，{更|gèng}{不用|bú yòng}{说|shuō}{学|xué}{好|hǎo}{了|le}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{一|yí}{个|gè}{同学|tóng xué}，{父母|fù mǔ}{让|ràng}{他|tā}{学|xué}{了|le}{热门|rè mén}{的|de}{计算机|jì suàn jī}{专业|zhuān yè}，{可|kě}{他|tā}{一向|yí xiàng}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{的|de}{是|shì}{历史|lì shǐ}。{四|sì}{年|nián}{里|lǐ}{他|tā}{学|xué}{得|de}{很|hěn}{痛苦|tòng kǔ}，{成绩|chéng jì}{只是|zhǐ shì}{中等|zhōng děng}，{毕业|bì yè}{以后|yǐ hòu}{还是|hái shi}{去|qù}{做|zuò}{了|le}{跟|gēn}{历史|lì shǐ}{有关|yǒu guān}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}。
>
> {第|dì}{二|èr}，{热门|rè mén}{专业|zhuān yè}{不|bú}{会|huì}{永远|yǒng yuǎn}{热门|rè mén}。{今天|jīn tiān}{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{抢|qiǎng}{着|zhe}{学|xué}{的|de}{专业|zhuān yè}，{四|sì}{年|nián}{以后|yǐ hòu}{可能|kě néng}{已经|yǐ jīng}{不|bù}{缺|quē}{人|rén}{了|le}。{相反|xiāng fǎn}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{如果|rú guǒ}{真正|zhēn zhèng}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{专业|zhuān yè}，{就|jiù}{愿意|yuàn yì}{下功夫|xià gōng fu}，{往往|wǎng wǎng}{能|néng}{做|zuò}{得|de}{比|bǐ}{别人|bié ren}{好|hǎo}，{自然|zì rán}{也|yě}{不|bú}{怕|pà}{找|zhǎo}{不|bu}{到|dào}{工作|gōng zuò}。
>
> {当然|dāng rán}，{兴趣|xìng qù}{不|bú}{是|shì}{唯一|wéi yī}{的|de}{标准|biāo zhǔn}。{找|zhǎo}{工作|gōng zuò}{的|de}{压力|yā lì}{是|shì}{真实|zhēn shí}{的|de}，{选|xuǎn}{专业|zhuān yè}{以前|yǐ qián}{了解|liǎo jiě}{一下|yí xià}{就业|jiù yè}{情况|qíng kuàng}，{也|yě}{是|shì}{必要|bì yào}{的|de}。
>
> {总之|zǒng zhī}，{兴趣|xìng qù}{是|shì}{最好|zuì hǎo}{的|de}{老师|lǎo shī}。{在|zài}{兴趣|xìng qù}{和|hé}{就业|jiù yè}{之间|zhī jiān}，{我|wǒ}{会|huì}{先|xiān}{选|xuǎn}{兴趣|xìng qù}，{再|zài}{想|xiǎng}{办法|bàn fǎ}{让|ràng}{兴趣|xìng qù}{变成|biàn chéng}{能力|néng lì}。

(About 330 characters.) "Choosing a subject: interest matters more than what's fashionable.
Every year after the university entrance exam, many parents and students agonise over the choice:
what they like, or what will find them a job? I think the first thing to look at is interest.
First, four years of university are no easy ride. Many specialist courses are both hard and dull;
without interest it's hard to keep going, let alone do well. A classmate of mine was made to study
computing, a popular subject, by his parents, but what he'd always loved was history. He was
miserable for four years, his results were only average, and after graduating he went into work
connected with history anyway. Second, popular subjects don't stay popular. The subject everyone is
scrambling for today may have plenty of graduates four years from now. Whereas someone who really
loves their subject is willing to put in the work, often does better than others, and naturally
needn't fear not finding a job. Of course, interest isn't the only criterion. The pressure of
finding work is real, and it makes sense to look at employment prospects before choosing. In short,
interest is the best teacher. Between interest and jobs, I'd choose interest first, then find a way
to turn it into skill."

{高考|gāo kǎo} is the university entrance exam, {热门|rè mén} "popular, in demand" (lesson 10), {就业|jiù yè} "employment",
{痛苦|tòng kǔ} "painful, miserable" (HSK 5), {唯一|wéi yī} "only" (HSK 5), {标准|biāo zhǔn} "standard" (HSK 4).

Checklist:
- **[[Thesis]]** in the first paragraph ({我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}…), repeated in the conclusion ({总之|zǒng zhī}…).
- **Two reasons**, each with an example or an explanation ({第|dì}{一|yī}…{第|dì}{二|èr}…).
- **A concession** ({当然|dāng rán}…), then back to your view.
- **Connectors**: {首先|shǒu xiān}, {第|dì}{一|yī} / {第|dì}{二|èr}, {相反|xiāng fǎn}, {当然|dāng rán}, {总之|zǒng zhī}; {不|bú}{是|shì}…{而|ér}{是|shì}…; {更|gèng}{不用|bú yòng}{说|shuō}.
- **[[Register]]**: an essay can say {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi} and {我|wǒ}{的|de}{一|yí}{个|gè}{同学|tóng xué}; keep spoken words ({呀|ya}, {吧|ba}) out.
- **Length**: count the characters, at least 300.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Children and school
{他|tā}{一向|yí xiàng}{很|hěn}{用功|yòng gōng}，{从来|cóng lái}{不用|bú yòng}{父母|fù mǔ}{操|cāo}{心|xīn}。
= He's always worked hard; his parents never have to worry about him.
{学|xué}{好|hǎo}{一|yì}{门|mén}{外语|wài yǔ}，{一定|yí dìng}{要|yào}{下功夫|xià gōng fu}。
= To learn a foreign language well, you have to put in the work.
{这|zhè}{首|shǒu}{歌|gē}{伴随|bàn suí}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{整个|zhěng gè}{青春|qīng chūn}。
= This song was with me all through my youth.
{这么|zhè me}{多|duō}{作业|zuò yè}{把|bǎ}{孩子|hái zi}{累|lèi}{坏|huài}{了|le}。
= All this homework has worn the child out.
{名额|míng é}{有限|yǒu xiàn}，{报名|bào míng}{要|yào}{快|kuài}。
= Places are limited: sign up soon.
{孩子|hái zi}{到|dào}{了|le}{青春期|qīng chūn qī}，{需要|xū yào}{更|gèng}{多|duō}{的|de}{理解|lǐ jiě}。
= Children in adolescence need more understanding.
```

{操|cāo}{心|xīn} (to worry about, take trouble over) is HSK 5's.

## Pronunciation

- {好学|hào xué} hào xué: {好|hào} is fourth tone, "fond of", as in {爱好|ài hào} ài hào. {好|hǎo}{学生|xué sheng} hǎo xué sheng is "a good
  student": the same characters, a different word.
- {一向|yí xiàng} yí xiàng and {一辈子|yí bèi zi} yí bèi zi: {一|yī} rises before a fourth tone. {一辈子|yí bèi zi} ends on a light syllable.
- {婴儿|yīng ér} yīng ér: two syllables, not erhua. {娃娃|wá wa} wá wa, {胡子|hú zi} hú zi and {马虎|mǎ hu} mǎ hu end light.
- {少儿|shào ér} shào ér: {少|shào} is shào, "young", as in {少年|shào nián}; {少|shǎo} shǎo is "few".
- {枯燥|kū zào} kū zào and {诞生|dàn shēng} dàn shēng: watch the tones, 1+4 and 4+1.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{一向|yí xiàng}{等|děng}{了|le}{他|tā}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}~~: a single stretch of waiting takes {一直|yì zhí}: {我|wǒ}{一直|yì zhí}{等|děng}{了|le}{他|tā}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}. {一向|yí xiàng} is for
  habits: {他|tā}{一向|yí xiàng}{很|hěn}{准时|zhǔn shí}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{下功夫|xià gōng fu}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}~~: {下功夫|xià gōng fu} takes no object; the area goes in {在|zài}…{上|shàng}: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{上|shàng}{下|xià}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{功夫|gōng fu}, or
  {学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{要|yào}{下功夫|xià gōng fu}.
- ~~{妈妈|mā ma}{伴随|bàn suí}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}~~: {伴随|bàn suí} is written and for things; a person keeps you company with {陪|péi}:
  {妈妈|mā ma}{陪|péi}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}.
- ~~{这个|zhè ge}{消息|xiāo xi}{把|bǎ}{妈妈|mā ma}{高兴|gāo xìng}~~: {把|bǎ} needs a result or degree after the verb: {这个|zhè ge}{消息|xiāo xi}{把|bǎ}{妈妈|mā ma}{高兴|gāo xìng}{坏|huài}{了|le} / {高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}
  {说不出话来|shuō bu chū huà lái}.
- {诞生|dàn shēng} for an ordinary birth sounds grand: {我|wǒ}{出生|chū shēng}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}, not {我|wǒ}{诞生|dàn shēng}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng} (unless you're joking).
- {好学|hào xué} hào xué, not hǎo xué, when it means "eager to learn".

## Key points

- {一向|yí xiàng}: always, all along (a habit or quality); {一直|yì zhí} for one continuous stretch.
- {在|zài}…{上|shàng}{下功夫|xià gōng fu}: put effort into; {下|xià}{了|le}{不|bù}{少|shǎo}{功夫|gōng fu}.
- {伴随|bàn suí}({着|zhe}): to go along with (written; things and processes); {陪|péi} / {陪伴|péi bàn} for people.
- {把|bǎ} with a non-living subject: cause + {把|bǎ} + person affected + verb + result ({这么|zhè me}{多|duō}{作业|zuò yè}{把|bǎ}{孩子|hái zi}{累|lèi}{坏|huài}{了|le}).
- Stages: {婴儿|yīng ér}, {娃娃|wá wa}, {少儿|shào ér}, {未成年人|wèi chéng nián rén}, {青春期|qīng chūn qī}; school: {初等|chū děng} / {中等|zhōng děng} / {高等|gāo děng}, {专科|zhuān kē}, {升学|shēng xué}, {招生|zhāo shēng}, {名额|míng é}, {就读|jiù dú},
  {必修|bì xiū} / {选修|xuǎn xiū}, {理科|lǐ kē} / {文科|wén kē}; study: {用功|yòng gōng}, {用心|yòng xīn}, {马虎|mǎ hu}, {辅导|fǔ dǎo}, {补课|bǔ kè}, {补习|bǔ xí}, {难点|nán diǎn}, {枯燥|kū zào}.
- New characters: {诞|dàn} {枯|kū} {迈|mài} {娃|wá} {淘|táo} {辈|bèi} {婴|yīng} {仰|yǎng}; new radical {非|fēi}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Engagement, marriage and the extended family
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Li Ming has proposed to Wang Fang. The next day she shows Anna the ring, and a week later the two
families meet over dinner: parents, a grandmother, an aunt, a sister and her children. On the way
you'll learn the words of proposing and marrying, the Chinese names for relatives (which say whose
side of the family someone is on), and how to describe people's looks and characters.

The grammar is colloquial, the language of teasing and fond exasperation:

- {看|kàn} / {瞧|qiáo} + {把|bǎ} + someone + adjective + {得|de}: **{看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}…{得|de}**, "look how… you are!" ({看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}！);
- {瞧|qiáo}{你|nǐ} / {看|kàn}{你|nǐ} + adjective + {的|de}: {瞧|qiáo}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{的|de}！, the same idea without {把|bǎ};
- {人家|rén jia}: other people; someone you've mentioned; and, coyly, "me";
- {特地|tè dì}, {特意|tè yì}, {偷偷|tōu tōu}: specially, on purpose, secretly.

## {看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}: look how happy you are!

When someone shows a strong feeling, a friend or relative can tease them, or sympathise, with {看|kàn} or
{瞧|qiáo} + {把|bǎ} + the person + an adjective + {得|de}, and stop there:

{看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}！ — Look at you, you're so happy!

{瞧|qiáo}{把|bǎ}{他|tā}{急|jí}{得|de}！ — Look how worked up he is!

{看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{孩子|hái zi}{冻|dòng}{得|de}！ — Look how cold the poor child is!

- The {得|de} is a degree complement with its ending left off: the full sentence would be {看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}
  ({嘴|zuǐ}{都|dōu}{合不上|hé bu shàng}{了|le}), "so happy (you can't close your mouth)". The listener fills it in.
- {把|bǎ} here brings in the person who feels it. Like lesson 21's {这么|zhè me}{多|duō}{作业|zuò yè}{把|bǎ}{孩子|hái zi}{累|lèi}{坏|huài}{了|le}, there's no doer
  doing anything on purpose: the feeling has "done it" to them.
- The adjectives are feelings and states: {高兴|gāo xìng}, {美|měi} (pleased with oneself), {急|jí}, {累|lèi}, {冻|dòng}, {吓|xià}, {乐|lè}.
- It's spoken, warm and a little teasing. You'll also see it written {看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{的|de}: the two are said the
  same (de).

This is the pattern **{看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}…{得|de}**.

## {瞧|qiáo}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{的|de}: the same without {把|bǎ}

{瞧|qiáo} (spoken "look") or {看|kàn}, + {你|nǐ} / {他|tā} / {她|tā} + adjective + {的|de}:

{瞧|qiáo}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{的|de}！ — Look how pleased you are!

{看|kàn}{你|nǐ}{急|jí}{的|de}，{慢慢|màn màn}{说|shuō}。 — Look at you, all in a rush. Take your time.

{瞧|qiáo}{他|tā}{美|měi}{的|de}！ — Look how pleased with himself he is!

{瞧|qiáo}{你|nǐ}{说|shuō}{的|de}！ is a set reply, "Oh, what a thing to say!", to brush off praise or a polite apology:

"{你|nǐ}{帮|bāng}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{这么|zhè me}{大|dà}{的|de}{忙|máng}，{真|zhēn}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{怎么|zěn me}{谢|xiè}{你|nǐ}。""{瞧|qiáo}{你|nǐ}{说|shuō}{的|de}，{我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{朋友|péng you}{嘛|ma}。" ("You've helped me so much,
I don't know how to thank you." "Oh, don't be silly, we're friends." {嘛|ma} is lesson 23's particle,
"after all".)

## {人家|rén jia}: others, that person, and "me"

{人家|rén jia} rénjia (light at the end) has three uses:

| Use | Example |
|---|---|
| other people, "people" in general | {人家|rén jia}{都|dōu}{结婚|jié hūn}{了|le}，{你|nǐ}{还|hái}{不|bù}{着急|zháo jí}？ Everyone else is married, and you're not worried? |
| a person already mentioned: he, she, they | {你|nǐ}{别|bié}{生气|shēng qì}{了|le}，{人家|rén jia}{也|yě}{是|shì}{好|hǎo}{意|yì}。 Don't be cross: she meant well. |
| "I, me", coy or sulky (mostly young women and children, in jokes) | {人家|rén jia}{等|děng}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{了|le}！ I've been waiting for you for an hour! |

- In the second use, {人家|rén jia} is a little more distant than {他|tā} / {她|tā}, and often defends the person: {人家|rén jia}
  {帮|bāng}{了|le}{你|nǐ}，{你|nǐ}{还|hái}{不|bú}{谢谢|xiè xie}{人家|rén jia}？
- The third is playful. Said by an adult man, it's a joke.
- {人家|rén jiā} rénjiā, with a full second syllable, is a different word, "a household": {村|cūn}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{十|shí}{户|hù}{人家|rén jiā}.

## {特地|tè dì}, {特意|tè yì} and {偷偷|tōu tōu}

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {特地|tè dì} | specially, for this one purpose (often a trip or an effort) | {他|tā}{特地|tè dì}{从|cóng}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{赶|gǎn}{来|lái}{参加|cān jiā}{婚礼|hūn lǐ}。 He came all the way from Shanghai just for the wedding. |
| {特意|tè yì} | on purpose, deliberately (stresses the intention) | {这|zhè}{道|dào}{菜|cài}{是|shì}{特意|tè yì}{为|wèi}{你|nǐ}{做|zuò}{的|de}。 I made this dish specially for you. |
| {偷偷|tōu tōu} | secretly, on the quiet | {他|tā}{偷偷|tōu tōu}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{戒指|jiè zhi}。 He bought a ring without telling anyone. |

- {特地|tè dì} and {特意|tè yì} are often interchangeable. {特地|tè dì} leans to the special trip or effort ({特地|tè dì}{赶|gǎn}{来|lái},
  {特地|tè dì}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}), {特意|tè yì} to the thought behind it ({特意|tè yì}{选|xuǎn}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{的|de}{颜色|yán sè}).
- {偷偷|tōu tōu} usually takes {地|de} in writing ({偷偷|tōu tōu}{地|de}{看|kàn}{了|le}{她|tā}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}) and can be doubled further in speech
  ({偷偷摸摸|tōu tōu mō mō}, furtively, with a hint of disapproval).

## Proposing and marrying

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {求婚|qiú hūn} | to propose | {他|tā}{向|xiàng}{她|tā}{求婚|qiú hūn}{了|le}。 He proposed to her. |

## The extended family

Chinese kinship words tell you whose side someone is on and whether they're older or younger:

| | Father's side | Mother's side |
|---|---|---|
| grandparents | {爷爷|yé ye}, {奶奶|nǎi nai} | {外公|wài gōng}, {外婆|wài pó} (also {姥爷|lǎo ye}, {姥姥|lǎo lao}) |
| aunt (parent's sister) | {姑姑|gū gu} | {姨|yí} ({阿姨|ā yí}) |
| uncle (parent's brother) | {叔叔|shū shu} (younger), {伯伯|bó bo} (older) | {舅舅|jiù jiu} |

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {侄子|zhí zi} | a brother's son (nephew); a brother's daughter is {侄女|zhí nǚ} |
| {外甥|wài shēng} | a sister's son (nephew); a sister's daughter is {外甥女|wài shēng nǚ} |
| {媳妇|xí fu} | daughter-in-law ({儿媳妇|ér xí fu}); in the north, also "wife" (spoken) |
| {夫人|fū rén} | wife (formal, of someone else); Mrs |
| {长辈|zhǎng bèi} | one's elders, the older generation |
| {家属|jiā shǔ} | family members (of a patient, an employee): {病人|bìng rén}{家属|jiā shǔ} |
| {亲属|qīn shǔ} | relatives (formal, written) |
| {称呼|chēng hu} | to address, call; a form of address |

- {外|wài} (outside) marks relatives through one's mother or through a sister or daughter: {外公|wài gōng}, {外婆|wài pó},
  {外甥|wài shēng}, and {外孙|wài sūn} (a daughter's son).
- {姑姑|gū gu} (often just {姑|gū}) is a father's sister; {姨|yí} a mother's sister. {阿姨|ā yí} is also what children call
  any woman of their parents' age, which is why a mother's sister is often {小姨|xiǎo yí} (the youngest) or
  {大姨|dà yí} (the eldest).
- {夫人|fū rén} is polite and formal: {王先生|Wáng xiān sheng}{和|hé}{夫人|fū rén} (Mr and Mrs Wang), {您|nín}{夫人|fū rén} (your wife). For your own wife,
  say {我|wǒ}{爱人|ài ren}, {我|wǒ}{太太|tài tai} or {我|wǒ}{妻子|qī zi}.
- {媳妇|xí fu} is xí fu: the second syllable is light. {我|wǒ}{媳妇|xí fu} is a northern, homely "my wife".
- {称呼|chēng hu} is both the verb and the noun: {我|wǒ}{该|gāi}{怎么|zěn me}{称呼|chēng hu}{您|nín}？ (how should I address you?), {一|yí}{个|gè}{称呼|chēng hu}.
  Engaged couples call each other's parents {叔叔|shū shu} and {阿姨|ā yí} until the wedding, then {爸|bà} and {妈|mā}.

1. The first dinner at which the two families met, and how the stiffness turned to warmth.
2. She asked Li Ming's zodiac sign and declared it a good match ({跟|gēn}{我们|wǒ men}{芳芳|Fāng fāng}{合得来|hé de lái}), and everyone

**The two families' first meal.** "Last Saturday evening our two families finally met. Li Ming's
mum chose the place, a quiet old restaurant. I'd been nervous about this meal for days: I changed
outfits three times, and in the end my sister helped me choose one in a tasteful colour.

Seven of us came from my family: Dad, Mum, Grandma, my sister, her husband and their two children.
Four came from Li Ming's: his mum and dad and his aunt. Li Ming is an only child, and his aunt has
always doted on him; she came all the way from Tianjin for this. The moment we met she took my hand: 'Our Li Ming has always
been a good boy. You'll have to keep him in line from now on.'

At first everyone was a little formal. Li Ming stood up, red in the face, poured tea for each of the
older people, called my parents 'Uncle' and 'Auntie' and my grandmother 'Grandma'. Grandma looked him
up and down through her reading glasses, then asked: 'Xiao Li, what's your animal sign?' Li Ming said
the dog. Grandma nodded: 'Good. You'll get on with our Fangfang.' Everyone burst out laughing, and
the atmosphere relaxed at once.

During the meal my seven-year-old nephew kept staring at Li Ming, and at last he couldn't hold back:
'Are you the man who's going to marry my auntie?' Li Ming answered seriously: 'Yes. Do you agree?'
My nephew thought about it and said: 'Then you have to be nice to her, or I don't agree.' Even Dad,
always so serious, laughed out loud.

Near the end of the meal, Li Ming's mother took a small box out of her bag, with a pearl necklace
inside. She said Li Ming's grandmother had left it to her; she had worn it for thirty years and had
always meant to give it to her son's future wife when he married. She took my hand and said: 'From
now on we're one family.' Looking at the necklace I was moved and shy at once, and almost cried.

After the meal Grandma took a red envelope out of her pocket and pressed it into Li Ming's hand:
'Your first visit: it's our family's custom.' Li Ming looked at me, embarrassed, and I laughed: 'Take
it, it's Grandma's way of saying welcome.' In our family, the older people always give a red envelope
the first time they meet a future member of the family, as a welcome.

Finally Dad raised his glass and said a few words. He said that with his daughter getting married,
a father finds it a little hard to let go, but seeing how steady and sensible Li Ming is, he isn't
worried. He hoped we'd understand and look after each other and make a happy little home. The two
families drank a toast together, and the small private room was full of laughter.

On the way home Li Ming asked me: 'So is your grandma happy with me or not?' I said: 'Didn't you
see? She didn't stop smiling all evening.'

We plan to marry next autumn. There's more than a year until the wedding and a lot to prepare, but
I'm not in the least worried. That evening, for the first time, I really felt that marriage isn't
just about two people: it's a happy event for two families."

```speak
{他|tā}{特地|tè dì}{从|cóng}{外地|wài dì}{赶|gǎn}{回来|huí lái}{参加|cān jiā}{婚礼|hūn lǐ}。
= He came back from out of town just for the wedding.
{我|wǒ}{该|gāi}{怎么|zěn me}{称呼|chēng hu}{您|nín}？
= How should I address you?
{她|tā}{嫁|jià}{给|gěi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{温柔|wēn róu}{的|de}{人|rén}。
= She married a gentle man.
{祝|zhù}{你们|nǐ men}{婚姻|hūn yīn}{幸福|xìng fú}！
= Wishing you a happy marriage!
```

## Pronunciation

- {人家|rén jia} rén jia (others, "me"), light at the end; {人家|rén jiā} rén jiā (a household) is another word.
- {娶|qǔ} qǔ (third tone) and {去|qù} qù (fourth): {娶|qǔ}{媳妇|xí fu} qǔ xí fu, not qù.
- {嫁|jià} jià and {家|jiā} jiā: the same syllable, a falling tone for the verb.
- {侄子|zhí zi} zhí zi, {外甥|wài shēng} wài shēng, {舅舅|jiù jiu} jiù jiu, {姑姑|gū gu} gū gu, {媳妇|xí fu} xí fu, {眉毛|méi mao} méi mao: kinship and body
  words that end light (except {外甥|wài shēng}).
- {瞧|qiáo} qiáo (second tone): q + iao, lips spread then rounded.
- {看中|kàn zhòng} kàn zhòng: {中|zhòng} is fourth tone here, as in {中奖|zhòng jiǎng} (to win a prize).

## Common mistakes

- {嫁|jià} usually takes {给|gěi} before the husband: {她|tā}{嫁|jià}{给|gěi}{了|le}{他|tā}, the safe form ({嫁|jià}{了|le} + the husband is heard, but less often). ({娶|qǔ} takes the wife directly: {他|tā}{娶|qǔ}
  {了|le}{她|tā}.)
- ~~{他|tā}{娶|qǔ}{给|gěi}{她|tā}~~: {娶|qǔ} has no {给|gěi}.
- ~~{看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{了|le}~~: the pattern ends in {得|de} (or {的|de}): {看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}！
- {我|wǒ}{夫人|fū rén} is heard, but for your own wife {我|wǒ}{爱人|ài ren} / {我|wǒ}{太太|tài tai} / {我|wǒ}{妻子|qī zi} is more modest; {夫人|fū rén} is for
  someone else's wife.
- {姑姑|gū gu} / {姨|yí} and {叔叔|shū shu} / {舅舅|jiù jiu} are not interchangeable: they tell which parent is the link.
- {人家|rén jia} rénjia "others" never takes {们|men}: ~~{人家|rén jia}{们|men}~~.

## Key points

- {看|kàn} / {瞧|qiáo} + {把|bǎ} + person + adjective + {得|de}: teasing or sympathy ({看|kàn}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}！); {瞧|qiáo}{你|nǐ} + adjective + {的|de}
  ({瞧|qiáo}{你|nǐ}{美|měi}{的|de}！); {瞧|qiáo}{你|nǐ}{说|shuō}{的|de}！ "don't be silly".
- {人家|rén jia}: others; that person; coy "me".
- {特地|tè dì} (a special trip or effort), {特意|tè yì} (on purpose), {偷偷|tōu tōu}({地|de}) (secretly).
- {求婚|qiú hūn}, {订婚|dìng hūn}, {戒指|jiè zhi}, {婚姻|hūn yīn}, {嫁|jià}{给|gěi}, {娶|qǔ}, {喜事|xǐ shì}, {终身|zhōng shēn}{大事|dà shì}, {继承|jì chéng}; relatives: {姑姑|gū gu}, {姨|yí}, {舅舅|jiù jiu}, {侄子|zhí zi}, {外甥|wài shēng}, {媳妇|xí fu}, {夫人|fū rén},
  {长辈|zhǎng bèi}, {家属|jiā shǔ}, {亲属|qīn shǔ}, {称呼|chēng hu}.
- New characters: {逗|dòu} {姻|yīn} {孕|yùn} {谐|xié} {嘿|hēi} {戒|jiè} {舅|jiù} {嫁|jià} {眉|méi} {瞧|qiáo} {娶|qǔ} {甥|shēng} {哇|wā} {媳|xí} {珠|zhū} {侄|zhí}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Conflict, debate and reconciliation
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Two of Li Ming's colleagues in the translation department fall out over a rushed job, and Li Ming
ends up in the middle. This lesson is about quarrelling and making up: the words for arguments,
anger and blame, for listening and admitting you were wrong, and the colloquial patterns people
reach for in the heat of the moment.

The grammar is mostly spoken:

- **{这|zhè}{也|yě}{不|bù} X，{那|nà}{也|yě}{不|bù} Y**: "won't do this, won't do that", for someone nothing pleases;
- **{放|fàng}{着|zhe} X {不|bù} Y**: to pass over an obvious choice ({放|fàng}{着|zhe}{电梯|diàn tī}{不|bú}{坐|zuò});
- {明明|míng míng}: "obviously", against what someone says or does;
- {倒是|dào shi}: contrary to expectation; "it's true that…"; "come on, do…!";
- {干脆|gān cuì}: "simply, just" (cut the matter short);
- {也好|yě hǎo}, {算了|suàn le}, {得了|dé le} and the particles {啦|la} and {嘛|ma};
- {露|lòu} lòu, "to show" in speech ({露面|lòu miàn}, {露一手|lòu yì shǒu}).

You'll also see the same complaint said in a quarrel and written in a formal email, and tell a
story from four pictures.

## {这|zhè}{也|yě}{不|bù} X，{那|nà}{也|yě}{不|bù} Y: nothing will do

Two clauses with {这|zhè}{也|yě} and {那|nà}{也|yě} and a negative, for someone who rejects everything, or for a
situation where nothing works:

{这|zhè}{也|yě}{不|bù}{吃|chī}，{那|nà}{也|yě}{不|bù}{吃|chī}，{你|nǐ}{到底|dào dǐ}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{什么|shén me}？ — You won't eat this, you won't eat that: what do you want?

{他|tā}{这|zhè}{也|yě}{不|bù}{满意|mǎn yì}，{那|nà}{也|yě}{不|bù}{满意|mǎn yì}。 — Nothing satisfies him.

{我|wǒ}{这|zhè}{也|yě}{不|bú}{会|huì}，{那|nà}{也|yě}{不|bú}{会|huì}，{怎么|zěn me}{找|zhǎo}{工作|gōng zuò}？ — I can't do anything: how am I going to find a job?

- The two verbs or adjectives can be the same ({这|zhè}{也|yě}{不|bù}{吃|chī}，{那|nà}{也|yě}{不|bù}{吃|chī}) or two of a kind ({这|zhè}{也|yě}{不|bú}{让|ràng}{说|shuō}，{那|nà}{也|yě}{不|bú}
  {让|ràng}{问|wèn}).
- It complains or exaggerates: it isn't a list of real things.
- The positive form, {这|zhè}{也|yě}{想|xiǎng} X，{那|nà}{也|yě}{想|xiǎng} X, is for someone who wants everything: {孩子|hái zi}{在|zài}{商店|shāng diàn}{里|lǐ}{这|zhè}{也|yě}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}，{那|nà}{也|yě}
  {想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}.

This is the pattern **{这|zhè}{也|yě}{不|bù} X，{那|nà}{也|yě}{不|bù} Y**.

## {放|fàng}{着|zhe} X {不|bù} Y: passing over the obvious choice

{放|fàng}{着|zhe} (leaving there) + something available + {不|bù} + the verb you'd expect, then what the person does
instead:

{放|fàng}{着|zhe}{电梯|diàn tī}{不|bú}{坐|zuò}，{非|fēi}{要|yào}{走|zǒu}{楼梯|lóu tī}。 — There's a lift right there, and he insists on taking the stairs.

{放|fàng}{着|zhe}{好好|hǎo hǎo}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}{不|bú}{做|zuò}，{你|nǐ}{要|yào}{去|qù}{冒险|mào xiǎn}？ — You'd throw over a perfectly good job to take a gamble?

{放|fàng}{着|zhe}{现成|xiàn chéng}{的|de}{饭|fàn}{不|bù}{吃|chī}，{又|yòu}{去|qù}{买|mǎi}{外卖|wài mài}。 — There's food ready, and you go and buy a takeaway.

- It nearly always criticises or wonders at a choice: the speaker thinks X was the sensible thing.
- The second half often has {非|fēi}{要|yào} (insist on), {却|què} or {反而|fǎn ér} (HSK 5's "instead").
- {现成|xiàn chéng} is "ready-made"; {外卖|wài mài} (takeaway) is HSK 3's.

This is the pattern **{放|fàng}{着|zhe} X {不|bù} Y**.

## {明明|míng míng}: obviously (and yet…)

{明明|míng míng} says something is plainly true, usually to set it against what someone says or does:

{他|tā}{明明|míng míng}{知道|zhī dào}，{却|què}{说|shuō}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}。 — He knows perfectly well, but says he doesn't.

{明明|míng míng}{是|shì}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{错|cuò}，{你|nǐ}{还|hái}{怪|guài}{我|wǒ}？ — It's obviously your fault, and you're blaming me?

{明明|míng míng} goes after the subject or at the start of the clause, and the other half ({却|què}, {还|hái}, {怎么|zěn me}) says what
doesn't fit. It sounds indignant or puzzled; in a calm statement use {显然|xiǎn rán} (HSK 5).

## {倒是|dào shi}: three uses

{倒是|dào shi} dào shi (light at the end) adds the speaker's attitude:

| Use | Example |
|---|---|
| contrary to expectation, "actually" | {平时|píng shí}{最|zuì}{忙|máng}{的|de}{他|tā}，{今天|jīn tiān}{倒是|dào shi}{来|lái}{得|de}{最|zuì}{早|zǎo}。 He's usually the busiest, but today he was actually first. |
| "it's true that… (but)": a concession, with the adjective twice | {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{好看|hǎo kàn}{倒是|dào shi}{好看|hǎo kàn}，{就是|jiù shì}{太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}。 It's nice enough, it's just too expensive. |
| urging: "come on, do…!" | {你|nǐ}{倒是|dào shi}{说话|shuō huà}{呀|ya}！ Say something, will you! |

- {那|nà}{倒是|dào shi} / {那|nà}{倒|dào}{也|yě}{是|shì} (that's true, fair enough) concedes a point in conversation.
- {倒|dào} alone (HSK 5) works in the same places; {倒是|dào shi} is a little softer and very common in speech.

## {干脆|gān cuì}: simply, just

{干脆|gān cuì} gān cuì as an adverb cuts a matter short: instead of hesitating, just do it:

{太|tài}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{干脆|gān cuì}{打车|dǎ chē}{吧|ba}。 — It's too late: let's just take a taxi.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{说|shuō}{不|bu}{清楚|qīng chu}，{干脆|gān cuì}{当面|dāng miàn}{谈|tán}。 — We'll never sort this out like this: let's just talk face to face.

As an adjective, {干脆|gān cuì} is "straightforward, decisive": {他|tā}{说话|shuō huà}{很|hěn}{干脆|gān cuì} (he doesn't beat about the bush),
{办事|bàn shì}{干脆|gān cuì} (gets things done without fuss). {={干|gān}=} here is gān, "dry"; in traditional the word is {+{干脆|gān cuì}+}.

## {就算|jiù suàn}, {也好|yě hǎo}, {算了|suàn le} and {得了|dé le}

- {就算|jiù suàn}…{也|yě}…: even if (spoken), the concession of module 1: {就算|jiù suàn}{你|nǐ}{翻|fān}{得|de}{再|zài}{好|hǎo}，{过|guò}{了|le}{期限|qī xiàn}{也|yě}{没|méi}{用|yòng}。 (Even
  if your translation is excellent, it's no use after the deadline.) {即使|jí shǐ} is the written partner.
- {也好|yě hǎo}: (1) …{也好|yě hǎo}，…{也好|yě hǎo}: whether… or…: {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{也好|yě hǎo}，{不|bú}{去|qù}{也好|yě hǎo}，{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{声|shēng}。 (2) At the end: "that's
  fine too", accepting a change: {不|bú}{去|qù}{也好|yě hǎo}，{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}{休息|xiū xi}。
- {算了|suàn le}: "forget it, let it go": {算了|suàn le}，{别|bié}{说|shuō}{了|le}。 {算了|suàn le}{吧|ba}，{这|zhè}{次|cì}{就|jiù}{原谅|yuán liàng}{他|tā}。
- {得了|dé le} dé le: "that's enough, all right": {得了|dé le}，{别|bié}{哭|kū}{了|le}。 {得了|dé le}{吧|ba}！ is "oh, come off it!" (not
  believing someone). {不得了|bù dé liǎo} (HSK 5's "terribly") and {了不得|liǎo bu dé} are other words: there {了|le} is liǎo.

## {啦|la} and {嘛|ma}

- {啦|la} la is {了|le} + {啊|a} run together: a change or a done thing, said with feeling: {好|hǎo}{啦|la}，{别|bié}{生气|shēng qì}{啦|la}！
  (All right, don't be cross any more!) {我|wǒ}{来|lái}{啦|la}！ (Here I am!)
- {嘛|ma} ma says "obviously, after all" or softens a request: {他|tā}{还是|hái shi}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}{嘛|ma}。 (He's only a child,
  after all.) {有|yǒu}{话|huà}{好好|hǎo hǎo}{说|shuō}{嘛|ma}。 (Let's talk about it calmly, come on.) It isn't the question particle
  {吗|ma}: {嘛|ma} is never a yes–no question.

## {露|lòu}: to show (spoken)

露 has two readings. Lesson 17's {露|lù} lù (dew) and the written words {暴露|bào lù} bào lù (to expose) and {露出|lù chū}
lù chū (to reveal, show) have lù. In everyday phrases it's {露|lòu} lòu:

| Phrase | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {露面|lòu miàn} | to show one's face, appear | {经理|jīng lǐ}{今天|jīn tiān}{一直|yì zhí}{没|méi}{露面|lòu miàn}。 The manager hasn't shown up all day. |
| {露一手|lòu yì shǒu} | to show off a skill | {今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{大家|dà jiā}{露一手|lòu yì shǒu}，{做|zuò}{个|gè}{拿手菜|ná shǒu cài}。 Today I'll show you what I can do and cook my best dish. |
| {露脸|lòu liǎn} | to put in an appearance; to shine | {这|zhè}{次|cì}{比赛|bǐ sài}{他|tā}{可|kě}{露脸|lòu liǎn}{了|le}。 He really made a name for himself in this competition. |

{拿手菜|ná shǒu cài} is one's best dish ({拿手|ná shǒu}, good at).

## Quarrels and fights

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {冲突|chōng tū} | conflict; to clash | {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{的|de}{意见|yì jiàn}{发生|fā shēng}{了|le}{冲突|chōng tū}。 Their views clashed. |
| {对立|duì lì} | to be opposed; opposition | {双方|shuāng fāng}{的|de}{立场|lì chǎng}{完全|wán quán}{对立|duì lì}。 The two sides' positions are completely opposed. |
| {对抗|duì kàng} | to confront, resist | {跟|gēn}{父母|fù mǔ}{对抗|duì kàng} to defy one's parents |
| {冲动|chōng dòng} | impulse; impulsive | {别|bié}{冲动|chōng dòng}，{先|xiān}{冷静|lěng jìng}{一下|yí xià}。 Don't do anything rash: calm down first. |
| {争吵|zhēng chǎo} | to quarrel (written) | {两|liǎng}{人|rén}{发生|fā shēng}{了|le}{争吵|zhēng chǎo}。 The two of them had a quarrel. |
| {吵架|chǎo jià} | to quarrel (spoken) | {他们|tā men}{俩|liǎ}{又|yòu}{吵架|chǎo jià}{了|le}。 They've been arguing again. |
| {打架|dǎ jià} | to fight (physically) | {小时候|xiǎo shí hou}{我|wǒ}{常|cháng}{跟|gēn}{弟弟|dì di}{打架|dǎ jià}。 As kids my brother and I fought a lot. |
| {争论|zhēng lùn} | to argue, debate | {大家|dà jiā}{争论|zhēng lùn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{上午|shàng wǔ}。 Everyone argued all morning. |
| {争议|zhēng yì} | controversy, dispute | {这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{争议|zhēng yì}。 It's a very controversial question. |
| {质疑|zhì yí} | to question, query | {有|yǒu}{人|rén}{质疑|zhì yí}{这个|zhè ge}{数字|shù zì}。 Some people questioned the figure. |
| {主张|zhǔ zhāng} | to advocate; a view | {我|wǒ}{主张|zhǔ zhāng}{先|xiān}{听听|tīng ting}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{意见|yì jiàn}。 I'm for hearing what everyone thinks first. |
| {赞同|zàn tóng} | to approve of, agree | {我|wǒ}{赞同|zàn tóng}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{看法|kàn fǎ}。 I agree with you. |
| {指责|zhǐ zé} | to criticise, blame | {别|bié}{总|zǒng}{指责|zhǐ zé}{别人|bié ren}。 Stop always blaming other people. |
| {嘲笑|cháo xiào} | to ridicule, laugh at | {不要|bú yào}{嘲笑|cháo xiào}{别人|bié ren}{的|de}{发音|fā yīn}。 Don't laugh at people's pronunciation. |
| {欺骗|qī piàn} | to deceive | {他|tā}{欺骗|qī piàn}{了|le}{所有|suǒ yǒu}{人|rén}。 He fooled everyone. |
| {强迫|qiǎng pò} | to force | {不要|bú yào}{强迫|qiǎng pò}{孩子|hái zi}{吃|chī}{东西|dōng xi}。 Don't force children to eat. |
| {暗示|àn shì} | to hint; a hint | {她|tā}{暗示|àn shì}{我|wǒ}{该|gāi}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 She hinted it was time for me to go. |
| {暴露|bào lù} | to expose, reveal | {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{暴露|bào lù}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{问题|wèn tí}。 This affair has brought a lot of problems to light. |
| {举动|jǔ dòng} | an act, a move | {他|tā}{的|de}{举动|jǔ dòng}{让|ràng}{大家|dà jiā}{很|hěn}{惊讶|jīng yà}。 His behaviour surprised everyone. |

- {冲突|chōng tū} and {冲动|chōng dòng} have chōng (to rush, clash); in traditional both are {+{冲突|chōng tū}+}, {+{冲动|chōng dòng}+}.
- {争吵|zhēng chǎo} is the written word for a quarrel (in news, reports); {吵架|chǎo jià} is what you say. {打架|dǎ jià} involves blows.
- {争论|zhēng lùn} is arguing about something (a question, a plan); {争议|zhēng yì} is the dispute that remains ({有|yǒu}{争议|zhēng yì}, {引起|yǐn qǐ}
  {争议|zhēng yì}). Lesson 26 brings {立场|lì chǎng} (position, standpoint).
- {强迫|qiǎng pò} is qiǎng pò: {强|qiǎng} qiǎng "to force" ({强|qiáng} qiáng "strong" is another reading).

## Feelings: anger, scorn and surprise

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {愤怒|fèn nù} | angry, indignant (written) | {大家|dà jiā}{对|duì}{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{行为|xíng wéi}{感到|gǎn dào}{愤怒|fèn nù}。 People are angry about this behaviour. |
| {恨|hèn} | to hate | {我|wǒ}{恨|hèn}{自己|zì jǐ}{当时|dāng shí}{没|méi}{说|shuō}{出来|chū lái}。 I hate myself for not saying it then. |
| {狠|hěn} | ruthless; firmly, hard | {他|tā}{狠|hěn}{狠|hěn}{地|de}{批评|pī píng}{了|le}{我|wǒ}。 He gave me a real dressing-down. |
| {嫌|xián} | to dislike, mind, find (too…) | {她|tā}{嫌|xián}{我|wǒ}{说话|shuō huà}{太|tài}{直|zhí}。 She thinks I'm too blunt. |
| {赖|lài} | to put the blame on; to hang on | {别|bié}{赖|lài}{我|wǒ}！ Don't blame me! {赖|lài}{在|zài}{床|chuáng}{上|shàng}{不|bù}{起来|qǐ lái} to lie in and not get up |
| {混|hùn} | to mix (up); to muddle through | {别|bié}{把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{词|cí}{混|hùn}{在|zài}{一起|yì qǐ}。 Don't mix these two words up. |
| {服|fú} | to be convinced by, accept | {你|nǐ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{对|duì}，{我|wǒ}{服|fú}{了|le}。 You're right, I give in. |

<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. A quarrel with a colleague, how it was resolved, and what the writer learned about conflict.
2. She was angry with him and with herself for speaking so rashly. Remembering her mother's way of
   stopping fights, she realised that in a quarrel everyone tries to prove they're right and nobody
   really listens.
3. Shi Feng came to talk to her face to face, explained the client's pressure, and admitted
   honestly that her translation was more careful than his.
4. That disagreeing is fine: it isn't about agreeing with everything; but listen to the other side
   first ({先|xiān}{听|tīng}{完|wán}{别人|bié ren}{的|de}{话|huà}，{再说|zài shuō}"{不|bù}"，{也|yě}{不|bù}{迟|chí}).

**After the quarrel**, by Jiang Hui. "In my third month at the company, I had a real row with my
colleague Shi Feng. The cause is simple enough: to save time, he changed my translation without a
word. But at the time I was furious: I felt he hadn't just changed a few sentences but looked down
on me as a newcomer.

We quarrelled in the office that day, louder and louder, neither giving way. He found me too slow; I
accused him of not respecting other people. While I was talking he kept looking down at his phone,
which made me even angrier. Everyone in the office stopped what they were doing. Looking back, what we were arguing about wasn't the
translation but face. It was thanks to Li Ming beside us, telling us again and again to calm down,
that we didn't say anything worse.

When I got home I couldn't sleep. I hated him, and I hated myself a little too: why do I say such
rash things the moment I'm upset? I remembered fighting with my brother as a child: each time my mum
made us stop first and each say what we'd done wrong. Back then I often got impatient: I felt she
was being unfair to me, when it was obviously my brother who'd started it. Only as an adult did I
understand that in a quarrel everyone is busy proving they're right, and hardly anyone really
listens to the other side.

The next day I happened to arrive half an hour earlier than usual, and to my surprise Shi Feng was
already there. I was a bit taken aback; he, on the other hand, was very calm, came straight up to
me and said he'd like to talk face to face. He told me that the client had kept phoning to chase him
that day and he'd been frantic: it never crossed his mind I'd mind. And he said something honest:
'Actually your translation is more careful than mine. I noticed it as I was changing it.' That
moved me at once. I admitted too that in trying so hard to be perfect, I'd held up the whole
project.

After that talk we made a rule: if we disagree, we say it face to face, not behind each other's
backs; if there's a problem, we ask first and don't rush to conclusions. Several weeks on, we still
disagree; sometimes we argue for ages over how to translate one word, but we've never quarrelled
again. Once he even said with a laugh: 'You were right to query that. I give in.'

Our department has a new habit now too: every Friday afternoon we have a coffee together and bring
out whatever problems came up that week. Someone jokingly calls it 'quarrel time'. But this way,
small misunderstandings don't pile up and turn into big conflicts.

This taught me a lesson: conflict between colleagues often comes from misunderstanding. Opposition
and confrontation don't solve problems; if you're willing to sit down calmly and hear the other
side's position, the problem is often half solved. Of course, that doesn't mean forcing yourself to
agree to everything. Where you need to stand firm, stand firm; but hearing the other person out
before you say 'no' is never too late."

> {一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{的|de}{下午|xià wǔ}，{小区|xiǎo qū}{的|de}{游乐场|yóu lè chǎng}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{孩子|hái zi}{在|zài}{玩|wán}。{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{六|liù}{岁|suì}{左右|zuǒ yòu}{的|de}{小|xiǎo}{男|nán}{孩|hái}{同时|tóng shí}{看中|kàn zhòng}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{足球|zú qiú}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{抓|zhuā}{住|zhù}{了|le}{球|qiú}{的|de}{这边|zhè biān}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{抓|zhuā}{住|zhù}{了|le}{那边|nà biān}，{谁|shéi}{也|yě}{不|bù}{肯|kěn}{放|fàng}{手|shǒu}。
>
> "{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{先|xiān}{拿|ná}{到|dào}{的|de}！""{明明|míng míng}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{先|xiān}{看见|kàn jiàn}{的|de}！"{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{一边|yì biān}{抢|qiǎng}{一边|yì biān}{大|dà}{声|shēng}{吵架|chǎo jià}。{抢|qiǎng}{着|zhe}{抢|qiǎng}{着|zhe}，{个子|gè zi}{小|xiǎo}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{的|de}{那个|nà ge}{男|nán}{孩|hái}{没|méi}{站|zhàn}{稳|wěn}，{摔|shuāi}{在|zài}{了|le}{地上|dì shang}，"{哇|wā}"{的|de}{一|yì}{声|shēng}{哭|kū}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}。
>
> {这|zhè}{时候|shí hou}，{一|yí}{位|wèi}{老|lǎo}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{走|zǒu}{了|le}{过来|guò lái}。{她|tā}{蹲|dūn}{下来|xià lái}，{先|xiān}{把|bǎ}{哭|kū}{的|de}{孩子|hái zi}{扶|fú}{起来|qǐ lái}，{然后|rán hòu}{温柔|wēn róu}{地|de}{问|wèn}{他们|tā men}："{你们|nǐ men}{俩|liǎ}{都|dōu}{想|xiǎng}{踢|tī}{球|qiú}，{对|duì}{吧|ba}？{可是|kě shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{踢|tī}，{多|duō}{没意思|méi yì si}{啊|a}。{要不|yào bù}{你们|nǐ men}{一起|yì qǐ}{踢|tī}，{看|kàn}{谁|shéi}{踢|tī}{得|de}{远|yuǎn}？"{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}{你|nǐ}{看看|kàn kan}{我|wǒ}，{我|wǒ}{看看|kàn kan}{你|nǐ}，{都|dōu}{不|bù}{说话|shuō huà}{了|le}。
>
> {过|guò}{了|le}{一会儿|yí huìr}，{游乐场|yóu lè chǎng}{里|lǐ}{传|chuán}{来|lái}{了|le}{笑|xiào}{声|shēng}。{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}{你|nǐ}{一|yì}{脚|jiǎo}，{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{脚|jiǎo}，{把|bǎ}{球|qiú}{踢|tī}{来|lái}{踢|tī}{去|qù}，{玩|wán}{得|de}{满头大汗|mǎn tóu dà hàn}。{刚才|gāng cái}{的|de}{争吵|zhēng chǎo}，{好像|hǎo xiàng}{根本|gēn běn}{没有|méi yǒu}{发生|fā shēng}{过|guo}。

(About 260 characters.) "One Saturday afternoon the compound playground was full of children.
Two boys of about six both took a fancy to the same football; one grabbed one side and one the
other, and neither would let go. 'I got it first!' 'I saw it first, obviously!' They squabbled
loudly as they pulled. In the middle of it the smaller boy lost his footing, fell over and burst
into tears. Just then an old woman came over. She crouched down, helped the crying child up, and
asked them gently: 'You both want to play football, don't you? But kicking a ball on your own is
no fun. Why don't you play together and see who can kick it furthest?' The two boys looked at each
other and went quiet. A little later there was laughter in the playground: the two of them kicked
the ball back and forth, a kick each, until they were dripping with sweat. The quarrel of a moment
ago seemed never to have happened."

{游乐场|yóu lè chǎng} (playground), {摔|shuāi} (to fall, HSK 4), {蹲|dūn} (to crouch, lesson 29), {扶|fú} (to help up, HSK 5), {满头大汗|mǎn tóu dà hàn}
(dripping with sweat), {抢|qiǎng}{着|zhe}{抢|qiǎng}{着|zhe} (HSK 5's A{着|zhe}A{着|zhe}: in the middle of…). Time words and connectors carry
the four pictures: {一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{的|de}{下午|xià wǔ}, {这|zhè}{时候|shí hou}, {过|guò}{了|le}{一会儿|yí huìr}.
</details>

## Write it: a formal complaint

A complaint is one of the exam's practical texts. Write 150–200 characters to your building's
property-management office ({物业|wù yè}) about noise from the flat above at night: say who you are, what
the problem is and since when, what you've already tried, and what you'd like them to do.

<details>
<summary>A model complaint</summary>

> {物业管理处|wù yè guǎn lǐ chù}：
>
> {你们|nǐ men}{好|hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{是|shì}5{号|hào}{楼|lóu}1201{的|de}{住户|zhù hù}。{最近|zuì jìn}{一|yí}{个|gè}{月|yuè}，{楼|lóu}{上|shàng}1301{几乎|jī hū}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{十一|shí yī}{点|diǎn}{以后|yǐ hòu}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{声音|shēng yīn}，{像|xiàng}{是|shì}{在|zài}{搬|bān}{家具|jiā jù}、{跑步|pǎo bù}，{有时|yǒu shí}{一直|yì zhí}{到|dào}{凌晨|líng chén}{一|yì}{点|diǎn}。{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{家人|jiā rén}{因此|yīn cǐ}{常常|cháng cháng}{睡|shuì}{不|bu}{好|hǎo}，{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{上班|shàng bān}{也|yě}{受到|shòu dào}{了|le}{影响|yǐng xiǎng}。
>
> {我|wǒ}{曾经|céng jīng}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}{上|shàng}{楼|lóu}，{当面|dāng miàn}{跟|gēn}{他们|tā men}{沟通|gōu tōng}，{对方|duì fāng}{也|yě}{表示|biǎo shì}{会|huì}{注意|zhù yì}，{可是|kě shì}{情况|qíng kuàng}{并|bìng}{没有|méi yǒu}{改变|gǎi biàn}。{为了|wèi le}{避免|bì miǎn}{邻居|lín jū}{之间|zhī jiān}{发生|fā shēng}{冲突|chōng tū}，{我|wǒ}{希望|xī wàng}{物业|wù yè}{能|néng}{出面|chū miàn}，{提醒|tí xǐng}{他们|tā men}{晚上|wǎn shang}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{以后|yǐ hòu}{减少|jiǎn shǎo}{噪声|zào shēng}。
>
> {谢谢|xiè xie}！
>
> 5{号|hào}{楼|lóu}1201{住户|zhù hù} {王先生|Wáng xiān sheng}
>
> 2031{年|nián}3{月|yuè}12{日|rì}

(About 190 characters.) "To the property management office: Hello. I'm a resident of 1201,
Building 5. For the past month, almost every night after eleven there has been loud noise from 1301
above, like furniture being moved or someone running, sometimes until one in the morning. As a
result my family and I often sleep badly, and our work the next day suffers. I've been upstairs
twice to talk to them in person; they said they'd be careful, but nothing has changed. To avoid a
conflict between neighbours, I'd like the office to step in and remind them to keep the noise down
after ten at night. Thank you. Mr Wang, resident of 1201, Building 5. 12 March 2031"

{住户|zhù hù} (resident, household), {凌晨|líng chén} (small hours, lesson 19), {因此|yīn cǐ} (as a result, HSK 4), {曾经|céng jīng} (once,
before, HSK 5), {对方|duì fāng} (the other party, HSK 5), {避免|bì miǎn} (to avoid, HSK 4), {出面|chū miàn} (to step in, act on
someone's behalf).

Checklist:
- **Format**: the addressee and a colon; who you are; the date at the end.
- **Facts first**: since when, what time, what kind of noise; then what you've tried.
- **[[Register]]**: polite and calm: {希望|xī wàng}, {提醒|tí xǐng}, {减少|jiǎn shǎo}; no {明明|míng míng}, {凭|píng}{什么|shén me} or {啦|la}.
- **A clear request** at the end.
</details>

## Pronunciation

- {强迫|qiǎng pò} qiǎng pò and {勉强|miǎn qiǎng} miǎn qiǎng: {强|qiǎng} is qiǎng (to force) in both; {强|qiáng} qiáng is "strong".
- {恨|hèn} hèn, {狠|hěn} hěn and {很|hěn} hěn: listen for the falling tone of "hate".
- {得了|dé le} dé le ("that's enough") and {不得了|bù dé liǎo} bù dé liǎo: dé in both, but {了|le} is le, then liǎo.
- {倒是|dào shi} dào shi, {教训|jiào xun} jiào xun: light second syllables.
- {啦|la} la and {嘛|ma} ma are always light; {嘛|ma} is never a question.
- {露面|lòu miàn} lòu miàn, {露一手|lòu yì shǒu} lòu yì shǒu (spoken lòu) beside {暴露|bào lù} bào lù (written lù).
- {为难|wéi nán} wéi nán: second tone on {为|wéi}, as in {成为|chéng wéi} chéng wéi.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{这|zhè}{也|yě}{不|bù}{吃|chī}，{那|nà}{也|yě}{吃|chī}~~: both halves are negative: {这|zhè}{也|yě}{不|bù}{吃|chī}，{那|nà}{也|yě}{不|bù}{吃|chī}.
- ~~{放|fàng}{着|zhe}{电梯|diàn tī}{不|bù}，{走|zǒu}{楼梯|lóu tī}~~: the verb comes after {不|bù}: {放|fàng}{着|zhe}{电梯|diàn tī}{不|bú}{坐|zuò}.
- {明明|míng míng}{他|tā}{是|shì}{错|cuò}{的|de} is understood, but {明明|míng míng} usually comes after the subject: {他|tā}{明明|míng míng}{错|cuò}{了|le} / {明明|míng míng}{是|shì}{他|tā}{错|cuò}{了|le}.
- {嘛|ma} isn't a question: ~~{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{嘛|ma}？~~ for "are you going?" is {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{吗|ma}？ ({你|nǐ}{去|qù}{嘛|ma}！ is "go on, go!").
- ~~{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{恨|hèn}~~ for "I'm very angry": {恨|hèn} is "to hate (someone, something)"; angry is {生气|shēng qì} / {愤怒|fèn nù}.
- {干脆|gān cuì} is gān cuì, not gàn cuì.
- {不已|bù yǐ} after a verb, in writing: ~~{不已|bù yǐ}{感动|gǎn dòng}~~ → {感动|gǎn dòng}{不已|bù yǐ}.

## Key points

- {这|zhè}{也|yě}{不|bù} X，{那|nà}{也|yě}{不|bù} Y: nothing will do; {放|fàng}{着|zhe} X {不|bù} Y: passing over the obvious choice (often {非|fēi}{要|yào} after).
- {明明|míng míng}: obviously (against what follows); {倒是|dào shi}: actually / it's true that / come on; {那|nà}{倒|dào}{也|yě}{是|shì}.
- {干脆|gān cuì}: just, simply; straightforward. {就算|jiù suàn}…{也|yě}: even if. {也好|yě hǎo}: whether…or…; fine too.
- {算了|suàn le} (forget it), {得了|dé le} (enough; {得了|dé le}{吧|ba}, come off it); {啦|la} = {了|le} + {啊|a}; {嘛|ma} (after all; softening).
- {露|lòu} lòu in {露面|lòu miàn}, {露一手|lòu yì shǒu}, {露脸|lòu liǎn}; lù in {暴露|bào lù}, {露出|lù chū}.
- Quarrels: {冲突|chōng tū}, {对立|duì lì}, {对抗|duì kàng}, {争吵|zhēng chǎo} / {吵架|chǎo jià}, {打架|dǎ jià}, {争论|zhēng lùn}, {争议|zhēng yì}, {指责|zhǐ zé}, {嘲笑|cháo xiào}; making up: {倾听|qīng tīng}, {当面|dāng miàn}, {认错|rèn cuò}, {实话|shí huà},
  {教训|jiào xun}, {误解|wù jiě}, {多亏|duō kuī}.
- New characters: {嘲|cháo} {妨|fáng} {愤|fèn} {怒|nù} {恨|hèn} {狠|hěn} {讶|yà} {勉|miǎn} {啦|la} {嘛|ma} {欺|qī} {倾|qīng} {恰|qià} {谓|wèi} {嫌|xián} {惑|huò}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Character and values
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Who do we admire, and why? Wang Fang writes a profile of a retired bus driver who has spent twelve
years helping patients find their way round a hospital, and friends argue about whether pop idols
make good role models. The words are for qualities (honest, modest, tenacious), for praise and
honours, for giving and helping, and for the inner life: beliefs, desires, weaknesses.

The grammar:

- {凡是|fán shì}…{都|dōu}: every, without exception ({凡是|fán shì}{去|qù}{过|guo}{的|de}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{说|shuō}{好|hǎo});
- {待|dài} dài: to treat people ({待|dài}{人|rén}{热情|rè qíng}), not HSK 4's {待|dāi} dāi (to stay);
- {自我|zì wǒ}: self, the self, before verbs ({自我|zì wǒ}{介绍|jiè shào}, {自我|zì wǒ}{管理|guǎn lǐ}) and as a noun ({找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{自我|zì wǒ}).

You'll also answer an opinion question aloud, the last task of the speaking test, and write an
argued essay.

## {凡是|fán shì}…{都|dōu}: every, without exception

{凡是|fán shì} opens a noun phrase that sets out a whole class of things or people; {都|dōu} in the main clause says
it holds for every one of them:

{凡是|fán shì}{去|qù}{过|guo}{那里|nà lǐ}{的|de}{人|rén}，{都|dōu}{说|shuō}{那里|nà lǐ}{很|hěn}{美|měi}。 — Everyone who has been there says it's beautiful.

{凡是|fán shì}{跟|gēn}{孩子|hái zi}{有关|yǒu guān}{的|de}{事|shì}，{她|tā}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{在意|zài yì}。 — She cares about anything to do with children.

{凡是|fán shì}{报|bào}{了|le}{名|míng}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}，{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}{参加|cān jiā}。 — Any student who has signed up can take part.

- {凡是|fán shì} goes at the very start, before the phrase it covers: {凡是|fán shì}…{的|de}{人|rén} / {的|de}{事|shì} / {的|de}{东西|dōng xi}. The subject of the
  main clause is often left out or comes back as a pronoun.
- {都|dōu} can't be left out.
- It's a little more emphatic and formal than {所有|suǒ yǒu}…{都|dōu} or {只要|zhǐ yào}{是|shì}…{都|dōu}: notices, rules and opinions use
  it ({凡是|fán shì}{迟到|chí dào}{的|de}，{一律|yí lǜ}{不|bù}{能|néng}{进场|jìn chǎng}: lesson 27's {一律|yí lǜ}, "without exception").
- In writing, {凡|fán} alone does the same job: {凡|fán}{年|nián}{满|mǎn}{十八|shí bā}{岁|suì}{的|de}{公民|gōng mín} (every citizen aged eighteen or over).

## {待|dài}: to treat people

{待|dài} dài, fourth tone, is "to treat, to behave towards (people)":

{她|tā}{待|dài}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{热情|rè qíng}。 — She's very warm with people.

{老板|lǎo bǎn}{待|dài}{我们|wǒ men}{像|xiàng}{家人|jiā rén}{一样|yí yàng}。 — The boss treats us like family.

- It mostly comes with {人|rén} or a person and a manner: {待|dài}{人|rén}{真诚|zhēn chéng}, {待客|dài kè} (to treat guests). {对待|duì dài} (HSK 5)
  is the everyday two-syllable verb ({怎么|zěn me}{对待|duì dài}{批评|pī píng}), and {对|duì} + person + {很|hěn}{好|hǎo} is what you'd say in a
  chat: {他|tā}{对|duì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}.
- {待人接物|dài rén jiē wù} (how one treats people and handles things) is a fixed phrase: {他|tā}{待人接物|dài rén jiē wù}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{礼貌|lǐ mào}.
- The same character is dāi in HSK 4's {待|dāi} (to stay: {在|zài}{家|jiā}{待|dāi}{着|zhe}) and dài in {等待|děng dài} (to wait), {接待|jiē dài} and
  lesson 13's {招待|zhāo dài}.

## {自我|zì wǒ}: the self

{自我|zì wǒ} means "self". Before a two-syllable verb, it makes "self-…" or "…oneself":

| Phrase | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {自我|zì wǒ}{介绍|jiè shào} | to introduce oneself; a self-introduction |
| {自我|zì wǒ}{管理|guǎn lǐ} | self-management |
| {自我|zì wǒ}{批评|pī píng} | self-criticism |
| {自我|zì wǒ}{保护|bǎo hù} | to protect oneself |
| {自我|zì wǒ}{感觉|gǎn jué}{良好|liáng hǎo} | to think well of oneself (often ironic: smug) |

As a noun it's "the self", one's own identity: {找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{自我|zì wǒ} (to find oneself), {失去|shī qù}{自我|zì wǒ} (to lose oneself),
{超越|chāo yuè}{自我|zì wǒ} (to go beyond one's limits). {自我|zì wǒ} is written and abstract; in conversation {自己|zì jǐ} does most of
this work ({介绍|jiè shào}{一下|yí xià}{自己|zì jǐ}).

## Values and honours

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {诚信|chéng xìn} | integrity, honesty (in dealings) | {做|zuò}{生意|shēng yi}{要|yào}{讲|jiǎng}{诚信|chéng xìn}。 In business you have to be honest. |
| {道德|dào dé} | morality, ethics | {这|zhè}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{道德|dào dé}{问题|wèn tí}。 This is a moral question. |
| {荣誉|róng yù} | honour | {这个|zhè ge}{奖|jiǎng}{是|shì}{全|quán}{队|duì}{的|de}{荣誉|róng yù}。 This prize is an honour for the whole team. |
| {称号|chēng hào} | (honorary) title | {她|tā}{获得|huò dé}{了|le}"{优秀|yōu xiù}{志愿者|zhì yuàn zhě}"{的|de}{称号|chēng hào}。 She was given the title "Outstanding Volunteer". |
| {评选|píng xuǎn} | to choose (by votes or judging) | {每|měi}{年|nián}{评选|píng xuǎn}{一|yí}{次|cì} chosen once a year |
| {公认|gōng rèn} | generally recognised | {他|tā}{是|shì}{大家|dà jiā}{公认|gōng rèn}{的|de}{好|hǎo}{老师|lǎo shī}。 Everyone agrees he's a good teacher. |
| {认可|rèn kě} | to approve, recognise; recognition | {她|tā}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}{得到|dé dào}{了|le}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{认可|rèn kě}。 Her work has won everyone's recognition. |
| {榜样|bǎng yàng} | role model, example | {哥哥|gē ge}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{榜样|bǎng yàng}。 My brother is my role model. |
| {偶像|ǒu xiàng} | idol | {年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{的|de}{偶像|ǒu xiàng} young people's idol |
| {崇拜|chóng bài} | to worship, idolise | {他|tā}{从小|cóng xiǎo}{就|jiù}{崇拜|chóng bài}{科学|kē xué}{家|jiā}。 He's idolised scientists since he was small. |
| {树立|shù lì} | to set up, establish (an example, an image) | {树立|shù lì}{榜样|bǎng yàng} to set an example |
| {确立|què lì} | to establish (a goal, a system) | {确立|què lì}{目标|mù biāo} to set a goal |
| {立|lì} | to stand; to set up | {立|lì}{规矩|guī ju} to lay down rules; {门口|mén kǒu}{立|lì}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{块|kuài}{牌子|pái zi}。 A sign stands at the door. |

- {诚信|chéng xìn} is honesty you can rely on, above all in business and promises ({诚实|chéng shí} + {信用|xìn yòng}); {老实|lǎo shi} (below) is
  being honest and straightforward as a person.

### Stroke traps

- **{德|dé}**: 彳, then {十|shí}, then 罒 (lying flat), then a horizontal, then {心|xīn}. The short horizontal above {心|xīn}
  is easy to forget: 15 strokes.
- **{奉|fèng}**: the three horizontals, then the long left-falling and right-falling strokes, then two more
  horizontals and the vertical last, through the middle.
- **{予|yǔ}**: the turn at the top (horizontal, then down to the left), the dot, then the horizontal with
  its turn and the vertical hook last.
- **{贯|guàn}**: the box-like top (a turn, another turn, the short vertical, the long horizontal), then {贝|bèi}.
- **{夸|kuā}**: {大|dà}, then two horizontals (the short one first), then the last stroke turning down with a hook.
- **{杰|jié}** is {木|mù} over 灬: write {木|mù} (four strokes), then the four dots.
- **{佩|pèi}**: 亻, then {几|jǐ}'s left-falling stroke and its turn, then the short horizontal and {巾|jīn} inside.

1. A retired bus driver who has volunteered at a hospital's information desk every weekday morning
   for twelve years, and what makes her a role model.
2. Years before, her mother, who couldn't walk well or read, was lost and in tears in the hospital
   hall; Guan thought every older person coming for the first time must feel the same.

**Guan Xiumei: an ordinary person's twelve years.** "At half past seven in the morning, the hall
of the city's No. 1 Hospital is already packed. Next to the information desk, a grey-haired woman
is bending over, patiently teaching an old man to register on a self-service machine. She wears a
plain blue waistcoat with one word on the back: 'Volunteer'.

Her name is Guan Xiumei. She's sixty-eight, and before she retired she drove a bus. From the year
she retired, she has been here on time every weekday morning: twelve full years now.

Asked why she volunteers, Auntie Guan thought for a moment and told a story. More than ten years
ago she brought her mother to see a doctor. Her mother couldn't walk well and couldn't read; she
couldn't find the right department in the hall and was so upset she cried. 'I thought then: every
older person who comes to a hospital for the first time must get this anxious.' After retiring she
didn't go travelling or stay home to look after a grandchild: she came here.

It wasn't easy at first. The hospital has more than twenty departments across several buildings,
upstairs and down, and it took her a whole month to memorise where each one was. Later, when the
hospital brought in self-service machines that many old people couldn't use, she learned them
first herself and then taught people one by one. Sometimes anxious patients are rude to her, but
she never gets cross. 'They're here because they're ill and they feel awful,' she says. 'We should
treat people gently.'

Her daughter told me that at first the family weren't keen: they worried it would be too much for
her. 'But she's so tenacious: she goes in wind and rain,' her daughter said with a smile. 'Now the
whole family is proud of her.'

In twelve years she has lost count of the patients she's helped. Last year she was named one of
the city's 'Outstanding Volunteers' and given prize money, all of which she gave to the hospital's
charitable fund for patients in difficulty. When the honours come up, she looks a little
embarrassed: 'I'm just an ordinary person, and what I do is small stuff.'

But to many people she has long been a role model. Xiao Liu, a nurse at the information desk, says
that since Auntie Guan came the hall has been much more orderly, and young volunteers have joined
one after another. 'She never lectures anyone, but everything she does spurs us on.'

As the interview was ending, I asked her how long she plans to keep going. She laughed: 'As long as
I can still walk, I'll keep doing it. Helping others is really helping your future self. Who won't
be old one day?'

We often think of role models as far away: outstanding scientists, first-class athletes, stars that
everyone idolises. But Auntie Guan made me see that a role model can be right beside us. She has no
astonishing genius and no lofty slogans; all she has is a firm conviction and twelve years of
perseverance without a break. Ordinariness like hers is precisely the least ordinary thing of all."

answer). Answer this one aloud: {在|zài}{你|nǐ}{心目|xīn mù}{中|zhōng}，{什么|shén me}{样|yàng}{的|de}{人|rén}{可以|kě yǐ}{算是|suàn shì}{榜样|bǎng yàng}？{为什么|wèi shén me}？ Plan your view, two
reasons with an example, and a closing sentence.

<details>
<summary>A model answer</summary>

> {在|zài}{我|wǒ}{心目|xīn mù}{中|zhōng}，{榜样|bǎng yàng}{不|bù}{一定|yí dìng}{是|shì}{杰出|jié chū}{的|de}{名人|míng rén}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{那些|nà xiē}{在|zài}{平凡|píng fán}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}{中|zhōng}，{一贯|yí guàn}{认真|rèn zhēn}、{待|dài}{人|rén}{真诚|zhēn chéng}{的|de}{人|rén}。
>
> {我|wǒ}{这样|zhè yàng}{想|xiǎng}，{主要|zhǔ yào}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{原因|yuán yīn}。{第|dì}{一|yī}，{名人|míng rén}{离|lí}{我们|wǒ men}{太|tài}{远|yuǎn}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{往往|wǎng wǎng}{只|zhǐ}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{他们|tā men}{成功|chéng gōng}{的|de}{一|yí}{面|miàn}，{却|què}{看|kàn}{不|bu}{到|dào}{他们|tā men}{付出|fù chū}{了|le}{多少|duō shao}。{身边|shēn biān}{的|de}{人|rén}{就|jiù}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}，{我们|wǒ men}{能|néng}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{他们|tā men}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{是|shì}{怎么|zěn me}{做|zuò}{的|de}，{更|gèng}{容易|róng yì}{向|xiàng}{他们|tā men}{学习|xué xí}。{比如|bǐ rú}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{中学|zhōng xué}{老师|lǎo shī}，{她|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{第|dì}{一|yī}{个|gè}{到|dào}{学校|xué xiào}，{对|duì}{每|měi}{个|gè}{学生|xué sheng}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{耐心|nài xīn}，{这|zhè}{一|yì}{点|diǎn}{我|wǒ}{一直|yì zhí}{很|hěn}{佩服|pèi fú}。{第|dì}{二|èr}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{有|yǒu}{没有|méi yǒu}{能力|néng lì}{当然|dāng rán}{重要|zhòng yào}，{可是|kě shì}{人品|rén pǐn}{更|gèng}{重要|zhòng yào}。{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{就算|jiù suàn}{再|zài}{有|yǒu}{才华|cái huá}，{如果|rú guǒ}{不|bù}{讲|jiǎng}{诚信|chéng xìn}，{也|yě}{不|bù}{值得|zhí de}{我们|wǒ men}{学习|xué xí}。
>
> {所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}，{榜样|bǎng yàng}{不|bú}{在于|zài yú}{多|duō}{有名|yǒu míng}，{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}{他|tā}{的|de}{做法|zuò fǎ}{能|néng}{不|bu}{能|néng}{让|ràng}{我们|wǒ men}{变成|biàn chéng}{更|gèng}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{人|rén}。

(About 210 characters, two minutes spoken.) "To my mind, a role model doesn't have to be an
outstanding celebrity: it's the people who, in ordinary life, are always conscientious and sincere
with others. I think so for two main reasons. First, celebrities are too far from us: we usually see
only their success, not how much they put in. People around us are different: we can see what they
do every day, so it's easier to learn from them. My secondary-school teacher, for example, was the
first to arrive at school every day and patient with every pupil; I've always admired that. Second,
ability matters, of course, but character matters more. However talented someone is, if they can't
be trusted, they aren't worth learning from. So I think what makes a role model isn't how famous
they are, but whether what they do makes us better people."

{才华|cái huá} (talent) is lesson 01's; {不|bú}{在于|zài yú}…{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}… "it isn't a matter of… but of…" ({于|yú}: lesson 27).
</details>

## Write it: an argued essay

Write 300–400 characters on {名人|míng rén}{应|yīng}{不|bu}{应该|yīng gāi}{成为|chéng wéi}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{的|de}{榜样|bǎng yàng}？ (Should celebrities be role models for young
people?) Take a side, give two reasons with examples, admit what the other side gets right, and
conclude.

<details>
<summary>A model essay and a checklist</summary>

> {名人|míng rén}{不|bú}{是|shì}{天生|tiān shēng}{的|de}{榜样|bǎng yàng}
>
> {现在|xiàn zài}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{偶像|ǒu xiàng}，{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{认为|rèn wéi}，{名人|míng rén}{有|yǒu}{那么|nà me}{大|dà}{的|de}{影响力|yǐng xiǎng lì}，{就|jiù}{应该|yīng gāi}{成为|chéng wéi}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{的|de}{榜样|bǎng yàng}。{我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}，{名人|míng rén}{可以|kě yǐ}{是|shì}{榜样|bǎng yàng}，{但|dàn}{不|bù}{应该|yīng gāi}{自动|zì dòng}{成为|chéng wéi}{榜样|bǎng yàng}。
>
> {首先|shǒu xiān}，{出名|chū míng}{和|hé}{人品|rén pǐn}{是|shì}{两回事|liǎng huí shì}。{一|yí}{个|gè}{歌手|gē shǒu}{唱|chàng}{得|de}{好|hǎo}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{演员|yǎn yuán}{演|yǎn}{得|de}{好|hǎo}，{只能|zhǐ néng}{说明|shuō míng}{他们|tā men}{在|zài}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{行业|háng yè}{里|lǐ}{很|hěn}{优秀|yōu xiù}，{并|bìng}{不|bù}{能|néng}{说明|shuō míng}{他们|tā men}{在|zài}{生活|shēng huó}{中|zhōng}{也|yě}{值得|zhí de}{学习|xué xí}。{有的|yǒu de}{明星|míng xīng}{外表|wài biǎo}{光鲜|guāng xiān}，{私下|sī xià}{却|què}{不|bù}{讲|jiǎng}{诚信|chéng xìn}，{如果|rú guǒ}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{把|bǎ}{他们|tā men}{的|de}{一切|yí qiè}{都|dōu}{当成|dàng chéng}{榜样|bǎng yàng}，{就|jiù}{很|hěn}{容易|róng yì}{受到|shòu dào}{坏|huài}{的|de}{影响|yǐng xiǎng}。
>
> {其次|qí cì}，{凡是|fán shì}{真正|zhēn zhèng}{的|de}{榜样|bǎng yàng}，{都|dōu}{需要|xū yào}{经得起|jīng de qǐ}{时间|shí jiān}{的|de}{考验|kǎo yàn}。{明星|míng xīng}{的|de}{热度|rè dù}{来|lái}{得|de}{快|kuài}，{去|qù}{得|de}{也|yě}{快|kuài}，{今天|jīn tiān}{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{夸|kuā}{他|tā}，{明天|míng tiān}{可能|kě néng}{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{人|rén}{记得|jì de}{了|le}。{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{能|néng}{不|bu}{能|néng}{成为|chéng wéi}{榜样|bǎng yàng}，{应该|yīng gāi}{看|kàn}{他|tā}{长期|cháng qī}{的|de}{做法|zuò fǎ}，{而|ér}{不|bú}{是|shì}{一时|yì shí}{的|de}{名气|míng qi}。
>
> {当然|dāng rán}，{我|wǒ}{并|bìng}{不|bù}{反对|fǎn duì}{追星|zhuī xīng}。{有的|yǒu de}{名人|míng rén}{勤劳|qín láo}、{自律|zì lǜ}，{热心|rè xīn}{公益|gōng yì}，{确实|què shí}{能|néng}{激励|jī lì}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}。{关键|guān jiàn}{是|shì}，{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{要|yào}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{眼光|yǎn guāng}，{学习|xué xí}{他们|tā men}{的|de}{优点|yōu diǎn}，{而|ér}{不|bú}{是|shì}{崇拜|chóng bài}{他们|tā men}{的|de}{一切|yí qiè}。
>
> {总之|zǒng zhī}，{名人|míng rén}{能|néng}{不|bu}{能|néng}{成为|chéng wéi}{榜样|bǎng yàng}，{不|bú}{在于|zài yú}{有|yǒu}{多|duō}{出名|chū míng}，{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}{他|tā}{的|de}{所作所为|suǒ zuò suǒ wéi}。

(About 360 characters.) "Celebrities aren't born role models. Many young people today have their
own idols, and some argue that with so much influence, celebrities ought to be young people's role
models. I think celebrities can be role models, but shouldn't automatically become them. First,
fame and character are two different things. A singer who sings well, an actor who acts well: that
only shows they excel in their own field, not that their lives are worth copying. Some stars look
glamorous but aren't honest in private; if young people take everything about them as a model,
it's easy to be badly influenced. Second, every true role model has to stand the test of time. A
star's popularity comes fast and goes fast: today everyone is praising them, tomorrow no one may
remember them. Whether someone can be a role model should depend on how they act over the long run,
not on a moment's fame. Of course, I'm not against being a fan. Some celebrities are hard-working,
self-disciplined and generous to good causes, and they really can inspire young people. The key is
for young people to have their own judgment: to learn from their strengths, not idolise everything
about them. In short, whether a celebrity can be a role model depends not on how famous they are,
but on what they do."

{天生|tiān shēng} is "innate, born", {影响力|yǐng xiǎng lì} influence, {行业|háng yè} a trade or field (HSK 5), {光鲜|guāng xiān} glamorous, {私下|sī xià} in
private, {经得起|jīng de qǐ} to stand up to, {考验|kǎo yàn} a test (lesson 05), {热度|rè dù} popularity (lesson 10), {名气|míng qi} fame
(lesson 10), {追星|zhuī xīng} to be a fan of a star, {一时|yì shí} (for a moment) lesson 25's word, {所作所为|suǒ zuò suǒ wéi} what one does (a set phrase).

Checklist:
- **[[Thesis]]** ({我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}…) with a qualification ({可以|kě yǐ}{是|shì}…{但|dàn}{不|bù}{应该|yīng gāi}…).
- **Two reasons** ({首先|shǒu xiān}…{其次|qí cì}…), each explained; the lesson's {凡是|fán shì}…{都|dōu} in one of them.
- **A concession** ({当然|dāng rán}，{我|wǒ}{并|bìng}{不|bù}{反对|fǎn duì}…), then {关键|guān jiàn}{是|shì}… to come back to your view.
- **[[Conclusion]]** with {总之|zǒng zhī} and a balanced pair ({不|bú}{在于|zài yú}…{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}…).
- **[[Register]]**: written but not stiff: {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}, {并|bìng}{不|bù}, {确实|què shí}; no {啦|la}, {嘛|ma}.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Values
{凡是|fán shì}{认识|rèn shi}{她|tā}{的|de}{人|rén}，{都|dōu}{说|shuō}{她|tā}{待|dài}{人|rén}{热情|rè qíng}。
= Everyone who knows her says she's warm with people.
{他|tā}{是|shì}{大家|dà jiā}{公认|gōng rèn}{的|de}{好|hǎo}{榜样|bǎng yàng}。
= He's a role model everyone agrees on.
{我|wǒ}{非常|fēi cháng}{佩服|pèi fú}{他|tā}{的|de}{勇气|yǒng qì}。
= I really admire his courage.
{她|tā}{把|bǎ}{奖金|jiǎng jīn}{全部|quán bù}{捐|juān}{给|gěi}{了|le}{公益|gōng yì}{基金|jī jīn}。
= She gave all her prize money to a charity fund.
{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{心目|xīn mù}{中|zhōng}，{诚信|chéng xìn}{比|bǐ}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{重要|zhòng yào}。
= To my mind, integrity matters more than anything.
{我|wǒ}{为|wèi}{你|nǐ}{感到|gǎn dào}{自豪|zì háo}。
= I'm proud of you.
```

## Pronunciation

- {待|dài} dài (to treat) and {待|dāi} dāi (to stay): {待|dài}{人|rén} dài rén, but {在|zài}{家|jiā}{待|dāi}{着|zhe} dāi zhe.
- {给予|jǐ yǔ} jǐ yǔ: written {给|gěi} is jǐ, as in {供给|gōng jǐ} (lesson 18). Two third tones: said jí yǔ.
- {一流|yī liú} yī liú: {一|yī} keeps the first tone. {一贯|yí guàn} yí guàn changes as usual before the fourth tone.
- {踏实|tā shi} tā shi: first tone and light, though {踏|tà} alone is tà.
- {崇拜|chóng bài} chóng bài: ch, not sh; {崇|chóng} is chóng, like {虫|chóng} (insect).
- {朴素|pǔ sù} pǔ sù, {夸奖|kuā jiǎng} kuā jiǎng, {谦虚|qiān xū} qiān xū: {谦|qiān} has q + ian.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{凡是|fán shì}{去|qù}{过|guo}{的|de}{人|rén}{说|shuō}{好|hǎo}~~: {凡是|fán shì} needs {都|dōu}: {凡是|fán shì}{去|qù}{过|guo}{的|de}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{说|shuō}{好|hǎo}.
- ~~{我们|wǒ men}{凡是|fán shì}…~~: {凡是|fán shì} starts the phrase it covers: {凡是|fán shì}{我们|wǒ men}{认识|rèn shi}{的|de}{人|rén}{都|dōu}…
- ~~{他|tā}{待|dài}{我|wǒ}~~ ending there: {待|dài} needs a manner: {他|tā}{待|dài}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} / {他|tā}{待|dài}{我|wǒ}{像|xiàng}{亲人|qīn rén}{一样|yí yàng}.
- ~~{给予|jǐ yǔ} gěi yǔ~~: it's jǐ yǔ.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{自豪|zì háo}{你|nǐ}~~: {自豪|zì háo} takes {为|wèi} + the cause: {我|wǒ}{为|wèi}{你|nǐ}{感到|gǎn dào}{自豪|zì háo} / {我|wǒ}{为|wèi}{你|nǐ}{自豪|zì háo}.
- ~~{很|hěn}{一流|yī liú}~~: {一流|yī liú} is already "first-class": {一流|yī liú}{的|de}{大学|dà xué}, {他|tā}{的|de}{水平|shuǐ píng}{是|shì}{一流|yī liú}{的|de}.
- {佩服|pèi fú} is admiration, {崇拜|chóng bài} worship: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{崇拜|chóng bài}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{耐心|nài xīn} sounds overblown; {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{佩服|pèi fú}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{耐心|nài xīn}.

## Key points

- {凡是|fán shì}…{都|dōu}: every one without exception (written, emphatic); {都|dōu} is required.
- {待|dài} dài + person + manner: to treat ({待|dài}{人|rén}{热情|rè qíng}); {对待|duì dài}, {待人接物|dài rén jiē wù}; dāi is "to stay".
- {自我|zì wǒ} before verbs ({自我|zì wǒ}{介绍|jiè shào}, {自我|zì wǒ}{管理|guǎn lǐ}) and as a noun ({找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{自我|zì wǒ}).
- Values and honours: {诚信|chéng xìn}, {道德|dào dé}, {荣誉|róng yù}, {称号|chēng hào}, {榜样|bǎng yàng}, {偶像|ǒu xiàng}, {崇拜|chóng bài}, {公认|gōng rèn}, {认可|rèn kě}, {树立|shù lì}, {确立|què lì}; giving: {奉献|fèng xiàn}, {公益|gōng yì},
  {捐款|juān kuǎn} / {捐赠|juān zèng}, {回报|huí bào}, {感激|gǎn jī}, {给予|jǐ yǔ} (jǐ), {赋予|fù yǔ}; inspiring: {鼓舞|gǔ wǔ}, {激励|jī lì}, {激发|jī fā}, {启发|qǐ fā}, {启示|qǐ shì}.
- Character: {杰出|jié chū}, {高尚|gāo shàng}, {平凡|píng fán}, {朴素|pǔ sù}, {谦虚|qiān xū}, {勤劳|qín láo}, {老实|lǎo shi}, {踏实|tā shi}, {顽强|wán qiáng}, {坚定|jiān dìng}, {坚决|jiān jué}, {勇于|yǒng yú}, {乐于|lè yú}, {自律|zì lǜ}, {专注|zhuān zhù}, {一流|yī liú}
  (yī), {一贯|yí guàn}, {默默|mò mò}.
- New characters: {榜|bǎng} {崇|chóng} {德|dé} {奉|fèng} {凡|fán} {赋|fù} {予|yǔ} {夸|kuā} {杰|jié} {佩|pèi} {誉|yù} {朴|pǔ} {谦|qiān} {踏|tā} {顽|wán} {贯|guàn} {豪|háo}; new radicals {={几|jǐ}=}, {言|yán}, 豕.

lessons.title: Memories, journeys and time
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

After the engagement, Wang Fang takes Li Ming to meet her {外公|wài gōng} and {外婆|wài pó} in the village where she
spent her childhood summers. The trip becomes a personal essay about going back: what has changed,
what hasn't, and what time does to places and people. You'll learn the many Chinese words for time
(the moment, the past, afterwards, the years), for journeys, and for remembering and longing.

The grammar:

- **{到|dào}…{为止|wéi zhǐ}**: up to, until ({到|dào}{目前|mù qián}{为止|wéi zhǐ}, so far);
- X {了|le}{就|jiù} X {了|le}: what's done is done ({丢|diū}{了|le}{就|jiù}{丢|diū}{了|le});
- {不禁|bù jīn}: can't help (doing), in writing;
- {不时|bù shí}: from time to time;
- {不曾|bù céng} and {从未|cóng wèi}: never, in writing;
- {好不|hǎo bù} + adjective: how very… ({好不|hǎo bú}{热闹|rè nao}), which isn't negative;
- {落|là} là: to leave something behind ({把|bǎ}{伞|sǎn}{落|là}{在|zài}{车|chē}{上|shàng}{了|le}).

The lesson ends the module with its handwriting review, a passage to retell and a thank-you letter.

## {到|dào}…{为止|wéi zhǐ}: up to, until

{到|dào} + a time, a place or an amount + {为止|wéi zhǐ} marks where something stops:

{到|dào}{今天|jīn tiān}{为止|wéi zhǐ}，{报名|bào míng}{的|de}{已经|yǐ jīng}{有|yǒu}{三百|sān bǎi}{人|rén}{了|le}。 — As of today, three hundred people have signed up.

{到|dào}{目前|mù qián}{为止|wéi zhǐ}，{一切|yí qiè}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{顺利|shùn lì}。 — So far everything has gone smoothly.

{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{课|kè}{就|jiù}{上|shàng}{到|dào}{这儿|zhèr}{为止|wéi zhǐ}。 — That's where we'll stop today's class.

- {为止|wéi zhǐ} is wéi zhǐ: {为|wéi} wéi, "to be, to act as", as in {成为|chéng wéi}.
- The point can be a time ({到|dào}{上|shàng}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{为止|wéi zhǐ}), a place in a text or a task ({到|dào}{第|dì}{五|wǔ}{课|kè}{为止|wéi zhǐ}), or a limit
  ({吃|chī}{到|dào}{饱|bǎo}{为止|wéi zhǐ}, eat until you're full).
- {到|dào}{目前|mù qián}{为止|wéi zhǐ} (so far, up to now) is the commonest form, in speech and writing. {截至|jié zhì} (lesson 27) is
  its formal partner in reports.

This is the pattern **{到|dào}…{为止|wéi zhǐ}**.

## X {了|le}{就|jiù} X {了|le}: what's done is done

The same verb (or adjective) before and after {了|le}{就|jiù}, then a reassurance:

{丢|diū}{了|le}{就|jiù}{丢|diū}{了|le}，{再|zài}{买|mǎi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{吧|ba}。 — If it's lost, it's lost: just buy another.

{过去|guò qù}{了|le}{就|jiù}{过去|guò qù}{了|le}，{别|bié}{再|zài}{想|xiǎng}{了|le}。 — It's in the past: stop thinking about it.

{错过|cuò guò}{了|le}{就|jiù}{错过|cuò guò}{了|le}，{下|xià}{次|cì}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{机会|jī huì}。 — We missed it, so what: there'll be another chance.

It accepts something that can't be changed, often to comfort someone, and is followed by {没关系|méi guān xi},
{没|méi}{什么|shén me}, {别|bié}…, or what to do instead. In a calmer register: {既然|jì rán}{已经|yǐ jīng}…，{就|jiù}…

## {不禁|bù jīn} and {不时|bù shí}

- {不禁|bù jīn} bù jīn: "can't help (doing)", for a feeling that comes by itself. It's written and goes
  before the verb: {看|kàn}{到|dào}{老|lǎo}{照片|zhào piàn}，{我|wǒ}{不禁|bù jīn}{笑|xiào}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}。 (Looking at the old photos, I couldn't help laughing.)
  In speech, {忍不住|rěn bu zhù} (can't help it) does the same and can also take a negative ({忍不住|rěn bu zhù}{不|bú}{看|kàn}).
- {不时|bù shí} bù shí: "from time to time, every so often", written: {他|tā}{一边|yì biān}{听|tīng}，{一边|yì biān}{不时|bù shí}{地|de}{点|diǎn}{点头|diǎn tóu}。 (He
  listened, nodding every so often.) In speech, {时不时|shí bù shí} or {不时|bù shí} both work.

{禁|jīn} here is jīn, first tone ("to bear"), not the jìn of {禁止|jìn zhǐ} (to forbid).

## {不曾|bù céng} and {从未|cóng wèi}: never

Both are the written negatives of {曾经|céng jīng} (once, HSK 5), "have never…":

| Written | Spoken |
|---|---|
| {我|wǒ}{从未|cóng wèi}{去|qù}{过|guo}{那里|nà lǐ}。 | {我|wǒ}{从来|cóng lái}{没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}{那里|nà lǐ}。 |
| {他|tā}{不曾|bù céng}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}{大|dà}{海|hǎi}。 | {他|tā}{没|méi}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}{大|dà}{海|hǎi}。 |

- {从未|cóng wèi} = {从来|cóng lái} + {未|wèi} (lesson 27's written {没|méi}); {不曾|bù céng} = {不|bù} + {曾|céng}. Both usually keep {过|guo} after the verb.
- They suit essays, stories and formal speech: {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{事情|shì qing}，{我|wǒ}{以前|yǐ qián}{从未|cóng wèi}{遇到|yù dào}{过|guo}.

## {好不|hǎo bù} + adjective: how very…

In front of a two-syllable adjective, {好不|hǎo bù} means "how very…", in a lively, slightly literary way:

{街|jiē}{上|shàng}{好不|hǎo bú}{热闹|rè nao}！ — How lively the streets were!

{那|nà}{天|tiān}{她|tā}{好不|hǎo bù}{得意|dé yì}。 — How pleased with herself she was that day.

It looks like a negative, but it isn't: {好不|hǎo bú}{热闹|rè nao} is the same as {好|hǎo}{热闹|rè nao}, "really lively". The one
famous trap is {好不|hǎo bù}{容易|róng yì}, which means the same as {好容易|hǎo róng yì} (lesson 05): "with great difficulty":
{我|wǒ}{好不|hǎo bù}{容易|róng yì}{才|cái}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{他|tā} and {我|wǒ}{好容易|hǎo róng yì}{才|cái}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{他|tā} both say "it took me ages to find him".

## {落|là} là: to leave behind

{落|là} là (fourth tone) is a spoken verb: to leave something behind by mistake, to forget to bring it:

{糟糕|zāo gāo}，{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{伞|sǎn}{落|là}{在|zài}{车|chē}{上|shàng}{了|le}！ — Oh no, I've left my umbrella on the train!

{你|nǐ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{落|là}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{了|le}。 — You left your phone at my place.

Also "to fall behind": {他|tā}{病|bìng}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}，{落|là}{下|xià}{了|le}{不|bù}{少|shǎo}{课|kè}。 {落|luò} luò (HSK 4) is "to fall" ({叶子|yè zi}{落|luò}{了|le}), and in
this lesson's {角落|jiǎo luò} (a corner), jiǎo luò, it's luò too.
