1. Going back to her grandparents' village: childhood memories, what has changed in the village and
   in her grandfather, and what she has realised about home.
2. A new road has halved the walk, guesthouses have been built by the fields and city people come at
   weekends, but most young people have left, so it's quieter. The river is as clear as ever ({依旧|yī jiù}
   {那么|nà me}{清|qīng}).
3. That time passes for everyone, but some things can't be carried off by the years ({有些|yǒu xiē}{东西|dōng xi}，{是|shì}{岁月|suì yuè}
   {带|dài}{不|bu}{走|zǒu}{的|de}); she seems to see herself as a child.
4. As a child she longed for faraway places ({最|zuì}{向往|xiàng wǎng}{的|de}{是|shì}{远方|yuǎn fāng}) and later only thought of leaving
   ({当初|dāng chū}{我|wǒ}{只|zhǐ}{想|xiǎng}{着|zhe}{离开|lí kāi});
   now she misses it, feels grateful, and sees that what she treasures most has always been there.

**Going back.** "At this moment I'm sitting in my grandparents' courtyard, writing this. The
moonlight falls on the old persimmon tree and casts a faint shadow on the ground. Inside, Grandma is
still chatting with Li Ming, and every so often there's a burst of laughter.

As a child I spent every summer holiday here. How long those summers were! At dawn Grandpa would
wake me to go fishing by the river, and I could hardly get my eyes open; at noon Grandma cut
watermelon for us in a corner of the courtyard; late at night it was pitch dark all around, and I
was too scared to go to the toilet on my own, so Grandpa waited at the door with a torch. Lying in
bed, I'd gaze at the stars through the window and imagine faraway places. What I longed for most then
was the distance: the sea, high mountains, and the far-off countries in books.

Later I went to secondary school, my summers filled up with extra classes and summer camps, and I
came back less and less. At first I didn't think it a pity at all: life in the city was so full.
But at some point, I couldn't say when, I missed the summers here more and more.
Late at night in Beijing I'd find myself thinking of the river, of Grandpa holding my hand, and the
two trails of footprints we left on the bank, one big, one small.

This time I brought Li Ming so that my grandparents could meet him. The way from the county town to
the village used to take over an hour on foot; now there's a new road and it takes half an hour. The
village has changed a lot too: where there used to be only crops by the fields, a few guesthouses have gone up,
and city people often come for weekend trips; but most young people have gone to work elsewhere, and
the village is much quieter than it used to be. Only the river, twenty years on, is as clear as
ever.

The one who has changed most is Grandpa. Two years ago he could still walk to the end of the village on
his own; now he has to rest after a little while. At dinner, looking at his head of silver
hair, I was lost for words for a moment. Grandma says Grandpa had a very hard life when he was
young: he was the eldest of four brothers, and it was he who held the whole family together. These
decades of storms and hardship he has never told me about, and I never thought to ask.

After dinner Grandpa brought out an old notebook: the diary he kept when he was young, the writing
already a little faded. He turned the pages one by one for Li Ming, telling him how the village had
changed over the decades. Sitting beside them, I felt I was getting to know Grandpa properly for the
first time.

In the afternoon Li Ming went fishing by the river with Grandpa. I watched them from a distance: one
supporting the other, walking slowly, talking and laughing. In that instant I seemed to see myself
twenty years ago. So time does fly: we're all quietly growing up and growing old; but some things
the years can't take away.

Looking back on this short trip, I don't feel much sadness; mostly I feel grateful. Back then I
only thought of leaving: I believed a better life was only to be found far away. Now I understand
that what I treasure most has been here all along. Tomorrow morning we'll turn round and leave, but
I've already told Grandma: from now on we'll come back every summer."
</details>

## Say it: retell a passage

Listen, read the passage twice, then close it and retell it in your own words in about a minute and
a half (the test's retelling task, as reported). Keep the order of events and the people's
feelings.

```speak
# The diary on the train
{去年|qù nián}{冬天|dōng tiān}，{七十|qī shí}{岁|suì}{的|de}{张|Zhāng}{爷爷|yé ye}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{女儿|nǚ ér}。
= Last winter, seventy-year-old Grandpa Zhang took the train to visit his daughter.
{下|xià}{车|chē}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{他|tā}{才|cái}{发现|fā xiàn}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{旧|jiù}{包|bāo}{落|là}{在|zài}{了|le}{车|chē}{上|shàng}。
= Only after getting off did he realise he'd left his old bag on the train.
{包|bāo}{里|lǐ}{没有|méi yǒu}{钱|qián}，{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{一|yì}{本|běn}{用|yòng}{了|le}{五十|wǔ shí}{年|nián}{的|de}{日记|rì jì}，{记|jì}{着|zhe}{他|tā}{和|hé}{老伴儿|lǎo bànr}{的|de}{一辈子|yí bèi zi}。
= There was no money in it, just a diary he'd kept for fifty years, recording his whole life with his wife.
{张|Zhāng}{爷爷|yé ye}{急|jí}{得|de}{一|yì}{晚上|wǎn shang}{没|méi}{睡着|shuì zháo}，{女儿|nǚ ér}{安慰|ān wèi}{他|tā}{说|shuō}："{丢|diū}{了|le}{就|jiù}{丢|diū}{了|le}，{别|bié}{太|tài}{难过|nán guò}{了|le}。"
= Grandpa Zhang was so upset he didn't sleep all night. His daughter comforted him: "If it's lost, it's lost. Try not to be too sad."
{可是|kě shì}{张|Zhāng}{爷爷|yé ye}{心里|xīn li}{明白|míng bai}，{那|nà}{本|běn}{日记|rì jì}{是|shì}{再|zài}{也|yě}{找|zhǎo}{不|bu}{回来|huí lái}{的|de}。
= But Grandpa Zhang knew in his heart that the diary could never be replaced.
{没想到|méi xiǎng dào}，{三|sān}{天|tiān}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{敲门|qiāo mén}。
= Then, to everyone's surprise, three days later there was a knock at the door.
{原来|yuán lái}{是|shì}{火车|huǒ chē}{上|shàng}{的|de}{一|yí}{位|wèi}{列车员|liè chē yuán}，{她|tā}{在|zài}{座位|zuò wèi}{下面|xià miàn}{发现|fā xiàn}{了|le}{这个|zhè ge}{包|bāo}，{按照|àn zhào}{日记|rì jì}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{地址|dì zhǐ}{一路|yí lù}{找|zhǎo}{了|le}{过来|guò lái}。
= It was a train attendant. She'd found the bag under a seat and followed the address in the diary all the way there.
{她|tā}{说|shuō}，{看|kàn}{了|le}{日记|rì jì}{的|de}{第|dì}{一|yī}{页|yè}，{就|jiù}{知道|zhī dào}{这个|zhè ge}{包|bāo}{对|duì}{主人|zhǔ rén}{一定|yí dìng}{非常|fēi cháng}{重要|zhòng yào}。
= She said that one look at the diary's first page told her the bag must matter a great deal to its owner.
{张|Zhāng}{爷爷|yé ye}{要|yào}{给|gěi}{她|tā}{钱|qián}，{她|tā}{怎么|zěn me}{也|yě}{不|bù}{肯|kěn}{收|shōu}。
= Grandpa Zhang wanted to give her money, but she wouldn't take it.
{张|Zhāng}{爷爷|yé ye}{接|jiē}{过|guò}{包|bāo}，{翻|fān}{开|kāi}{日记|rì jì}，{看|kàn}{到|dào}{老伴儿|lǎo bànr}{年轻|nián qīng}{时|shí}{的|de}{照片|zhào piàn}，{不禁|bù jīn}{流|liú}{下|xià}{了|le}{眼泪|yǎn lèi}。
= Grandpa Zhang took the bag, opened the diary, saw the photo of his wife when she was young, and couldn't hold back his tears.
{到|dào}{今天|jīn tiān}{为止|wéi zhǐ}，{他|tā}{还|hái}{常常|cháng cháng}{跟|gēn}{别人|bié ren}{讲|jiǎng}{起|qǐ}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}。
= To this day he still often tells people about it.
```

{老伴儿|lǎo bànr} is one's husband or wife (of an old couple), {安慰|ān wèi} to comfort (HSK 5), {列车员|liè chē yuán} a train attendant,
{敲门|qiāo mén} to knock, {按照|àn zhào} according to (HSK 4).

<details>
<summary>A model retelling</summary>

> {去年|qù nián}{冬天|dōng tiān}，{张|Zhāng}{爷爷|yé ye}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{去|qù}{女儿|nǚ ér}{家|jiā}。{下|xià}{车|chē}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{他|tā}{把|bǎ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{旧|jiù}{包|bāo}{落|là}{在|zài}{了|le}{火车|huǒ chē}{上|shàng}。{包|bāo}{里|lǐ}{没有|méi yǒu}{什么|shén me}{值钱|zhí qián}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}，{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{一|yì}{本|běn}{写|xiě}{了|le}{五十|wǔ shí}{年|nián}{的|de}{日记|rì jì}，{里面|lǐ miàn}{记|jì}{着|zhe}{他|tā}{和|hé}{老伴儿|lǎo bànr}{的|de}{故事|gù shi}。{张|Zhāng}{爷爷|yé ye}{非常|fēi cháng}{着急|zháo jí}，{一|yí}{夜|yè}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{睡|shuì}{好|hǎo}。{女儿|nǚ ér}{劝|quàn}{他|tā}{别|bié}{太|tài}{难过|nán guò}，{可是|kě shì}{他|tā}{知道|zhī dào}，{那|nà}{本|běn}{日记|rì jì}{对|duì}{他|tā}{来|lái}{说|shuō}{比|bǐ}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{重要|zhòng yào}。{没想到|méi xiǎng dào}，{三|sān}{天|tiān}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{一|yí}{位|wèi}{列车员|liè chē yuán}{按照|àn zhào}{日记|rì jì}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{地址|dì zhǐ}，{把|bǎ}{包|bāo}{送|sòng}{了|le}{回来|huí lái}。{张|Zhāng}{爷爷|yé ye}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{老伴儿|lǎo bànr}{的|de}{照片|zhào piàn}，{忍不住|rěn bu zhù}{哭|kū}{了|le}。{直到|zhí dào}{现在|xiàn zài}，{他|tā}{还|hái}{常常|cháng cháng}{跟|gēn}{人|rén}{说|shuō}{起|qǐ}{这|zhè}{位|wèi}{好|hǎo}{心|xīn}{的|de}{列车员|liè chē yuán}。

(About 180 characters.) Retell in the third person; you can change words ({不禁|bù jīn}{流|liú}{下|xià}{了|le}{眼泪|yǎn lèi} → {忍不住|rěn bu zhù}{哭|kū}{了|le},
{到|dào}{今天|jīn tiān}{为止|wéi zhǐ} → {直到|zhí dào}{现在|xiàn zài}) as long as the story stays the same. {值钱|zhí qián} is "valuable".
</details>

## Write it: a thank-you letter

A thank-you letter is one of the exam's practical texts. Write 150–200 characters to the owner of
a guesthouse ({民宿|mín sù}) you stayed in: say when you stayed, what you enjoyed, one thing the owner did
for you, and a wish or a plan to come back.

<details>
<summary>A model letter</summary>

> {洪阿姨|Hóng ā yí}：
>
> {您|nín}{好|hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{上|shàng}{周末|zhōu mò}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{您|nín}{家|jiā}{民宿|mín sù}{的|de}{小季|Xiǎo Jì}。{回|huí}{到|dào}{北京|Běi jīng}{已经|yǐ jīng}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{天|tiān}{了|le}，{可是|kě shì}{我|wǒ}{还|hái}{常常|cháng cháng}{想|xiǎng}{起|qǐ}{在|zài}{村|cūn}{里|lǐ}{度过|dù guò}{的|de}{那|nà}{两|liǎng}{天|tiān}。
>
> {您|nín}{的|de}{民宿|mín sù}{虽然|suī rán}{不|bú}{大|dà}，{但是|dàn shì}{干净|gān jìng}、{安静|ān jìng}，{院子|yuàn zi}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{花|huā}{开|kāi}{得|de}{特别|tè bié}{好|hǎo}。{最|zuì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{感动|gǎn dòng}{的|de}{是|shì}{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}，{我们|wǒ men}{要|yào}{去|qù}{车站|chē zhàn}，{我|wǒ}{的|de}{男朋友|nán péng you}{把|bǎ}{手机|shǒu jī}{落|là}{在|zài}{了|le}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}，{是|shì}{您|nín}{骑|qí}{着|zhe}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{追|zhuī}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{里|lǐ}{路|lù}{给|gěi}{我们|wǒ men}{送|sòng}{来|lái}{的|de}。{要不是|yào bu shì}{您|nín}，{我们|wǒ men}{那|nà}{天|tiān}{就|jiù}{麻烦|má fan}{了|le}。
>
> {这|zhè}{次|cì}{出游|chū yóu}{让|ràng}{我们|wǒ men}{非常|fēi cháng}{难忘|nán wàng}。{明年|míng nián}{夏天|xià tiān}，{我们|wǒ men}{还|hái}{想|xiǎng}{带|dài}{家人|jiā rén}{一起|yì qǐ}{来|lái}{住|zhù}{几|jǐ}{天|tiān}。
>
> {祝|zhù}{您|nín}{生意兴隆|shēng yì xīng lóng}，{身体|shēn tǐ}{健康|jiàn kāng}！
>
> {小季|Xiǎo Jì}
>
> 6{月|yuè}18{日|rì}

(About 180 characters.) "Dear Auntie Hong, How are you? I'm Xiao Ji, who stayed at your
guesthouse last weekend. I've been back in Beijing for several days, but I still often think of the
two days we spent in the village. Your guesthouse isn't big, but it's clean and quiet, and the
flowers in the courtyard are lovely. What touched me most was the second morning: we were leaving
for the station, my boyfriend had left his phone in the room, and you rode your bike a kilometre
after us to bring it. Without you we'd have been in real trouble that day. We'll never forget this
trip. Next summer we'd like to bring our families to stay for a few days. Wishing you a thriving
business and good health! Xiao Ji, 18 June"

{度过|dù guò} is "to spend (time)", {={里|lǐ}=} a Chinese mile, half a kilometre, {要不是|yào bu shì} "if it hadn't been
for", {生意兴隆|shēng yì xīng lóng} "may business prosper", a set wish for a shopkeeper.

Checklist:
- **Opening**: who you are and when you stayed.
- **The thanks**: one concrete thing the person did, and its effect ({要不是|yào bu shì}{您|nín}…).
- **Closing**: a plan or wish, then {祝|zhù}{您|nín}…!, your name and the date.
- **[[Register]]**: {您|nín} throughout; warm, not chatty.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Time and memory
{到|dào}{目前|mù qián}{为止|wéi zhǐ}，{一切|yí qiè}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{顺利|shùn lì}。
= So far everything has gone smoothly.
{丢|diū}{了|le}{就|jiù}{丢|diū}{了|le}，{别|bié}{太|tài}{难过|nán guò}{了|le}。
= If it's lost, it's lost: don't be too upset.
{看|kàn}{到|dào}{老|lǎo}{照片|zhào piàn}，{我|wǒ}{不禁|bù jīn}{笑|xiào}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}。
= Looking at the old photos, I couldn't help laughing.
{我|wǒ}{从未|cóng wèi}{去|qù}{过|guo}{那么|nà me}{遥远|yáo yuǎn}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}。
= I've never been anywhere so far away.
{糟糕|zāo gāo}，{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{手机|shǒu jī}{落|là}{在|zài}{出租车|chū zū chē}{上|shàng}{了|le}！
= Oh no, I've left my phone in the taxi!
{那|nà}{时候|shí hou}{的|de}{夏天|xià tiān}{好不|hǎo bú}{漫长|màn cháng}。
= How long those summers were.
```

## Pronunciation

- {落|là} là (to leave behind) and {落|luò} luò (to fall): {把|bǎ}{伞|sǎn}{落|là}{在|zài}{车|chē}{上|shàng} là; {叶子|yè zi}{落|luò}{了|le} luò; {角落|jiǎo luò} jiǎo luò.
- {不禁|bù jīn} bù jīn: {禁|jīn} is first tone here, so {不|bù} stays bù. {禁止|jìn zhǐ} jìn zhǐ is "to forbid".
- {为止|wéi zhǐ} wéi zhǐ: second tone on {为|wéi}.
- {同行|tóng xíng} tóng xíng (to travel together) vs tóng háng (people in the same trade).
- {钟头|zhōng tóu} zhōng tóu and {工夫|gōng fu} gōng fu: {工夫|gōng fu} ends light, {钟头|zhōng tóu} doesn't.
- {一时|yì shí} yì shí (yì before the second tone); {片刻|piàn kè} piàn kè; {瞬间|shùn jiān} shùn jiān: sh, not s.
- {好不|hǎo bú}{热闹|rè nao} hǎo bú rè nao, {好不|hǎo bú}{漫长|màn cháng} hǎo bú màn cháng: the {不|bù} of {好不|hǎo bù} changes before a fourth tone like
  any {不|bù}; {好不|hǎo bù}{容易|róng yì} hǎo bù róng yì keeps bù.

## Common mistakes

- {到|dào}{今天|jīn tiān}{为止|wéi zhǐ} is right, but ~~{到|dào}{为止|wéi zhǐ}{今天|jīn tiān}~~ isn't: the time goes between {到|dào} and {为止|wéi zhǐ}.
- {好不|hǎo bú}{热闹|rè nao} isn't "not lively": it's "really lively". Only {好不|hǎo bù}{容易|róng yì} is a special case (= {好容易|hǎo róng yì}).
- ~~{我|wǒ}{不禁|bù jīn}{不|bú}{笑|xiào}~~: {不禁|bù jīn} takes a positive verb; for "couldn't help not…", use {忍不住|rěn bu zhù}.
- {从未|cóng wèi} with an experience usually keeps {过|guo}: {我|wǒ}{从未|cóng wèi}{去|qù}{过|guo}, rather than a bare {我|wǒ}{从未|cóng wèi}{去|qù}.
- {落|là} là (spoken) and {忘|wàng} (HSK 2) both work for things you leave behind: {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{书|shū}{落|là}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{了|le} /
  {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{书|shū}{忘|wàng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{了|le}; only {忘|wàng} is for forgetting to do something: {我|wǒ}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{带|dài}{书|shū}.
- {怀念|huái niàn} is for the past: ~~{我|wǒ}{怀念|huái niàn}{明天|míng tiān}{的|de}{旅行|lǚ xíng}~~ → {我|wǒ}{期待|qī dài} (HSK 5) {明天|míng tiān}{的|de}{旅行|lǚ xíng}.

## Key points

- {到|dào}…{为止|wéi zhǐ}: up to, until ({到|dào}{目前|mù qián}{为止|wéi zhǐ}, so far).
- X {了|le}{就|jiù} X {了|le}: what's done is done ({丢|diū}{了|le}{就|jiù}{丢|diū}{了|le}).
- {不禁|bù jīn} + verb: can't help (written); {不时|bù shí}: from time to time; {不曾|bù céng} / {从未|cóng wèi} + verb + {过|guo}: never (written).
- {好不|hǎo bù} + adjective: how very (not negative); {好不|hǎo bù}{容易|róng yì} = {好容易|hǎo róng yì}.
- {落|là} là: to leave behind ({把|bǎ}…{落|là}{在|zài}…); luò: to fall.
- Time: {此刻|cǐ kè}, {瞬间|shùn jiān}, {片刻|piàn kè}, {一时|yì shí}, {钟头|zhōng tóu}, {工夫|gōng fu}, {当初|dāng chū}, {起初|qǐ chū}, {原先|yuán xiān} / {原本|yuán běn}, {先前|xiān qián}, {以往|yǐ wǎng}, {过后|guò hòu} / {事后|shì hòu}, {日后|rì hòu} / {往后|wǎng hòu}, {时光|shí guāng},
  {岁月|suì yuè}; journeys: {旅程|lǚ chéng}, {旅途|lǚ tú}, {路程|lù chéng}, {出游|chū yóu}, {同行|tóng xíng}, {民宿|mín sù}, {郊外|jiāo wài}; memory: {怀念|huái niàn}, {思念|sī niàn}, {向往|xiàng wǎng}, {幻想|huàn xiǎng}, {联想|lián xiǎng}, {回顾|huí gù}, {依旧|yī jiù} /
  {仍旧|réng jiù}.
- New characters: {钓|diào} {瞬|shùn} {遥|yáo} {睁|zhēng}; handwriting review of twenty earlier characters.

lessons.title: Li Qingzhao
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 25 was about memory, time and the things that stay the same: {依旧|yī jiù}. One of the most loved
poems in Chinese ends with that word. It's by {李清照|Lǐ Qīng zhào} (Li Qingzhao), the greatest woman poet of the
Song dynasty, and it's a {词|cí} (*cí*), a kind of poem written to a set tune. In this lesson you'll read
her life in Chinese, learn what a {词|cí} is, and read two short {词|cí} to the same tune, 《{如梦令|Rú mèng lìng}》, in full,
with notes, a modern paraphrase and our own translation.

## Her life

Dates for people of this period aren't always certain. Li Qingzhao was born in 1084 in what is now
Shandong; she died in the south, around 1155 or a little later: no record of her death survives
(sources: NOTES-m5.md). Read about her life in Chinese. {宋代|Sòng dài} is the Song dynasty (960–1279), {北宋|Běi Sòng} and
{南宋|Nán Sòng} its northern and southern halves, {词人|cí rén} a writer of {词|cí}, {金石|jīn shí} inscriptions on bronze and stone.

> **{李清照|Lǐ Qīng zhào}**
>
> {李清照|Lǐ Qīng zhào}{是|shì}{宋代|Sòng dài}{最|zuì}{有名|yǒu míng}{的|de}{女|nǚ}{词人|cí rén}。{她|tā}1084{年|nián}{出生|chū shēng}{在|zài}{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{山东|Shān dōng}，{从小|cóng xiǎo}{就|jiù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{读书|dú shū}{写作|xiě zuò}。
>

{流传|liú chuán} (to circulate, be handed down) is HSK 5's; {持续|chí xù} (to last) HSK 5's; {后序|hòu xù} an afterword; {浅白|qiǎn bái} plain, simple (of language); {都城|dū chéng} a capital; {占领|zhàn lǐng} to
occupy; {上任|shàng rèn} to take up a post; {保住|bǎo zhù} to keep safe; {具体|jù tǐ} (exact, specific) HSK 5's; {失传|shī chuán} lost (of works no
longer handed down); {则|zé} (lesson 26: "while, on the other hand", written); {国破家亡|guó pò jiā wáng} "the country
broken, the family gone"; {深沉|shēn chén} depth, gravity.

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

"Li Qingzhao is the most famous woman poet of the Song dynasty. She was born in 1084 in what is now
Shandong and loved reading and writing from childhood.

In 1101 Li Qingzhao married Zhao Mingcheng. Both loved books and both loved
collecting. They often spent their money on old books, calligraphy and painting, and inscriptions
on bronze and stone; whenever they bought something good, they studied and catalogued it together,
as happy as children. Later Zhao Mingcheng arranged the inscriptions they had collected into a
book. That was probably the happiest time of Li Qingzhao's life.

But the good days didn't last long. In 1127 Kaifeng, the Northern Song capital, was taken by the
army of the Jin state from the north, and the war soon reached Shandong. Their house was burned and
much of their collection couldn't be saved. The couple had to leave home and live in the south. In
1129, on his way to take up a post, Zhao Mingcheng fell seriously ill and died soon after.

From then on Li Qingzhao lived alone in the south for many years, and life was very hard. She
died around 1155; the exact date can no longer be known. She wrote a
great deal, but most of it has been lost; what has come down to us today is only part of it.

After Zhao Mingcheng's death, Li Qingzhao wrote an afterword for the book of inscriptions he had
compiled. In it she remembers the days when the two of them bought books, read and catalogued their
collection together, and writes of everything lost in the war. It is still moving to read today.

Her {词|cí} use plain language, with hardly a difficult character, yet they are full of feeling. People
often say that her early {词|cí} are light and lively, mostly about a girl's joys and love, while
her later {词|cí} are full of sorrow: a country broken, a family gone, the loneliness of being alone.
Because of this her {词|cí} have both a girl's innocence and the depth of someone who has weathered
storms. For more than nine hundred years she has been, in the eyes of Chinese readers, one of the most
outstanding women poets."
</details>

## What a {词|cí} is

A {词|cí} is a poem written to the pattern of a tune. The tunes themselves are mostly lost, but each one
left its pattern, and its name, the **{词牌|cí pái}** (*cípái*): how many lines, how many characters in each,
where the rhymes fall and which tones go where. Poets "filled in" the pattern with their own words
(the verb is {填词|tián cí}, to fill in a {词|cí}). So the name at the top of a {词|cí} is the tune, not the subject: many
poets wrote poems called 《{如梦令|Rú mèng lìng}》, about quite different things. The real subject is often given
after the tune's name, or taken from the first line, as with the two below.

《{如梦令|Rú mèng lìng}》 (*Rú mèng lìng*, "As if in a dream") is one of the shortest patterns: 33 characters in
seven lines of 6, 6, 5, 6, 2, 2 and 6 characters. The fifth and sixth lines are the same two
characters said twice, a pause before the last line. Compare the {诗|shī} of HSK 4's Du Fu, with lines of
equal length: a {词|cí}'s lines are uneven, closer to song.

## 《{如梦令|Rú mèng lìng}》: {常记|cháng jì}{溪亭|xī tíng}{日暮|rì mù}

Usually read as a memory of her youth: a summer outing on the water.

> {常记|cháng jì}{溪亭|xī tíng}{日暮|rì mù}，
> {沉醉|chén zuì}{不|bù}{知|zhī}{归路|guī lù}。
> {兴尽|xìng jìn}{晚回舟|wǎn huí zhōu}，
> {误入|wù rù}{藕花|ǒu huā}{深处|shēn chù}。
> {争渡|zhēng dù}，{争渡|zhēng dù}，
> {惊起|jīng qǐ}{一滩|yì tān}{鸥鹭|ōu lù}。

| Words | Notes |
|---|---|
| {常记|cháng jì} | often remember ({记|jì} = {记得|jì de}) |
| {溪亭|xī tíng} | a pavilion by a stream |
| {日暮|rì mù} | sunset, dusk ({暮|mù}: evening) |
| {沉醉|chén zuì} | (deeply) drunk; lost in pleasure |
| {不|bù}{知|zhī}{归路|guī lù} | couldn't find the way home ({归|guī}: to return) |
| {兴尽|xìng jìn} | enjoyment exhausted, having had one's fill ({兴|xìng} is xìng here, as in {兴趣|xìng qù}) |
| {晚回舟|wǎn huí zhōu} | turned the boat back late ({舟|zhōu}: boat) |
| {误入|wù rù} | strayed into by mistake |
| {藕花|ǒu huā} | lotus flowers ({藕|ǒu}: lotus root) |
| {深处|shēn chù} | the depths, deep in among |
| {争渡|zhēng dù} | rowing hard, struggling to get through ({渡|dù}: to cross water) |
| {惊起|jīng qǐ} | startled into flight |
| {一滩|yì tān} | a whole shoal, a sandbank's worth |
| {鸥鹭|ōu lù} | gulls and egrets, waterbirds |

**In modern Chinese**: {我|wǒ}{常常|cháng cháng}{想|xiǎng}{起|qǐ}{那|nà}{一|yí}{次|cì}：{在|zài}{溪边|xī biān}{的|de}{亭子|tíng zi}{里|lǐ}{玩|wán}{到|dào}{太阳|tài yang}{下|xià}{山|shān}，{喝|hē}{得|de}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{醉|zuì}{了|le}，{连|lián}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{的|de}{路|lù}{都|dōu}{找|zhǎo}{不|bu}{到|dào}{了|le}。{玩|wán}{够|gòu}{了|le}，{天|tiān}{也|yě}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{才|cái}{划|huá}{着|zhe}{船|chuán}{往|wǎng}{回|huí}{走|zǒu}，{没想到|méi xiǎng dào}{却|què}{划|huá}{进|jìn}{了|le}{荷花|hé huā}{的|de}{深处|shēn chù}。{怎么|zěn me}{划|huá}{出去|chū qù}{呀|ya}？{怎么|zěn me}{划|huá}{出去|chū qù}{呀|ya}？{船|chuán}{一|yí}{动|dòng}，{一滩|yì tān}{的|de}{水鸟|shuǐ niǎo}{都|dōu}{被|bèi}{惊|jīng}{得|de}{飞|fēi}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}。

**Our translation**:

> I often remember the pavilion by the stream at dusk,
> so drunk with pleasure we couldn't find the way home.
> Our fun all spent, we turned the boat back late
> and strayed deep in among the lotus flowers.
> Row hard, row hard!
> We startled a whole sandbank of gulls and egrets into the air.

{亭子|tíng zi} is a pavilion, {荷花|hé huā} the everyday word for lotus flowers, {划|huá} huá to row (HSK 5).

## 《{如梦令|Rú mèng lìng}》: {昨|zuó}{夜|yè}{雨疏风骤|yǔ shū fēng zhòu}

The same tune, another morning: a night of wind and rain, and the flowers outside.

> {昨|zuó}{夜|yè}{雨疏风骤|yǔ shū fēng zhòu}，
> {浓睡|nóng shuì}{不消残酒|bù xiāo cán jiǔ}。
> {试问|shì wèn}{卷帘人|juǎn lián rén}，
> {却道|què dào}{海棠|hǎi táng}{依旧|yī jiù}。
> {知否|zhī fǒu}，{知否|zhī fǒu}？
> {应是|yīng shì}{绿肥红瘦|lǜ féi hóng shòu}。

| Words | Notes |
|---|---|
| {雨疏风骤|yǔ shū fēng zhòu} | the rain light, the wind sudden and strong ({疏|shū}: sparse; {骤|zhòu}: sudden) |
| {浓睡|nóng shuì} | a deep sleep |
| {不消残酒|bù xiāo cán jiǔ} | didn't sleep off the last of the wine ({消|xiāo}: to get rid of; {残|cán}: leftover) |
| {试问|shì wèn} | to ask, try asking |
| {卷帘人|juǎn lián rén} | the one rolling up the blind, usually taken to be a maid ({卷帘|juǎn lián} juǎn lián: rolling up a blind, with lesson 12's juǎn, "to roll"; {帘|lián}: a blind) |
| {却道|què dào} | but (she) says |
| {海棠|hǎi táng} | crab-apple blossom |
| {依旧|yī jiù} | just as before (lesson 25) |
| {知否|zhī fǒu} | do you know? ({否|fǒu}: or not, written) |
| {应是|yīng shì} | it must be ({应|yīng}: should, surely) |
| {绿肥红瘦|lǜ féi hóng shòu} | the green plump, the red thin: the leaves full, the flowers fewer |

**In modern Chinese**: {昨天|zuó tiān}{夜|yè}{里|lǐ}{雨|yǔ}{不|bú}{大|dà}，{风|fēng}{却|què}{很|hěn}{急|jí}。{我|wǒ}{睡|shuì}{得|de}{很|hěn}{沉|chén}，{醒|xǐng}{来|lái}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{酒|jiǔ}{还|hái}{没有|méi yǒu}{完全|wán quán}{醒|xǐng}。{我|wǒ}{问|wèn}{正在|zhèng zài}{卷|juǎn}{窗帘|chuāng lián}{的|de}{人|rén}，{外面|wài miàn}{的|de}{海棠|hǎi táng}{花|huā}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}{了|le}，{那|nà}{人|rén}{却|què}{说|shuō}，{海棠|hǎi táng}{花|huā}{跟|gēn}{昨天|zuó tiān}{一样|yí yàng}。{你|nǐ}{知道|zhī dào}{吗|ma}？{你|nǐ}{知道|zhī dào}{吗|ma}？{经过|jīng guò}{一|yí}{夜|yè}{的|de}{风雨|fēng yǔ}，{现在|xiàn zài}{应该|yīng gāi}{是|shì}{绿|lǜ}{叶|yè}{多|duō}{了|le}，{红|hóng}{花|huā}{少|shǎo}{了|le}。

**Our translation**:

> Last night the rain was light, the wind sudden and wild;
> deep sleep didn't clear the last of the wine.
> I asked the one rolling up the blind,
> and was told the crab-apple was just as before.
> Don't you know, don't you know?
> It must be green grown plump and red grown thin.

{窗帘|chuāng lián} is a curtain or blind; {酒醒|jiǔ xǐng} is to sober up. The one rolling up the blind is usually taken to be
a maid. Her careless {依旧|yī jiù} and the
poet's {知否|zhī fǒu}，{知否|zhī fǒu} set two ways of seeing side by side: one glances and sees nothing changed; the other
knows a night's storm has stripped the flowers. The last four characters are famous for saying a
whole scene in colours: {绿|lǜ} for the leaves, {红|hóng} for the blossom, {肥|féi} and {瘦|shòu} (fat and thin, words for
bodies) for how much of each is left.

## Read it aloud

```speak
# 《{如梦令|Rú mèng lìng}》
{常记|cháng jì}{溪亭|xī tíng}{日暮|rì mù}，{沉醉|chén zuì}{不|bù}{知|zhī}{归路|guī lù}。
= I often remember the pavilion by the stream at dusk, so drunk with pleasure we couldn't find the way home.
{兴尽|xìng jìn}{晚回舟|wǎn huí zhōu}，{误入|wù rù}{藕花|ǒu huā}{深处|shēn chù}。
= Our fun all spent, we turned the boat back late and strayed deep in among the lotus flowers.
{争渡|zhēng dù}，{争渡|zhēng dù}，{惊起|jīng qǐ}{一滩|yì tān}{鸥鹭|ōu lù}。
= Row hard, row hard! We startled a whole sandbank of gulls and egrets into the air.
{昨|zuó}{夜|yè}{雨疏风骤|yǔ shū fēng zhòu}，{浓睡|nóng shuì}{不消残酒|bù xiāo cán jiǔ}。
= Last night the rain was light, the wind sudden and wild; deep sleep didn't clear the last of the wine.
{试问|shì wèn}{卷帘人|juǎn lián rén}，{却道|què dào}{海棠|hǎi táng}{依旧|yī jiù}。
= I asked the one rolling up the blind, and was told the crab-apple was just as before.
{知否|zhī fǒu}，{知否|zhī fǒu}？{应是|yīng shì}{绿肥红瘦|lǜ féi hóng shòu}。
= Don't you know, don't you know? It must be green grown plump and red grown thin.
```

## Key points

- {李清照|Lǐ Qīng zhào} (1084–about 1155): the great woman poet of the Song; married {赵明诚|Zhào Míng chéng} (1101), collected books
  and inscriptions with him; after 1127 lived in the south; he died in 1129.
- A {词|cí} is written to a tune's pattern, the {词牌|cí pái}: the name tells the form, not the subject.
- 《{如梦令|Rú mèng lìng}》: 33 characters, lines of 6 6 5 6 2 2 6, the two-character line said twice.
- {常记|cháng jì}{溪亭|xī tíng}{日暮|rì mù}: a happy memory of youth on the water; {昨|zuó}{夜|yè}{雨疏风骤|yǔ shū fēng zhòu}: a storm, a maid's {依旧|yī jiù} and the poet's
  {绿肥红瘦|lǜ féi hóng shòu}.
- Readings to remember: {兴尽|xìng jìn} xìng jìn, {卷帘|juǎn lián} juǎn lián, {知否|zhī fǒu} zhī fǒu, {应是|yīng shì} yīng shì.

lessons.title: The Ballad of Mulan
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 25 was about journeys and coming home after many years. The most famous homecoming in
Chinese poetry is a girl's: {木兰|Mù lán} (Mulan), who rides to war in her old father's place, fights for
years without anyone knowing she's a woman, and comes home to her family. Her story is told in
《{木兰诗|Mù lán shī}》 (*Mùlán shī*, the Ballad of Mulan, also called 《{木兰辞|Mù lán cí}》), a folk ballad that many Chinese pupils
learn at school. In this lesson you'll read the story in our own Chinese, then its opening and
closing lines in the original, with notes and our translation, and see how later retellings
changed it.

## Where the ballad comes from

The ballad is old and its author unknown. It was probably first written down around the sixth
century; the usual view today is that it began as a folk song of the {北朝|Běi cháo} (the Northern Dynasties,
the states that ruled north China from the late fourth to the late sixth century), and its setting is often
placed in the {北魏|Běi Wèi} (Northern Wei, 386–534). The text we read comes from 《{乐府诗集|Yuè fǔ Shī jí}》, a large
collection of songs and ballads compiled by {郭茂倩|Guō Mào qiàn} (Guo Maoqian); another anthology, 《{文苑英华|Wén yuàn Yīng huá}》, treats it
as a Tang poem. Sources: NOTES-m5.md.

The ballad is in lines of five characters, with some longer ones, rhyming and easy to sing: a {乐府|yuè fǔ}
(*yuèfǔ*), a song in the folk style, not one of the strict poems of HSK 4's Du Fu.

## The story

Read the story in modern Chinese. {可汗|kè hán} kè hán is the khan, the ruler; {军帖|jūn tiě} a call-up list; {战马|zhàn mǎ} a
war horse; {黄河|Huáng Hé} the Yellow River; {尚书郎|shàng shū láng} a high official post; {女扮男装|nǚ bàn nán zhuāng} (a woman dressed as a man).

> **{木兰|Mù lán}{的|de}{故事|gù shi}**
>
> {很|hěn}{久|jiǔ}{以前|yǐ qián}，{北方|běi fāng}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{姑娘|gū niang}，{名|míng}{叫|jiào}{木兰|Mù lán}。{一|yì}{天|tiān}，{她|tā}{坐|zuò}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}{织布|zhī bù}，{可是|kě shì}{织|zhī}{着|zhe}{织|zhī}{着|zhe}，{就|jiù}{停|tíng}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}，{一|yì}{声|shēng}{接|jiē}{一|yì}{声|shēng}{地|de}{叹气|tàn qì}。{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{人|rén}{问|wèn}{她|tā}{在|zài}{想|xiǎng}{什么|shén me}，{她|tā}{说|shuō}：{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{了|le}{军帖|jūn tiě}，{可汗|kè hán}{要|yào}{大量|dà liàng}{招兵|zhāo bīng}，{每|měi}{一|yí}{卷|juàn}{名单|míng dān}{上|shàng}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{父亲|fù qīn}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}。{父亲|fù qīn}{年纪|nián jì}{大|dà}{了|le}，{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{又|yòu}{没有|méi yǒu}{哥哥|gē ge}{可以|kě yǐ}{替|tì}{他|tā}{去|qù}。
>
> {木兰|Mù lán}{想|xiǎng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{久|jiǔ}，{终于|zhōng yú}{下|xià}{了|le}{决心|jué xīn}：{替|tì}{父亲|fù qīn}{去|qù}{打仗|dǎ zhàng}。{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}，{她|tā}{跑|pǎo}{遍|biàn}{了|le}{集市|jí shì}：{在|zài}{东|dōng}{边|biān}{的|de}{集市|jí shì}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一|yì}{匹|pǐ}{好|hǎo}{马|mǎ}，{在|zài}{西|xī}{边|biān}{的|de}{集市|jí shì}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{马鞍|mǎ ān}，{又|yòu}{买|mǎi}{齐|qí}{了|le}{其他|qí tā}{用品|yòng pǐn}。{一大早|yí dà zǎo}，{她|tā}{告别|gào bié}{了|le}{父母|fù mǔ}，{女扮男装|nǚ bàn nán zhuāng}，{跟|gēn}{着|zhe}{军队|jūn duì}{出发|chū fā}{了|le}。{晚上|wǎn shang}，{她|tā}{在|zài}{黄河|Huáng Hé}{边|biān}{过|guò}{夜|yè}，{听|tīng}{不|bu}{到|dào}{父母|fù mǔ}{叫|jiào}{她|tā}{的|de}{声音|shēng yīn}，{只|zhǐ}{听|tīng}{到|dào}{黄河|Huáng Hé}{的|de}{水|shuǐ}{哗哗|huā huā}{地|de}{流|liú}。{再|zài}{往|wǎng}{北|běi}{走|zǒu}，{她|tā}{到|dào}{了|le}{更|gèng}{远|yuǎn}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}，{耳|ěr}{边|biān}{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{战马|zhàn mǎ}{的|de}{叫|jiào}{声|shēng}。
>
> {北方|běi fāng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{非常|fēi cháng}{冷|lěng}，{夜|yè}{里|lǐ}{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{寒风|hán fēng}{和|hé}{战马|zhàn mǎ}{的|de}{叫|jiào}{声|shēng}。{战争|zhàn zhēng}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{年|nián}。{很|hěn}{多|duō}{将军|jiāng jūn}{和|hé}{士兵|shì bīng}{死|sǐ}{在|zài}{了|le}{战场|zhàn chǎng}{上|shàng}，{木兰|Mù lán}{却|què}{活|huó}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}，{十|shí}{年|nián}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{跟|gēn}{着|zhe}{军队|jūn duì}{回|huí}{到|dào}{了|le}{都城|dū chéng}。{皇帝|huáng dì}{见|jiàn}{到|dào}{她|tā}，{夸|kuā}{她|tā}{立|lì}{了|le}{大|dà}{功|gōng}，{要|yào}{给|gěi}{她|tā}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}{的|de}{官位|guān wèi}，{还|hái}{给|gěi}{了|le}{她|tā}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{奖赏|jiǎng shǎng}。{可是|kě shì}{木兰|Mù lán}{说|shuō}，{她|tā}{什么|shén me}{官|guān}{都|dōu}{不要|bú yào}，{只|zhǐ}{想|xiǎng}{要|yào}{一|yì}{匹|pǐ}{跑|pǎo}{得|de}{快|kuài}{的|de}{马|mǎ}，{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{回|huí}{到|dào}{家乡|jiā xiāng}。
>
> {听说|tīng shuō}{木兰|Mù lán}{回来|huí lái}{了|le}，{全|quán}{家人|jiā rén}{都|dōu}{高兴|gāo xìng}{极|jí}{了|le}：{年|nián}{老|lǎo}{的|de}{父母|fù mǔ}{互相|hù xiāng}{扶|fú}{着|zhe}，{到|dào}{城|chéng}{外|wài}{去|qù}{接|jiē}{她|tā}；{姐姐|jiě jie}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{打扮|dǎ ban}{好|hǎo}{了|le}，{等|děng}{着|zhe}{见|jiàn}{她|tā}；{弟弟|dì di}{磨刀|mó dāo}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{杀|shā}{猪|zhū}{杀|shā}{羊|yáng}，{招待|zhāo dài}{客人|kè rén}。{木兰|Mù lán}{走|zǒu}{进|jìn}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}，{脱|tuō}{下|xià}{了|le}{军装|jūn zhuāng}，{换|huàn}{上|shàng}{了|le}{以前|yǐ qián}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}，{梳|shū}{好|hǎo}{了|le}{头发|tóu fa}，{对|duì}{着|zhe}{镜子|jìng zi}{化|huà}{好|hǎo}{了|le}{妆|zhuāng}，{然后|rán hòu}{走|zǒu}{出门|chū mén}{去|qù}，{见|jiàn}{她|tā}{的|de}{战友|zhàn yǒu}。
>
> {战友|zhàn yǒu}{们|men}{都|dōu}{大吃一惊|dà chī yì jīng}。{他们|tā men}{跟|gēn}{木兰|Mù lán}{一起|yì qǐ}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{十二|shí èr}{年|nián}{的|de}{仗|zhàng}，{竟然|jìng rán}{从来|cóng lái}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{她|tā}{是|shì}{个|gè}{姑娘|gū niang}！
>
> {诗|shī}{的|de}{最后|zuì hòu}，{用|yòng}{两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{兔子|tù zi}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{比方|bǐ fang}：{平时|píng shí}，{公|gōng}{兔|tù}{和|hé}{母|mǔ}{兔|tù}{很|hěn}{容易|róng yì}{分|fēn}{清楚|qīng chu}；{可是|kě shì}{当|dāng}{两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{兔子|tù zi}{贴|tiē}{着|zhe}{地面|dì miàn}{一起|yì qǐ}{跑|pǎo}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{谁|shéi}{又|yòu}{能|néng}{分|fēn}{得|de}{出|chū}{哪|nǎ}{只|zhī}{是|shì}{公|gōng}{的|de}，{哪|nǎ}{只|zhī}{是|shì}{母|mǔ}{的|de}{呢|ne}？

{织布|zhī bù} is to weave cloth, {叹气|tàn qì} to sigh (HSK 5), {招兵|zhāo bīng} to recruit soldiers, {名单|míng dān} a list of names, {集市|jí shì} a
market, {马鞍|mǎ ān} a saddle, {寒风|hán fēng} a freezing wind, {哗哗|huā huā} the sound of rushing water, {战场|zhàn chǎng} a battlefield, {立功|lì gōng} to win distinction,
{官位|guān wèi} an official post, {奖赏|jiǎng shǎng} a reward, {磨刀|mó dāo} to sharpen a knife, {军装|jūn zhuāng} a uniform, {梳|shū} to comb, {战友|zhàn yǒu} a
comrade in arms; {大吃一惊|dà chī yì jīng} (to get a big surprise) is lesson 28's idiom and {比方|bǐ fang} (a comparison)
lesson 26's word; {一|yí}{卷|juàn}{名单|míng dān} is "a roll of names" ({一|yí}{卷|juàn} is yí juàn, lesson 27's measure word).

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

"Long ago, in the north, there was a girl called Mulan. One day she sat by the door weaving,
but as she wove she kept stopping and sighing, one sigh after another. When her family asked what
she was thinking about, she said: last night she had seen the call-up lists. The khan was raising a
great army, and her father's name was on every roll. Her father was old, and there was no older
brother at home to go in his place.

Mulan thought for a long time, and at last made up her mind: she would go to war in her father's
place. The next day she went all round the markets: a good horse at the east market, a saddle at the west
market, and everything else she needed. Early in the morning she said goodbye to her parents,
dressed as a man, and set off with the army. That night she camped by the Yellow River: she couldn't hear her parents calling her,
only the river rushing by. Further north still, in far-off places, all she heard was the war horses
neighing.

Winters in the north were bitterly cold, and at night there was only the freezing wind and the
neighing of the horses. The war went on for many years. Many generals and soldiers died on the battlefield, but Mulan survived, and
after ten years she returned with the army to the capital. When the emperor saw her, he praised her
great deeds and offered her a high post and many rewards. But Mulan said she wanted no office at
all: all she wanted was a fast horse to get home sooner.

When they heard Mulan was back, the whole family was overjoyed: her old parents, holding each other
up, went outside the town to meet her; her sister got dressed up at home, waiting to see her; her
younger brother sharpened his knife to kill a pig and sheep for the guests. Mulan went into her own
room, took off her uniform, put on her old clothes, combed her hair, made herself up in front of the
mirror, and then went out to see her comrades.

Her comrades were astonished. They had fought alongside Mulan for twelve years, and never once
known she was a girl!

At the end the poem draws a comparison with two hares: usually a buck and a doe are easy to tell
apart; but when two hares run side by side close to the ground, who can say which is the male and
which the female?"
</details>

## The opening lines

> {唧唧|jī jī}{复|fù}{唧唧|jī jī}，{木兰|Mù lán}{当户织|dāng hù zhī}。
> {不闻|bù wén}{机杼声|jī zhù shēng}，{唯闻|wéi wén}{女叹息|nǚ tàn xī}。

| Words | Notes |
|---|---|
| {唧唧|jī jī} | jī jī, a sound said twice: the click of the loom, or, as many read it, sighing |
| {={复|fù}=} (traditional {+{復|fù}+}) | again (written: {又|yòu}, {再|zài}) |
| {当户织|dāng hù zhī} | weaving, facing the door ({当|dāng}: facing; {户|hù}: a door, as in lesson 07's {户|hù} "a household") |
| {不闻|bù wén} | doesn't hear ({闻|wén} wén: to hear, in old Chinese; HSK 4's {闻|wén} "to smell" is the modern sense) |
| {机杼|jī zhù} | the loom and its shuttle |
| {唯|wéi} | only (HSK 5's {唯一|wéi yī}) |
| {女|nǚ} | the girl (Mulan) |
| {叹息|tàn xī} | to sigh (written: {叹气|tàn qì}) |

**In modern Chinese**: {唧唧|jī jī}，{唧唧|jī jī}，{木兰|Mù lán}{对|duì}{着|zhe}{门|mén}{在|zài}{织布|zhī bù}。{可是|kě shì}{听|tīng}{不|bu}{到|dào}{织布机|zhī bù jī}{的|de}{声音|shēng yīn}，{只|zhǐ}{听|tīng}{到|dào}{她|tā}{在|zài}{叹气|tàn qì}。

**Our translation**:

> Click-clack, and click-clack again: Mulan weaves facing the door.
> But no sound of loom and shuttle comes, only the sighs of the girl.

## The closing lines

> {雄兔|xióng tù}{脚扑朔|jiǎo pū shuò}，{雌兔|cí tù}{眼迷离|yǎn mí lí}；
> {双兔|shuāng tù}{傍地走|bàng dì zǒu}，{安能|ān néng}{辨|biàn}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{雄雌|xióng cí}？

| Words | Notes |
|---|---|
| {雄|xióng} / {雌|cí} | male / female (of animals: written; in speech {公|gōng} and lesson 22's {母|mǔ}) |
| {兔|tù} | a hare, a rabbit ({兔子|tù zi}) |
| {扑朔|pū shuò} | (of legs) kicking, scrabbling |
| {迷离|mí lí} | (of eyes) half-closed, blurred |
| {双兔|shuāng tù} | the two hares |
| {傍地走|bàng dì zǒu} | running close to the ground ({傍|bàng}: alongside) |
| {安能|ān néng} | how could (one), written: {怎么|zěn me}{能|néng} |
| {辨|biàn} | to tell apart ({辨别|biàn bié}) |

**In modern Chinese**: {公|gōng}{兔子|tù zi}{的|de}{脚|jiǎo}{爱|ài}{乱|luàn}{动|dòng}，{母|mǔ}{兔子|tù zi}{的|de}{眼睛|yǎn jing}{常常|cháng cháng}{眯|mī}{着|zhe}；{可是|kě shì}{两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{兔子|tù zi}{贴|tiē}{着|zhe}{地面|dì miàn}{一起|yì qǐ}{跑|pǎo}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{谁|shéi}{能|néng}{分|fēn}{得|de}{清|qīng}{哪|nǎ}{只|zhī}{是|shì}{公|gōng}{的|de}，{哪|nǎ}{只|zhī}{是|shì}{母|mǔ}{的|de}{呢|ne}？

**Our translation**:

> The buck hare's feet go scrabbling, the doe's eyes are half-shut;
> but when two hares run side by side over the ground, who can tell if I am he or she?

The speaker of the last line, {我|wǒ}, is Mulan herself, or the poem speaking for her. The image gave
Chinese an idiom: {扑朔迷离|pū shuò mí lí} (*pū shuò mí lí*), "so confusing you can't tell what's what": {案情|àn qíng}{扑朔迷离|pū shuò mí lí}
(the case is baffling).

## Read it aloud

```speak
# 《{木兰诗|Mù lán shī}》
{唧唧|jī jī}{复|fù}{唧唧|jī jī}，{木兰|Mù lán}{当户织|dāng hù zhī}。
= Click-clack, and click-clack again: Mulan weaves facing the door.
{不闻|bù wén}{机杼声|jī zhù shēng}，{唯闻|wéi wén}{女叹息|nǚ tàn xī}。
= But no sound of loom and shuttle comes, only the sighs of the girl.
{雄兔|xióng tù}{脚扑朔|jiǎo pū shuò}，{雌兔|cí tù}{眼迷离|yǎn mí lí}；
= The buck hare's feet go scrabbling, the doe's eyes are half-shut;
{双兔|shuāng tù}{傍地走|bàng dì zǒu}，{安能|ān néng}{辨|biàn}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{雄雌|xióng cí}？
= but when two hares run side by side over the ground, who can tell if I am he or she?
```

## Later Mulans

The ballad says almost nothing about Mulan herself: not even her family name. Later retellings
filled in the gaps:

- **A Ming play.** The writer {徐渭|Xú Wèi} (Xu Wei, 1521–1593) turned the story into a two-act play,
  and gave Mulan the family name {花|huā} (*huā*, flower): the {花木兰|Huā Mù lán} of most modern versions.
- **Opera and film in China.** {梅兰芳|Méi Lán fāng} (Mei Lanfang) played Mulan in a Peking opera version in the 1910s;
  the story has been staged in many regional operas and filmed several times.
- **Disney.** An animated film (1998), and later a live-action one, made Mulan known around the world.
  They add new characters and change the story's details, but keep the core: a daughter who takes her
  father's place, and the surprise when she comes home.

Each version reflects its own time. The ballad's Mulan asks for nothing but to go home; many modern
retellings make her a heroine who wants to prove herself. Reading the original, you notice how much
of it is about her family: the sighs at the loom, her parents waiting outside the town, the younger
brother sharpening the knife for a feast.

## Key points

- 《{木兰诗|Mù lán shī}》 (《{木兰辞|Mù lán cí}》): an anonymous folk ballad, probably of the Northern Dynasties, preserved in
  《{乐府诗集|Yuè fǔ Shī jí}》; mostly lines of five characters.
- The story: Mulan takes her old father's place in the army, fights for years dressed as a man,
  refuses office, comes home; her comrades never knew.
- Opening: {唧唧|jī jī}{复|fù}{唧唧|jī jī}，{木兰|Mù lán}{当户织|dāng hù zhī}。{不闻|bù wén}{机杼声|jī zhù shēng}，{唯闻|wéi wén}{女叹息|nǚ tàn xī}。
- Closing: {雄兔|xióng tù}{脚扑朔|jiǎo pū shuò}，{雌兔|cí tù}{眼迷离|yǎn mí lí}；{双兔|shuāng tù}{傍地走|bàng dì zǒu}，{安能|ān néng}{辨|biàn}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{雄雌|xióng cí}？ (the idiom {扑朔迷离|pū shuò mí lí}).
- Later versions: {徐渭|Xú Wèi}'s Ming play gave her the surname {花|huā}; {梅兰芳|Méi Lán fāng}'s Peking opera; Disney's films.

lessons.title: Building an argument
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The last module of HSK 6 is about how Chinese is used to argue, to write formally and to play with
language, and it ends with the exam. The exam's last writing task is an argued essay of at least
300 characters, and the level-6 standard expects you to comment on a news article: say what it
claims, judge the claim and defend your own view. This lesson gives you the tools for that:

- written connectors that move an argument forward: {进而|jìn ér} (and then, going further), {即便|jí biàn}…{也|yě} (even if)
  and {则|zé} (whereas; then, in that case);
- the words that measure how far a claim goes: {未必|wèi bì} (not necessarily), {不至于|bú zhì yú} (not go so far as),
  {足以|zú yǐ} (enough to), {得以|dé yǐ} (manage to, be enabled to), {毫不|háo bù} / {毫无|háo wú} (not at all), {看似|kàn sì} (seemingly), {算是|suàn shì}
  (can be counted as), {试图|shì tú} (to attempt) and {料|liào} (to expect: {没|méi}{料|liào}{到|dào});
- the vocabulary of reasoning and research: {前提|qián tí}, {假设|jiǎ shè}, {推测|tuī cè}, {证实|zhèng shí}, {排除|pái chú}, {片面|piàn miàn}, {理性|lǐ xìng}, {文献|wén xiàn}, {课题|kè tí}, {立场|lì chǎng}…

Every argued text has the same four parts, and this lesson names them: the **[[thesis]]** ({论点|lùn diǎn}, the view
the text defends), the **[[grounds]]** ({论据|lùn jù}: reasons, facts and examples), a **[[concession]]** (admitting
what is true on the other side) and the **[[conclusion]]**. Together they are the **discourse
structure** of an argument.

The story: {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) now writes commentary pieces ({评论|píng lùn}) for the news website, and her editor
{郑华|Zhèng Huá} (Zheng Hua) is reading her latest draft, on a survey that has been all over the internet.

## {即便|jí biàn}…{也|yě}: even if (written)

{即便|jí biàn} means "even if": the first clause states a condition, even a true one, and {也|yě} in the second says
the result doesn't change. It's the written partner of {即使|jí shǐ} (HSK 4), {就算|jiù suàn} (lesson 23) and {哪怕|nǎ pà}
(HSK 5):

{即便|jí biàn}{明天|míng tiān}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{比赛|bǐ sài}{也|yě}{照|zhào}{常|cháng}{进行|jìn xíng}。 — Even if it rains tomorrow, the match will go ahead as usual.

{即便|jí biàn}{数据|shù jù}{完全|wán quán}{准确|zhǔn què}，{也|yě}{不|bù}{足以|zú yǐ}{证明|zhèng míng}{这个|zhè ge}{结论|jié lùn}。 — Even if the data are completely accurate, that isn't enough to prove the conclusion.

{即便|jí biàn}{是|shì}{专家|zhuān jiā}，{也|yě}{会|huì}{有|yǒu}{看|kàn}{错|cuò}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}。 — Even experts get things wrong sometimes.

| Word | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {就算|jiù suàn}…{也|yě} | spoken | {就算|jiù suàn}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{说|shuō}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{知道|zhī dào}。 |
| {哪怕|nǎ pà}…{也|yě} | spoken and written; a strong "even if" | {哪怕|nǎ pà}{再|zài}{忙|máng}，{他|tā}{也|yě}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{读书|dú shū}。 |
| {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě} | neutral | {即使|jí shǐ}{失败|shī bài}{了|le}，{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{收获|shōu huò}。 |
| {即便|jí biàn}…{也|yě} | written | {即便|jí biàn}{条件|tiáo jiàn}{有限|yǒu xiàn}，{也|yě}{要|yào}{按时|àn shí}{完成|wán chéng}。 |

In an argument, {即便|jí biàn}…{也|yě} is how you **[[concede]]** a point and keep your view: you grant the other side
something ("even if the figures are right") and show that your conclusion still stands.

## {进而|jìn ér}: and then, going one step further

{进而|jìn ér} joins two actions or ideas when the second goes a step further than the first: first A, and on
that basis B. It's written, and usually starts the second clause:

{我们|wǒ men}{先|xiān}{要|yào}{了解|liǎo jiě}{情况|qíng kuàng}，{进而|jìn ér}{提出|tí chū}{解决|jiě jué}{办法|bàn fǎ}。 — First we need to understand the situation, and then go on to propose a solution.

{读者|dú zhě}{先|xiān}{是|shì}{质疑|zhì yí}{这|zhè}{篇|piān}{报道|bào dào}，{进而|jìn ér}{开始|kāi shǐ}{质疑|zhì yí}{整个|zhěng gè}{网站|wǎng zhàn}。 — Readers first questioned the report, and then went on to question the whole website.

{从而|cóng ér} (HSK 5) looks like it but does a different job: {从而|cóng ér} gives the **result** of an action ({他|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{坚持|jiān chí}{练习|liàn xí}，{从而|cóng ér}{提高|tí gāo}{了|le}{水平|shuǐ píng}: and so his level went up), while {进而|jìn ér} gives the **next step** ({他|tā}{先|xiān}{学会|xué huì}{了|le}{拼音|pīn yīn}，{进而|jìn ér}{开始|kāi shǐ}{学|xué}{写|xiě}{汉字|hàn zì}: and then he went on to characters). If you can say "and as a result", it's {从而|cóng ér}; if "and then, going further", {进而|jìn ér}.

## {则|zé}: whereas; then, in that case

{则|zé} is a written word with two uses you need.

**1. Contrast ("whereas", "while").** {则|zé} comes after the second subject, never before it:

{北方|běi fāng}{人|rén}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{面|miàn}{条|tiáo}，{南方|nán fāng}{人|rén}{则|zé}{更|gèng}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}。 — Northerners love noodles, whereas southerners prefer rice.

{前者|qián zhě}{看重|kàn zhòng}{价格|jià gé}，{后者|hòu zhě}{则|zé}{看重|kàn zhòng}{质量|zhì liàng}。 — The former care most about price; the latter, about quality. ({前者|qián zhě} and {后者|hòu zhě} are lesson 27's.)

**2. Condition and consequence ("then").** After {如果|rú guǒ}, {若|ruò} or a condition, {则|zé} is the written {就|jiù}:

{如果|rú guǒ}{不|bù}{及时|jí shí}{处理|chǔ lǐ}，{则|zé}{后果|hòu guǒ}{十分|shí fēn}{严重|yán zhòng}。 — If it isn't dealt with promptly, the consequences will be very serious.

You already know {则|zé} inside {否则|fǒu zé} (HSK 4: otherwise) and {规则|guī zé} (rules). Don't use {则|zé} in conversation:
in speech, the contrast is {而|ér} or nothing at all ({北方|běi fāng}{人|rén}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{面|miàn}{条|tiáo}，{南方|nán fāng}{人|rén}{更|gèng}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}), and the "then" is {就|jiù}.

## How far does a claim go? {未必|wèi bì}, {不至于|bú zhì yú}, {足以|zú yǐ}, {得以|dé yǐ}

An argument is often won or lost on how strongly each sentence claims something. These four words
set the strength.

- **{未必|wèi bì}** (not necessarily) is softer than {不|bù} and more formal than {不|bù}{一定|yí dìng}: {贵|guì}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}{未必|wèi bì}{好|hǎo}。 (Expensive
  things aren't necessarily good.) {他|tā}{说|shuō}{的|de}{未必|wèi bì}{是|shì}{真|zhēn}{的|de}。 It's the commonest way to doubt a claim politely.
- **{不至于|bú zhì yú}** (won't go so far as to, isn't so bad that) says something is not as extreme as feared: {他|tā}
  {不至于|bú zhì yú}{连|lián}{这|zhè}{点|diǎn}{小|xiǎo}{事|shì}{都|dōu}{做|zuò}{不|bu}{好|hǎo}{吧|ba}。 (Surely he can manage something this small.) {问题|wèn tí}{不至于|bú zhì yú}{那么|nà me}{严重|yán zhòng}。 It can
  stand alone as a reply: ——{这么|zhè me}{下去|xià qù}，{公司|gōng sī}{会|huì}{倒闭|dǎo bì}{吗|ma}？——{不至于|bú zhì yú}。
- **{足以|zú yǐ}** (enough to, sufficient to) + verb: {这些|zhè xiē}{证据|zhèng jù}{足以|zú yǐ}{说明|shuō míng}{问题|wèn tí}。 (This evidence is enough to show where
  the problem is.) {一|yí}{次|cì}{失败|shī bài}{不|bù}{足以|zú yǐ}{说明|shuō míng}{什么|shén me}。 (One failure doesn't prove anything.) {不|bù}{足以|zú yǐ} is very common in
  arguments.
- **{得以|dé yǐ}** (written: to manage to, to be enabled to) says that something became possible because of
  what came before; the subject is usually the thing that gets done: {在|zài}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{帮助|bāng zhù}{下|xià}，{问题|wèn tí}{终于|zhōng yú}{得以|dé yǐ}{解决|jiě jué}。
  (With everyone's help, the problem was finally solved.) {由于|yóu yú}{资金|zī jīn}{到|dào}{位|wèi}，{这个|zhè ge}{课题|kè tí}{才|cái}{得以|dé yǐ}{继续|jì xù}。

Notice the difference between {足以|zú yǐ} and {得以|dé yǐ}: {足以|zú yǐ} is about **sufficiency** (is it enough?), {得以|dé yǐ} about
**possibility made real** (it got done, thanks to something).

## {毫不|háo bù} and {毫无|háo wú}: not in the least

{毫|háo} is a tiny amount (you know it from {毫米|háo mǐ}, a millimetre). {毫不|háo bù} and {毫无|háo wú} mean "not in the least", "not at
all", and they're strong and formal:

- **{毫不|háo bù}** + a two-syllable verb or adjective: {毫不|háo bú}{在意|zài yì} (not to care in the least), {毫不|háo bú}{客气|kè qi} (without any
  hesitation or politeness), {毫不|háo bù}{怀疑|huái yí} (not doubt at all), {毫不|háo bù}{奇怪|qí guài} (not at all surprising).
- **{毫无|háo wú}** + a noun ({无|wú} is "have no"): {毫无|háo wú}{道理|dào li} (completely unreasonable), {毫无|háo wú}{疑问|yí wèn} (beyond doubt), {毫无|háo wú}{兴趣|xìng qù}
  (no interest at all), {毫无|háo wú}{价值|jià zhí} (utterly worthless).

{他|tā}{毫不|háo bú}{在意|zài yì}{别人|bié ren}{的|de}{看法|kàn fǎ}。 — He couldn't care less what other people think.

{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{说法|shuō fǎ}{毫无|háo wú}{道理|dào li}。 — That claim makes no sense whatsoever.

The pair also gives you {无疑|wú yí} (undoubtedly): {读书|dú shū}{无疑|wú yí}{是|shì}{好|hǎo}{事|shì}。 (Reading is undoubtedly a good thing.)
In an argument, {毫无|háo wú}{疑问|yí wèn} and {无疑|wú yí} are strong: use them for what really can't be doubted, or a reader
will notice that you haven't proved it.

## {看似|kàn sì}, {算是|suàn shì}, {试图|shì tú} and {料|liào}

- **{看似|kàn sì}** (seemingly, it looks as if) + an adjective or a clause, almost always with a "but in fact" after
  it: {这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{看似|kàn sì}{简单|jiǎn dān}，{其实|qí shí}{很|hěn}{复杂|fù zá}。 (The question looks simple but is actually complicated.) It's how a
  commentary sets up a claim to take apart.
- **{算是|suàn shì}** (can be counted as, more or less): {这|zhè}{次|cì}{考试|kǎo shì}{算是|suàn shì}{顺利|shùn lì}。 (The exam went fairly smoothly, all things
  considered.) {他|tā}{算是|suàn shì}{我们|wǒ men}{班|bān}{最|zuì}{会|huì}{说话|shuō huà}{的|de}{人|rén}{了|le}。 It admits something is so, with a little reserve.
- **{试图|shì tú}** (to attempt, try to) + verb, written, often for an attempt that failed or was resisted: {他|tā}{试图|shì tú}{说服|shuō fú}
  {大家|dà jiā}，{但|dàn}{没有|méi yǒu}{成功|chéng gōng}。 (He tried to win everyone over, but didn't succeed.) In speech, {想|xiǎng} or {想|xiǎng}{办法|bàn fǎ}.
- **{料|liào}** (liào, to expect, anticipate) is a written verb, mostly in {没|méi}{料|liào}{到|dào} (didn't expect) and {料|liào}{到|dào}: {谁|shéi}{也|yě}{没|méi}{料|liào}{到|dào}
  {他|tā}{会|huì}{放弃|fàng qì}。 (Nobody expected him to give up.) {预料|yù liào} (to predict, foresee) is the two-syllable word:
  {结果|jié guǒ}{和|hé}{我们|wǒ men}{预料|yù liào}{的|de}{一样|yí yàng}。 (You met {料|liào} as a noun, material, in lesson 12: a different item with the same
  character and reading.)

   family environment, not the books, may be the cause ({起|qǐ}{作用|zuò yòng}{的|de}{很|hěn}{可能|kě néng}{不|bú}{是|shì}{书|shū}{本身|běn shēn}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{家庭|jiā tíng}{的|de}{整体|zhěng tǐ}{环境|huán jìng}).
3. The fifth: books matter, reading is one of the main ways a child learns about the world, and
   books at home are a good thing in themselves ({当然|dāng rán}，{我|wǒ}{并|bìng}{不|bú}{是|shì}{说|shuō}{书|shū}{不|bú}{重要|zhòng yào}).
4. Not hostile: the survey isn't wrong in itself ({调查|diào chá}{本身|běn shēn}{并|bìng}{没有|méi yǒu}{错|cuò}); what the writer criticises is how
   people read it: reports that quote one striking line and skip the limitations.

"**Do children from homes with many books read better?** Recently a survey set off a lively
discussion online. It found that children with more books at home mostly scored higher in reading
than others of their age. Quite a few articles concluded from this that if you just buy more books,
your child's reading will improve. Some parents bought a hundred books at once, and some bookshops promptly
brought out 'reading lists for clever children'. For a while, 'buying books for children' was a hot topic.

In my view, this conclusion seems reasonable but doesn't necessarily hold. The survey itself isn't
wrong; the question is how we interpret its results.

First, a connection between 'many books' and 'good results' doesn't mean the former brought about the
latter. Let's imagine another situation: families willing to buy their children lots of books often
also care more about education, and the parents have more time to read and talk with their children.
In other words, what makes the difference may well be not the books themselves but the family
environment as a whole, of which many books are only an indirect sign. For example, in a family where the parents read with the
child for half an hour every day, even if there are only a few dozen books at home, the child's reading
won't necessarily be poor. Researchers have already
carried out similar surveys, and once family income and other factors were ruled out, the difference
between the two groups of children became very small. Unless these factors are ruled out, it's hard
to confirm that there really is cause and effect between books and results.

Second, even if the survey's data are entirely accurate, that isn't enough to show that 'buying books
is all it takes'. The survey only covered families in a few particular cities; whether the conclusion
applies to other regions needs further study. And some reports quoted only the most eye-catching line
of the survey, ignoring the limitations the researchers themselves mentioned at the end of their
report: a reading like that can hardly avoid being one-sided. Besides, a reading score is only one way of
measuring a child and can't stand for all a child can do. Whether a child loves reading, and whether
they really think while they read, can hardly be shown by the marks of a single test.

Of course, I'm not saying books don't matter. Quite the opposite: reading is undoubtedly one of the
main ways a child comes to know the world. With books at home, children can open one whenever they
like, and that in itself is a good thing. And books
vary: the ones that suit a child's age are worth the most. What I object to is not buying books, but turning a
complicated question into a slogan.

So when we face a survey, we must first distinguish 'connected' from 'cause and effect', and then go
on to ask what other factors have been overlooked. In the end, data can only tell us 'what'; the
'why' is for us to think out. Only if we look at data rationally will we avoid
being led by the nose by a conclusion that only looks simple. For parents, rather than spending a lot
of money on books, it would be better to set aside half an hour a day and read one with their
child."
</details>

How the commentary is built, paragraph by paragraph:

| Paragraph | Its job | Signal words |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the news: what was claimed | {日前|rì qián}, {由此|yóu cǐ}{认定|rèn dìng} |
| 2 | the thesis | {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}, {看似|kàn sì}…{其实|qí shí}{未必|wèi bì} |
| 3 | reason 1, with evidence | {首先|shǒu xiān}, {不妨|bù fáng}{设想|shè xiǎng}, {换句话说|huàn jù huà shuō}, {已|yǐ}{有|yǒu}{研究者|yán jiū zhě} |
| 4 | reason 2 | {其次|qí cì}, {即便|jí biàn}…{也|yě}{不|bù}{足以|zú yǐ} |
| 5 | the concession | {当然|dāng rán}，{我|wǒ}{并|bìng}{不|bú}{是|shì}{说|shuō}…, {恰恰|qià qià}{相反|xiāng fǎn} |
| 6 | the conclusion, and advice | {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}, {进而|jìn ér}, {只有|zhǐ yǒu}…{才|cái}{不至于|bú zhì yú}, {与其|yǔ qí}…{不如|bù rú} |

## Write it: an argued essay

The HSK 6 exam asks for an essay of at least 300 characters giving and defending your opinion (as
reported from the sample papers). Write 300–400 characters on this: {有|yǒu}{人|rén}{认为|rèn wéi}，{孩子|hái zi}{应该|yīng gāi}{从小|cóng xiǎo}{就|jiù}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}
{手机|shǒu jī}；{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{认为|rèn wéi}，{这样|zhè yàng}{做|zuò}{弊大于利|bì dà yú lì}。{你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{看|kàn}？ (Some people think children should have a phone of their own from
an early age; others think this does more harm than good. What do you think? {弊大于利|bì dà yú lì}: the harm outweighs the
benefit.)

Plan in four parts:

1. **[[Thesis]]**: one or two sentences: {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}…; {在|zài}{我|wǒ}{看来|kàn lái}…; {我|wǒ}{并|bìng}{不|bù}{完全|wán quán}{赞成|zàn chéng}….
2. **[[Grounds]]**: two reasons, each with an example or a fact ({首先|shǒu xiān}…{其次|qí cì}…; {一|yì}{方面|fāng miàn}…{另|lìng}{一|yì}{方面|fāng miàn}…).
3. **[[Concession]]**: grant one point to the other side, then keep your view ({当然|dāng rán}…; {即便|jí biàn}…{也|yě}…; {诚然|chéng rán} is possible
   but very bookish: {当然|dāng rán} is usually enough).
4. **[[Conclusion]]**: draw it together ({由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}…; {总之|zǒng zhī}…), ideally with a practical suggestion.

Checklist: Is the thesis clear by the end of the first paragraph? Does each reason have an
example? Did you use {未必|wèi bì} or {不|bù}{一定|yí dìng} where you aren't sure, instead of claiming too much? Is the register
written ({不至于|bú zhì yú}, {即便|jí biàn}, {进而|jìn ér}) and not chatty ({吧|ba}, {啊|a}, {嘛|ma})? Did you count to at least 300?

<details>
<summary>A model (about 360 characters)</summary>

> **{孩子|hái zi}{该|gāi}{不|bu}{该|gāi}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}？**
>
> {如今|rú jīn}，{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}{的|de}{孩子|hái zi}{上|shàng}{小学|xiǎo xué}{就|jiù}{有|yǒu}{了|le}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}。{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{认为|rèn wéi}{这样|zhè yàng}{很|hěn}{方便|fāng biàn}，{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{担心|dān xīn}{孩子|hái zi}{会|huì}{因此|yīn cǐ}{养成|yǎng chéng}{坏|huài}{习惯|xí guàn}。{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{看来|kàn lái}，{孩子|hái zi}{可以|kě yǐ}{有|yǒu}{手机|shǒu jī}，{但|dàn}{前提|qián tí}{是|shì}{父母|fù mǔ}{要|yào}{和|hé}{孩子|hái zi}{一起|yì qǐ}{定|dìng}{好|hǎo}{规矩|guī ju}。
>
> {首先|shǒu xiān}，{手机|shǒu jī}{首要|shǒu yào}{的|de}{作用|zuò yòng}{是|shì}{联系|lián xì}。{孩子|hái zi}{放学|fàng xué}{以后|yǐ hòu}{去|qù}{上|shàng}{课外班|kè wài bān}，{或者|huò zhě}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{回|huí}{家|jiā}，{有|yǒu}{了|le}{手机|shǒu jī}，{父母|fù mǔ}{就|jiù}{能|néng}{随时|suí shí}{知道|zhī dào}{孩子|hái zi}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}。{其次|qí cì}，{手机|shǒu jī}{也|yě}{是|shì}{学习|xué xí}{的|de}{途径|tú jìng}{之|zhī}{一|yī}。{查|chá}{一|yí}{个|gè}{词|cí}、{看|kàn}{一|yí}{段|duàn}{科普|kē pǔ}{视频|shì pín}，{都|dōu}{能|néng}{让|ràng}{孩子|hái zi}{学|xué}{到|dào}{书本|shū běn}{以外|yǐ wài}{的|de}{知识|zhī shi}，{进而|jìn ér}{培养|péi yǎng}{他们|tā men}{自己|zì jǐ}{找|zhǎo}{答案|dá àn}{的|de}{习惯|xí guàn}。
>
> {当然|dāng rán}，{我|wǒ}{并|bìng}{不|bù}{否认|fǒu rèn}{手机|shǒu jī}{的|de}{坏处|huài chu}。{有的|yǒu de}{孩子|hái zi}{一|yì}{拿|ná}{起|qǐ}{手机|shǒu jī}{就|jiù}{放|fàng}{不|bu}{下|xià}，{影响|yǐng xiǎng}{了|le}{学习|xué xí}{和|hé}{睡眠|shuì mián}。{不过|bú guò}，{即便如此|jí biàn rú cǐ}，{问题|wèn tí}{也|yě}{未必|wèi bì}{出|chū}{在|zài}{手机|shǒu jī}{本身|běn shēn}，{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}{怎么|zěn me}{用|yòng}。{如果|rú guǒ}{父母|fù mǔ}{规定|guī dìng}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{用|yòng}{多|duō}{长|cháng}{时间|shí jiān}、{在|zài}{什么|shén me}{地方|dì fang}{用|yòng}，{并且|bìng qiě}{自己|zì jǐ}{也|yě}{做|zuò}{出|chū}{榜样|bǎng yàng}，{情况|qíng kuàng}{就|jiù}{不至于|bú zhì yú}{那么|nà me}{糟|zāo}。
>
> {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}，{与其|yǔ qí}{简单|jiǎn dān}{地|de}{说|shuō}"{给|gěi}"{或者|huò zhě}"{不|bù}{给|gěi}"，{不如|bù rú}{把|bǎ}{重心|zhòng xīn}{放|fàng}{在|zài}{教|jiāo}{孩子|hái zi}{怎样|zěn yàng}{使用|shǐ yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}。{这样|zhè yàng}，{手机|shǒu jī}{才|cái}{能|néng}{真正|zhēn zhèng}{成为|chéng wéi}{孩子|hái zi}{成长|chéng zhǎng}{的|de}{帮手|bāng shou}。

"**Should children have their own phones?** Nowadays more and more children have a phone of their
own by primary school. Some think this is convenient; others worry children will pick up bad habits
from it. In my view children can have a phone, but on the condition that the parents set rules
together with the child.

First, a phone's main purpose is contact. When children go to an after-school class or come home on
their own, with a phone the parents can always know where they are. Second, a phone is also one way
of learning: looking up a word or watching a short popular-science video teaches children things
beyond their textbooks, and goes on to build the habit of finding answers for themselves.

Of course, I don't deny the downside. Some children can't put the phone down once they pick it up,
and their studies and sleep suffer. But even so, the problem isn't necessarily the phone itself but
how it's used. If parents set how long and where it may be used each day, and set an example
themselves, things needn't get that bad.

So rather than simply saying 'yes' or 'no', it's better to put the emphasis on teaching children how
to use a phone. Then the phone can really become a help as they grow up."

{课外班|kè wài bān}: an after-school class; {帮手|bāng shou}: a helper; {即便如此|jí biàn rú cǐ}: even so (written).
</details>

## Speaking: give your opinion

The speaking test ends with two opinion questions, with a few minutes to prepare each (as
reported). Use the essay's shape out loud: thesis, two reasons, a concession, a conclusion. Listen
to the model, then answer in your own words.

```speak
# {你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{看|kàn}{网上|wǎng shàng}{的|de}{各种|gè zhǒng}{调查|diào chá}{结果|jié guǒ}？
{你|nǐ}{经常|jīng cháng}{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{调查|diào chá}{结果|jié guǒ}{吗|ma}？{你|nǐ}{相信|xiāng xìn}{这些|zhè xiē}{结果|jié guǒ}{吗|ma}？
= Do you often see survey results online? Do you believe them?
{我|wǒ}{经常|jīng cháng}{看|kàn}{到|dào}，{不过|bú guò}{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{会|huì}{马上|mǎ shàng}{相信|xiāng xìn}，{至少|zhì shǎo}{要|yào}{先|xiān}{想|xiǎng}{一|yì}{想|xiǎng}。
= I see them often, but I don't believe them straight away: at least I think about them first.
{首先|shǒu xiān}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{报道|bào dào}{只|zhǐ}{引|yǐn}{了|le}{最|zuì}{吸引|xī yǐn}{人|rén}{的|de}{一|yí}{句|jù}{话|huà}，{忽略|hū lüè}{了|le}{调查|diào chá}{的|de}{局限|jú xiàn}。
= First, lots of reports quote only the most eye-catching line and skip the survey's limitations.
{其次|qí cì}，{两|liǎng}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{有|yǒu}{关联|guān lián}，{未必|wèi bì}{就|jiù}{有|yǒu}{因果关系|yīn guǒ guān xì}。
= Second, if two things are connected, that doesn't necessarily mean one causes the other.
{当然|dāng rán}，{调查|diào chá}{本身|běn shēn}{是|shì}{有|yǒu}{价值|jià zhí}{的|de}，{可以|kě yǐ}{帮|bāng}{我们|wǒ men}{了解|liǎo jiě}{大致|dà zhì}{的|de}{情况|qíng kuàng}。
= Of course, surveys have value in themselves: they can give us a rough picture.
{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}，{看|kàn}{调查|diào chá}{要|yào}{理性|lǐ xìng}，{不要|bú yào}{被|bèi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{看似|kàn sì}{简单|jiǎn dān}{的|de}{结论|jié lùn}{牵着走|qiān zhe zǒu}。
= So I think we should read surveys rationally and not be led by the nose by a conclusion that only looks simple.
```

## Say it

```speak
# Arguing carefully
{这个|zhè ge}{说法|shuō fǎ}{看似|kàn sì}{有|yǒu}{道理|dào li}，{其实|qí shí}{未必|wèi bì}{站得住|zhàn de zhù}。
= That claim looks reasonable, but it doesn't necessarily hold up.
{一|yí}{次|cì}{失败|shī bài}{不|bù}{足以|zú yǐ}{说明|shuō míng}{什么|shén me}。
= One failure doesn't prove anything.
{即便|jí biàn}{他|tā}{说|shuō}{的|de}{是|shì}{真|zhēn}{的|de}，{也|yě}{不|bù}{能|néng}{排除|pái chú}{其他|qí tā}{原因|yuán yīn}。
= Even if what he says is true, other causes can't be ruled out.
{毫无|háo wú}{疑问|yí wèn}，{这|zhè}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{恰当|qià dàng}{的|de}{例子|lì zi}。
= Without a doubt, that's an apt example.
{问题|wèn tí}{不至于|bú zhì yú}{那么|nà me}{严重|yán zhòng}{吧|ba}。
= Surely the problem isn't that serious.
{谁|shéi}{也|yě}{没|méi}{料|liào}{到|dào}{结果|jié guǒ}{会|huì}{是|shì}{这样|zhè yàng}。
= Nobody expected it to turn out like this.
```

## Pronunciation

- {进而|jìn ér} jìn ér: two syllables, with no linking sound: the apostrophe in the run-together spelling
  jìn'ér marks the break. {而|ér} is second tone.
- {大都|dà dōu} dà dōu here (mostly), not dū as in {首都|shǒu dū} and {都市|dū shì}. {都|dōu} dōu is the adverb; dū is a capital or a big city.
- {比方|bǐ fang} bǐ fang and {情形|qíng xing} qíng xing: light second syllables.
- {毫不|háo bù} háo bù, {毫无|háo wú} háo wú: in {毫不|háo bù} the {不|bù} follows the usual rule for the next syllable: bú before a
  fourth tone ({毫不|háo bú}{在意|zài yì} háo bú zài yì, {毫不|háo bú}{客气|kè qi} háo bú kè qi), bù before the others ({毫不|háo bù}{怀疑|huái yí} háo bù huái yí).
- {未必|wèi bì} wèi bì: both fourth tones, with the wèi of {未来|wèi lái}.
- {料|liào} liào and {了|le} liǎo ({了解|liǎo jiě}) are different syllables: liào is fourth tone.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{南方|nán fāng}{人|rén}{则|zé}{更|gèng}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}，{北方|běi fāng}{人|rén}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{面|miàn}{条|tiáo}~~ is upside down: {则|zé} introduces the **second**, contrasting half, and it
  comes after its subject: {北方|běi fāng}{人|rén}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{面|miàn}{条|tiáo}，{南方|nán fāng}{人|rén}{则|zé}{更|gèng}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}。
- ~~{则|zé}{南方|nán fāng}{人|rén}{更|gèng}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}~~: {则|zé} never comes before the subject; write {南方|nán fāng}{人|rén}{则|zé}….
- ~~{毫无|háo wú}{在意|zài yì}~~: {毫无|háo wú} takes a noun ({毫无|háo wú}{兴趣|xìng qù}); with a verb or adjective, {毫不|háo bù}: {毫不|háo bú}{在意|zài yì}.
- ~~{问题|wèn tí}{得以|dé yǐ}{严重|yán zhòng}~~: {得以|dé yǐ} is for something that gets done or becomes possible, a good result: {问题|wèn tí}{得以|dé yǐ}{解决|jiě jué}.
  For "enough to", {足以|zú yǐ}: {这|zhè}{足以|zú yǐ}{说明|shuō míng}{问题|wèn tí}{的|de}{严重|yán zhòng}.
- {他|tā}{试图|shì tú}{今天|jīn tiān}{完成|wán chéng} is heard, but {试图|shì tú} sounds odd for a simple plan: it suggests a hard or failed attempt. For
  "plans to", say {他|tā}{打算|dǎ suàn}{今天|jīn tiān}{完成|wán chéng}.
- Don't use {即便|jí biàn}, {则|zé} and {进而|jìn ér} in a chat with friends: they're written. Say {就算|jiù suàn}…{也|yě}, {就|jiù} and {然后|rán hòu}{再|zài}.

## Key points

- {即便|jí biàn}…{也|yě} (written even if), beside {就算|jiù suàn} (spoken), {哪怕|nǎ pà} and {即使|jí shǐ}; it's how an argument concedes a point.
- {进而|jìn ér} (and then, going further) gives the next step; {从而|cóng ér} gives the result.
- {则|zé}: "whereas" after the second subject ({前者|qián zhě}…，{后者|hòu zhě}{则|zé}…); written "then" after a condition.
- How strong a claim is: {未必|wèi bì} (not necessarily), {不至于|bú zhì yú} (not that bad), {足以|zú yǐ} / {不|bù}{足以|zú yǐ} (enough / not enough
  to), {得以|dé yǐ} (got done, thanks to something), {毫不|háo bù} + verb, {毫无|háo wú} + noun, {无疑|wú yí} (undoubtedly), {看似|kàn sì}…{其实|qí shí},
  {算是|suàn shì}, {试图|shì tú} (attempt), {没|méi}{料|liào}{到|dào} / {预料|yù liào}.
- An argued text: thesis ({论点|lùn diǎn}), grounds ({论据|lùn jù}), concession, conclusion; a commentary first says what the
  news claimed.
- New characters: {呈|chéng} {涉|shè} {径|jìng} (✎ {呈|chéng} {径|jìng}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Formal and practical writing
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Since HSK 4 you've met the written words of Chinese a few at a time: {此|cǐ} and {与|yǔ}, then {便|biàn}, {其|qí} and {如何|rú hé},
then {于|yú} inside {由于|yóu yú} and {对于|duì yú}. Level 6 completes the set, and this lesson puts it in one place. Two
kinds of text need it most, and the exam asks for both:

- **[[practical texts]]** ({应用文|yìng yòng wén}): notices ({公告|gōng gào}, {启事|qǐ shì}), requests, complaints, letters of thanks. The exam's
  first writing task is one of these, at least 150 characters, such as a notice looking for a
  flatmate (as reported from the sample papers);
- **reports**: the language of {前者|qián zhě} and {后者|hòu zhě}, {本身|běn shēn}, {层面|céng miàn} and {定义|dìng yì}, which you'll need to read the exam's
  longer passages.

What changes between speech and writing is the **[[register]]**: the same message can be said in
everyday words or written in formal ones, and choosing the right one is part of getting it right.
At the end of the lesson you'll see one message twice, as a chat and as a notice.

The story: {王芳|Wáng Fāng} and {李明|Lǐ Míng} are moving into a flat of their own, so {安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) needs a new flatmate for
the {新城|Xīn chéng} flat. And at the art museum where Anna works, a new exhibition is about to open.

## {于|yú}: in, at, from, than (written)

You know {于|yú} inside words: {由于|yóu yú}, {对于|duì yú}, {关于|guān yú}, {于是|yú shì}, {终于|zhōng yú}, {属于|shǔ yú}, {在于|zài yú}, {等于|děng yú}, {高于|gāo yú} / {低于|dī yú}. On its own it's the
written preposition for time and place, and for "than" or "to" after some verbs and adjectives:

| Use | Example | Spoken |
|---|---|---|
| time | {该|gāi}{馆|guǎn}{建|jiàn}{于|yú}1958{年|nián}。 | {这个|zhè ge}{博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{是|shì}1958{年|nián}{建|jiàn}{的|de}。 |
| place | {会议|huì yì}{将|jiāng}{于|yú}{本|běn}{周五|zhōu wǔ}{在|zài}{三|sān}{楼|lóu}{举行|jǔ xíng}。 | {会|huì}{是|shì}{这个|zhè ge}{星期|xīng qī}{五|wǔ}{在|zài}{三|sān}{楼|lóu}{开|kāi}。 |
| "from" (a source) | {这个|zhè ge}{说法|shuō fǎ}{源于|yuán yú}{一|yí}{个|gè}{古老|gǔ lǎo}{的|de}{故事|gù shi}。 | {这个|zhè ge}{说法|shuō fǎ}{来自|lái zì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{老|lǎo}{故事|gù shi}。 |
| "than" | {今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{人数|rén shù}{多|duō}{于|yú}{去年|qù nián}。 | {今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{人|rén}{比|bǐ}{去年|qù nián}{多|duō}。 |
| "to" | {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{适用|shì yòng}{于|yú}{初|chū}{学者|xué zhě}。 | {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{适合|shì hé}{初|chū}{学者|xué zhě}{用|yòng}。 |

A whole family of two-character verbs and adjectives ends in {于|yú}, and they're all written: {位于|wèi yú} (to be
located in), {用于|yòng yú} (to be used for), {源于|yuán yú} (to originate in, lesson 15), {出于|chū yú} (out of, lesson 26), {限于|xiàn yú} (to be
limited to), {易于|yì yú} (easy to), {处于|chǔ yú} (to be in a state of), {便于|biàn yú} (convenient for). Two are this lesson's:

- **{限于|xiàn yú}** (to be limited to, confined to): {本|běn}{次|cì}{活动|huó dòng}{限于|xiàn yú}{本|běn}{校|xiào}{学生|xué sheng}{参加|cān jiā}。 (This event is open to students of the
  school only.) {限于|xiàn yú}{时间|shí jiān}，{今天|jīn tiān}{只|zhǐ}{讲|jiǎng}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}。 (For reasons of time, I'll make only three points today.)
- **{易于|yì yú}** (easy to, apt to): {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{方法|fāng fǎ}{易于|yì yú}{掌握|zhǎng wò}。 (This method is easy to master.) Its opposite is {难以|nán yǐ} (hard to:
  {难以|nán yǐ}{理解|lǐ jiě}).

**{至于|zhì yú}** (as for, as to) turns to a new topic, often a less important or separate one: {我们|wǒ men}{已经|yǐ jīng}{决定|jué dìng}{去|qù}
{苏州|Sū zhōu}{了|le}，{至于|zhì yú}{住|zhù}{哪儿|nǎr}，{到|dào}{了|le}{再说|zài shuō}。 (We've decided on Suzhou; as for where to stay, we'll see when we get there.) Don't
confuse it with lesson 26's {不至于|bú zhì yú} (not go so far as to).

## {因|yīn}, {之所以|zhī suǒ yǐ}…{是|shì}{因为|yīn wèi}, {为此|wèi cǐ}, {为何|wèi hé}

- **{因|yīn}** (because of; because) is the written {因为|yīn wèi}, often directly before a noun: {因|yīn}{病|bìng}{请假|qǐng jià} (to ask for
  sick leave), {因|yīn}{雨|yǔ}{推迟|tuī chí} (put off because of rain), {因|yīn}{故|gù} (for some reason: notices use it when they
  don't say why). {比赛|bǐ sài}{因|yīn}{雨|yǔ}{推迟|tuī chí}{到|dào}{下|xià}{周|zhōu}。
- **{之所以|zhī suǒ yǐ}…{是|shì}{因为|yīn wèi}** (the reason why … is that …) puts the **result first** and then gives the cause, for
  emphasis: {他|tā}{之所以|zhī suǒ yǐ}{成功|chéng gōng}，{是|shì}{因为|yīn wèi}{从来|cóng lái}{不|bú}{放弃|fàng qì}。 (The reason he succeeded is that he never gave up.) Compare the
  neutral order {因为|yīn wèi}{他|tā}{从来|cóng lái}{不|bú}{放弃|fàng qì}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{成功|chéng gōng}{了|le}。 {之所以|zhī suǒ yǐ} always comes after the subject.
- **{为此|wèi cǐ}** (wèi cǐ, for this reason, to this end) starts a sentence that responds to what came before:
  {很|hěn}{多|duō}{读者|dú zhě}{反映|fǎn yìng}{字|zì}{太|tài}{小|xiǎo}。{为此|wèi cǐ}，{我们|wǒ men}{对|duì}{网页|wǎng yè}{进行|jìn xíng}{了|le}{修改|xiū gǎi}。 (Many readers said the print was too small. We have therefore
  changed the page.)
- **{为何|wèi hé}** (wèi hé, why) is the written {为什么|wèi shén me}: {为何|wèi hé}{会|huì}{出现|chū xiàn}{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{情况|qíng kuàng}？

## {以便|yǐ biàn} and {以免|yǐ miǎn}: so that, so as not to

Both begin the **second** clause and give its purpose. **{以便|yǐ biàn}** (so that, in order to) introduces what you
want to make possible; **{以免|yǐ miǎn}** (so as not to, lest) introduces what you want to avoid:

{请|qǐng}{提前|tí qián}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{到|dào}{场|chǎng}，{以便|yǐ biàn}{工作|gōng zuò}{人员|rén yuán}{安排|ān pái}{座位|zuò wèi}。 — Please arrive ten minutes early so that staff can seat you.

{请|qǐng}{保管|bǎo guǎn}{好|hǎo}{贵重|guì zhòng}{物品|wù pǐn}，{以免|yǐ miǎn}{丢失|diū shī}。 — Please look after your valuables so that they aren't lost.

Spoken, you'd say {好让|hǎo ràng}… and {免得|miǎn de}… (or {不然|bù rán}…): {早|zǎo}{点儿|diǎnr}{来|lái}，{好让|hǎo ràng}{我们|wǒ men}{安排|ān pái}{座位|zuò wèi}；{东西|dōng xi}{拿|ná}{好|hǎo}，{免得|miǎn de}{丢|diū}{了|le}。 The single
character **{免|miǎn}** (to be spared, to avoid) is written too: {免|miǎn}{收|shōu}{门票|mén piào} (no admission charge), and on a door {闲人免进|xián rén miǎn jìn}
(staff only: literally "idle people spared from entering", a set phrase).

Notes on a few of them:

- **{该|gāi}** (gāi) here is not HSK 3's {该|gāi} "should": it's a written demonstrative, "the said", for something
  just named: {王|wáng}{先生|xiān sheng}{在|zài}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。{该|gāi}{公司|gōng sī}…. It goes directly before the noun, without a measure word.
- **{特|tè}** is in set phrases of letters and notices: {特此|tè cǐ}{通知|tōng zhī} (this notice is hereby given), {特此|tè cǐ}{感谢|gǎn xiè} (with
  thanks hereby given). {此|cǐ} is "this" and {特|tè} "specially".
- **{未|wèi}** is "not" for the past ({未|wèi}{参加|cān jiā}, did not take part) and "not yet": {尚未|shàng wèi} (not yet, very formal),
  {未经|wèi jīng}{许可|xǔ kě} (without permission). You know it in {未必|wèi bì} and {未来|wèi lái}.
- **{一一|yī yī}** keeps {一|yī} as yī both times: yī yī, never yí yī. It's an exception to the tone rule.
- **{加以|jiā yǐ}** takes a two-syllable verb **as its object**: {加以|jiā yǐ}{解决|jiě jué}, {加以|jiā yǐ}{说明|shuō míng}, {加以|jiā yǐ}{改进|gǎi jìn} (to improve). It sounds
  official; in speech, just use the verb: {要|yào}{研究|yán jiū}{一下|yí xià}.
- **{一律|yí lǜ}** is for rules: {本|běn}{店|diàn}{商品|shāng pǐn}{一律|yí lǜ}{八|bā}{折|zhé} (everything in the shop is 20 % off).

| Word | Strength | Example |

| {不许|bù xǔ} | not allowed (spoken too) | {考试|kǎo shì}{时|shí}{不许|bù xǔ}{说话|shuō huà}。 |

| {严禁|yán jìn} | strictly forbidden | {馆|guǎn}{内|nèi}{严禁|yán jìn}{吸|xī}{烟|yān}。 |

don't confuse it with HSK 4's {不得不|bù dé bù} (bù dé bù, to have to).

- **{截至|jié zhì}** (up to, as of a date) and **{截止|jié zhǐ}** (to close, a deadline): {截至|jié zhì}{十|shí}{月|yuè}{底|dǐ}，{已|yǐ}{有|yǒu}{三千|sān qiān}{人|rén}{报名|bào míng}。 (As of the
  end of October, three thousand people had signed up.) {报名|bào míng}{截止|jié zhǐ}{日期|rì qī}{是|shì}{十一|shí yī}{月|yuè}{五|wǔ}{日|rì}。 (Registration closes on 5

### Stroke order

- **{抄|chāo}**: 扌 first; then {少|shǎo}: the vertical hook, the dots on either side, the long left-falling stroke last.
- **{截|jié}**: the short horizontal and vertical at the top left first, then the long horizontal of 戈,
  then 隹 inside, then the slanting hook, the left-falling stroke and the dot of 戈 last.
- **{旬|xún}**: the left-falling stroke, the horizontal-turn-hook of 勹, then {日|rì} inside.

## Write it: practical texts

The exam's first writing task is a practical text of at least 150 characters. Write 150–200
characters for one of these, then compare the model.

1. **A flatmate-wanted notice** ({合租|hé zū}{启事|qǐ shì}): you have a spare room in a flat near your work. Say where the
   flat is, what the room has, what you'd like in a flatmate, and how to get in touch.
2. **A request to a landlord**: the water heater in your flat has broken twice this month. Ask the
   landlord to replace it, and say when you're at home.
3. **A complaint** ({投诉信|tóu sù xìn}) to a gym: the swimming pool has been closed for a month without notice,
   though your membership includes it.

your name and the date).
